\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathcal{B}(G_K)\text{ is nonempty and convex for the specialization to the }\Gamma\text{-building.}
statements.conclusion_latex: \text{All maximal facets in }\mathfrak{F}\text{ have equal dimension, and }F\in\mathfrak{F}\text{ is maximal iff }\dim(F\cap X)\text{ is maximal. statements.title: Automorphism groups and split extension for D4 Dynkin diagrams
statements.statement_plain: Assume deg(L/K)=1, equivalently that G_K* is split. Then the affine diagram tilde D_K has type D4, with automorphism group S4, while the ordinary diagram D_K has automorphism group S3. The subgroup Xi is the unique Sylow-2 subgroup of A4 and is isomorphic to (Z/2Z)^2. Thus 1 -> (Z/2Z)^2 -> S4 -> S3 -> 1 is exact and splits by taking the stabilizer in S4 of any non-central affine D4 node.

The group \Xi is the unique Sylow 2-subgroup of A_4 and \Xi\cong(\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z)^2. There is an exact sequence 1\to(\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z)^2\to S_4\to S_3\to1, which splits after choosing any one of the four non-central nodes of the affine D_4 Dynkin diagram and identifying S_3 with its stabilizer subgroup in S_4.

statements.title: Axiomatic definition of a Coxeter system
statements.statement_plain: A Coxeter system is a pair (W,S) where W is generated by involutions S and the finite-order products ss' give the presentation relations (ss')^m=1. With one generator W is Z/2Z; with two generators W is dihedral of order 2m(s,s').
statements.statement_latex: A Coxeter system is a pair (W,S) such that W is a group, S\subseteq W generates W, every s\in S has order 2, and, writing m(s,s')=\operatorname{ord}(ss') and I=\{(s,s')\in S^2:m(s,s')<\infty\}, the presentation relations (ss')^{m(s,s')}=1 for (s,s')\in I give a presentation of W. For |S|=1, W\cong\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z; for |S|=2, W is dihedral of order 2m(s,s').
assumptions_latex: W\text{ is a group}
S\subseteq W
S\text{ generates }W
s^2=1\text{ for every }s\in S
statements.conclusion_latex: With m(s,s')=\operatorname{ord}(ss') and I=\{(s,s')\in S^2:m(s,s')<\infty\}, the relations (ss')^{m(s,s')}=1 for (s,s')\in I, together with generators S, form a presentation of W. If |S|=1, then W\cong\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z; if |S|=2, then W is dihedral of order 2m(s,s').
statements.scope_note: The order m(s,s') may be infinite; I consists of the pairs for which it is finite. The rank-one and rank-two conclusions are stated in the source after the definition.

statements.title: Coroots and orthogonal reflections from an invariant scalar product
statements.statement_plain: An invariant scalar product on V induces a degenerate symmetric form on affine functionals A*, with exactly the constant functionals isotropic. Every affine root is anisotropic; its coroot is 2psi divided by <psi,psi>, its gradient is the coroot of its linear part, the coroot and root define the same reflecting hyperplane, and the affine reflection restricts to the orthogonal reflection across that hyperplane.
statements.statement_latex: Given a scalar product on V invariant under W(\nabla\Psi), identify V with V^* and define the symmetric bilinear form on A^* by \langle\psi,\eta\rangle=\langle\dot\psi,\dot\eta\rangle. This form is degenerate, and its isotropic vectors are exactly the constant functionals. For each \psi\in\Psi, define \psi^{\vee}=2\psi/\langle\psi,\psi\rangle; then \nabla(\psi^{\vee})=\dot\psi^{\vee}, H_{\psi^{\vee}}=H_{\psi}, and r_{\psi}|_{A} is the orthogonal reflection across H_{\psi}.
assumptions_latex: \langle-,-\rangle\text{ is a scalar product on }V\text{ invariant under }W(\nabla\Psi).

statements.title: Coxeter graph of a Coxeter system
statements.statement_plain: Given a Coxeter system (W,S), the Coxeter graph is the pair (G,f) with vertex set S. Distinct generators s and s' are joined exactly when the order m(s,s') of ss' is at least 3, equivalently when they do not commute. Each edge {s,s'} is labeled by m(s,s'), which is either infinity or an integer at least 3.
statements.statement_latex: For a Coxeter system (W,S), its Coxeter graph is the pair (G,f), where V(G)=S and distinct s,s'\in S are adjacent exactly when m(s,s')=\operatorname{ord}(ss')\ge 3 (equivalently, they do not commute), and f maps the edge \{s,s'\} to m(s,s')\in\{\infty\}\cup\{n\in\mathbb Z:n\ge 3\}.
assumptions_latex: (W,S)\text{ is a Coxeter system.}
statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Cox}(W,S)=(G,f),\quad V(G)=S,\quad \{s,s'\}\in E(G)\iff s\ne s'\text{ and }m(s,s')=\operatorname{ord}(ss')\ge 3,\quad f(\{s,s'\})=m(s,s')\in\{\infty\}\cup\{n\in\mathbb Z:n\ge3\}.
statements.scope_note: Definition of the Coxeter graph associated with an arbitrary Coxeter system (W,S).

statements.title: Subgroups generated by subsets of Coxeter generators
statements.statement_plain: Given a Coxeter system (W,S), the subgroup W_X generated by any subset X of S consists exactly of the elements whose support is contained in X. It satisfies W_X intersect S = X and W_X intersect W_Y = W_{X intersect Y}; moreover, (W_X,X) is itself a Coxeter system.
statements.statement_latex: Let (W,S) be a Coxeter system. For each subset X\subseteq S, define W_X=\langle X\rangle. Then W_X=\{w\in W:\operatorname{supp}(w)\subseteq X\}; in particular W_X\cap S=X, and for X,Y\subseteq S, W_X\cap W_Y=W_{X\cap Y}. The pair (W_X,X) is a Coxeter system.
assumptions_latex: (W,S) is a Coxeter system.
X,Y\subseteq S.
statements.conclusion_latex: W_X=\langle X\rangle=\{w\in W:\operatorname{supp}(w)\subseteq X\},\quad W_X\cap S=X,\quad W_X\cap W_Y=W_{X\cap Y},\quad (W_X,X)\text{ is a Coxeter system}.
statements.scope_note: For subsets of the simple generators in a Coxeter system, defines the generated subgroup and records its support, intersection, and induced Coxeter-system properties.

statements.title: Coxeter exchange and parity deletion lemma
statements.statement_plain: Exchange and deletion lemma for a Coxeter system: If a reduced word (s1,...,sq) for w and a simple reflection s satisfy length(sw) <= length(w), one factor can be deleted at an index j so that ss1...s_{j-1}=s1...s_j and the remaining word is reduced for sw of length q-1. Any word w=s1...sq in simple reflections has a reduced subword whose number of factors is congruent to q modulo 2.
statements.statement_latex: \text{(Exchange and deletion lemma)}\quad\begin{gathered}\text{If }(s_1,\ldots,s_q)\text{ is reduced for }w\in W,\ s\in S,\ \ell(sw)\le\ell(w),\\\exists j\in\{1,\ldots,q\}:\ ss_1\cdots s_{j-1}=s_1\cdots s_j,\quad (s_1,\ldots,s_{j-1},s_{j+1},\ldots,s_q)\text{ is reduced for }sw\text{ of length }q-1;\\\text{for every expression }w=s_1\cdots s_q\text{ with }s_i\in S,\ \exists\ 1\le j_1<\cdots<j_k\le q\text{ such that }(s_{j_1},\ldots,s_{j_k})\text{ is reduced for }w,\ k\equiv q\pmod 2.\end{gathered}
assumptions_latex: (W,S) is a Coxeter system with length function \ell.
(s_1,\ldots,s_q) is a reduced decomposition of w\in W and s\in S for the first assertion.
For the second assertion, s_1,\ldots,s_q\in S and w=s_1\cdots s_q.
statements.conclusion_latex: If \ell(sw)\leq\ell(w), then there exists j with 1\leq j\leq q such that ss_1\cdots s_{j-1}=s_1\cdots s_j and (s_1,\ldots,s_{j-1},s_{j+1},\ldots,s_q) is a reduced decomposition of sw, of length q-1. Moreover, for any expression w=s_1\cdots s_q with s_i\in S, there are indices 1\leq j_1<\cdots<j_k\leq q such that (s_{j_1},\ldots,s_{j_k}) is a reduced decomposition of w and k\equiv q\pmod 2.
statements.scope_note: Coxeter-system exchange condition and parity-preserving deletion to a reduced subexpression.

statements.title: Length, reduced decompositions, support, and associated reflections
statements.statement_plain: In a Coxeter system, the length of an element is the minimum number of generators in a product for it. Reduced decompositions attain this minimum; the set of generators appearing in any reduced decomposition, called the support, is independent of the choice. Conjugating each factor by the preceding prefix gives pairwise distinct reflections, and the resulting set depends only on the element.
statements.statement_latex: Let (W,S) be a Coxeter system and w\in W. Define \ell(w) to be the least integer q\ge0 such that w is a product of q elements of S. A reduced decomposition of w is a sequence (s_1,\ldots,s_q)\in S^q with w=s_1\cdots s_q and q=\ell(w). The set \mathbf S_w=\{s_1,\ldots,s_q\} is independent of the chosen reduced decomposition and is called the support of w. For any reduced decomposition, t_j=(s_1\cdots s_{j-1})s_j(s_1\cdots s_{j-1})^{-1}, 1\le j\le q, are pairwise distinct, and their set depends only on w.
assumptions_latex: (W,S) is a Coxeter system

statements.title: B-adapted and B-N-adapted homomorphisms
statements.statement_plain: A homomorphism φ:G→Ĝ is B-adapted when its kernel is contained in B and every conjugate of φ(B) by an element of Ĝ is φ(hBh⁻¹) for some h in G. It is B-N-adapted when, for the same h chosen for each g, the corresponding conjugacy equality also holds for N.
statements.statement_latex: Let \varphi:\mathbf{G}\to\widehat{\mathbf{G}} be a homomorphism. It is called B-adapted, respectively B-N-adapted, if (i) \ker(\varphi)\subseteq\mathbf{B}, and (ii) for every g\in\widehat{\mathbf{G}} there exists h\in\mathbf{G} such that \varphi(h\mathbf{B}h^{-1})=g\varphi(\mathbf{B})g^{-1}, respectively such that this equality and \varphi(h\mathbf{N}h^{-1})=g\varphi(\mathbf{N})g^{-1} both hold.
assumptions_latex: \varphi:\mathbf{G}\to\widehat{\mathbf{G}}\text{ is a group homomorphism; }\mathbf{B},\mathbf{N}\text{ are the fixed Tits-system subgroups.}
statements.conclusion_latex: \varphi\text{ is B-adapted iff }\ker(\varphi)\subseteq\mathbf{B}\text{ and }\forall g\in\widehat{\mathbf{G}}\,\exists h\in\mathbf{G}:\ \varphi(h\mathbf{B}h^{-1})=g\varphi(\mathbf{B})g^{-1}.\ \varphi\text{ is B-N-adapted iff }\ker(\varphi)\subseteq\mathbf{B}\text{ and }\forall g\in\widehat{\mathbf{G}}\,\exists h\in\mathbf{G}:\ \varphi(h\mathbf{B}h^{-1})=g\varphi(\mathbf{B})g^{-1}\ \land\ \varphi(h\mathbf{N}h^{-1})=g\varphi(\mathbf{N})g^{-1}.
statements.scope_note: These notions are defined relative to the fixed Tits-system subgroups B and N; in the B-N-adapted condition, the same h must satisfy both conjugacy equalities for each g.

statements.title: Combinatorial building of a Tits system
statements.statement_plain: A Tits system has an associated abstract simplicial, or combinatorial, building. Its simplices represent parabolic subgroups, faces correspond to reverse inclusion, and its chambers are equivariantly identified with the conjugates of the minimal parabolic subgroup B.
statements.statement_latex: For a Tits system \((\mathrm{G},\mathfrak{B},\mathrm{N},\mathrm{R})\), the combinatorial building \({}^{v}\mathcal{I}\) is an abstract simplicial complex whose simplices represent parabolic subgroups, with face relation inverse to inclusion; its chambers correspond \(\mathrm{G}\)-equivariantly to the conjugates of \(\mathfrak{B}\).
assumptions_latex: \((\mathrm{G},\mathfrak{B},\mathrm{N},\mathrm{R})\) is a Tits system with Weyl group \({}^{v}\mathbf{W}\).
statements.conclusion_latex: There is an associated combinatorial building \({}^{v}\mathcal{I}\), an abstract simplicial complex whose simplices represent parabolic subgroups and whose face relation is inverse to subgroup inclusion; its chambers are in bijection with the conjugates of the minimal parabolic subgroup \(\mathfrak{B}\), compatibly with the \(\mathrm{G}\)-action by inner automorphisms.
statements.scope_note: Definition of the combinatorial building attached to a Tits system, including its simplices, face relation, chambers, and equivariant chamber-subgroup correspondence.

statements.title: Definition of a Tits system
statements.statement_plain: A quadruple (G,B,N,S), where G is a group, B and N are subgroups, and S is a subset of W=N/(B∩N), is a Tits system when B and N generate G and B∩N is normal in N; S generates W and every element of S has order two; sBw is contained in BwB union BswB for every s in S and w in W; and sBs is not B for every s in S. Expressions involving W use classes modulo B∩N. Moreover, S consists exactly of the elements w for which B union BwB is a subgroup of G, so S is unique when G, B, and N are fixed. The group W is the Weyl group, and (W,S) is a Coxeter system. The source notes that the order-two clause follows from the remaining axioms.
statements.statement_latex: A quadruple (G,B,N,S), where G is a group, B,N\leq G, and S\subseteq W:=N/(B\cap N), is a Tits system when: \text{(TI) }\langle B\cup N\rangle=G\text{ and }B\cap N\trianglelefteq N;\ \text{(T2) }S\text{ generates }W\text{ and every }s\in S\text{ has order }2;\ \text{(T3) }sBw\subseteq BwB\cup BswB\text{ for all }s\in S,w\in W;\ \text{(T4) }sBs\neq B\text{ for all }s\in S.\text{ Moreover, }S=\{w\in W:B\cup BwB\text{ is a subgroup of }G\},\text{ so }S\text{ is unique when }G,B,N\text{ are fixed. The group }W\text{ is called the Weyl group, and }(W,S)\text{ is a Coxeter system. The source notes that the order-two clause in (T2) follows from the remaining axioms.}
assumptions_latex: G\text{ is a group},\quad B,N\leq G,\quad S\subseteq W:=N/(B\cap N).
statements.conclusion_latex: (G,B,N,S)\text{ is a Tits system; }W\text{ is its Weyl group and }(W,S)\text{ is a Coxeter system.}
statements.scope_note: Abstract group-theoretic Tits-system axioms. Expressions involving elements of W are interpreted using their classes modulo B\cap N.

statements.title: Irreducible Coxeter and Tits Systems
statements.statement_plain: For a Tits system (G,B,N,S) with associated Coxeter system (W,S), the Coxeter system is irreducible when its generating set cannot be partitioned into two nonempty subsets whose elements commute across the partition; equivalently, its Coxeter graph is connected and nonempty. The Tits system is irreducible when its associated Coxeter system is irreducible.
statements.statement_latex: For a Tits system (G,B,N,S) with associated Coxeter system (W,S), a Coxeter system (W,S) is irreducible if there do not exist nonempty subsets S_1,S_2 with S=S_1\sqcup S_2 such that every element of S_1 commutes with every element of S_2; equivalently, the Coxeter graph of (W,S) is connected and nonempty. The Tits system (G,B,N,S) is irreducible if (W,S) is irreducible.
assumptions_latex: (G,B,N,S)\text{ is a Tits system with associated Coxeter system }(W,S).
statements.conclusion_latex: (G,B,N,S)\text{ is irreducible}\iff(W,S)\text{ is irreducible},\quad (W,S)\text{ is irreducible}\iff\nexists\,S_1,S_2\neq\varnothing:\ S=S_1\sqcup S_2\ \text{and}\ st=ts\ \forall s\in S_1,\ t\in S_2;\ \text{equivalently, the Coxeter graph of }(W,S)\text{ is connected and nonempty}.
statements.scope_note: Defines irreducibility first for a Coxeter system and then for a Tits system through its associated Coxeter system.

statements.title: Parabolic subgroups and their types in a Tits system
statements.statement_plain: In the surrounding Tits-system setting, a subgroup P of G is parabolic exactly when it contains a conjugate of B. Such a P is conjugate to B_X for a unique subset X of S, called its type. For every subset Y of S containing X, there is a unique parabolic subgroup of type Y containing P; these describe the parabolic overgroups of P. Every parabolic subgroup is self-normalizing. Distinct parabolic subgroups whose intersection is parabolic are not conjugate, and two parabolic subgroups lying in a common subgroup that are G-conjugate are conjugate by an element of that common subgroup.

For each }\mathrm{Y}\supseteq\mathrm{X}\text{ in }\mathrm{S}\text{ there is a unique parabolic subgroup of type }\mathrm{Y}\text{ containing }\mathrm{P},\text{ yielding the parabolic overgroups of }\mathrm{P}.\text{ Every parabolic subgroup is self-normalizing; distinct parabolics with parabolic intersection are nonconjugate; and two parabolics lying in a common subgroup }\mathbf{P}\text{ that are }\mathrm{G}\text{-conjugate are conjugate within }\mathbf{P}.
assumptions_latex: \mathrm{G},\mathrm{B},\mathrm{S}\text{ are in the surrounding Tits-system context}
\mathrm{P}\leq\mathrm{G}

statements.title: Saturated Tits Systems and Strong Equivalence
statements.statement_plain: Given a Tits system (G,B,N,S), let H be the intersection of nBn^{-1} over n in N and let N-tilde be NH. Then H is normal in N-tilde, equals B intersected with N-tilde, and the inclusion of N induces an isomorphism from the Weyl group W to N-tilde modulo B intersected with N-tilde. The system is saturated exactly when N-tilde equals N. The quadruple (G,B,N-tilde,S) is the associated saturated Tits system and is equivalent to the original. Two Tits systems are strongly equivalent when their associated saturated systems differ by at most an inner automorphism; equivalent systems may fail to be strongly equivalent except when the Weyl group is finite, and the corresponding N subgroups need not be conjugate.
statements.statement_latex: \text{For a Tits system }(G,B,N,S),\ H=\bigcap_{n\in N}nBn^{-1}\text{ and }\widetilde N=NH.\text{ Then }H\trianglelefteq\widetilde N,\ H=B\cap\widetilde N,\text{ and }N\hookrightarrow\widetilde N\text{ induces }W\cong\widetilde N/(B\cap\widetilde N).\text{ The system is saturated when }\widetilde N=N;\ (G,B,\widetilde N,S)\text{ is its associated saturated system, equivalent to the original. Two systems are strongly equivalent when their associated saturated systems agree up to an inner automorphism; equivalence need not imply strong equivalence (unless }W\text{ is finite), and corresponding }N\text{-groups need not be conjugate}.
assumptions_latex: (G,B,N,S) is a Tits system with Weyl group W.
H=\bigcap_{n\in N}nBn^{-1},\quad \widetilde N=NH.
statements.conclusion_latex:
H\leq G\text{ is normalized by }N,\quad H\trianglelefteq\widetilde N,\quad H=B\cap\widetilde N,\quad W\cong\widetilde N/(B\cap\widetilde N).\\
(G,B,N,S)\text{ is saturated iff }\widetilde N=N.\\
(G,B,\widetilde N,S)\text{ is the saturated Tits system associated with }(G,B,N,S)\text{ and is equivalent to it}.\\
\text{Two Tits systems are strongly equivalent iff their associated saturated systems coincide up to an inner automorphism; equivalent systems need not be strongly equivalent, except when }W\text{ is finite, and }N,N'\text{ need not be conjugate}.

statements.title: Tits Systems and Saturated Tits Systems
statements.statement_plain: A Tits system is a tuple (G, B, N, S) with G a group, B and N subgroups of G, and S a subset of W = N/(B intersection N), satisfying four axioms: B and N generate G with B intersection N normal in N; S generates W and every element of S has order two; for every s in S and w in W, sBw is contained in BwB union BswB; and sBs is not equal to B for every s in S. For any w in W and lift n in N, the cosets wB = nB and Bw = Bn are well-defined. The system is saturated if the intersection of nBn^{-1} over all n in N equals B intersection N.
statements.statement_latex: \text{A Tits system is a tuple }(G,B,N,S)\text{ with G a group, }B,N\leq G,\text{ and }S\subseteq W:=N/(B\cap N),\text{ satisfying: }\langle B\cup N\rangle=G\text{ and }B\cap N\trianglelefteq N;\ S\text{ generates }W\text{ and each }s\in S\text{ has order }2;\ \forall s\in S,\forall w\in W,\ sBw\subseteq BwB\cup BswB;\ \forall s\in S,\ sBs\neq B.\text{ For }w\in W\text{ and any lift }n\in N,\ wB:=nB\text{ and }Bw:=Bn\text{ are well-defined cosets of }B\text{ in }G.\text{ The system is saturated when additionally }\bigcap_{n\in N}nBn^{-1}=B\cap N.
statements.conclusion_latex: (G,B,N,S)\text{ is a Tits system precisely when axioms TS1--TS4 hold, and it is saturated if additionally }\bigcap_{n\in N}nBn^{-1}=B\cap N.
statements.scope_note: Defines an abstract Tits system from a group G, subgroups B and N, and a generating set S in W=N/(B\cap N), including the associated coset notation and the additional saturation axiom.

statements.title: Type of a gallery in an affine Tits system
statements.statement_plain: For adjacent chambers in the affine Tits-system chamber system, the shared wall is unique. The type of a gallery without backtracking is the sequence of the types of these shared walls between successive chambers.
statements.statement_latex: If \Gamma=(\mathbf{C}_0,\ldots,\mathbf{C}_n) is a gallery without backtracking in \mathcal{I}, its type is \mathbf{s}(\Gamma)=(s_1,\ldots,s_n), where for each 1\leq i\leq n, s_i\in\mathbf{S} is the type of the uniquely determined wall shared by the adjacent chambers \mathbf{C}_{i-1} and \mathbf{C}_i.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal{I} is the chamber system of an affine Tits system whose wall types are indexed by \mathbf{S}.
\Gamma=(\mathbf{C}_0,\ldots,\mathbf{C}_n) is a gallery without backtracking in \mathcal{I}; consecutive chambers are distinct and share a wall.
statements.conclusion_latex: For each adjacent pair (\mathbf{C}_{i-1},\mathbf{C}_i), the common wall is uniquely determined and has a type s_i\in\mathbf{S}; the type of \Gamma is \mathbf{s}(\Gamma)=(s_1,\ldots,s_n)\in\mathbf{S}^n.
statements.scope_note: Defines the type sequence of a no-backtracking gallery, using the uniquely determined common wall type at each step.

statements.title: Apartment transport, facet stabilizers, fixed points, and conjugacy in a Tits-system building
statements.statement_plain: Let (G, B, N, S) be a Tits system with associated building B. Any two apartments containing a common facet F are related by an element of G fixing every vertex of F. The stabilizer of F is its parabolic subgroup P_F, and the fixed-point set of P_F in the building is exactly the faces of F, including F. If two facets of one chamber are carried to one another by an element g of G, they are equal and g lies in P_F1. Finally, two facets in a fixed apartment are conjugate under G exactly when they are conjugate under N.
statements.statement_latex: \text{Let }(G,B,N,S)\text{ be a Tits system and }\mathcal B\text{ its associated building. Then: (1) any two apartments containing a common facet }\mathcal F\text{ are related by some }g\in G\text{ fixing every vertex of }\mathcal F; (2) }\operatorname{Stab}_G(\mathcal F)=P_{\mathcal F};\text{ (3) }\operatorname{Fix}_{\mathcal B}(P_{\mathcal F})\text{ is exactly the set of faces of }\mathcal F\text{, including }\mathcal F;\text{ (4) if facets }\mathcal F_1,\mathcal F_2\text{ of the same chamber satisfy }g\mathcal F_1=\mathcal F_2\text{ for }g\in G,\text{ then }\mathcal F_1=\mathcal F_2\text{ and }g\in P_{\mathcal F_1};\text{ (5) two facets in a fixed apartment }\mathcal A\text{ are }G\text{-conjugate if and only if they are }N\text{-conjugate}.
assumptions_latex: (G,B,N,S)\text{ is a Tits system, and }\mathcal B\text{ is the associated building.}
statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&\text{(1) If }\mathcal A_1,\mathcal A_2\text{ contain a common facet }\mathcal F\text{ of }\mathcal B,\text{ then some }g\in G\text{ sends }\mathcal A_1\text{ to }\mathcal A_2\text{ and fixes every vertex of }\mathcal F.\\&\text{(2) For every facet }\mathcal F,\ \operatorname{Stab}_G(\mathcal F)=P_{\mathcal F}.\\&\text{(3) The fixed-point set of }P_{\mathcal F}\text{ in }\mathcal B\text{ is exactly the set of faces of }\mathcal F,\text{ including }\mathcal F.\\&\text{(4) If facets }\mathcal F_1,\mathcal F_2\text{ of one chamber satisfy }g\mathcal F_1=\mathcal F_2\text{ for }g\in G,\text{ then }\mathcal F_1=\mathcal F_2\text{ and }g\in P_{\mathcal F_1}.\\&\text{(5) For facets }\mathcal F_1,\mathcal F_2\in\mathcal A,\ \mathcal F_1\text{ and }\mathcal F_2\text{ are }G\text{-conjugate iff they are }N\text{-conjugate.}\end{aligned}

statements.title: Bruhat decomposition and parabolic consequences of a Tits system
statements.statement_plain: For a Tits system (G,B,N,S) with Weyl group W=N/(B intersect N), the Weyl group bijects with the B-double cosets via w to BwB, giving the Bruhat decomposition of G. Every parabolic subgroup is conjugate to a unique standard parabolic subgroup and is self-normalizing. If a subgroup Q contains parabolic subgroups Q1 and Q2, any element of G conjugating Q1 to Q2 lies in Q.
statements.statement_latex: Let $(G,B,N,S)$ be a Tits system with Weyl group $W=N/(B\cap N)$. Then the map $w\mapsto BwB$ is a bijection from $W$ to the set of $B$-double cosets in $G$, yielding $G=\bigsqcup_{w\in W}BwB$. Every parabolic subgroup of $G$ is conjugate to a unique standard parabolic subgroup and equals its normalizer. If $Q\leq G$ contains parabolic subgroups $Q_1,Q_2$ and $g\in G$ satisfies $gQ_1g^{-1}=Q_2$, then $g\in Q.
assumptions_latex: (G,B,N,S)\text{ is a Tits system with Weyl group }W
W=N/(B\cap N)

statements.title: Building actions yielding saturated Tits systems
statements.statement_plain: Let G act simplicially on a thick building. Suppose that for any two apartment-chamber pairs there is an element of G carrying the first pair to the second while fixing every vertex common to the two chambers, and suppose every element stabilizing a chamber fixes all its vertices. For a fixed apartment and chamber, let B and N be their respective stabilizers. Then (B,N) is a saturated Tits system in G, and its Weyl group is N modulo B intersection N. An automorphism is called special when stabilizing a chamber forces it to fix all vertices of that chamber.
statements.statement_latex: Let G act on a thick building \mathcal B by simplicial automorphisms. Assume that for any apartment-chamber pairs (\mathcal A',\mathcal C') and (\mathcal A'',\mathcal C''), some g\in G carries the first pair to the second and fixes every vertex common to \mathcal C' and \mathcal C'', and assume that every element stabilizing a chamber fixes all of its vertices. Fix an apartment-chamber pair (\mathcal A,\mathcal C), set B=\operatorname{Stab}_G(\mathcal C) and N=\operatorname{Stab}_G(\mathcal A). Then (B,N) is a saturated Tits system in G, with Weyl group N/(B\cap N). A simplicial automorphism of \mathcal B or of an apartment is called special if stabilizing a chamber forces it to fix every vertex of that chamber.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal B\text{ is a thick building and }G\text{ acts on }\mathcal B\text{ by simplicial automorphisms}.

\forall (\mathcal A',\mathcal C'),(\mathcal A'',\mathcal C'')\ \exists g\in G:\ g(\mathcal A',\mathcal C')=(\mathcal A'',\mathcal C'')\text{ and }g\text{ fixes every vertex common to }\mathcal C'\text{ and }\mathcal C''.
\forall g\in G,\ \bigl(g\mathcal C=\mathcal C\bigr)\Rightarrow g\text{ fixes every vertex of }\mathcal C.
statements.conclusion_latex: (B,N)\text{ is a saturated Tits system in }G,\qquad W\cong N/(B\cap N).
statements.scope_note: Abstract criterion for a strongly transitive simplicial action on a thick building. For a fixed apartment-chamber pair, B is the chamber stabilizer and N the apartment stabilizer; the source also defines special automorphisms as those for which chamber stabilization implies fixation of all chamber vertices.

statements.title: Characterization of galleries without backtracking
statements.statement_plain: A chamber sequence starting at F(B) is a gallery without backtracking exactly when each chamber C_j has the factorization b_1 sbar_1 ... b_j sbar_j F(B), with b_j in B, s_j in S, and sbar_j in v^{-1}(s_j). In that case the gallery has type (s_1,...,s_m).
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Gamma=(\mathbf C_0,\ldots,\mathbf C_m)\) be a sequence of chambers with \(\mathbf C_0=\mathbf F(\mathbf B)\). Then the following are equivalent: (i) \(\Gamma\) is a gallery without backtracking; (ii) there exist \(b_j\in\mathbf B\), \(s_j\in\mathbf S\), and \(\bar s_j\in v^{-1}(s_j)\) for \(j=1,\ldots,m\) such that \(\mathbf C_j=b_1\bar s_1\cdots b_j\bar s_j\,\mathbf F(\mathbf B)\) for \(j=1,\ldots,m\). Under these equivalent conditions, \(\Gamma\) is of type \((s_1,\ldots,s_m)\).
assumptions_latex: The chambers and symbols \(\mathbf B\), \(\mathbf S\), \(v\), and \(\mathbf F(\mathbf B)\) are those of the affine Tits-system chamber system used in the source.
\(\Gamma=(\mathbf C_0,\ldots,\mathbf C_m)\) is a finite sequence of chambers with \(\mathbf C_0=\mathbf F(\mathbf B)\).
statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Gamma\) is a gallery without backtracking iff there exist \(b_j\in\mathbf B\), \(s_j\in\mathbf S\), and \(\bar s_j\in v^{-1}(s_j)\) such that \(\mathbf C_j=b_1\bar s_1\cdots b_j\bar s_j\,\mathbf F(\mathbf B)\) for all \(j=1,\ldots,m\); then its type is \((s_1,\ldots,s_m)\).
statements.scope_note: Characterization of no-backtracking galleries and their type in the chamber system associated with the affine Tits system of the source.

statements.title: Homomorphisms of Saturated Tits Systems
statements.statement_plain: For a saturated Tits system (G,B,N,S), a homomorphism to (G',B',N',S') satisfying the kernel, normality, abelian quotient, normalization, and factorization conditions yields G'=T'f(G)=f(G)T', f^{-1}(T')=T, normalization of every f(BwB) by T', and an isomorphism W to W' sending S bijectively to S'.
statements.statement_latex: Let \((G,B,N,S)\) and \((G',B',N',S')\) be Tits systems with \((G,B,N,S)\) saturated. If \(f:G\to G'\) maps \(B\) to \(B'\) and \(N\) to \(N'\), \(\ker(f)\subseteq T\), \(f(G)\trianglelefteq G'\) with abelian quotient \(G'/f(G)\), \(T'\) normalizes \(f(B)\), and \(B'=f(B)T'\), \(N'=f(N)T'\), then \(G'=T'f(G)=f(G)T'\), \(f^{-1}(T')=T\), \(T'\) normalizes each \(f(BwB)\) for \(w\in W\), and the induced map \(W\to W'\) is an isomorphism carrying \(S\) bijectively onto \(S'\).
assumptions_latex: \((G,B,N,S)\) and \((G',B',N',S')\) are Tits systems, with \((G,B,N,S)\) saturated.
\(f:G\to G'\) is a group homomorphism mapping \(B\) to \(B'\) and \(N\) to \(N'\).
\(\ker(f)\subseteq T\); \(f(G)\) is normal in \(G'\) and \(G'/f(G)\) is abelian; \(T'\) normalizes \(f(B)\); and \(B'=f(B)T'\), \(N'=f(N)T'\).
statements.conclusion_latex: \(G'=T'f(G)=f(G)T'\), \(f^{-1}(T')=T\), and \(T'\) normalizes \(f(BwB)\) for every \(w\in W\). The map \(W\to W'\) induced by \(f\) is an isomorphism carrying \(S\) bijectively onto \(S'\).
statements.scope_note: Functoriality and preservation of Weyl-group data for homomorphisms satisfying the stated saturation, kernel, normality, normalization, and factorization hypotheses.

statements.title: Projection onto a Tits-system subposet
statements.statement_plain: Fix an index i. For every P in the poset P, the intersection of all members of the subposet P_i that contain P is itself a member of P_i; denote it by pi_i(P). If P=G_X for X contained in S, then pi_i(P)=G_{X union S_i complement}, and its P_i-type is the intersection of the P-type of P with S_i. The map pi_i is order-preserving, G-equivariant, and, in the source's terminology, a section of the inclusion of P_i into P.
statements.statement_latex: Fix i. For every P\in\mathcal P, the intersection \bigcap_{P\subset P_i\in\mathcal P_i}P_i is an element of \mathcal P_i; denote it by \pi_i(P). statements.title: Quotients of Tits systems by normal subgroups of T
statements.statement_plain: Let (G,B,N,S) be a Tits system with T equal to B intersect N. Quotienting G, B, and N by a subgroup Z of T that is normal in G produces a Tits system with the same Weyl group. Saturation is preserved by this quotient.

statements.title: Tits building associated to a finite-rank Tits system
statements.statement_plain: For a Tits system (G,B,N,S) with finite S, form the simplicial complex of finite collections of maximal proper parabolics having parabolic intersection, with G acting by conjugation. Facets correspond equivariantly to proper parabolic subgroups with incidence reversed, so chambers are the conjugates of B. The standard chamber is the collection of standard maximal parabolics and the standard apartment is the union of its N-conjugates. Facet stabilizers fix vertices; the stated apartment transport property holds; this complex is the Tits building with apartments gA, and G is transitive on apartment-chamber pairs. The building depends only on the G-conjugacy class of (B,N), while the standard chamber depends on B and the standard apartment on T=B intersect N; identifying that apartment with all parabolics containing T is only often, not always, valid.

Then (V,\mathcal B) is a simplicial complex and facets correspond G-equivariantly to proper parabolic subgroups with incidence reversed; chambers correspond to gBg^{-1}. The set \mathcal C is the standard chamber, \mathcal A the standard apartment, facet stabilizers fix vertices, the stated apartment transport property holds, \mathcal B is the Tits building with apartments g\mathcal A, and G is transitive on apartment-chamber pairs. statements.title: Extremal Elements and Nibbling Orders
statements.statement_plain: For a subset M of the vector root system, an element is extremal when its positive ray is an extremal ray of the cone generated by M. A nibbling order is a total order in which each element is extremal among the elements greater than it in the order. Such an order exists exactly when the generated cone is strictly convex, equivalently when its polar has nonempty interior or when M lies in the positive roots for some vector chamber. Then any chosen extremal element can be first. In particular, the positive roots for a chamber admit an order starting with any simple root, and restricting the order to a subset preserves the nibbling property.
statements.statement_latex: Let M\subset{}^{v}\Sigma. An element m\in M is extremal if the ray \mathbf R_{+}m is an extremal generator of the convex cone with origin 0 generated by M. A total order on M is nibbling if every m\in M is extremal in the subset of elements of M greater than m. A nibbling order exists exactly when the cone generated by M is strictly convex (equivalently, its polar has nonempty interior, equivalently, M\subset{}^{v}\Sigma^{+}(D) for some vector chamber D); in that case an order may be chosen with any prescribed extremal element of M first. In particular, for each vector chamber D, {}^{v}\Sigma^{+}(D) admits a nibbling order beginning with any simple root a\in B(D). If M'\subset M, the restriction of a nibbling order on M to M' is nibbling.
assumptions_latex: M\subset{}^{v}\Sigma
M'\subset M
D\text{ is a vector chamber}
statements.conclusion_latex: A nibbling order on M exists if and only if the cone generated by M is strictly convex, equivalently its polar has nonempty interior; equivalently, M is contained in the positive vector roots {}^{v}\Sigma^{+}(D) for some vector chamber D. When this holds, there is a nibbling order whose first element is any prescribed extremal element of M. In particular, {}^{v}\Sigma^{+}(D) has a nibbling order beginning with any simple root a\in B(D), and restricting a nibbling order on M to M' yields a nibbling order on M'.

statements.title: Affine Dynkin diagram automorphisms and the Xi extension
statements.statement_plain: For an irreducible reduced finite root system Phi and its associated affine root system Psi, choose a special node x of the affine Dynkin diagram. The length-zero subgroup Xi acts simply transitively on the special nodes. Deleting x gives the finite Dynkin diagram D, whose automorphism group is the stabilizer of x, and the full affine diagram automorphism group is Xi semidirect the stabilizer. Therefore 1 -> Xi -> Aut(tilde D) -> Aut(D) -> 1 is an x-independent split exact sequence; intrinsically, the map comes from the derivative Aut(Psi) -> Aut(Phi) on the Weyl-group quotients.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Psi=\Psi_{\Phi}\) be the affine root system associated to an irreducible reduced finite root system \(\Phi\), with affine Dynkin diagram \(\widetilde{\mathcal D}\), and let \(x\) be a special node. Writing \(\Xi\) for the length-zero subgroup and \(\mathcal D\) for the diagram obtained by deleting \(x\) and its incident edges, the action map \(\omega\mapsto\omega x\) identifies \(\Xi\) bijectively with the special nodes, \(\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal D)=\operatorname{Aut}(\widetilde{\mathcal D})_x\), and \(\operatorname{Aut}(\widetilde{\mathcal D})=\Xi\rtimes\operatorname{Aut}(\widetilde{\mathcal D})_x\). Thus \(1\to\Xi\to\operatorname{Aut}(\widetilde{\mathcal D})\to\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal D)\to1\) is exact and independent of \(x\), with a splitting determined by \(x\); intrinsically, the quotient map is induced by the derivative homomorphism \(\operatorname{Aut}(\Psi)\to\operatorname{Aut}(\Phi)\).
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi\) is an irreducible reduced finite root system.
\(\Psi=\Psi_{\Phi}\) is its associated affine root system with affine Dynkin diagram \(\widetilde{\mathcal D}\), and \(x\) is a special node.
\(\Xi\) is the length-zero subgroup acting on \(\widetilde{\mathcal D}\); \(\mathcal D\) is obtained by deleting \(x\) and its incident edges.
statements.conclusion_latex: The map \(\Xi\to\{\text{special nodes of }\widetilde{\mathcal D}\}\), \(\omega\mapsto\omega x\), is bijective; \(\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal D)=\operatorname{Aut}(\widetilde{\mathcal D})_x\) and \(\operatorname{Aut}(\widetilde{\mathcal D})=\Xi\rtimes\operatorname{Aut}(\widetilde{\mathcal D})_x\). Consequently, \(1\to\Xi\to\operatorname{Aut}(\widetilde{\mathcal D})\to\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal D)\to1\) is an exact sequence independent of the choice of \(x\), and choosing \(x\) gives a splitting. The map is intrinsically induced by the derivative homomorphism \(\operatorname{Aut}(\Psi)\to\operatorname{Aut}(\Phi)\) on the quotients \(\operatorname{Aut}(\Psi)/W(\Psi)\) and \(\operatorname{Aut}(\Phi)/W(\Phi)\).
statements.scope_note: Automorphism structure of the affine Dynkin diagram associated to an irreducible reduced finite root system.

statements.title: Affine Weyl translation lattices for a special valuation
statements.statement_plain: For a special valuation, W and its extended version \widehat W split as translation parts by V semidirect the Weyl group. The translation part of W is characterized by coordinate valuations and a sum condition; the translation part of \widehat W consists of valuation images of torus elements with coordinates given by half the differences of paired diagonal coefficient valuations. Doubling any translation in \widehat W\cap V gives one in W\cap V.
statements.statement_latex: Assume that the valuation \varphi is special. Then each of W and \widehat{W} is the semidirect product of its intersection with V and the Weyl group W(\Phi) acting linearly on V. For v\in V, with coordinates v_i=a_i(v), one has v\in W\cap V exactly when v_i\in\omega(K^*) (1\le i\le r) and \sum_{i=1}^r v_i lies in the subgroup generated by \{\omega(k)\mid (z,k)\in Z\setminus\{(0,0)\}\}\cup 2\omega(K^*). Moreover, v\in\widehat{W}\cap V exactly when there exists t\in T with v_i=\frac12(\omega(c_{ii}(t))-\omega(c_{-i,-i}(t))) for every i. Consequently, 2(\widehat{W}\cap V)\subset W\cap V.

statements.title: Chamber fundamental domains and facet stabilizers
statements.statement_plain: The closure of any chamber is a fundamental domain for the affine Weyl group action. For an affine Weyl group element and a facet, fixing one point is equivalent to fixing the facet and its closure pointwise, preserving the facet, or being a product of reflections in hyperplanes containing it. Consequently, the group acts simply transitively on the chambers.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal C\) be a chamber in \(A\). Its closure \(\overline{\mathcal C}\) is a fundamental domain for the action of \(W(\Psi)\) on \(A\). For every \(w\in W(\Psi)\) and every facet \(\mathcal F\), the following are equivalent: \(w\) fixes some point of \(\mathcal F\); \(w\) fixes every point of \(\mathcal F\); \(w\) fixes every point of \(\overline{\mathcal F}\); \(w\) leaves \(\mathcal F\) invariant; and \(w\) is a product of reflections along hyperplanes containing \(\mathcal F\). In particular, \(W(\Psi)\) acts simply transitively on the set of chambers.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal C\text{ is a chamber in the affine space }A.
w\in W(\Psi)\text{ and }\mathcal F\text{ is a facet of }A.
statements.conclusion_latex: \overline{\mathcal C}\text{ is a fundamental domain for }W(\Psi)\curvearrowright A;\quad [\exists x\in\mathcal F,\,w(x)=x]\iff[\forall x\in\mathcal F,\,w(x)=x]\iff[\forall x\in\overline{\mathcal F},\,w(x)=x]\iff w(\mathcal F)=\mathcal F\iff w\text{ is a product of reflections along hyperplanes containing }\mathcal F.\text{ Consequently, }W(\Psi)\text{ acts simply transitively on the set of chambers.}
statements.scope_note: Affine Weyl group action on the affine space A, its facets, and its chambers.

statements.title: Facet Types and Stabilizers in an Affine Coxeter Chamber
statements.statement_plain: For an affine Coxeter system decomposed into irreducible factors, every facet has a unique Weyl-group translate in the fixed chamber. Chamber facets are indexed by subsets X of simple reflections that omit at least one generator from every irreducible factor, equivalently those generating finite standard parabolic subgroups. The stabilizer of the facet indexed by X, and of every point in it, is the subgroup generated by X; the chamber itself corresponds to the empty subset.
statements.statement_latex: Let $(\mathbf W,\mathbf S)$ be an affine Coxeter system with irreducible decomposition $\mathbf W=\prod_i\mathbf W_i$ and $\mathbf S=\bigsqcup_i\mathbf S_i$, acting on an affine space with chamber $\mathbf C$ and walls $\mathbf L_s$. Every facet has a unique representative among the facets of $\mathbf C$. For $\mathbf T=\{\mathbf X\subseteq\mathbf S\mid\mathbf X\cap\mathbf S_i\neq\mathbf S_i\ \forall i\}=\{\mathbf X\subseteq\mathbf S\mid\mathbf W_{\mathbf X}\text{ finite}\}$, the sets $\mathbf C_{\mathbf X}=\{a\in\mathbf C\mid\mathbf X=\{s\in\mathbf S:a\in\mathbf L_s\}\}$ are exactly the facets of $\mathbf C$, and $\mathbf C=\mathbf C_{\varnothing}$. The stabilizer of $\mathbf C_{\mathbf X}$ and of each of its points is $\mathbf W_{\mathbf X}=\langle\mathbf X\rangle$.
assumptions_latex: $(\mathbf W,\mathbf S)$ is an affine Coxeter system with irreducible affine decomposition $\mathbf W=\prod_{i=1}^m\mathbf W_i$ and $\mathbf S=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^m\mathbf S_i$, acting on an affine space with fixed chamber $\mathbf C$ and walls $\mathbf L_s$ for $s\in\mathbf S$.
For $\mathbf X\subseteq\mathbf S$, write $\mathbf W_{\mathbf X}=\langle\mathbf X\rangle$ for the standard parabolic subgroup.
statements.conclusion_latex: Every facet $\mathbf F$ has a unique representative facet in $\mathbf C$ under the $\mathbf W$-action. For $\mathbf T=\{\mathbf X\subseteq\mathbf S\mid \mathbf X\cap\mathbf S_i\neq\mathbf S_i\ \forall i\}=\{\mathbf X\subseteq\mathbf S\mid \mathbf W_{\mathbf X}\text{ is finite}\}$, the sets $\mathbf C_{\mathbf X}=\{a\in\mathbf C\mid \mathbf X=\{s\in\mathbf S:a\in\mathbf L_s\}\}$ are exactly the facets of $\mathbf C$, with $\mathbf C=\mathbf C_{\varnothing}$. The stabilizer of $\mathbf C_{\mathbf X}$, and of every point of it, is $\mathbf W_{\mathbf X}$; a facet has type $\mathbf X$ when it is carried to $\mathbf C_{\mathbf X}$ by an element of $\mathbf W$.
statements.scope_note: Facet orbit representatives, facet types, and standard-parabolic stabilizers for an affine Coxeter chamber.

statements.title: Gradient Root System and Translation Kernel of an Affine Weyl Group
statements.statement_plain: The gradients of the affine roots form a finite root system. Their coroots span the translation space. If two affine roots in the system are related by scaling by r and adding a constant, then r can only be ±1/2, ±1, or ±2, with the stated coroot scaling. The map from the affine Weyl group onto the finite Weyl group is surjective, and its kernel is exactly the translation subgroup contained in the affine Weyl group.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Phi=\{\dot\psi\mid\psi\in\Psi\}\subset V^*\). Then \(\Phi\) is a finite root system. For every \(\psi\in\Psi\), \(\dot\psi^\vee\) is the coroot of \(\dot\psi\), and \(\{\dot\psi^\vee\mid\psi\in\Psi\}\) spans \(V\). If \(\psi\in\Psi\), \(c,r\in\mathbb R\), and \(\eta:=r\psi+c\in\Psi\), then \(r\in\{\pm\tfrac12,\pm1,\pm2\}\) and \(\dot\psi^\vee=r\dot\eta^\vee\). The map \(\nabla:W(\Psi)\to W(\Phi)\) is surjective, and its kernel is the subgroup of translations contained in \(W(\Psi)\).
assumptions_latex: \(\Psi\) is the affine root system under consideration on a real affine space with translation space \(V\), and \(\dot\psi\in V^*\) denotes the gradient of \(\psi\in\Psi\).
\(W(\Psi)\) and \(W(\Phi)\) denote the corresponding affine and finite Weyl groups.
statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi=\{\dot\psi\mid\psi\in\Psi\}\subset V^*\) is a finite root system; each \(\dot\psi^\vee\) is the coroot of \(\dot\psi\) and these coroots span \(V\); if \(\eta=r\psi+c\in\Psi\) with \(c,r\in\mathbb R\), then \(r\in\{\pm\tfrac12,\pm1,\pm2\}\) and \(\dot\psi^\vee=r\dot\eta^\vee\); and \(\nabla:W(\Psi)\to W(\Phi)\) is surjective with kernel equal to the subgroup of translations contained in \(W(\Psi)\).
statements.scope_note: Structure of the finite gradient root system associated with an affine root system and of the induced map between their Weyl groups.

statements.title: Translations and Root Spacing in an Affine Root System
statements.statement_plain: Let Psi be an affine root system. For each affine root psi, let u_psi be the least positive shift for which psi+u_psi is again an affine root, and let t_psi be the product of the reflections in these two parallel affine roots. Then t_psi acts on the apartment and its affine dual by the stated translation formulas. A shift psi+r is an affine root exactly when r is an integral multiple of u_psi. The number u_psi depends only on the Weyl orbit of the derivative of psi and is a positive integral multiple of c(Psi).
statements.statement_latex: \text{Let }\Psi\text{ be an affine root system. For each }\psi\in\Psi,\text{ let }u_\psi>0\text{ be the least number such that }\psi'=\psi+u_\psi\in\Psi,\text{ and put }t_\psi=r_{\psi'}r_\psi.\text{ Then }t_\psi(x)=x-u_\psi\dot\psi^{\vee}\text{ for every }x\in A,\text{ and }t_\psi(\eta)=\eta+u_\psi\dot\eta(\dot\psi^{\vee})\text{ for every }\eta\in A^*.\text{ For every }r\in\mathbf R,\ \psi+r\in\Psi\iff r\in u_\psi\mathbf Z.\text{ Moreover, }u_\psi\text{ depends only on the Weyl orbit of }\dot\psi\text{ and is a positive integral multiple of }c(\Psi).

statements.title: Axioms of an Abstract Affine Root System
statements.statement_plain: An affine root system is a set of nonconstant affine functionals on A that spans A*, has finitely many linear parts, is preserved by the normalized reflections attached to its roots, has integral root-coroot pairings, and is discrete among roots sharing a linear part. Those reflections generate the affine Weyl group W(Psi), and the rank is dim V, positive exactly when Psi is nonempty.
statements.statement_latex: A subset \(\Psi\subset A^*\) is an affine root system if (AR1) \(\Psi\) spans \(A^*\), consists of nonconstant affine functionals, and \(\Phi:=\nabla(\Psi)\subset V^*\) is finite; (AR2) for each \(\psi\in\Psi\) there is \(\dot\psi^\vee\in V\) with \(\dot\psi(\dot\psi^\vee)=2\) such that the reflection \(r_{\psi,\dot\psi^\vee}(x)=x-\dot x(\dot\psi^\vee)\psi\) on \(A^*\) preserves \(\Psi\); (AR3) \(\dot\psi(\dot\eta^\vee)\in\mathbf Z\) for all \(\psi,\eta\in\Psi\); and (AR4) for every \(a\in\Phi\), \(\{\psi\in\Psi\mid\dot\psi=a\}\) has no accumulation point. The subgroup of transformations generated by these reflections is the affine Weyl group \(W(\Psi)\), and the rank is \(\dim V\), positive exactly when \(\Psi\ne\varnothing\).
assumptions_latex: \Psi\subset A^*,\quad \Phi:=\nabla(\Psi)\subset V^*
For each \psi\in\Psi, choose \dot\psi^\vee\in V with \dot\psi(\dot\psi^\vee)=2.
statements.conclusion_latex: \Psi\text{ is an affine root system};\quad W(\Psi)=\langle r_{\psi,\dot\psi^\vee}\mid\psi\in\Psi\rangle\text{ is its affine Weyl group};\quad \operatorname{rank}(\Psi)=\dim V,\ \operatorname{rank}(\Psi)>0\iff\Psi\neq\varnothing.
statements.scope_note: Abstract affine-root-system definition: AR1 finite linear-part image and spanning/nonconstant conditions; AR2 reflection preservation; AR3 integral root-coroot pairings; AR4 no accumulation for roots with fixed linear part. The same passage defines the affine Weyl group and rank.

statements.title: Automorphism Groups of Affine Dynkin Diagrams of Type D
statements.statement_plain: For affine Dynkin diagrams of type D, the automorphism group and distinguished subgroup Xi are classified by cases. For D4, the automorphism group is S4 and Xi is the unique Sylow-2 subgroup of A4, hence a Klein four group. For D_{2n} with n>2, the automorphism group is (Z/2Z)^2 semidirect Z/2Z, generated by the two terminal-node swaps and a branch swap; Xi is the Klein four subgroup generated by the two branch-switching involutions. For D_{2n-1} with n>2, the same automorphism-group description holds and Xi is the unique cyclic subgroup of order 4.
statements.statement_latex: If \(\Psi\) is of type \(D_4\), then \(\operatorname{Aut}(\widetilde{\mathcal D})\cong S_4\), and \(\Xi\) is the unique Sylow-2 subgroup of \(A_4\), hence \(\Xi\cong (\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z)^2\). If \(\Psi\) is of type \(D_{2n}\) with \(n>2\), then \(\operatorname{Aut}(\widetilde{\mathcal D})\cong (\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z)^2\rtimes\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z\), generated by the involutions that switch the two left terminal nodes, switch the two right terminal nodes, and switch the left and right branches; the subgroup \(\Xi\) generated by the two branch-switching involutions is isomorphic to \((\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z)^2\). If \(\Psi\) is of type \(D_{2n-1}\) with \(n>2\), then \(\operatorname{Aut}(\widetilde{\mathcal D})\cong (\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z)^2\rtimes\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z\) with the same generators, and \(\Xi\) is the unique subgroup isomorphic to \(\mathbf Z/4\mathbf Z\).
assumptions_latex: \(\Psi\) is an affine root system whose affine Dynkin diagram has type \(D_4\), \(D_{2n}\) with \(n>2\), or \(D_{2n-1}\) with \(n>2\).
statements.conclusion_latex: The automorphism groups \(\operatorname{Aut}(\widetilde{\mathcal D})\) and the distinguished subgroup \(\Xi\) have the following case-by-case descriptions.
statements.scope_note: Classification of the symmetry group of the affine Dynkin diagram \(\widetilde{\mathcal D}\) and of the distinguished subgroup \(\Xi\) for the D-series cases stated in the proposition.

statements.title: Special points and special Coxeter vertices
statements.statement_plain: A point x in the affine space A is special exactly when every wall has an equipollent wall passing through x. When the affine Weyl group W is irreducible, a vertex s of its Coxeter graph is special exactly when the corresponding extremal point of the closure of the fundamental chamber is a special point.
statements.statement_latex: x\in\mathbf A\text{ is special}\iff \forall\text{ walls }\mathbf L\subset\mathbf A,\ \exists\text{ a wall }\mathbf L'\text{ equipollent to }\mathbf L\text{ with }x\in\mathbf L'.\quad \text{If }\mathbf W\text{ is irreducible, a Coxeter vertex }s\text{ is special}\iff \bigcap_{t\in\mathbf S,\,t\ne s}\mathbf L_t\text{ is special}.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbf A\) is an affine space equipped with its walls.
For the definition of a special Coxeter vertex, \(\mathbf W\) is irreducible with Coxeter generating set \(\mathbf S\) and chamber \(\mathbf C\).
statements.conclusion_latex: A point \(x\in\mathbf A\) is special if and only if, for every wall \(\mathbf L\) of \(\mathbf A\), an equipollent wall containing \(x\) exists. If \(\mathbf W\) is irreducible, a vertex \(s\) of the Coxeter graph is special if and only if the corresponding extremal point \(\bigcap_{t\in\mathbf S,\,t\ne s}\mathbf L_t\) of \(\overline{\mathbf C}\) is a special point.

statements.title: Automorphism groups of labeled affine Dynkin diagrams and Xi
statements.statement_plain: For the labeled affine Dynkin diagram attached to an affine root system, the automorphism group and distinguished subgroup Xi are classified as follows: type A1 gives Z/2 for both; type An with n>1 gives the dihedral group of order 2(n+1), with Xi the index-2 rotation subgroup; types Bn, Bn-dual, Cn, and Cn-dual give Z/2 for both; type BCn gives the trivial group for both; and type D4 gives S4 for the automorphism group, with Xi the Klein four group (the unique Sylow-2 subgroup of A4).
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widetilde{\mathcal D}\) be the labeled affine Dynkin diagram attached to an affine root system \(\Psi\). Then: (1) if \(\Psi\) has type \(A_{1}\), \(\Xi=\operatorname{Aut}(\widetilde{\mathcal D})\cong\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z\); (2) if \(\Psi\) has type \(A_{n}\) with \(n>1\), \(\operatorname{Aut}(\widetilde{\mathcal D})\cong\mathbf Z/(n+1)\mathbf Z\rtimes\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z\) is dihedral of order \(2(n+1)\), and \(\Xi\) is its index-2 subgroup of rotations; (3) if \(\Psi\) has type \(B_{n},B_{n}^{\vee},C_{n},\) or \(C_{n}^{\vee}\), \(\Xi=\operatorname{Aut}(\widetilde{\mathcal D})\cong\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z\); (4) if \(\Psi\) has type \(BC_{n}\), \(\Xi=\operatorname{Aut}(\widetilde{\mathcal D})=\{1\}\); (5) if \(\Psi\) has type \(D_{4}\), \(\operatorname{Aut}(\widetilde{\mathcal D})\cong S_{4}\), and \(\Xi\) is the unique Sylow-2 subgroup of \(A_{4}\), hence \(\Xi\cong(\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z)^{2}\).
assumptions_latex: \(\Psi\) is an affine root system of one of the explicitly listed types: \(A_{1}\), \(A_{n}\) with \(n>1\), \(B_{n}\), \(B_{n}^{\vee}\), \(C_{n}\), \(C_{n}^{\vee}\), \(BC_{n}\), or \(D_{4}\).
\(\widetilde{\mathcal D}\) is the labeled affine Dynkin diagram attached to \(\Psi\).
statements.conclusion_latex: For the listed types, \(\operatorname{Aut}(\widetilde{\mathcal D})\) and \(\Xi\) are respectively: \(A_{1}\): both are \(\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z\); \(A_{n}\) with \(n>1\): \(\operatorname{Aut}(\widetilde{\mathcal D})\cong \mathbf Z/(n+1)\mathbf Z\rtimes\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z\) (the dihedral group of order \(2(n+1)\)), with \(\Xi\) its index-2 rotation subgroup; \(B_{n},B_{n}^{\vee},C_{n},C_{n}^{\vee}\): both are \(\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z\); \(BC_{n}\): both are trivial; \(D_{4}\): \(\operatorname{Aut}(\widetilde{\mathcal D})\cong S_{4}\), and \(\Xi\) is the unique Sylow-2 subgroup of \(A_{4}\), hence \(\Xi\cong(\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z)^{2}\).
statements.scope_note: Type-by-type classification of automorphism groups of the labeled affine Dynkin diagram and the distinguished subgroup Xi for exactly the affine root-system types stated in the source.

statements.title: Reducible and Irreducible Affine Root Systems
statements.statement_plain: A nonempty affine root system is reducible when it is the union of two nonempty subsets that are orthogonal in both directions: every gradient in one subset evaluates to zero on every coroot gradient in the other, and conversely. Otherwise it is irreducible.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Psi\) be a nonempty affine root system. It is called reducible if there exist nonempty subsets \(\Psi_1,\Psi_2\subset\Psi\) such that \(\Psi=\Psi_1\cup\Psi_2\) and, for every \(\psi\in\Psi_1\) and \(\eta\in\Psi_2\), \(\dot\psi(\dot\eta^{\vee})=0=\dot\eta(\dot\psi^{\vee})\). Otherwise, \(\Psi\) is called irreducible.
assumptions_latex: \Psi\neq\varnothing
\Psi\text{ is an affine root system}
statements.conclusion_latex: \Psi\text{ is reducible if such nonempty orthogonal subsets }\Psi_1,\Psi_2\text{ exist; otherwise }\Psi\text{ is irreducible}.
statements.scope_note: Defines reducibility by an orthogonal decomposition into two nonempty subsets; the orthogonality condition implies the subsets are disjoint.

statements.title: Affine root subsystem associated with a closed symmetric gradient subset
statements.statement_plain: Let A be an affine space over V and let Psi be an affine root system with gradient root system Phi. For a closed symmetric subset Phi' of Phi, let W be the subspace of V annihilated by Phi'. The roots in Psi whose gradients lie in Phi' form an affine root system on the quotient affine space A/W. If Psi is reduced, this subsystem is reduced.
statements.statement_latex: \text{Let }A\text{ be an affine space over }V,\ \Psi\subset A^*\text{ an affine root system with gradient root system }\Phi,\text{ and }\Phi'\subset\Phi\text{ a closed symmetric subset. If }W\subset V\text{ is the subspace annihilated by }\Phi',\text{ then }\Psi'=\{\psi\in\Psi\mid\dot\psi\in\Phi'\}\text{ is an affine root system in }(A/W)^*.\text{ If }\Psi\text{ is reduced, then }\Psi'\text{ is reduced}.
assumptions_latex: A\text{ is an affine space over }V
\Psi\subset A^*\text{ is an affine root system with gradient root system }\Phi
\Phi'\subset\Phi\text{ is closed and symmetric}
W=\{v\in V: a(v)=0\text{ for every }a\in\Phi'\}
statements.conclusion_latex: \Psi'=\{\psi\in\Psi\mid\dot\psi\in\Phi'\}\text{ is an affine root system in }(A/W)^*;\quad \Psi\text{ reduced}\Rightarrow\Psi'\text{ reduced}.
statements.scope_note: Formation of an affine root subsystem by selecting roots with gradients in a closed symmetric subset and passing to the corresponding quotient affine space.

statements.statement_plain: Let Psi_1 and Psi_2 be irreducible affine root systems. Any isomorphism from Psi_1 to Psi_2 extends uniquely to a vector-space isomorphism from A_1^* to A_2^* that sends the line of constant functions to the line of constant functions. statements.title: Normalization of Affine Root-System Isomorphisms
statements.statement_plain: Any isomorphism between affine root systems can be made strong by independently rescaling the source's irreducible components by nonzero real scalars; the resulting system maps strongly to the target.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varphi:\Psi\to\Psi'\) be an isomorphism of affine root systems. If \(\Psi=\Psi_1\oplus\cdots\oplus\Psi_n\) is the decomposition into irreducible pieces and \(A=A_1\times\cdots\times A_n\) the corresponding affine-space decomposition, then there exists an affine root system \(\Psi''\subset A^*\) of the form \(\Psi''=r_1\Psi_1\oplus\cdots\oplus r_n\Psi_n\), with each \(r_i\in\mathbf R^\times\), such that the induced map \(\varphi':\Psi''\to\Psi'\) is a strong isomorphism.
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi:\Psi\to\Psi'\) is an isomorphism of affine root systems.
\(\Psi=\Psi_1\oplus\cdots\oplus\Psi_n\) is the decomposition into irreducible pieces, and \(A=A_1\times\cdots\times A_n\) is the corresponding decomposition of the affine space.
statements.conclusion_latex: There exist \(r_1,\ldots,r_n\in\mathbf R^\times\) and an affine root system \(\Psi''=r_1\Psi_1\oplus\cdots\oplus r_n\Psi_n\subset A^*\) such that the composition \(\varphi':\Psi''\to\Psi'\) of \(\varphi\) with the natural bijection \(\Psi''\to\Psi\) is a strong isomorphism.
statements.scope_note: Abstract affine root systems decomposed into irreducible components; rescaling each component normalizes an isomorphism to a strong isomorphism.

statements.title: Automorphisms of the affine Dynkin diagram of type D_{2n}
statements.statement_plain: For affine Dynkin type D_{2n} with n>2, the automorphism group is (Z/2Z)^2 semidirect by Z/2Z. It is generated by involutions swapping the left pair, the right pair, and the two branches. The two distinct branch-swapping involutions commute; their product is the unique nontrivial central element, and they generate a Klein-four subgroup Xi.
statements.statement_latex: For \(\Psi\) of type \(D_{2n}\) with \(n>2\), \(\operatorname{Aut}(\widetilde{\mathcal D})\cong (\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z)^2\rtimes\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z\). It is generated by involutions swapping the two left terminal nodes, swapping the two right terminal nodes, and swapping the left and right branches. There are two distinct branch-switching involutions; they commute, their product is the unique nontrivial central element, and they generate \(\Xi\cong(\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z)^2\).
assumptions_latex: \(\Psi\) is of type \(D_{2n}\) with \(n>2\).
statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Aut}(\widetilde{\mathcal D})\cong (\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z)^2\rtimes\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z\), generated by the three stated involutions; the two branch-switching involutions commute, have product equal to the unique nontrivial central element, and generate \(\Xi\cong(\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z)^2\).
statements.scope_note: For the affine Dynkin diagram \(\widetilde{\mathcal D}\) associated with a root system \(\Psi\) of type \(D_{2n}\), with \(n>2\).

statements.title: Linear Relations in a Decomposed Affine Root System
statements.statement_plain: For a direct-sum decomposition of an affine root system and the corresponding product chamber or alcove, the distinguished affine roots are the union of the distinguished roots from the components. A linear combination of these roots is zero exactly when its sum on each component is a real constant and those component constants sum to zero.

Moreover, for any coefficients \((n_\psi)_{\psi\in\Psi(\mathcal C)^0}\), \(\sum_{\psi\in\Psi(\mathcal C)^0}n_\psi\psi=0\) if and only if there exist \(c_1,\ldots,c_n\in\mathbf R\) such that \(\sum_{\psi\in\Psi_i(\mathcal C_i)^0}n_\psi\psi=c_i\) for every \(i\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_i=0\).

statements.title: Finite Root Systems and Incidence Attached to a Facet
statements.statement_plain: For a point x in the affine apartment, the affine roots vanishing at x form a finite root system depending only on the facet containing x. Their gradients are distinct, their coroots give the dual system, and the point stabilizer in the affine Weyl group is the Weyl group of this subsystem. Chambers containing the facet correspond to Weyl chambers of the subsystem, while incident facets correspond to its parabolic subsets with reversed incidence; reducedness passes to the subsystem.

Then \Psi_x is a finite root system in the subspace of A_x^* it spans; \nabla|_{\Psi_x} is injective; \Psi_x depends only on the facet \mathcal F containing x (write \Psi_{\mathcal F}); its coroots form the dual root system; W(\Psi)_x\cong W(\Psi_x); for every chamber \mathcal C with \mathcal F\subset\overline{\mathcal C}, \Psi(\mathcal C)^0\cap\Psi_{\mathcal F} is a basis and chambers containing \mathcal F correspond bijectively to Weyl chambers of \Psi_{\mathcal F}; facets containing \mathcal F in their closure correspond bijectively to parabolic subsets via \mathcal F'\mapsto\{\psi\in\Psi_{\mathcal F}:\psi(\mathcal F')\ge0\}, with incidence order reversed under this correspondence; if \Psi is reduced then so is \Psi_x.
assumptions_latex: x\in A, where A carries the affine root system Ψ and affine Weyl group W(Ψ).
\mathcal F is the facet containing x.

statements.title: Strong Isomorphisms and Isomorphisms of Affine Root Systems
statements.statement_plain: For two affine root systems, a strong isomorphism is induced by an affine-space isomorphism whose linear part carries corresponding coroots to one another. An isomorphism is a bijection of the root sets preserving every integral linear combination that remains a root, in both directions.
statements.statement_latex: A strong isomorphism \(\Psi_1\to\Psi_2\) is an affine-space isomorphism \(f:A_2\to A_1\) such that \(f^*:A_1^*\to A_2^*\) induces a bijection \(\Psi_1\to\Psi_2\) and, for every \(\psi\in\Psi_2\), with \(\eta=(f^*)^{-1}(\psi)\), satisfies \((\nabla f)(\dot\psi^{\vee})=\dot\eta^{\vee}\). An isomorphism \(\Psi_1\to\Psi_2\) is a bijection \(\varphi:\Psi_1\to\Psi_2\) such that for all \(\psi,\eta\in\Psi_1\) and \(r,s\in\mathbf Z\), if \(r\psi+s\eta\in\Psi_1\), then \(\varphi(r\psi+s\eta)=r\varphi(\psi)+s\varphi(\eta)\), with the analogous condition required of \(\varphi^{-1}\).
assumptions_latex: A_i\text{ is an affine space under the }\mathbf R\text{-vector space }V_i\quad(i=1,2).
\Psi_i\subset A_i^*\text{ is an affine root system}\quad(i=1,2).
statements.conclusion_latex: \text{These conditions define the notions of strong isomorphism and isomorphism }\Psi_1\to\Psi_2.
statements.scope_note: Defines strong isomorphisms induced by affine-space isomorphisms with coroot compatibility, and abstract isomorphisms preserving all integral root combinations in both directions.

statements.title: Invariants and Strongness of Affine-Root-System Isomorphisms
statements.statement_plain: Let Psi_1 and Psi_2 be irreducible affine root systems, let phi be an isomorphism between them, and let f* be its extension to the affine-functional spaces. The induced map preserves the pairing of the linear part of every affine functional with the coroot of every affine root. It sends c(Psi_1) times the constant-one functional to either plus or minus c(Psi_2) times the constant-one functional. If the constants c(Psi_i) agree and the sign is positive, then phi is a strong isomorphism.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Psi_1\) and \(\Psi_2\) be irreducible affine root systems, let \(\varphi:\Psi_1\to\Psi_2\) be an isomorphism, and let \(f^*:A_1^*\to A_2^*\) be its extension. For \(\alpha_1\in A_1^*\) and \(\eta_1\in\Psi_1\), writing \(\alpha_2=f^*(\alpha_1)\) and \(\eta_2=\varphi(\eta_1)\), one has \(\dot\alpha_1(\dot\eta_1^\vee)=\dot\alpha_2(\dot\eta_2^\vee)\). There exists \(\varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}\) with \(f^*(c(\Psi_1)\mathbf 1_{A_1})=\varepsilon c(\Psi_2)\mathbf 1_{A_2}\). If additionally \(c(\Psi_1)=c(\Psi_2)\) and \(\varepsilon=1\), then \(\varphi\) is a strong isomorphism.
assumptions_latex: \(\Psi_1\) and \(\Psi_2\) are irreducible affine root systems.
\(\varphi:\Psi_1\to\Psi_2\) is an isomorphism.
\(f^*:A_1^*\to A_2^*\) is the extension of \(\varphi\) described in Proposition 1.3.52.
statements.conclusion_latex: For \(\alpha_1\in A_1^*\) and \(\eta_1\in\Psi_1\), writing \(\alpha_2=f^*(\alpha_1)\) and \(\eta_2=\varphi(\eta_1)\), one has \(\dot\alpha_1(\dot\eta_1^\vee)=\dot\alpha_2(\dot\eta_2^\vee)\). Moreover, there exists \(\varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}\) such that \(f^*(c(\Psi_1)\mathbf 1_{A_1})=\varepsilon c(\Psi_2)\mathbf 1_{A_2}\). If \(c(\Psi_1)=c(\Psi_2)\) and \(\varepsilon=1\), then \(\varphi\) is a strong isomorphism.
statements.scope_note: Invariance of affine-root-system pairings and constant-function vectors under an isomorphism, with a sign constraint and a sufficient criterion for strongness.

statements.title: Rescaled Gradient Root System
statements.statement_plain: In the standing affine-root-system notation, rescaling every gradient a by the inverse parameter u_a produces a root system in V* with the same Weyl group as the gradient root system Phi. If \(\Psi\) is reduced, then \(\bar{\Psi}=\{u_a^{-1}a\mid a\in\Phi^{\mathrm{nd}}\}\), so \(\bar{\Psi}\) is also reduced.
assumptions_latex: In the standing affine-root-system notation, \(\Psi\) has gradient root system \(\Phi\subset V^*\), with parameters \(u_a\) for \(a\in\Phi\).

statements.title: Panels, Chamber Adjacency, and Minimal Galleries
statements.statement_plain: A panel is a codimension-one face of a chamber, and two chambers are adjacent if they share a common panel. A gallery of length n joining two facets is a sequence of n+1 chambers in which consecutive chambers are adjacent and the facets are faces of the first and last chambers, respectively. The gallery is minimal if no shorter gallery joins those facets.
statements.statement_latex: A panel is a codimension-one face of a chamber of \(\mathcal B\), and two chambers are adjacent when they share a common panel. For facets \(\mathcal F,\mathcal F'\) in \(\mathcal B\), a gallery of length \(n\) joining them is a sequence of chambers \(\mathcal C_0,\ldots,\mathcal C_n\) such that each consecutive pair is adjacent, \(\mathcal F\) is a face of \(\mathcal C_0\), and \(\mathcal F'\) is a face of \(\mathcal C_n\). It is minimal if no gallery of smaller length joins \(\mathcal F\) and \(\mathcal F'\).
assumptions_latex: \mathcal F,\mathcal F'\text{ are facets in }\mathcal B
n\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}
statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&P\text{ is a panel}\iff P\text{ is a codimension-one face of a chamber of }\mathcal B;\\&\mathcal C\text{ and }\mathcal C'\text{ are adjacent}\iff\mathcal C\text{ and }\mathcal C'\text{ share a common panel};\\&(\mathcal C_0,\ldots,\mathcal C_n)\text{ is a gallery joining }\mathcal F\text{ and }\mathcal F'\\&\quad\iff \mathcal C_i\text{ is adjacent to }\mathcal C_{i+1}\ (0\le i<n),\ \mathcal F\text{ is a face of }\mathcal C_0,\ \mathcal F'\text{ is a face of }\mathcal C_n;\\&\text{the gallery is minimal}\iff\text{no gallery of length less than }n\text{ joins }\mathcal F\text{ and }\mathcal F'.\end{aligned}
statements.scope_note: Definitions of panels, chamber adjacency, galleries, and minimal galleries in the abstract building \(\mathcal B\).

statements.title: Retraction images of chambers incident with a wall
statements.statement_plain: Let I be an affine building, A an apartment, C a chamber of A, and rho the retraction onto A centered at C. For a wall F of I, define C1 and C2 as the two chambers of A specified by rho(F), with C1 on the same side as C. Exactly one chamber C' having F as a panel retracts to C1, while every other chamber having F as a panel retracts to C2.

Then there exists a unique chamber \(C'\) of \(\mathcal I\) having \(F\) as a panel with \(\rho(C')=C_1\); every chamber \(C''\neq C'\) of \(\mathcal I\) having \(F\) as a panel satisfies \(\rho(C'')=C_2\).
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal I\) is an affine building.
\(A\) is an apartment of \(\mathcal I\), \(C\) is a chamber of \(A\), and \(\rho=\rho_{A;C}\).

statements.title: Unique Chamber-Centered Retraction onto an Apartment
statements.statement_plain: Given an apartment A and a chamber C contained in it, there is a unique retraction rho from the affine building I onto A that fixes C and restricts on every apartment through C to the action of some element of G. Moreover, \(\rho|_A=\mathrm{Id}_A\); if \(x\in\overline{\mathbf C}\), then \(\rho^{-1}(x)=\{x\}\); and if \(F\) is a facet of type \(X\), then \(\rho(F)\) is of type \(X\), \(\rho(\overline F)=\overline{\rho(F)}\), and the restriction of \(\rho\) to \(\overline F\) is an affine bijection from \(F\) onto \(\rho(F)\).
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is an apartment of \(\mathcal I\).
\(\mathbf C\) is a chamber contained in \(A\).
statements.conclusion_latex: There exists a unique map \(\rho:\mathcal I\to A\) such that (i) \(\rho(\mathbf C)=\mathbf C\), and (ii) for every apartment \(A'\) containing \(\mathbf C\), there exists \(g\in G\) with \(\rho(x)=g.x\) for all \(x\in A'\). The restriction \(\rho|_A\) is the identity; if \(x\in\overline{\mathbf C}\), then \(\rho^{-1}(x)=\{x\}\). If \(F\) is a facet of type \(X\), then \(\rho(F)\) is of type \(X\), \(\rho(\overline F)=\overline{\rho(F)}\), and the restriction of \(\rho\) to \(\overline F\) is an affine bijection from \(F\) onto \(\rho(F)\).

statements.title: Convex Sets, Radius, and Barycenters
statements.statement_plain: In a uniquely geodesic space (X,d), a subset M is convex when the image of the unique geodesic between any two points of M is contained in M. For convex M, its radius is r(M) = inf{diam(x,M) | x in M}; a barycenter is a point x in M attaining this infimum.
statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be a uniquely geodesic space. A subset \(M\subseteq X\) is convex if, for every \(x,y\in M\), the image of the unique geodesic joining \(x\) and \(y\) lies in \(M\). For a convex set \(M\), define \(r(M):=\inf\{\operatorname{diam}(x,M)\mid x\in M\}\). A barycenter of \(M\) is a point \(x\in M\) such that \(\operatorname{diam}(x,M)=r(M)\).
assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a uniquely geodesic space
\(M\subseteq X\); for the radius and barycenter clauses, \(M\) is convex
statements.conclusion_latex: Convexity is defined by containment of each joining geodesic image in \(M\); for convex \(M\), \(r(M):=\inf\{\operatorname{diam}(x,M)\mid x\in M\}\), and a barycenter is any \(x\in M\) with \(\operatorname{diam}(x,M)=r(M)\).
statements.scope_note: Definitions for a subset of a uniquely geodesic space; the radius and barycenter clauses apply when the subset M is convex.

statements.title: Length Metric
statements.statement_plain: Let (X,d) be a metric space in which every pair of points is joined by at least one rectifiable curve. The length metric between x and y is the infimum of the lengths of all rectifiable curves joining them. It is at least d(x,y) and defines a metric on X.
statements.statement_latex:
Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space in which every pair $x,y\in X$ is joined by at least one rectifiable curve. Define
\[
d_{\ell}(x,y)=\inf\{\ell(c):c\text{ is a rectifiable curve joining }x\text{ to }y\}.
\]
Then $d_{\ell}(x,y)\ge d(x,y)$ for all $x,y\in X$, and $d_{\ell}$ is a metric on $X.
assumptions_latex: (X,d)\text{ is a metric space}
\forall x,y\in X,\ \exists\text{ a rectifiable curve joining }x\text{ to }y
statements.conclusion_latex: d_{\ell}(x,y)\ge d(x,y)\text{ for all }x,y\in X,\quad\text{and }d_{\ell}\text{ is a metric on }X.

statements.title: Canonical irreducible product decomposition of a Euclidean reflection-group action
statements.statement_plain: A Euclidean affine space acted on by a discrete group generated by orthogonal reflections has a canonical product decomposition into affine quotient factors. The acting group correspondingly splits as a direct product; the zeroth factor acts trivially, while every other factor is a nontrivial discrete reflection group with irreducible canonical linear representation on the factor's translation space.
statements.statement_latex: If \(\mathbf W\) is a discrete group of Euclidean displacements of the Euclidean affine space \(\mathbf A\), generated by orthogonal reflections, then \(\mathbf A\) decomposes canonically as \(\mathbf A_0\times\cdots\times\mathbf A_m\) into Euclidean affine quotients such that \(\mathbf W\cong\prod_{i=0}^m\mathbf W_i\), \(\mathbf W_0=\{\mathrm I\}\), and every \(\mathbf W_i\) for \(i\ge1\) is nontrivial with irreducible canonical linear representation on \({}^{v}\mathbf A_i\).
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbf A\) is a Euclidean affine space.
\(\mathbf W\) is a discrete group of Euclidean displacements generated by orthogonal reflections.
statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbf A\) decomposes canonically as a product \(\mathbf A_0\times\cdots\times\mathbf A_m\) of Euclidean affine quotient spaces, and \(\mathbf W\) identifies with a direct product \(\mathbf W_0\times\cdots\times\mathbf W_m\), where \(\mathbf W_0=\{\mathrm I\}\) and, for each \(1\le i\le m\), \(\mathbf W_i\) is a nontrivial discrete reflection group whose canonical linear representation on the translation space \({}^{v}\mathbf A_i\) is irreducible.
statements.scope_note: Canonical decomposition of a Euclidean affine reflection-group action into a trivial factor and irreducible reflection-group factors.

statements.title: Dynkin diagram of a finite root set or root system
statements.statement_plain: The diagram data consist of a graph, edge labels 3, 4, 6, or infinity, marked multipliable vertices, and oriented adjacent pairs recording decreasing root length. For a finite set Pi satisfying the stated scalar-product condition, vertices are roots whose halves are absent, edges join nonorthogonal roots, labels come from the squared-cosine formula, marked vertices are those whose doubles occur, and orientation points from the longer root to the shorter one. The Dynkin diagram of a root system Phi is formed from positive multiples of basis elements and is basis-independent up to canonical isomorphism.
statements.statement_latex: A quadruplet (G,f,M,F) consists of a graph G, an edge-label map f:E(G)\to\{3,4,6,\infty\}, a set M of multipliable vertices, and a set F of ordered adjacent pairs. statements.title: Rectifiable and geodesic curves
statements.statement_plain: For a curve c parametrized on [0,1] in a metric space, rectifiable means it has finite length. It is geodesic when it is rectifiable and every subinterval restriction, reparametrized to [0,1], has length equal to the distance between its endpoints and to the total endpoint distance times the parameter interval length.
statements.statement_latex: For a curve c:[0,1]\to X in a metric space (X,d), c is rectifiable if \ell(c)<\infty. It is geodesic if it is rectifiable and, for every 0<t_1<t_2<1, \ell\!\left(c|_{[t_1,t_2]}\right)=d\!\left(c(t_1),c(t_2)\right)=d\!\left(c(0),c(1)\right)|t_1-t_2|, where c|_{[t_1,t_2]}:[0,1]\to X is defined by c|_{[t_1,t_2]}(s)=c\!\left(t_1+s(t_2-t_1)\right).
assumptions_latex: c:[0,1]\to X is a curve in a metric space (X,d), with length denoted by \ell(c).
statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rectifiable}(c)\iff \ell(c)<\infty;\quad \operatorname{geodesic}(c)\iff \left(\ell(c)<\infty\ \land\ \forall\,0<t_1<t_2<1,\ \ell\!\left(c|_{[t_1,t_2]}\right)=d\!\left(c(t_1),c(t_2)\right)=d\!\left(c(0),c(1)\right)|t_1-t_2|\right),\quad c|_{[t_1,t_2]}(s)=c\!\left(t_1+s(t_2-t_1)\right).
statements.scope_note: Definitions for curves parametrized on [0,1] in a metric space.

statements.title: Sector-germ stabilizers and minimal-parabolic chambers
statements.statement_plain: Assume G acts on the building I with its standard apartment A and vectorial building, and that B is self-normalizing. Then B is the stabilizer of the standard sector germ containing the sectors x + D for x in A. G acts transitively on sector germs, with the stabilizer of g.T_B equal to gBg^{-1}. Sector germs correspond G-equivariantly to minimal parabolic subgroups, equivalently to chambers of the vectorial building, by matching stabilizers.
statements.statement_latex: Assume \(\mathbf G\) acts on the building \(\mathcal I\) with standard apartment \(\mathbf A\), standard sector germ determined by \(\mathfrak B\), and vectorial building \({}^{v}\mathcal I\), and assume \(\mathfrak B\) is self-normalizing. Then \(\mathfrak B\) is the stabilizer of the standard sector germ containing the sectors \(x+\mathbf D\) for \(x\in\mathbf A\); \(\mathbf G\) acts transitively on sector germs with \(\operatorname{Stab}(g\mathbin{.}\mathfrak T_{\mathfrak B})=g\mathfrak B g^{-1}\); and sector germs are \(\mathbf G\)-equivariantly in bijection with minimal parabolic subgroups, equivalently chambers of \({}^{v}\mathcal I\), via equality of stabilizers.
assumptions_latex: The group \(\mathbf G\) acts on the building \(\mathcal I\), with standard apartment \(\mathbf A\), standard sector germ determined by \(\mathfrak B\), and vectorial building \({}^{v}\mathcal I\).
\(\mathfrak B\) is self-normalizing: \(N_{\mathbf G}(\mathfrak B)=\mathfrak B\).
statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak B\) stabilizes the standard sector germ containing the sectors \(x+\mathbf D\) for \(x\in\mathbf A\). The \(\mathbf G\)-action on sector germs of \(\mathcal I\) is transitive, and \(\operatorname{Stab}(g\mathbin{.}\mathfrak T_{\mathfrak B})=g\mathfrak B g^{-1}\). There is a \(\mathbf G\)-equivariant bijection between sector germs, minimal parabolic subgroups, and chambers of \({}^{v}\mathcal I\), characterized by equality of stabilizers.

statements.title: Bornology and Bornological Group
statements.statement_plain: A bornology on a set X is a family of subsets containing all finite subsets, closed under finite unions, and closed under taking subsets. When X is a group, compatibility with the group law means that the set product M^{-1}M' of any two bounded subsets is bounded.
statements.statement_latex: A bornology on a set \(X\) is a collection \(\mathcal B\) of subsets of \(X\) containing all finite subsets, closed under finite unions, and downward closed: if \(M\in\mathcal B\) and \(M'\subseteq M\), then \(M'\in\mathcal B\). If \(X\) is a group, \(\mathcal B\) is compatible with the group law, making \(X\) a bornological group, when \(M^{-1}M'\in\mathcal B\) whenever \(M,M'\in\mathcal B\).
assumptions_latex: X is a set.
For the compatibility clause, X is a group and M,M' are bounded subsets in \(\mathcal B\).
statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal B\) contains every finite subset of X, is closed under finite unions and taking subsets, and in the group case satisfies \(M^{-1}M'\in\mathcal B\) for all \(M,M'\in\mathcal B\).

statements.statement_plain: For an affine-type Tits system (G,B,N), its associated bornology is contained in every group-law-compatible bornology in which B is bounded.
