statements.title: Barycenters and fixed points of bounded-set stabilizers
statements.statement_plain: Let (X,d) be a complete non-positively curved geodesic space. Every nonempty bounded closed convex subset M has a unique barycenter, invariant under every isometry of X that maps M to itself. For any nonempty bounded subset M, its setwise stabilizer in the isometry group of X has a fixed point in X.
statements.statement_latex: \text{Let }(X,d)\text{ be a complete non-positively curved geodesic space. If }M\subset X\text{ is nonempty, bounded, closed, and convex, then }M\text{ has a unique barycenter, and this barycenter is invariant under every isometry of }X\text{ mapping }M\text{ to itself. If }M\subset X\text{ is merely nonempty and bounded, then its setwise stabilizer in }\operatorname{Isom}(X)\text{ has a fixed point in }X.
assumptions_latex: (X,d)\text{ is a complete non-positively curved geodesic space.}
M\subset X\text{ is nonempty, bounded, closed, and convex for the barycenter assertion.}
M\subset X\text{ is nonempty and bounded for the stabilizer fixed-point assertion.}
statements.conclusion_latex: \text{In the first case, }M\text{ has a unique barycenter invariant under every isometry of }X\text{ preserving }M.\text{ In the second case, }\operatorname{Stab}_{\operatorname{Isom}(X)}(M)\text{ has a fixed point in }X.

statements.title: Classification of foldings of the affine D4 diagram
statements.statement_plain: For a subgroup of the automorphism group of the affine D4 diagram, the resulting folding is determined by its orbit sizes on the four non-central vertices. The partitions 1+1+1+1, 2+2, 1+1+2, 1+3, and 4 yield respectively the trivial split D4 case, affine C2-dual with finite B2, affine and finite B3, affine G2, and affine BC1.

statements.title: Restriction of Valued-Root-Datum Bornology to G1
statements.statement_plain: Under the hypotheses and notation of section 7.6, let p be the orthogonal projection from V to L1 and let S1 be the subgroup of T on which p composed with v vanishes. The bornology B(phi) restricted to G1 is compatible with phi1. It equals B(phi1) exactly when G1 is contained in G1^0 S1. A subset M of G1 is B(phi)-bounded exactly when it is B(phi1)-bounded and contained in G1^0 times the inverse image under p composed with v of a bounded subset X of L1. For subgroups of G1, boundedness is equivalent to B(phi1)-boundedness together with containment in G1^0 S1.

assumptions_latex: Retain the hypotheses and notation of §7.6.
p:V\to L_1 is the orthogonal projection.
S_1=\{t\in T\mid (p\circ v)(t)=0\}\le T.

statements.title: Compatibility Conditions and Induced Quasi-Valuation
statements.statement_plain: Assume the root datum and the associated system are compatible: their vector-space and Weyl-group data agree, they use the same subgroup N, and each U_a is the union of the U_alpha mapping to a. Choosing an origin in the apartment, the stated supremum formulas, with the doubled-root rule, define the source's quasi-valuation satisfying V0, V1, V2, V4, V5, and the weakened V3 bis axiom.

assumptions_latex: \(\left(\mathrm{T},(\mathrm{U}_a)_{a\in\Phi}\right)\) and \(\left(\mathrm{N},\nu,(\mathrm{U}_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\Sigma}\right)\) use the notations of (5.2.30) and are compatible.

statements.conclusion_latex: After choosing an origin in \(\mathbf A\cong\mathrm V\), set \(\alpha_{a,k}=\{x\in\mathbf A\mid a(x)+k\ge0\}\), define \(\varphi_a(u)=\sup\{k\in\mathbf R\mid u\in\mathbf U_{\alpha_{a,k}}\}\) for \(a\in\Phi^{\mathrm{red}}\), and for \(a\in\Phi\setminus\Phi^{\mathrm{red}}\), \(u\in\mathbf U_{2a}\), set \(\varphi_{2a}(u)=2\varphi_a(u)\). statements.title: Extension of a valuation
statements.statement_plain: An extension of phi is a map phi_0 from H to the nonnegative reals together with infinity whose level set U_{0,k} is, for every real k, a subgroup between H_[k] and H_(k), and whose commutators at levels k and l lie in level k+l. Phi is extendable when an extension exists.
statements.statement_latex: An extension of the valuation \(\varphi\) is a map \(\varphi_0:\mathbf H\to\mathbf R_{+}\cup\{\infty\}\) such that, for every \(k\in\mathbf R\), the level set \(\mathbf U_{0,k}:=\varphi_0^{-1}([k,\infty])\) is a subgroup of \(\mathbf H\) satisfying \(\mathbf H_{[k]}\subseteq\mathbf U_{0,k}\subseteq\mathbf H_{(k)}\), and for all \(k,\ell\in\mathbf R\), \((\mathbf U_{0,k},\mathbf U_{0,\ell})\subseteq\mathbf U_{0,k+\ell}\). The valuation \(\varphi\) is called extendable if it has an extension.
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi\) is a valuation with associated subgroup \(\mathbf H\) and filtration subgroups \(\mathbf H_{[k]}\) and \(\mathbf H_{(k)}\).
statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varphi\) is called extendable when such an extension \(\varphi_0\) exists.
statements.scope_note: Definition of extending a valuation to the subgroup \(\mathbf H\) in the rank-one root-group setting.

statements.title: Topological Compatibility of a Root-Datum Valuation
statements.statement_plain: A valuation phi of the root datum of (G,S) is compatible with the topology on G(k) when, for every root a, the subgroups U_{a,phi,r} for real r are bounded open subgroups of U_a(k) and form a neighborhood basis of the identity. Under compatibility, a sequence in U_a(k) converges to the identity exactly when its phi_a-values tend to infinity.
statements.statement_latex: A valuation \(\varphi\) of the root datum of \((G,S)\) is compatible with the topology on \(G(k)\) if, for every \(a\in\Phi\), the subgroups \(U_{a,\varphi,r}\) for \(r\in\mathbf R\) are bounded open subgroups of \(U_a(k)\) and constitute a neighborhood basis of \(1\). If \(\varphi\) is compatible, then every sequence \((u_i)\) in \(U_a(k)\) converges to \(1\) if and only if \(\varphi_a(u_i)\) converges to \(\infty\).
assumptions_latex: \varphi\text{ is a valuation of the root datum of }(G,S).
statements.conclusion_latex: \varphi\text{ is compatible with the topology on }G(k)\text{ when, for every }a\in\Phi,\ \{U_{a,\varphi,r}\}_{r\in\mathbf R}\text{ consists of bounded open subgroups of }U_a(k)\text{ forming a neighborhood basis of }1.\text{ If compatible, then for every sequence }(u_i)\subseteq U_a(k),\ u_i\to1\iff\varphi_a(u_i)\to\infty.
statements.scope_note: Compatibility of a root-datum valuation with the topology on root groups, together with the resulting convergence criterion.

statements.title: Action of products of M_{a,k} elements on a root-datum valuation
statements.statement_plain: For i=1,...,p choose a_i in Phi, k_i in Gamma_{a_i}, and m_i in M_{a_i,k_i}. Writing n=m_1...m_p and r_i for the reflection r_{a_i}, the induced action on the valuation is n·phi = phi - v, where v is the sum over i of k_i times the preceding reflections applied to a_i^vee, an element of V.

assumptions_latex: \varphi\text{ is a valuation of the given root datum}
a_i\in\Phi,\ k_i\in\Gamma_{a_i},\ m_i\in M_{a_i,k_i}\quad(i=1,\ldots,p)
n=m_1\cdots m_p,\quad r_i=r_{a_i}
statements.conclusion_latex: n\cdot\varphi=\varphi-v,\qquad v=\sum_{i=1}^{p}k_i\,(r_1\cdots r_{i-1})(a_i^\vee)\in V

statements.title: Opposite root-group factorization and commutator bounds
statements.statement_plain: Let u and u' be nonidentity elements in opposite root groups whose valuation values i and j satisfy i+j>0. Their product has a unique factorization uu'=x' z x in which x and x' remain in the corresponding nonidentity root groups with valuation values i and j, while z belongs to the Iwahori subgroup Z(k)^0. When u belongs to the 2a-root group, the commutator and the difference between x and u satisfy the stated filtered-root-group bounds. When u' belongs to the -2a-root group, the inverse commutator and the difference between x' and u' satisfy the analogous bounds.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varphi\in\mathcal A\), \(a\in\Phi\), \(u\in U_a(k)^*\), and \(u'\in U_{-a}(k)^*\), with \(\varphi_a(u)=i\), \(\varphi_{-a}(u')=j\), and \(i+j>0\). There exist unique \(x\in U_a(k)^*\), \(x'\in U_{-a}(k)^*\), and \(z\in Z(k)^0\) such that \(uu'=x'zx\), \(\varphi_a(x)=i\), and \(\varphi_{-a}(x')=j\). If \(u\in U_{2a}(k)^*\), then \((u,u')=uu'u^{-1}u'^{-1}\in U_{-a,\varphi,i+2j}Z(k)^0U_{a,\varphi,2i+j}\) and \(\varphi_a(xu^{-1})\ge 2i+j\). If \(u'\in U_{-2a}(k)^*\), then \((u^{-1},u'^{-1})\in U_{-a,\varphi,i+2j}Z(k)^0U_{a,\varphi,2i+j}\) and \(\varphi_{-a}(x'u'^{-1})\ge i+2j\).

statements.title: Opposite-root commutator containment estimates
statements.statement_plain: Let i and j be real numbers with i+j>0, let u belong to the a-root filtration subgroup at level i, and let u' belong to the opposite-root filtration subgroup at level j. Their commutator belongs to the ordered product of the -2a, -a, Z(k)^0, a, and 2a factors at levels i+3j, i+2j, 2i+j, and 3i+j as displayed. If u additionally belongs to the 2a-root filtration subgroup at level 2i, the commutator belongs to the stated ordered product of the -2a, -a, Z(k)^0, and a factors at levels 2i+4j, 2i+3j, and 2i+j.
statements.statement_latex: \text{Let }i,j\in\mathbf{R}\text{ with }i+j>0,\quad u\in U_{a,\varphi,i},\quad u'\in U_{-a,\varphi,j}.\text{ Then }[u,u']\in U_{-2a,\varphi,i+3j}\,U_{-a,\varphi,i+2j}\,Z(k)^0\,U_{a,\varphi,2i+j}\,U_{2a,\varphi,3i+j}.\text{ If additionally }u\in U_{2a,\varphi,2i},\text{ then }[u,u']\in U_{-2a,\varphi,2i+4j}\,U_{-a,\varphi,2i+3j}\,Z(k)^0\,U_{a,\varphi,2i+j}.
assumptions_latex: i,j\in\mathbf{R}
i+j>0
u\in U_{a,\varphi,i}
u'\in U_{-a,\varphi,j}
statements.conclusion_latex: [u,u']\in U_{-2a,\varphi,i+3j}\,U_{-a,\varphi,i+2j}\,Z(k)^0\,U_{a,\varphi,2i+j}\,U_{2a,\varphi,3i+j},\qquad u\in U_{2a,\varphi,2i}\Longrightarrow [u,u']\in U_{-2a,\varphi,2i+4j}\,U_{-a,\varphi,2i+3j}\,Z(k)^0\,U_{a,\varphi,2i+j}.
statements.scope_note: The notation is local to the given valuation \(\varphi\), and \([u,u']=uu'u^{-1}u'^{-1}\). The second containment retains the initial hypotheses and additionally assumes \(u\in U_{2a,\varphi,2i}\).

statements.title: Rank-One Commutator Estimates for a Valued Root Datum
statements.statement_plain: Let a valued root datum valuation \(\varphi\) and opposite-root elements u and u' have valuations i and j with i+j>0. Their product has a unique factorization uu'=x' z x with x and x' nontrivial elements of the corresponding root groups, preserving those valuations, and z in the Iwahori subgroup Z(k)^0. When u lies in U_{2a}(k)^*, the commutator [u,u'] lies in U_{-a,φ,i+2j} Z(k)^0 U_{a,φ,2i+j} and φ_a(xu^{-1}) is at least 2i+j. When u' lies in U_{-2a}(k)^*, the commutator [u^{-1},(u')^{-1}] lies in the same product and φ_{-a}(x'(u')^{-1}) is at least i+2j.
statements.statement_latex: \textbf{Proposition.}\ Let \(\varphi\in\mathcal A\), \(a\in\Phi\), and \(u\in U_a(k)^*\), \(u'\in U_{-a}(k)^*\) satisfy \(\varphi_a(u)=i\), \(\varphi_{-a}(u')=j\), and \(i+j>0\). Then there are unique \(x\in U_a(k)^*\), \(x'\in U_{-a}(k)^*\), and \(z\in Z(k)^0\) such that \(uu'=x'zx\), with \(\varphi_a(x)=i\) and \(\varphi_{-a}(x')=j\). If \(u\in U_{2a}(k)^*\), then \([u,u']\in U_{-a,\varphi,i+2j}Z(k)^0U_{a,\varphi,2i+j}\) and \(\varphi_a(xu^{-1})\ge 2i+j\). If \(u'\in U_{-2a}(k)^*\), then \([u^{-1},(u')^{-1}]\in U_{-a,\varphi,i+2j}Z(k)^0U_{a,\varphi,2i+j}\) and \(\varphi_{-a}(x'(u')^{-1})\ge i+2j\).
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi\in\mathcal A\) and \(a\in\Phi\).
\(u\in U_a(k)^*\), \(u'\in U_{-a}(k)^*\), with \(\varphi_a(u)=i\) and \(\varphi_{-a}(u')=j\).
\(i+j=\varphi_a(u)+\varphi_{-a}(u')>0\).
statements.conclusion_latex: There exist unique \(x\in U_a(k)^*\), \(x'\in U_{-a}(k)^*\), and \(z\in Z(k)^0\) such that \(uu'=x'zx\), \(\varphi_a(x)=i\), and \(\varphi_{-a}(x')=j\). If \(u\in U_{2a}(k)^*\), then \([u,u']\in U_{-a,\varphi,i+2j}\,Z(k)^0\,U_{a,\varphi,2i+j}\) and \(\varphi_a(xu^{-1})\ge 2i+j\). If \(u'\in U_{-2a}(k)^*\), then \([u^{-1},(u')^{-1}]\in U_{-a,\varphi,i+2j}\,Z(k)^0\,U_{a,\varphi,2i+j}\) and \(\varphi_{-a}(x'(u')^{-1})\ge i+2j\).

statements.title: Valuation determined by values on a root basis
statements.statement_plain: For two valuations of the root datum of (G,S), equality of the valuations is equivalent to equality of their valuation maps on every root in a basis Pi of the root system Phi.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Pi\) be a basis of the root system \(\Phi\), and let \(\varphi=(\varphi_a)_{a\in\Phi}\) and \(\varphi'=(\varphi'_a)_{a\in\Phi}\) be valuations of the root datum of \((G,S)\). Then \(\varphi'=\varphi\) if and only if \(\varphi'_a=\varphi_a\) for every \(a\in\Pi\).
assumptions_latex: \(\Pi\) is a basis of the root system \(\Phi\).
\(\varphi=(\varphi_a)_{a\in\Phi}\) and \(\varphi'=(\varphi'_a)_{a\in\Phi}\) are valuations of the root datum of \((G,S)\).
statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varphi'=\varphi\iff \forall a\in\Pi,\;\varphi'_a=\varphi_a\).
statements.scope_note: A valuation of a root datum is uniquely determined by its valuation maps on the roots in any chosen basis of the root system.

statements.title: Valuation formula for rank-two commutator factors
statements.statement_plain: In a rank-two root subsystem, if the commutator (u,u') of u in U_a and u' in U_b factors as u_2...u_{s-1} with u_i in U_{a_i}, then whenever a_i=pa+qb for 2<=i<=s-1 and p,q are natural numbers, the valuation satisfies phi_{a_i}(u_i)=p phi_a(u)+q phi_b(u').
statements.statement_latex: Let a,b and the rank-two subsystem \Psi, ordered roots a_1,\ldots,a_{2s}, and elements u,u',u_i satisfy the stated hypotheses. For i,p,q\in\mathbf N with 2\le i\le s-1 and a_i=pa+qb, one has \varphi_{a_i}(u_i)=p\varphi_a(u)+q\varphi_b(u').
assumptions_latex: a,b\in\Phi,\ b\notin\mathbf{R}a,\ b-a\notin\Phi.
\Psi=\Phi\cap(\mathbf{Z}a+\mathbf{Z}b),\quad a=a_1,\ldots,a_s=b,a_{s+1},\ldots,a_{2s}\text{ are the elements of }\Psi^{\mathrm{red}}\text{ in circular order}.
u\in U_a,\ u'\in U_b,\ (u,u')=u_2\cdots u_{s-1}\text{ with }u_j\in U_{a_j}.
i,p,q\in\mathbf{N},\ 2\le i\le s-1,\ a_i=pa+qb.
statements.conclusion_latex: \varphi_{a_i}(u_i)=p\,\varphi_a(u)+q\,\varphi_b(u').

statements.title: Valuation identities and rank-one consequences for root-group filtrations
statements.statement_plain: For a valuation of a root datum, the valuation of each root-group element is the supremum of the filtration levels containing it and is invariant under inversion (using axiom VI). Assuming V1, axiom V5 is equivalent to the stated V5 bis condition. The rank-one sets M_{a,k} are nonempty exactly for values attained on U_a^*, satisfy the displayed factorization inclusion, and obey M_{2a,2k} subset M_{a,k} when 2a is a root. The U_{a,k} form a neighborhood basis for a topological group structure on U_a. Gamma_a and Gamma'_a are the value sets defined by the displayed formulas.
statements.statement_latex: \varphi_a(u)=\sup\{k\in\mathbf R\cup\{\infty\}:u\in\mathbf U_{a,k}\},\quad \varphi_a(u^{-1})=\varphi_a(u)\ \text{(VI)};\quad (V5)\iff(V5\ \mathrm{bis})\ \text{when (V1) holds};\quad \mathbf M_{a,k}\ne\varnothing\iff k\in\varphi_a(\mathrm U_a^*),\quad \varphi_a^{-1}(k)\subseteq\mathrm U_{-a,-k}\mathbf M_{a,k}\mathrm U_{-a,-k},\quad \mathbf M_{2a,2k}\subseteq\mathbf M_{a,k}\ (2a\in\Phi),\quad \{\mathrm U_{a,k}\}_k\text{ is a neighborhood basis at }1,\quad \Gamma_a=\varphi_a(\mathrm U_a^*),\quad \Gamma'_a=\{\varphi_a(u):u\in\mathrm U_a^*,\ \varphi_a(u)=\sup\varphi_a(u\mathrm U_{2a})\}.
assumptions_latex: \varphi=(\varphi_a) is a valuation of the root datum (\mathrm T,(\mathrm U_a)) satisfying its valuation axioms.
For a\in\Phi, set \mathrm U_{2a,k}=\{1\} when 2a\notin\Phi, for k\in\mathbf R\cup\{\infty\}.
For a\in\Phi and k\in\mathbf R, define \mathbf M_{a,k}=\mathbf M_a\cap\mathrm U_{-a}\varphi_a^{-1}(k)\mathrm U_{-a}; when 2a\in\Phi, the valuation compatibility axiom (V4) is in force.
statements.conclusion_latex: For a\in\Phi and u\in\mathrm U_a, \varphi_a(u)=\sup\{k\in\mathbf R\cup\{\infty\}:u\in\mathbf U_{a,k}\} and, using (VI), \varphi_a(u^{-1})=\varphi_a(u). When (V1) holds, (V5) is equivalent to: for u\in\mathrm U_a and u',u''\in\mathrm U_{-a}, if u'uu''\in\mathrm M_a then \varphi_{-a}(u'')=-\varphi_a(u). Moreover, \mathbf M_{a,k}\ne\varnothing iff k\in\varphi_a(\mathrm U_a^*), and \varphi_a^{-1}(k)\subseteq\mathrm U_{-a,-k}\mathbf M_{a,k}\mathrm U_{-a,-k}; if 2a\in\Phi then \mathbf M_{2a,2k}\subseteq\mathbf M_{a,k}. The subgroups \mathrm U_{a,k} form a neighborhood basis at the identity for a topological group structure on \mathrm U_a. Finally, \Gamma_a=\varphi_a(\mathrm U_a^*) and \Gamma'_a=\{\varphi_a(u):u\in\mathrm U_a^*,\ \varphi_a(u)=\sup\varphi_a(u\mathrm U_{2a})\}.
statements.scope_note: Consequences and equivalent reformulation of the valuation axioms for root groups in a valued root datum, including rank-one factorization subsets, the induced root-group topology, and the definitions of the value sets.

statements.title: Generating Root Data over an Extension and over K
statements.statement_plain: The algebraic group determines generating root data both over the extension field and on its K-rational points. The two systems are compatible in the stated DDR sense; the normalizer modulo the torus is the relative Weyl group, and the invariant vector space corresponds to the dual of the span of the relative roots.

\widetilde{G}=G(\widetilde{K}) is generated by \widetilde{T}=T(\widetilde{K}) and the groups \widetilde{U}_{\alpha}(\widetilde{K}) for \alpha\in\widetilde{\Phi}; G(K) is generated by T=T(K) and U_a(K) for a\in\Phi.
The extension-field and K-rational root data are compared through the stated Gal(\widetilde{K}/K)-invariant subspace and the restriction relation between \widetilde{\Phi} and \Phi.

statements.title: Decomposition by irreducible root-system components
statements.statement_plain: Decompose the root system of a generating root datum into irreducible components. The root groups in each component generate a distinguished subgroup carrying the restricted generating root datum. The torus normalizes each such subgroup; subgroups from different components centralize one another, and their pairwise intersections lie in the center of the subgroup generated by all root groups and hence in the torus. The whole group is the product of the torus and the subgroup generated by all root groups.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Phi=\bigcup_{i\in I}\Phi_i\) be the decomposition into irreducible components of a generating root datum \((\mathbf T,(\mathbf U_a)_{a\in\Phi})\) in \(\mathbf G\). Set \(\mathbf G_i^0=\langle\mathbf U_a\mid a\in\Phi_i\rangle\) and \(\mathbf G^0=\langle\mathbf U_a\mid a\in\Phi\rangle\). Then each restricted datum \((\mathbf T\cap\mathbf G_i^0,(\mathbf U_a,\mathbf M_a\cap\mathbf G_i^0)_{a\in\Phi_i})\) is generating of type \(\Phi_i\); \(\mathbf T\) normalizes every \(\mathbf G_i^0\); for \(i\ne j\), the subgroups \(\mathbf G_i^0\) and \(\mathbf G_j^0\) centralize one another, each \(\mathbf G_i^0\) is a distinguished subgroup of \(\mathbf G\), and \(\mathbf G_i^0\cap\mathbf G_j^0\subseteq Z(\mathbf G^0)\subseteq\mathbf T\); moreover \(\mathbf G=\mathbf T\mathbf G^0\).
assumptions_latex: \Phi=\bigcup_{i\in I}\Phi_i\text{ is the decomposition into irreducible components}
(\mathbf T,(\mathbf U_a)_{a\in\Phi})\text{ is a generating root datum in }\mathbf G
statements.conclusion_latex: \text{For }\mathbf G_i^0:=\langle\mathbf U_a\mid a\in\Phi_i\rangle\text{ and }\mathbf G^0:=\langle\mathbf U_a\mid a\in\Phi\rangle,\text{ each }(\mathbf T\cap\mathbf G_i^0,(\mathbf U_a,\mathbf M_a\cap\mathbf G_i^0)_{a\in\Phi_i})\text{ is a generating root datum of type }\Phi_i;\ \mathbf T\text{ normalizes every }\mathbf G_i^0;\ [\mathbf G_i^0,\mathbf G_j^0]=1\text{ for }i\ne j;\ \mathbf G_i^0\text{ is distinguished in }\mathbf G;\ \mathbf G_i^0\cap\mathbf G_j^0\subseteq Z(\mathbf G^0)\subseteq\mathbf T\text{ for }i\ne j;\ \mathbf G=\mathbf T\mathbf G^0.
statements.scope_note: Structural decomposition theorem for a generating root datum indexed by the irreducible components of its root system.

statements.title: Valuation lattices for relative roots under change of valuation
statements.statement_plain: For a relative root a, define v_a as the common value of a generator of the valuation lattice \omega(k_{\widetilde a}) for any absolute root lifting a. In type R1, J_a and J_{a/2a} equal v_a times the integers. In type R2, J_a is one half of v_a times the integers and J_{a/2a} is v_a times the integers; J_{2a} is v_a times the integers when e_{a/b}=1, and v_a times the odd integers when e_{a/b}=2.

statements.title: Construction and parametrization of Chevalley-Steinberg valuations
statements.statement_plain: Rescale the pinning by a Galois-equivariant homomorphism theta from the lifted root system to the multiplicative group of the splitting field. The resulting Chevalley-Steinberg valuation phi' differs from the fixed valuation phi by the shift a(phi'-phi) equal to minus the valuation of theta(a) for every non-divisible root a. Conversely, prescribing the shifts omega_a for all a in Delta determines a unique Chevalley-Steinberg valuation.
statements.statement_latex: Given a pinning (\widetilde{x}_{\alpha}) and valuation \varphi, choose a Galois-equivariant homomorphism \theta:\widetilde{\Phi}\to\widetilde{\mathrm K}^{\times} and set \widetilde{x}'_{\alpha}(u)=\widetilde{x}_{\alpha}(\theta(\alpha)u). For each non-divisible a\in\Phi define \theta(a)=\theta(\alpha(a))\in\mathbf L_a^{\times}; the associated valuation \varphi' satisfies a(\varphi'-\varphi)=-\omega(\theta(a)). Conversely, prescribing \omega_a\in\omega(\mathbf L_a^{\times}) for every a\in\Delta yields one and only one Chevalley-Steinberg valuation \varphi' satisfying a(\varphi'-\varphi)=-\omega_a for all a\in\Delta.
assumptions_latex: A pinning (\widetilde{x}_{\alpha}) and a valuation \varphi are fixed.

\theta:\widetilde{\Phi}\to\widetilde{\mathrm K}^{\times} is a homomorphism satisfying \gamma\circ\theta=\theta\circ\gamma for every \gamma\in\operatorname{Gal}(\widetilde{\mathrm K}/\widetilde{\mathrm K}).
For each non-divisible a\in\Phi, define \theta(a)=\theta(\alpha(a)); then \theta(a)\in\mathbf L_a^{\times}.
For each a\in\Delta, choose \omega_a\in\omega(\mathbf L_a^{\times}).
statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde{x}'_{\alpha}(u)=\widetilde{x}_{\alpha}(\theta(\alpha)u)\quad(\alpha\in\widetilde{\Phi},\ u\in\widetilde{\mathrm K});\qquad a(\varphi'-\varphi)=-\omega(\theta(a))\quad\text{for every non-divisible }a\in\Phi.\quad\text{Conversely, the prescribed }\omega_a\text{ determine a unique Chevalley--Steinberg valuation }\varphi'\text{ with }a(\varphi'-\varphi)=-\omega_a\text{ for all }a\in\Delta.

statements.statement_plain: For two valuations of the same root datum of G, the valuations are equivalent exactly when their associated bornologies are equal, equivalently when the induced bornologies agree on every root group U_a, agree on N, or when for each root a there is a bijection f_a from the value set of the first valuation to that of the second satisfying psi_a = f_a composed with phi_a.

statements.title: Explicit SU_3 Rank-One Big-Cell Factorization
statements.statement_plain: In SU_3 defined by a quadratic extension L/K with involution sigma, use standard coordinates x_a(u,v) and x_{-a}(u',v') on opposite relative root groups and set t = 1 - sigma(u)u' + vv'. The big-cell domain W_a is the principal open subset where Norm_{L/K}(t) is nonzero, so d_a equals this norm. On W_a, beta_a factors the product into U_{-a}, T, and U_a with coordinates x_{-a}(t^{-1}(u' - uv'), t^{-1}v'), tilde a'(t), and x_a((t^sigma)^{-1}(u - v^sigma u'), t^{-1}v), respectively.
statements.statement_latex: For the SU_3 rank-one opposite relative root groups over the quadratic extension L/K, let t=1-u^\sigma u'+vv'. The open subset W_a\subset U_a\times U_{-a} is the principal open defined by d_a\!\left(x_a(u,v),x_{-a}(u',v')\right)=\operatorname{Norm}_{L/K}(t), equivalently by \operatorname{Norm}_{L/K}(t)\ne0. For such points, the morphism \beta_a:W_a\to U_{-a}\times T\times U_a satisfies \beta_a\!\left(x_a(u,v),x_{-a}(u',v')\right)=\left(x_{-a}\!\left(t^{-1}(u'-uv'),t^{-1}v'\right),\widetilde a'(t),x_a\!\left((t^\sigma)^{-1}(u-v^\sigma u'),t^{-1}v\right)\right).
assumptions_latex: L/K is the quadratic extension defining the unitary group SU_3, and \sigma is its nontrivial automorphism.
x_a(u,v) and x_{-a}(u',v') are the standard coordinates on the opposite relative root groups U_a and U_{-a} in SU_3.
statements.conclusion_latex: Set t=1-u^\sigma u'+vv'. Then W_a is the principal open subset of U_a\times U_{-a} on which \operatorname{Norm}_{L/K}(t)\ne0, and d_a\!\left(x_a(u,v),x_{-a}(u',v')\right)=\operatorname{Norm}_{L/K}(t). On W_a, the morphism \beta_a:W_a\to U_{-a}\times T\times U_a is given by \beta_a\!\left(x_a(u,v),x_{-a}(u',v')\right)=\left(x_{-a}\!\left(t^{-1}(u'-uv'),t^{-1}v'\right),\widetilde a'(t),x_a\!\left((t^\sigma)^{-1}(u-v^\sigma u'),t^{-1}v\right)\right).

statements.title: Chevalley valuations and associated bounded open subgroups
statements.statement_plain: For a split semisimple group, each root-datum valuation defines a bounded open subgroup generated by the bounded torus subgroup and level-zero root subgroups. Valuations obtained from a pinning form an equipollence affine space under V(S), parameterizing these subgroups; such valuations are called Chevalley valuations.
statements.statement_latex: Let G be split semisimple over k with maximal split torus S and root system \(\Phi\). For a valuation \(\varphi\) of the root datum, define \(\mathcal P_{\varphi}\) as the subgroup of \(G(k)\) generated by \(S(k)^0\) and \(U_{a,\varphi,0}\) for all \(a\in\Phi\). If \(o\) is a weak Chevalley system (equivalently, a k-pinning together with its unique weak Chevalley extension) and \(v\in V(S)\), then \(\varphi_{o+v}=\varphi_o+v\) and \(\mathcal P_{\varphi_{o+v}}=\mathcal P_{o,v}\). The equipollence class \(\{\varphi_{o+v}:v\in V(S)\}\) is an affine space under \(V(S)\), and a valuation of the split root datum arising from a pinning is called a Chevalley valuation.
assumptions_latex: G is split semisimple over k, with maximal split torus S and root system \(\Phi\).
\(\varphi\) is a valuation of the root datum; \(o\) is a weak Chevalley system (or a k-pinning with its unique weak Chevalley extension); and \(v\in V(S)\).
\(S(k)^0\) and \(U_{a,\varphi,0}\) denote the bounded torus subgroup and valuation filtration subgroups.
statements.conclusion_latex: For each root-datum valuation \(\varphi\), \(\mathcal P_{\varphi}=\langle S(k)^0, U_{a,\varphi,0}\ (a\in\Phi)\rangle\). For \(\varphi_{o+v}\), one has \(\varphi_{o+v}=\varphi_o+v\) and \(\mathcal P_{\varphi_{o+v}}=\mathcal P_{o,v}\); the equipollence class \(\{\varphi_{o+v}:v\in V(S)\}\) is an affine space under \(V(S)\) parametrizing these bounded open subgroups. A valuation arising from a pinning is called a Chevalley valuation.
statements.scope_note: Definitions and parameterization for valuations of the split root datum of a split semisimple group and their associated bounded open subgroups.

statements.title: Descent Definition for Relative Root-Group Valuations
statements.statement_plain: For a relative root a of type R1, define its valuation on U_a(k) by composing the identification with the lifted absolute root group and the absolute valuation. For type R2, write an element via the lifted root groups U_tilde a, U_tilde a', and U_tilde b, where tilde b equals tilde a plus tilde a'; define its valuation as the minimum of the two lift valuations and one half of the valuation on U_tilde b. For every non-divisible relative root a and real r, U_{a,phi,r} equals U_a(k) intersected with the product of U_{b,phi_l,r} over non-divisible roots b of Phi(T_l) restricting to a or 2a. Thus phi is the descent of phi_l.
statements.statement_latex: \text{If }a\text{ is of type R1, }\varphi_a\text{ is }U_a(k)\cong U_{\widetilde a}(k_{\widetilde a})\hookrightarrow U_{\widetilde a}(\ell)\xrightarrow{\varphi_{\ell,\widetilde a}}\mathbf R\cup\{\infty\}.\ \text{If }a\text{ is of type R2 and }u\mapsto(u_{\widetilde a},u_{\widetilde a'},u_{\widetilde b})\text{ under (2.6.2), then }\varphi_a(u)=\min\!\left(\varphi_{\ell,\widetilde a}(u_{\widetilde a}),\varphi_{\ell,\widetilde a'}(u_{\widetilde a'}),\tfrac12\varphi_{\ell,\widetilde b}(u_{\widetilde b})\right).
assumptions_latex: a\in\Phi is a relative root of type R1 or R2, and an absolute lift \widetilde a\in\widetilde\Phi is chosen.

For type R2, \widetilde a' is the unique other lift with \widetilde b=\widetilde a+\widetilde a'\in\widetilde\Phi; use the isomorphism U_a(k)\to U_{[\widetilde a]}(k_{\widetilde b})\subset U_{\widetilde a}(\ell)U_{\widetilde a'}(\ell)U_{\widetilde b}(\ell).
The maps \varphi_{\ell,\widetilde a}:U_{\widetilde a}(\ell)\to\mathbf R\cup\{\infty\} (and the corresponding maps for \widetilde a' and \widetilde b) are the absolute-root valuation maps.
statements.conclusion_latex: \text{For every non-divisible }a\in\Phi\text{ and }r\in\mathbf R,\quad U_{a,\varphi,r}=U_a(k)\cap\prod_{\substack{b\in\Phi(T_\ell)\text{ non-divisible}\\ b|_T\in\{a,2a\}}}U_{b,\varphi_\ell,r};\quad\varphi\text{ is the descent of }\varphi_\ell.
statements.scope_note: Defines relative root-group valuations in the quasi-split semisimple setting by descent from absolute-root valuations, with the induced filtration identity.

statements.title: Normalizer and Adjoint-Normalizer Actions on Root-Datum Valuations
statements.statement_plain: The normalizer N(k) transports valuations by conjugating root-group elements and relabeling roots, and this action factors through the Weyl group. The image of the normalizer in G_ad acts similarly. Its action is compatible with translations of valuations by V(S), yielding an action of V(S) semidirect product N_ad(k).
statements.statement_latex: The normalizer \(N(k)\) acts on valuations \(\varphi=(\varphi_a)_{a\in\Phi}\) of the root datum \((G,S)\) by transporting root indices and conjugating root-group elements: \((n\cdot\varphi)_a(u)=\varphi_{n^{-1}\cdot a}(n^{-1}un)\) for \(u\in U_a(k)\). This action factors through the Weyl group \(W=N(k)/Z(k)\). Under the natural surjective map \(G\to G_{\mathrm{ad}}\), the image \(N_{\mathrm{ad}}(k)\) acts by the same formula, and for \(v\in V(S)\) one has \(n\cdot(\varphi+v)=n\cdot\varphi+n\cdot v\); hence \(V(S)\rtimes N_{\mathrm{ad}}(k)\) acts on the set of root-datum valuations.
assumptions_latex: (G,S) is a root datum with root system \(\Phi=\Phi(S,G)\) and root groups \(U_a\)
\(N\) and \(Z\) are respectively the normalizer and centralizer of \(S\) in \(G\), with \(N(k)\) and \(Z(k)\) their k-points; \(W=N(k)/Z(k)\)
\(\varphi=(\varphi_a)_{a\in\Phi}\) is a valuation of the root datum, with \(u\in U_a(k)\)
There is a natural surjective homomorphism \(G\to G_{\mathrm{ad}}\) with central (possibly nonsmooth) kernel; \(N_{\mathrm{ad}}\) and \(Z_{\mathrm{ad}}\) are the images of \(N\) and \(Z\)
statements.conclusion_latex: For \(n\in N(k)\), define \((n\cdot\varphi)_a(u)=\varphi_{n^{-1}\cdot a}(n^{-1}un)\) for \(u\in U_a(k)\); this is a valuation and gives an action of \(N(k)\) on valuations, factoring through \(W=N(k)/Z(k)\). The same formula defines an action of \(N_{\mathrm{ad}}(k)\) (via its action on \(\Phi\) and \(G\)); the N(k)-action is induced through \(N(k)\to N_{\mathrm{ad}}(k)\). For \(v\in V(S)\), \(n\cdot(\varphi+v)=n\cdot\varphi+n\cdot v\), so these actions combine to an action of \(V(S)\rtimes N_{\mathrm{ad}}(k)\) on valuations.
statements.scope_note: Definition of normalizer and adjoint-normalizer actions on root-datum valuations and their compatibility with translations by V(S).

statements.title: Transitivity of Root-Datum Valuation Descent Under Unramified Extension
statements.statement_plain: Given K contained in a valued extension K' inside an algebraically closed extension of the original splitting field, with K' times the original splitting field an unramified splitting field, the Chevalley-Steinberg valuation extends to K'. Its descent to the relative root datum over K' is transitive and descends further to the original valuation over K.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subset K'\subset\mathrm E\) and the splitting fields and tori be as above, with \(\widetilde K'/K'\) unramified. A Chevalley–Steinberg system defining \(\widetilde\varphi\) over \(\widetilde K\) extends to \(\widetilde K'\), defining \(\widetilde\varphi'\). If \(\varphi'\) denotes its descent to the relative root datum over \(K'\), then \(\varphi'\) descends through \(K'/K\) to the valuation \(\varphi\) on the relative root datum over \(K\).
assumptions_latex: \(\mathrm E\) is an algebraically closed extension of \(\widetilde K\).
\(K'\subset\mathrm E\) contains \(K\) and has a valuation \(\omega'\) extending \(\omega\).
\(\widetilde K'=K'\widetilde K\) is the smallest Galois extension of \(K'\) splitting \(G\); assume \(\widetilde K'/K'\) is unramified.

After identifying \(X^*(T)\) and \(X^*(T')\), the absolute root systems satisfy \(\widetilde\Phi=\widetilde\Phi'\). Let \(S''\) be the maximal \(K'\)-split subtorus of \(T'\), with relative root system \(\Phi''\).
A Chevalley–Steinberg system \((\widetilde x_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\widetilde\Phi}\) defines the valuation \(\widetilde\varphi\) on the original split root datum.
statements.conclusion_latex: The same Chevalley–Steinberg system over \(\widetilde K'\) defines a valuation \(\widetilde\varphi'\) on the split root datum of \(G(\widetilde K')\), which descends to a valuation \(\varphi'\) on the relative root datum of \(G(K')\); this descent is transitive, so \(\varphi'\) descends further to the original valuation \(\varphi\) over \(K\).
statements.scope_note: Compatibility and transitivity of Chevalley–Steinberg valuation descent along an unramified splitting extension.

statements.title: Affine root-group filtrations and half-apartment fixed sets
statements.statement_plain: For a root a, affine root subgroups U_psi form arbitrarily small subgroups in U_a(k). Each U_psi is the subgroup fixing the associated half-apartment A_psi pointwise, while every nonidentity root-group element u fixes a half-apartment A_{psi_a^u} determined by an affine function of derivative a. Conjugation by s in S(k) shifts psi_a^u by omega(a(s)); for z in H_psi, membership in U_psi minus the identity is equivalent to psi <= psi_a^u and to psi_a^u(z) >= 0. When a and 2a are roots and u lies in U_{2a}(k), psi_{2a}^u=2 psi_a^u and U_psi intersected with U_{2a}(k) is contained in U_{2psi}. The fixed half-apartment of U_psi need not be maximal: it may fix a strictly larger half-apartment, for example when U_psi=U_{psi+epsilon} with epsilon>0.
statements.statement_latex: For a\in\Phi, the affine root subgroups U_\psi\subset U_a(k) satisfy: every identity neighborhood contains some U_\psi (with affine derivative a); U_\psi is exactly the subgroup fixing \mathcal A_\psi pointwise; each nontrivial u\in U_a(k) fixes \mathcal A_{\psi_a^u} for an affine \psi_a^u of derivative a; \psi_a^{sus^{-1}}=\omega(a(s))+\psi_a^u for s\in S(k); for z\in\mathcal H_\psi, U_\psi\setminus\{1\}=\{u\mid\psi\le\psi_a^u\}=\{u\mid\psi_a^u(z)\ge0\}; and if a,2a\in\Phi and u\in U_{2a}(k), then \psi_{2a}^u=2\psi_a^u and U_\psi\cap U_{2a}(k)\subset U_{2\psi}. The subgroup U_\psi can nevertheless fix a strictly larger half-apartment; in particular, U_\psi=U_{\psi+\epsilon} implies pointwise fixation of \mathcal A_{\psi+\epsilon} for every indicated \epsilon>0.
assumptions_latex: a\in\Phi, with root subgroup U_a(k), and \mathcal A the affine apartment.
\mathcal U is a neighborhood of the identity in U_a(k).
u\in U_a(k)^* and s\in S(k) where invoked.
z\in\mathcal H_\psi where invoked.

statements.conclusion_latex: (1) For every identity neighborhood \mathcal U\subset U_a(k), there is a real-valued affine function \psi on \mathcal A with derivative a such that U_\psi\subset\mathcal U. (2) U_\psi is the subgroup of U_a(k) consisting of elements fixing \mathcal A_\psi pointwise; hence every x\in\mathcal A with \psi(x)\ge0 is fixed by U_\psi. (3) For each u\in U_a(k)^*, there is a real-valued affine function \psi_a^u on \mathcal A with derivative a such that \operatorname{Fix}_{\mathcal A}(u)=\mathcal A_{\psi_a^u}. (4) For u\in U_a(k)^* and s\in S(k), \psi_a^{sus^{-1}}=\omega(a(s))+\psi_a^u. (6) If a,2a\in\Phi and u\in U_{2a}(k)\subset U_a(k), then \psi_{2a}^u=2\psi_a^u and U_\psi\cap U_{2a}(k)\subset U_{2\psi}. In addition, U_\psi may fix every point of a half-apartment strictly larger than \mathcal A_\psi; for example, if U_\psi=U_{\psi+\epsilon} for some \epsilon>0, then U_\psi fixes \mathcal A_{\psi+\epsilon} pointwise.

statements.statement_plain: For facets F1 contained in the closure of F2 and an affine root psi with gradient a, the associated root-group filtrations satisfy U_{a,F1,0+} subseteq U_{a,F2,0+} subseteq U_{a,F2,0} subseteq U_{a,F1,0}, with at most one strict inclusion. If no affine root in Psi'_a has F1 on its wall, all inclusions are equalities. Otherwise that root is unique, the endpoint filtrations equal U_{psi+} and U_psi, and the unique strict inclusion is determined by whether psi is zero, positive, or negative on F2 as in the three cases.

statements.title: Rank-One Root-Group Filtration Quotients
statements.statement_plain: The lemma gives four rank-one root-group filtration cases. At jumps in J_{2a}, the U_{2a} graded quotient is noncanonically f_l^0 for an unramified extension l/k and f_l=f for a ramified extension. If r lies in one-half J_{2a} inside J_a but not in J_{a/2a}, inclusion of the depth-2r U_{2a} quotient into the depth-r U_a quotient is an isomorphism, making the latter one-dimensional over f. If r lies in J_{a/2a} but not in one-half J_{2a}, l/k is ramified and projection to the corresponding graded quotient of U_a/U_{2a} is an isomorphism, again giving a one-dimensional f-vector space. If r lies in the intersection J_{a/2a} and one-half J_{2a}, l/k is unramified; the depth-r U_a quotient is noncanonically isomorphic to the depth-zero quotient, and reduction identifies that quotient with U_{f_l/f}(tilde f).
statements.statement_latex: For the rank-one root subgroups U_a and U_{2a} over k with extension \ell/k, the four cases hold: (1) for r\in J_{2a}, U_{2a}(k)_r/U_{2a}(k)_{r+} is noncanonically isomorphic to \mathfrak f_{\ell}^{0} when \ell/k is unramified and to \mathfrak f_{\ell}=\mathfrak f when ramified; (2) for r\in\tfrac12J_{2a}\subset J_a\setminus J_{a/2a}, inclusion U_{2a}(k)_{2r}/U_{2a}(k)_{2r+}\to U_a(k)_r/U_a(k)_{r+} is an isomorphism, so the latter is one-dimensional over \mathfrak f; (3) for r\in J_{a/2a}\setminus(\tfrac12J_{2a}), \ell/k is ramified and projection U_a(k)_r/U_a(k)_{r+}\to [U_a(k)/U_{2a}(k)]_r/[U_a(k)/U_{2a}(k)]_{r+} is an isomorphism, so the U_a quotient is one-dimensional over \mathfrak f; (4) for r\in J_{a/2a}\cap\tfrac12J_{2a}, \ell/k is unramified, U_a(k)_r/U_a(k)_{r+} is noncanonically isomorphic to U_a(k)_0/U_a(k)_{0+}, and reduction identifies U_a(k)_0/U_a(k)_{0+} isomorphically with U_{\mathfrak f_{\ell}/\mathfrak f}(\widetilde{\mathfrak f}).
assumptions_latex: r\in J_{2a}
r\in\tfrac12J_{2a}\subset J_a and r\notin J_{a/2a}
r\in J_{a/2a} and r\notin\tfrac12J_{2a}\subset J_a
r\in J_{a/2a}\cap\tfrac12J_{2a}

statements.title: Existence of Epsilon-Thickenings of Bounded Subsets and Facets
statements.statement_plain: Let X be an arbitrary bounded subset of the apartment A, or a facet of A. Define Psi_X by the root-group filtration jump condition in the source, and let Xi be the affine automorphisms of A that preserve the root and affine-root systems and stabilize X. For every sufficiently small positive epsilon, there is an Xi-invariant concave function f satisfying (Sch), agreeing with f_X on Psi_X, lying strictly between f_X plus one-half epsilon and f_X plus epsilon on the remaining roots, and satisfying Phi_f = Phi_X. Such a function is called an epsilon-thickening of X.

statements.title: Alternative Coordinate Description of H(L,L_2)
statements.statement_plain: In the defining setup of H(L,L_2), let L^0 be the L_2-vector subspace of trace-zero elements of L and choose lambda in L with lambda plus its sigma-conjugate equal to 1. The map sending (u,v) to (u, v minus lambda times u^sigma u) is an isomorphism of algebraic K-groups from H(L,L_2) to H^lambda. The underlying K-scheme of H^lambda is the restriction of scalars from L_2 to K of the additive group L times L^0, with multiplication (x,y)(x',y')=(x+x', y+y'-lambda x x'^sigma+lambda^sigma x^sigma x').
statements.statement_latex:
Let L^0 be the L_2-vector subspace of trace-zero elements of L, and let \lambda\in L satisfy \lambda+\lambda^\sigma=1. Then
\[
j_\lambda:(u,v)\longmapsto (u,v-\lambda u^\sigma u)
\]
is an isomorphism from the algebraic K-group H(L,L_2) onto the algebraic K-group H^\lambda whose underlying K-scheme is
\[
\operatorname{Res}_{L_2/K}(\mathbf L\times\mathbf L^0)
\]
and whose multiplication is
\[
(x,y)(x',y')=\bigl(x+x',\,y+y'-\lambda x{x'}^\sigma+\lambda^\sigma x^\sigma x'\bigr).
\]
assumptions_latex: K,L_2,L,\sigma,\text{ and }H(L,L_2)\text{ are as in the defining setup of }H(L,L_2).
L^0\text{ is the }L_2\text{-vector subspace of trace-zero elements of }L.
\lambda\in L\quad\text{and}\quad\lambda+\lambda^\sigma=1.
statements.conclusion_latex: j_\lambda:H(L,L_2)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^\lambda\text{ is an isomorphism of algebraic }K\text{-groups}.

statements.title: Restriction-of-Scalars Description and Pinning of a Case-I Root Group
statements.statement_plain: In case I, after extension to tilde K, the relative root group is the direct product of the groups indexed by the roots in tilde Delta_a, and these factors are permuted transitively by Gal(tilde K/K). For any alpha in that orbit, U_a is K-isomorphic to the restriction of scalars from L_alpha to K of the corresponding tilde U_alpha. An L_alpha-pinning induces a K-isomorphism from the restriction of scalars of the additive group onto U_a; the pair (L_alpha, x_a) is called a pinning of U_a. For every K-algebra R, the source has R-points L_alpha tensor_K R, and on K-points x_a identifies the additive group of L_alpha with U_a(K).

statements.title: Transport and comparison of relative root-group pinnings
statements.statement_plain: Transporting the lifted root group by an automorphism transports its coefficient field and pinning by conjugation, while the induced pinning of U_a is precomposed with the map induced by the inverse field isomorphism. The automorphisms of the additive object over its coefficient field are precisely multiplication by nonzero scalars. Consequently, a pinning of U_a is given by a suitable coefficient subextension and an isomorphism from the associated Weil-restricted additive object to U_a, and two such pinnings differ by a uniquely determined coefficient-field isomorphism and scalar multiplication.

statements.title: Addition and Translation of Concave Functions
statements.statement_plain: The sum of two concave functions on the extended root system is concave. Adding evaluation at a vector v preserves concavity. If the apartment point x and concave function f are translated together by v, the associated root subgroups and the generated group G(k)^sharp do not change.
statements.statement_latex: If f_1,f_2:\widehat{\Phi}\to\widetilde{\mathbf R} are concave, then f_1+f_2 is concave. In particular, if f is concave and v\in V, define (f+v)(a)=f(a)+a(v); this function is concave. Moreover, for every x\in\mathcal A, U_{a,x+v,f+v}=U_{a,x,f}, and hence G(k)^{\sharp}_{x+v,f+v}=G(k)^{\sharp}_{x,f}.

statements.title: Concave Function and Subgroups Attached to a Subset of the Apartment
statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty subset Omega of the affine space A, define the concave function f_Omega on Phi by f_Omega(a) = inf{k in R : a(x)+k >= 0 for every x in Omega}. Define U_Omega as the subgroup generated by the root filtration subgroups U_{a,f_Omega(a)} for all a in Phi, and define P_Omega = H times U_Omega. Equivalently, U_Omega is generated by the subgroups U_alpha for affine roots alpha containing Omega.
statements.statement_latex: f_{\Omega}:\Phi\to\mathbf R,\qquad f_{\Omega}(a)=\inf\{k\in\mathbf R\mid a(x)+k\ge 0\ \text{for all }x\in\Omega\}.\quad U_{f_{\Omega}}=\left\langle U_{a,f_{\Omega}(a)}\mid a\in\Phi\right\rangle,\qquad P_{f_{\Omega}}=H\cdot U_{f_{\Omega}},\qquad U_{\Omega}:=U_{f_{\Omega}},\quad P_{\Omega}:=P_{f_{\Omega}}.
assumptions_latex: \Omega\subseteq A,\ \Omega\neq\varnothing
A is identified with its vector space V via a chosen origin \varphi; roots a\in\Phi are viewed as functions on A
statements.conclusion_latex: U_{\Omega}=\left\langle U_{\alpha}\mid \alpha\text{ is an affine root containing }\Omega\right\rangle,\qquad P_{\Omega}=H\cdot U_{\Omega}.
statements.scope_note: For a nonempty subset of the affine apartment A, with the stated origin-based identification A\cong V and roots regarded as affine-linear functions.

statements.title: Extended Quasi-Concave Functions and Associated Subgroups
statements.statement_plain: Given an extension phi_0 of phi and a function f on the roots together with 0, U_f is the subgroup of G generated by the filtration subgroups U_{a,f(a)}. At a right-limit level r+, U_{0,r+} is the union of U_{0,s} for s>r. The function f is quasi-concave relative to (phi, phi_0) exactly when its restriction to the roots is quasi-concave and the associated subgroup H is contained in U_{0,f(0)}. Concavity implies quasi-concavity, and quasi-concavity implies U_f intersect U_0 equals U_{0,f(0)}.
statements.statement_latex: Let \varphi_0 be an extension of \varphi. For any function f:\Phi\cup\{0\}\to\widetilde{\mathbf R}, define U_f to be the subgroup of G generated by U_{a,f(a)} for a\in\Phi\cup\{0\}. For k=r+ with r\in\mathbf R, define U_{0,k}=\bigcup_{s\in\mathbf R\cup\{\infty\},\ s>r}U_{0,s}. The function f is quasi-concave relative to (\varphi,\varphi_0) exactly when f|_\Phi is quasi-concave and H_{f|_\Phi}\subseteq U_{0,f(0)}. Every concave f is quasi-concave, and every quasi-concave f satisfies U_f\cap U_0=U_{0,f(0)}.
assumptions_latex: \varphi_0\text{ is an extension of }\varphi.
f:\Phi\cup\{0\}\to\widetilde{\mathbf R}.
\text{For }k=r+\text{ with }r\in\mathbf R,\ U_{0,k}:=\bigcup_{s\in\mathbf R\cup\{\infty\},\ s>r}U_{0,s}.
statements.conclusion_latex: U_f:=\left\langle U_{a,f(a)}:a\in\Phi\cup\{0\}\right\rangle.\quad f\text{ is quasi-concave relative to }(\varphi,\varphi_0)\iff f|_\Phi\text{ is quasi-concave and }H_{f|_\Phi}\subseteq U_{0,f(0)}.\quad f\text{ concave}\Longrightarrow f\text{ quasi-concave};\qquad f\text{ quasi-concave}\Longrightarrow U_f\cap U_0=U_{0,f(0)}.
statements.scope_note: Local notation is retained: U_f is generated from the root and zero filtration subgroups, and right-limit levels use the source's r+ convention.

x\in\mathcal{A}=\mathcal{A}(S)

statements.title: Subgroups Attached to a Concave Function
statements.statement_plain: For a concave function f and a point x in the apartment, define subgroups of G(k): each U_{a,x,f} as the product of the levels at a and 2a; G(k)_{x,f}^{sharp} as the subgroup generated by all U_{a,x,f}; P_{x,f}=G(k)_{x,f} as its product with Z(k)_{f(0)}; the subgroup generated by U_{a,x,f} and U_{-a,x,f}; and its intersections with N(k) and Z(k).
statements.statement_latex: Let f be a concave function and x\in\mathcal A. Define the following subgroups of G(k): for a\in\Phi, U_{a,x,f}=U_{a,x,f(a)}\cdot U_{2a,x,f(2a)}; G(k)_{x,f}^{\sharp}=\langle U_{a,x,f}:a\in\Phi\rangle; \mathcal P_{x,f}:=G(k)_{x,f}:=G(k)_{x,f}^{\sharp}\cdot Z(k)_{f(0)}; G(k)_{x,f}^{(a)}=\langle U_{\pm a,x,f}\rangle; and N_{x,f}^{(a)}=N(k)\cap G(k)_{x,f}^{(a)}, Z_{x,f}^{(a)}=Z(k)\cap G(k)_{x,f}^{(a)}.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is a concave function}
x\in\mathcal A
a\in\Phi\text{ (where applicable)}
statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}U_{a,x,f}&=U_{a,x,f(a)}\cdot U_{2a,x,f(2a)}\quad(a\in\Phi),\\ G(k)_{x,f}^{\sharp}&=\left\langle U_{a,x,f}:a\in\Phi\right\rangle,\\ \mathcal P_{x,f}=G(k)_{x,f}&=G(k)_{x,f}^{\sharp}\cdot Z(k)_{f(0)},\\ G(k)_{x,f}^{(a)}&=\left\langle U_{\pm a,x,f}\right\rangle,\\ N_{x,f}^{(a)}&=N(k)\cap G(k)_{x,f}^{(a)},\qquad Z_{x,f}^{(a)}=Z(k)\cap G(k)_{x,f}^{(a)}.\end{aligned}
statements.scope_note: Definitions of subgroups of G(k) associated with a concave function f at a point x of the apartment.

statements.title: Chamber Sharp Subgroup Equals the Concave-Function Subgroup
statements.statement_plain: Let F be a facet in the apartment A and C a chamber whose closure contains F. Choose the positive root system Phi+ extending the system associated with (F,C), and let f be its associated concave function. For every point x in F, the source-defined sharp subgroup attached to C equals the sharp subgroup attached to x and f.
statements.statement_latex: \text{Let }\mathcal F\subset\mathcal A\text{ be a facet and }\mathcal C\subset\mathcal A\text{ a chamber with }\mathcal F\subset\overline{\mathcal C}.\text{ Let }\Psi_{\mathcal F}(\mathcal C)^+\text{ be the positive root system from Proposition 1.3.35, choose }\Phi^+\supset\nabla\Psi_{\mathcal F}(\mathcal C)^+,\text{ and set }f=f_{\Phi^+}\text{ as in Example 7.3.7(2).\text{ Then for every }x\in\mathcal F,\ G(k)_{\mathcal C}^{\sharp}=G(k)_{x,f}^{\sharp}.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal F\subset\mathcal A\text{ is a facet}
\mathcal C\subset\mathcal A\text{ is a chamber with }\mathcal F\subset\overline{\mathcal C}
\Psi_{\mathcal F}(\mathcal C)^+\text{ is the positive system of roots specified by Proposition 1.3.35}
\Phi^+\text{ is a positive system of roots with }\nabla\Psi_{\mathcal F}(\mathcal C)^+\subset\Phi^+
f=f_{\Phi^+}\text{ is the concave function of Example 7.3.7(2)}
statements.conclusion_latex: \forall x\in\mathcal F,\quad G(k)_{\mathcal C}^{\sharp}=G(k)_{x,f}^{\sharp}.
statements.scope_note: Equality of the source-defined sharp subgroup attached to a chamber with the sharp subgroup attached to any point of the facet via the specified concave function; notation is local to the source.

statements.title: Concavity and commutator bound for an infimal convolution of root functions
statements.statement_plain: For two root functions with quasi-concave restrictions, define h_* by the source's infimal-convolution formula over nonempty finite root sequences. If h_*(o) is not minus infinity, then h_* is finite on every root and its restriction h to the roots is concave. If the stated inclusion between the H-subgroups holds, then for subgroups X and Y at the respective zero levels, the commutator of X.U_f and Y.U_g is contained in (X,Y).H_[h_*(0)].U_h.
statements.statement_latex: Let f_*,g_*:\Phi\cup\{0\}\to\widetilde{\mathbf R} have quasi-concave restrictions to \Phi. For a\in\Phi\cup\{0\}, define h_*(a)=\inf\left\{\sum_i f_*(a_i)+\sum_j g_*(b_j)\right\}, where the infimum ranges over pairs of nonempty finite sequences (a_i),(b_j) in \Phi\cup\{\circ\} satisfying a=\sum_i a_i+\sum_j b_j. If h_*(\mathrm{o})\ne-\infty, then h_*(a)\ne-\infty for every a\in\Phi and h=h_*|_\Phi is concave. If moreover \mathrm H_{[h_*(0)]}\subset\mathrm H_{(h_*(0))}, and \mathrm X\leq\mathrm H_{(f_*(0))}, \mathrm Y\leq\mathrm H_{(g_*(0))}, then \left(\mathrm X.\mathrm U_f,\mathrm Y.\mathrm U_g\right)\subset\left(\mathrm X,\mathrm Y\right).\mathrm H_{[h_*(0)]}.\mathrm U_h.
assumptions_latex: f_*,g_*:\Phi\cup\{0\}\to\widetilde{\mathbf R},\quad f_*|_\Phi\text{ and }g_*|_\Phi\text{ are quasi-concave}.
h_*(a)=\inf\left\{\sum_i f_*(a_i)+\sum_j g_*(b_j)\right\},\quad a=\sum_i a_i+\sum_j b_j,\quad a_i,b_j\in\Phi\cup\{\circ\},\text{ with both sequences finite and nonempty}.
h_*(\mathrm{o})\ne-\infty.
\mathrm H_{[h_*(0)]}\subset\mathrm H_{(h_*(0))}.
\mathrm X\leq\mathrm H_{(f_*(0))},\qquad \mathrm Y\leq\mathrm H_{(g_*(0))}.
statements.conclusion_latex: h_*(a)\ne-\infty\ \text{for every }a\in\Phi,\quad h=h_*|_\Phi\ \text{is concave},\quad \left(\mathrm X.\mathrm U_f,\mathrm Y.\mathrm U_g\right)\subset\left(\mathrm X,\mathrm Y\right).\mathrm H_{[h_*(0)]}.\mathrm U_h.
statements.scope_note: Uses the source's local notation for root functions, associated H- and U-subgroups, and commutators; the visibly distinct symbols 0, \mathrm{o}, and \circ are retained.

statements.title: Facet subgroup via the associated function
statements.statement_plain: If F = gamma(x,E) is a facet, then its subgroup U_F equals U_{f_F}. The function f_F maps each root a to -a(x) when a is positive or zero on E, and to -a(x)+ when a is strictly negative on E.

\[
f_F(a)=
\begin{cases}
-a(x),&\text{if the root }a\text{ is positive or zero on }E,\\
-a(x)+,&\text{if the root }a\text{ is strictly negative on }E.
\end{cases}
\]
assumptions_latex: F=\gamma(x,E)\text{ is a facet}
statements.conclusion_latex: U_F=U_{f_F}

If for every \(p,q\in\mathbf{N}^{*}\) and \(a,b\in\Phi\cup\{\mathrm{o}\}\) with \(pa+qb\in\Phi\cup\{\mathrm{o}\}\) one has \(f(pa+qb)\le p f(a)+q g(b)\), then \(\mathrm{U}_f\) is normalized by \(\mathrm{U}_g\).

statements.title: Subgroup properties associated with a concave function
statements.statement_plain: For a concave function f and a point x of the apartment, commutators of filtered subgroups for non-proportional roots lie in the subgroups for positive integral root combinations. Products over closed positive root subsets form order-independent subgroups. The associated rank-one subgroup factors through the negative-root, positive-root, and normalizer terms; under the stated strict positivity conditions, including the additional doubled-root condition for a multipliable root, the normalizer term equals the centralizer term.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be a concave function and let \(x\in\mathcal A\). Then: (1) if \(a,b\in\Phi\) are non-proportional, \((U_{a,x,f},U_{b,x,f})\) is contained in the subgroup generated by all \(U_{pa+qb,x,f}\) with \(p,q\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\) and \(pa+qb\in\Phi\); (2) if \(\Phi^+\) is a positive system and \(\Phi^{\prime +}\subseteq\Phi^+\) is closed, then \(\prod_{a\in\Phi^{\prime +}}U_{a,x,f}\), taken in any order, is a subgroup of \(G(k)\) independent of the order; (3) \(G(k)_{x,f}^{(a)}=U_{-a,x,f}\,U_{a,x,f}\,N_{x,f}^{(a)}\); and (4) if \(f(a)+f(-a)>0\), and also \(f(2a)+f(-2a)>0\) when \(a\) is multipliable, then \(N_{x,f}^{(a)}=Z_{x,f}^{(a)}\).
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is a concave function and }x\in\mathcal A.
a\in\Phi\text{ for the rank-one assertions (3) and (4).
\text{For (1), }a,b\in\Phi\text{ are non-proportional.}
\text{For (2), }\Phi^+\text{ is a positive system and }\Phi^{\prime +}\subseteq\Phi^+\text{ is closed.}
\text{For (4), }f(a)+f(-a)>0\text{ and, if }a\text{ is multipliable, }f(2a)+f(-2a)>0.
statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}(1)\quad &(U_{a,x,f},U_{b,x,f})\subseteq\left\langle U_{pa+qb,x,f}:p,q\in\mathbb Z_{>0},\ pa+qb\in\Phi\right\rangle;\\(2)\quad &\prod_{a\in\Phi^{\prime +}}U_{a,x,f}\text{, in any order, is an order-independent subgroup of }G(k);\\(3)\quad &G(k)_{x,f}^{(a)}=U_{-a,x,f}\,U_{a,x,f}\,N_{x,f}^{(a)};\\(4)\quad &N_{x,f}^{(a)}=Z_{x,f}^{(a)}\text{ under the stated positivity assumptions.}\end{aligned}

statements.title: Commutator Containment for Positive Root-Group Subgroups
statements.statement_plain: Let L be a half-line in V* with origin o, contained in D0. For each apartment point x, define U_x^+ as the subgroup generated by the positive root groups U_{a,-a minus phi}. There is a constant k in (0,1] such that when x minus y lies in L, the commutator subgroup of U_x^+ and U_y^+ is contained in U_{x plus k times (y minus x)}^+. For v in L, k is the ratio of the infimum to supremum of a(v) over positive roots. In type BC1, k equals 1/2; in type A1, the commutator is trivial.
statements.statement_latex: Let L be a half-line with origin o in V^*, contained in D_0. For x\in A, let U_x^+ be generated by U_{a,-a(x-\varphi)} for a\in\Phi^+. There exists k\in(0,1] such that, for x,y\in A with x-y\in L, (U_x^+,U_y^+)\subset U_{x+k(y-x)}^+. For v\in L, k=\frac{\inf_{a\in\Phi^+}a(v)}{\sup_{a\in\Phi^+}a(v)}; in rank-one type BC_1, k=1/2, while in type A_1 the commutator is {I} for all x,y\in A.

statements.statement_plain: For quasi-concave root functions f and g satisfying the stated weighted inequality, and any subgroup X of H, U_g normalizes the product X times U_f exactly when the commutator of X with each root subgroup U_{g,a} is contained in U_{f,a}, and H_{f,g} is contained in X times U_f.

statements.title: Ordered root-group factorization for quasi-concave filtration subgroups
statements.statement_plain: Let g be concave on the roots together with the distinguished value o, with g(o)>o; let f be quasi-concave and majorize g on the roots; and let X be a subgroup of H containing H_g. For any ordering of the reduced roots and any insertion position j, multiplication of the corresponding filtered root-group elements with X inserted at position j defines a map onto X U_f. This map is injective, and it is bijective when every root group is complete for its filtration topology. In rank one, bijectivity does not require completeness.
statements.statement_latex: Let g:\Phi\cup\{\mathrm{o}\}\to\widetilde{\mathbf R} be concave with g(\mathrm{o})>\mathrm{o}, let f:\Phi\to\widetilde{\mathbf R} be quasi-concave and majorize g|_{\Phi}, and let \mathrm X\leq\mathrm H contain \mathrm H_g. For any ordering (a_1,\ldots,a_m) of \Phi^{\mathrm{rd}} and any 0\leq j\leq m, define \tau_j:\mathrm X\times\prod_{i=1}^m\mathrm U_{f,a_i}\to\mathrm X\cdot\mathrm U_f by (x,u_1,\ldots,u_m)\mapsto u_1\cdots u_jx u_{j+1}\cdots u_m. Then \tau_j is injective. If every \mathrm U_a (a\in\Phi) is complete for the topology whose neighborhood basis at 1 is \{\mathrm U_{a,k}:k\in\mathbf R\}, then \tau_j is bijective. When \Phi has rank one, this completeness hypothesis is unnecessary.

f:\Phi\to\widetilde{\mathbf R} is quasi-concave and majorizes g|_{\Phi}.
\mathrm H_g\subseteq\mathrm X\leq\mathrm H.
(a_1,\ldots,a_m) is an arbitrary ordering of \Phi^{\mathrm{rd}}, and 0\leq j\leq m.
For every a\in\Phi, \mathrm U_a is complete for the topology with neighborhood basis \{\mathrm U_{a,k}:k\in\mathbf R\}; this assumption is required only for the general bijectivity assertion.
statements.conclusion_latex: \tau_j is injective; under the stated completeness hypothesis it is bijective. If \Phi has rank one, bijectivity holds without the completeness hypothesis.
statements.scope_note: Factorization of \mathrm X\cdot\mathrm U_f into \mathrm X and filtered root groups attached to an arbitrary ordering of the reduced roots, with injectivity always and bijectivity under completeness (unconditional in rank one).

statements.title: Nilpotence and Order-Independent Product Decomposition of Positive Root Subgroups
statements.statement_plain: The positive unipotent group U+ is nilpotent. For a subset Psi of the positive roots, let Psi_red consist of roots a in Psi with a/2 not in Psi. Choose subgroups Y_a of U_a, define X_a as Y_a or Y_a Y_{2a} according as 2a is absent from or present in Psi, and let X be generated by the Y_a. If every commutator [Y_a,Y_b] lies in the subgroup generated by Y_{ma+nb} for positive integers m,n with ma+nb in Psi, then multiplication from the product of the X_a over Psi_red to X is bijective for any ordering of the factors.

If [Y_a,Y_b] is contained in the subgroup generated by all Y_{ma+nb} with m,n\in\mathbf N^{*} and ma+nb\in\Psi for every a,b\in\Psi, then \prod_{a\in\Psi^{\mathrm{red}}}X_a\to X is bijective independently of factor ordering.

statements.title: Affine structure and equivariance axioms for the canonical apartment
statements.statement_plain: For a maximal k-split torus S, the cocharacter space splits canonically into the derived-torus part V(S') and the central split part V(A_G). The corresponding apartment is an affine space under V(S'). The normalizer acts affinely with Weyl-group linear part, the centralizer acts by valuation-defined translations, and its maximal bounded subgroup and the center Z_G(k) act trivially. The stated root-valuation identity holds, and conjugation by G(k) gives affine maps between corresponding apartments with the natural linear maps. These axioms uniquely determine the affine structure.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a maximal \(k\)-split torus of \(G\), let \(S'\) be the unique maximal subtorus of \(S\) contained in \(G_{\mathrm{der}}\), and let \(A_G\) be the maximal \(k\)-split torus in the center \(Z_G\) of \(G\). For \(V(T)=\mathbf R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}X_*(T)\), the composite \(S'\to S\to S/A_G\) is an isogeny and yields the canonical decomposition \(V(S)=V(S')\oplus V(A_G)\). Writing \(V'=V(S')\), \(Z=Z_G(S)\), and \(N=N_G(S)\), the apartment \(\mathcal A(S)\) is an affine space under \(V'\). The action of \(N(k)\) on \(\mathcal A(S)\) is affine, with derivative given by its Weyl-group action on \(V'\); \(Z(k)\) acts by translations, where the translation for \(z\) is the image of \(-\omega_Z(z)\) under \(V(S)\to V'\), and \(Z(k)_b\) and \(Z_G(k)\) act trivially. In addition, \(a(v(s))=-\omega(a(s))\) for every \(a\in\Phi(S)\) and \(s\in S(k)\). For every \(g\in G(k)\), conjugation induces an affine isomorphism \(\mathcal A(S)\to\mathcal A(gSg^{-1})\) whose derivative is the natural map \(V(S')\to V(gS'g^{-1})\). These conditions uniquely determine the affine structure on the apartment.
assumptions_latex: S\text{ is a maximal }k\text{-split torus of }G.
S'\text{ is the unique maximal subtorus of }S\text{ contained in }G_{\mathrm{der}},\quad A_G\text{ is the maximal }k\text{-split torus in }Z_G.
V(T)=\mathbf R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}X_*(T),\quad V'=V(S'),\quad Z=Z_G(S),\quad N=N_G(S).
\mathcal A(S)\text{ is the apartment of }\mathcal B(G)\text{ corresponding to }S,\text{ and }\omega_Z\text{ is the valuation homomorphism on }Z(k).
statements.conclusion_latex: V(S)=V(S')\oplus V(A_G);\quad \mathcal A(S)\text{ is an affine space under }V';\quad N(k)\text{ acts on }\mathcal A(S)\text{ by affine transformations with derivative on }V'\text{ given by the Weyl-group action};\quad z\in Z(k)\text{ acts by translation by }v(z),\text{ the image of }-\omega_Z(z)\text{ under }V(S)\to V(S');\quad Z(k)_b\text{ and }Z_G(k)\text{ act trivially};\quad a(v(s))=-\omega(a(s))\text{ for all }a\in\Phi(S),\ s\in S(k);\quad g:\mathcal A(S)\to\mathcal A(gSg^{-1})\text{ is affine with derivative }g:V(S')\to V(gS'g^{-1})\text{ for every }g\in G(k).

statements.title: Compatible Valued-Root-Datum Apartments for Maximal Split Tori
statements.statement_plain: Let G be a connected reductive group over k. For every maximal k-split torus S, with normalizer N, centralizer Z, and S' the maximal torus in S intersected with the derived group, assume there is an affine space A(S) under V(S') satisfying Axiom 4.1.4. The normalizer N(k) acts as prescribed, and each element g of G(k) gives a compatible affine isomorphism from A(S) to A(gSg^{-1}). Also assume A(S) is an equipollence class of valuations of the root datum of (G,S), with the specified normalizer action.
statements.statement_latex: Let G be a connected reductive k-group. For each maximal k-split torus S\subset G, let N=N_G(S), Z=Z_G(S), and let S' be the maximal torus in S\cap G_{\mathrm{der}}. Assume that an affine space \mathcal A(S) under V(S') is assigned, satisfying Axiom 4.1.4. The normalizer N(k) acts on \mathcal A(S) as prescribed, and every g\in G(k) induces an affine isomorphism g:\mathcal A(S)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal A(gSg^{-1}), with the isomorphisms compatible with multiplication and with the prescribed N(k)-action. statements.title: Uniqueness and Equivalent Models of the Affine Apartment
statements.statement_plain: For an affine space satisfying Axiom 4.1.4(A1), the affine space, the splittings of extension (4.4.1), and the maximal compact (equivalently maximal finite) subgroups of the Lie group \widetilde W_R are uniquely and N(k)-equivariantly isomorphic as affine spaces under V', with identity on V'. A point x corresponds to its stabilizer \widetilde W_x, whose projection to W gives a splitting. Therefore any two such affine spaces have a unique N(k)-equivariant isomorphism inducing the identity on V' .

Under this correspondence, x\in\mathcal{A} maps to its stabilizer \widetilde{W}_x, whose projection to W splits (4.4.1). In particular, any two affine spaces satisfying Axiom 4.1.4(A1) admit a unique N(k)-equivariant isomorphism inducing the identity on V'.

For x\in\mathcal{A}, the corresponding subgroup is its stabilizer \widetilde{W}_x, and the restriction \widetilde{W}_x\to W of the natural projection splits (4.4.1). statements.title: Conjugacy and Weyl Torsor of Maximal Split-Torus Cocharacter Spaces
statements.statement_plain: For maximal k-split tori S1 and S2 in a connected reductive k-group G, an element of G(k) conjugates S1 to S2. The conjugation induces an isomorphism between the real cocharacter spaces of maximal tori in their intersections with the derived group, and all such induced isomorphisms form a torsor under the Weyl group.
statements.statement_latex: Let G be a connected reductive k-group. For maximal k-split tori S_1,S_2\subset G, let S_i' be a maximal torus in S_i\cap G_{\mathrm{der}} and put V_i=\mathbf{R}\otimes_{\mathbf{Z}}X_*(S_i'). Then some g\in G(k) satisfies \operatorname{Int}(g)(S_1)=S_2 and induces a real-linear isomorphism V_1\xrightarrow{\sim}V_2; the collection of all such induced isomorphisms is a torsor for the Weyl group W_G(S)(k).
assumptions_latex: k is a Henselian discretely valued field with perfect residue field.
G is a connected reductive k-group.
S_1,S_2\subset G are maximal k-split tori.
For i=1,2, let S_i' be a maximal torus in S_i\cap G_{\mathrm{der}}, and set V_i=\mathbf{R}\otimes_{\mathbf{Z}}X_*(S_i').
statements.conclusion_latex: There exists g\in G(k) such that \operatorname{Int}(g)(S_1)=S_2, and g induces an isomorphism V_1\xrightarrow{\sim}V_2 of real vector spaces. The set of all such induced isomorphisms is a torsor for the Weyl group W_G(S)(k).

statements.title: Canonical field attached to a radical ray
statements.statement_plain: For a radical ray a, the relative root group U_a is canonically a K-vector space and every pinning identifies the relevant restriction-of-scalars space with it. The multiplication operators coming from a pinning are pinning-independent and form a field L_a isomorphic to the coefficient field L, containing the K-scalars; its nonzero elements are exactly the automorphisms induced by K-rational elements of the neutral-component normalizer. Each alpha in \widetilde{\Delta}_a gives one K-embedding of L_a into \widetilde K, and all such embeddings occur exactly once. The map induced by m_a canonically and independently of pinning identifies L_a with L_{-a}.
statements.statement_latex: Let a be a radical ray with relative root group U_a. Then: (1) U_a has a canonical K-vector-space structure, and every pinning (L,x) identifies \Pi_{L/K}\mathfrak D with U_a as K-vector spaces. (2) The operators \mu_x(t):x(u)\mapsto x(tu), for t\in L, are independent of the pinning; they form a field L_a\cong L containing the K-homotheties of U_a. (3) The nonzero elements of L_a are exactly the automorphisms of U_a induced by K-rational elements of the neutral component of the normalizer of U_a in the adjoint group of G. (4) For each \alpha\in\widetilde{\Delta}_a, \mu_{x_a} depends only on \alpha, its inverse is a K-embedding L_a\hookrightarrow\widetilde K, and these embeddings exhaust all K-embeddings of L_a into \widetilde K exactly once. (5) The map x_a(u)\mapsto x_{-a}(u)=m_a x_a(u)m_a^{-1} induces a canonical, pinning-independent field isomorphism L_a\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{-a}.
assumptions_latex: a is a radical ray with corresponding relative root group U_a in the preceding Bruhat–Tits setup.
(L,x) is a pinning of U_a; \widetilde{\Delta}_a and \widetilde K are as defined in that setup.
The normalizer statement concerns K-rational elements of the neutral component of the normalizer of U_a in the adjoint group of G.
statements.conclusion_latex: The five stated properties hold: canonical K-vector-space and pinning identifications for U_a; a pinning-independent field L_a\cong L containing K-homotheties; characterization of L_a^\times by the indicated normalizer automorphisms; a bijection between \widetilde{\Delta}_a and K-embeddings L_a\hookrightarrow\widetilde K; and a pinning-independent canonical field isomorphism L_a\cong L_{-a} induced by x_a(u)\mapsto x_{-a}(u)=m_a x_a(u)m_a^{-1}.
statements.scope_note: In the setup preceding Proposition 3.10.16, for a radical ray a and its relative root group U_a, with pinnings, \widetilde{\Delta}_a, and splitting field \widetilde K as defined there.

statements.title: Normalizer action on valuation functions and associated stabilizers
statements.statement_plain: The normalizer N acts on valuation functions by transporting the root argument through its vectorial action and subtracting the displacement of the base valuation phi. Compatible affine automorphisms act by the analogous formula. H acts trivially, inducing an action of W=N/H. The stabilizer N_f^dagger in N intersect G^1 gives W_f^dagger=N_f^dagger/H^1; this subgroup has no nontrivial translations and identifies with a subgroup of the vector Weyl group, while N_f^0 is contained in N_f^dagger and W_f is distinguished in W_f^dagger.
statements.statement_latex: For \(n\in N=N(K)\) and \(a\in\Phi\), define \((n\!\cdot\! g)(a)=g\!\left({}^{t}\!\left({}^{v}v(n)\right)\!\cdot a\right)-a\!\left(v(n)\!\cdot\!\varphi-\varphi\right)\). More generally, for an affine automorphism \(u\) of \(A\) such that \({}^{t}({}^{v}u)\) preserves \(\Phi\), define \((u\!\cdot\! g)(a)=g\!\left({}^{t}({}^{v}u)\!\cdot a\right)-a\!\left(u\!\cdot\!\varphi-\varphi\right)\). The subgroup \(H\) acts trivially on \(F\), so \(W=N/H\) acts on \(F\). For \(f\in F\), set \(N_f^{\dagger}=\{n\in N\cap G^{1}\mid n\!\cdot f=f\}\) and \(W_f^{\dagger}=\nu(N_f^{\dagger})=N_f^{\dagger}/H^{1}\). Then \(W_f^{\dagger}\) has no nontrivial translation and is identified via \(w\mapsto{}^{v}w\) with a subgroup of the vector Weyl group \({}^{v}W\); moreover \(N_f^{0}\subseteq N_f^{\dagger}\), and \(W_f\) is a distinguished subgroup of \(W_f^{\dagger}\).
assumptions_latex: F=\{g:\Phi\to\mathbf R\} with fixed valuation \(\varphi\)
n\in N=N(K), a\in\Phi
u\in\operatorname{Aut}(A) with \({}^{t}({}^{v}u)(\Phi)=\Phi\)
H\subseteq N and the quotient W=N/H is as in the extract
f\in F and G^{1}\subseteq G
statements.conclusion_latex: N_f^{\dagger}=\{n\in N\cap G^{1}\mid n\cdot f=f\},\quad W_f^{\dagger}=\nu(N_f^{\dagger})=N_f^{\dagger}/H^{1}\hookrightarrow{}^{v}W,\quad N_f^{0}\subseteq N_f^{\dagger},\quad W_f\text{ distinguished in }W_f^{\dagger}.
statements.scope_note: Let F be the set of functions \(g:\Phi\to\mathbf R\) attached to a fixed valuation \(\varphi\); the normalizer action and stabilizer quotients are defined as in the extract.

statements.title: Affine roots and walls in the apartment of equipollent valuations
statements.statement_plain: The valuations equipollent to phi form an affine Euclidean space A under V. The closed half-space alpha_{a,k} consists of points x satisfying a(x minus phi) plus k at least zero, and its boundary is a wall when alpha is an affine root. For reduced roots, U_alpha is U_{a,k} and U_alpha+ is the union of U_{a,h} for h greater than k. Affine roots use a in Phi and k in Gamma'_a. The affine-root set, the associated pair set E, and the map to U_alpha are unchanged when the chosen equipollent valuation phi is replaced by another one.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be the set of valuations equipollent to \(\varphi\), an affine space under \(V\) with the Euclidean metric from the given scalar product. For \(a\in V^*\) and \(k\in\mathbf R\), let \(\alpha_{a,k}=\{x\in A\mid a(x-\varphi)+k\ge 0\}\), and write \(\partial\alpha\) for the boundary of a closed half-space. For \(\alpha=\alpha_{a,k}\) with \(a\in\Phi^{\mathrm{red}}\), set \(\mathbf U_\alpha=\mathbf U_{a,k}\) and \(\mathbf U_{\alpha+}=\bigcup_{h>k}\mathbf U_{a,h}\). Affine roots are the \(\alpha_{a,k}\) with \(a\in\Phi\) and \(k\in\Gamma'_a\), and walls are their boundaries. Denoting the affine-root set by \(\sum\), define \(\mathcal E=\{(\alpha,a)\in\sum\times\Phi:\alpha=\alpha_{a,k},\ k\in\Gamma'_a\}\). The sets \(\sum\), \(\mathcal E\), and the map \(\alpha\mapsto\mathbf U_\alpha\) are invariant under replacing \(\varphi\) by an equipollent valuation.

statements.title: Facets and chambers of the apartment A
statements.statement_plain: Let E be either the origin {o} or an open half-line from o in V. The germ gamma(x,E) is a facet of A exactly when, for every root a in Phi_x, the convex cone E lies in the hyperplane a(v)=0 or does not meet it. Every vector facet of Phi has this property. statements.conclusion_latex: The germ \(\gamma(x,E)\) is a facet of \(A\) if and only if, for every \(a\in\Phi_x\), \(E\) is contained in \(\{v\in V\mid a(v)=0\}\) or does not intersect that hyperplane. statements.title: Positive and Simple Affine Roots Relative to a Chamber
statements.statement_plain: Relative to a fixed chamber, an affine root is positive or negative according as it takes positive or negative values on that chamber, and a positive affine root is simple when it is not a sum of two positive affine roots. The simple affine roots form a basis of the affine root system; their nonnegative half-spaces cut out the chamber closure; and the derivatives of any all-but-one of them form a basis of the rational span of the k-root system.
statements.statement_latex: For \(\psi\in\Psi\), call \(\psi\) positive (respectively negative) when it takes positive (respectively negative) values on \(\mathcal C\). A positive affine root is simple if it is not the sum of two positive affine roots. If \(\Delta\) is the set of simple affine roots, then \(\Delta\) is a basis of the affine root system \(\Psi\), \(\overline{\mathcal C}=\{x\in\mathcal A\mid \psi(x)\ge 0\text{ for all }\psi\in\Delta\}\), and the derivatives of any \(|\Delta|-1\) members of \(\Delta\) form a basis of the \mathbf Q\text{-linear span of the }k\text{-root system }\Phi(S,G).
assumptions_latex: S\text{ is a fixed maximal }k\text{-split torus of }G.
\Psi\text{ is the set of affine roots of }G\text{ with respect to }S.
\ell\in\mathbf{Q}_{>0}\text{ is the least positive rational number such that }\psi+\ell\in\Psi\text{ for every }\psi\in\Psi.
\mathcal C\subset\mathcal A\text{ is a fixed chamber.}
statements.conclusion_latex: \Delta\text{ is a basis of }\Psi,\qquad \overline{\mathcal C}=\{x\in\mathcal A\mid \psi(x)\ge 0\text{ for every }\psi\in\Delta\},\qquad \{d\psi:\psi\in\Delta'\}\text{ is a basis of the }\mathbf Q\text{-linear span of }\Phi(S,G)\text{ for every }\Delta'\subset\Delta\text{ with }|\Delta'|=|\Delta|-1.

statements.title: Affine Root Systems Associated with a Quasi-split Group
statements.statement_plain: The sets Psi-prime and Psi are affine root systems with derivative root system Phi. Psi is reduced except when Phi has a BC_n component that splits over an unramified extension. For absolutely almost simple G, Psi is the standard system attached to Phi in the unramified non-2A_{2n} case, has type (BC_n,C_n) in the unramified 2A_{2n} case, is the dual of the standard system attached to the dual root system in the ramified non-2A_{2n} case, and is the standard system attached to Phi in the ramified 2A_{2n} case. Moreover, Psi-prime equals Psi unless Phi is non-reduced; in that case it has type (C_n dual, BC_n) for ramified 2A_{2n} and (C_n dual, C_n) for unramified 2A_{2n}.
statements.statement_latex:
The sets \(\Psi'\) and \(\Psi\) are affine root systems with derivative root system \(\Phi\). The system \(\Psi\) is reduced unless \(\Phi\) has a component of type \(BC_n\) that splits over an unramified extension. If \(G\) is absolutely almost simple, then
\[
\Psi=\begin{cases}
\Psi_\Phi,&G\text{ unramified and not of type }{}^2A_{2n},\\
(BC_n,C_n),&G\text{ unramified of type }{}^2A_{2n},\\
(\Psi_{\Phi^\vee})^\vee,&G\text{ ramified and not of type }{}^2A_{2n},\\
\Psi_\Phi,&G\text{ ramified of type }{}^2A_{2n}.
\end{cases}
\]
Moreover, \(\Psi'=\Psi\) unless \(\Phi\) is non-reduced. If \(\Phi\) is non-reduced and \(G\) is absolutely almost simple, then \(\Psi'\) has type \((C_n^\vee,BC_n)\) when \(G\) is ramified of type \({}^2A_{2n}\), and type \((C_n^\vee,C_n)\) when \(G\) is unramified of type \({}^2A_{2n}\).
assumptions_latex: G\text{ is in the established quasi-split valued-root-datum and apartment setting, with derivative root system }\Phi\text{ and associated sets }\Psi',\Psi.
G\text{ is absolutely almost simple for the stated case-by-case classifications of }\Psi\text{ and for the non-reduced-case classification of }\Psi'.
statements.conclusion_latex: \Psi'\text{ and }\Psi\text{ are affine root systems with derivative root system }\Phi;\quad \Psi\text{ is reduced unless }\Phi\text{ has a component of type }BC_n\text{ that splits over an unramified extension. If }G\text{ is absolutely almost simple, then }\Psi=\Psi_\Phi\text{ when }G\text{ is unramified and not of type }{}^2A_{2n},\;\Psi\text{ has type }(BC_n,C_n)\text{ when }G\text{ is unramified of type }{}^2A_{2n},\;\Psi=(\Psi_{\Phi^\vee})^\vee\text{ when }G\text{ is ramified and not of type }{}^2A_{2n},\text{ and }\Psi=\Psi_\Phi\text{ when }G\text{ is ramified of type }{}^2A_{2n}.\text{ Moreover, }\Psi'=\Psi\text{ unless }\Phi\text{ is non-reduced; in that case, for absolutely almost simple }G,\;\Psi'\text{ has type }(C_n^\vee,BC_n)\text{ in the ramified }{}^2A_{2n}\text{ case and type }(C_n^\vee,C_n)\text{ in the unramified }{}^2A_{2n}\text{ case}.

statements.statement_plain: Each affine-root hyperplane is a union of whole facets: if it meets a facet, it contains that facet. Every codimension-one facet of the apartment lies in an affine-root hyperplane, and the connected components of the complement of all affine-root hyperplanes are exactly the apartment's chambers.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A\) be an apartment with affine-root set \(\Psi\). (1) For every \(\psi\in\Psi\) and every \(z\in\mathcal H_\psi\), the facet \(\mathcal F_z\) of \(\mathcal A\) containing \(z\) satisfies \(\mathcal F_z\subseteq\mathcal H_\psi\). Consequently, \(\mathcal H_\psi\) is a union of facets, and any facet intersecting \(\mathcal H_\psi\) is contained in it. (2) Every codimension-one facet \(\mathcal F\) of \(\mathcal A\) is contained in some \(\mathcal H_\psi\) with \(\psi\in\Psi\). (3) The connected components of \(\mathcal A\setminus\bigcup_{\psi\in\Psi}\mathcal H_\psi\) are precisely the chambers contained in \(\mathcal A\).
assumptions_latex: \mathcal A\text{ is an apartment with affine-root set }\Psi.
\psi\in\\Psi\text{ is an affine root and }\mathcal H_\psi\text{ is its associated hyperplane.}
statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}(1)\;&z\in\mathcal H_\psi\implies \mathcal F_z\subseteq\mathcal H_\psi;\text{ hence }\mathcal H_\psi\text{ is a union of facets and any facet it intersects is contained in it}.\\(2)\;&\operatorname{codim}_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal F)=1\implies \exists\psi\in\Psi\text{ such that }\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal H_\psi.\\(3)\;&\pi_0\!\left(\mathcal A\setminus\bigcup_{\psi\in\Psi}\mathcal H_\psi\right)\text{ consists precisely of the chambers contained in }\mathcal A.\end{aligned}
statements.scope_note: Facet and chamber geometry of the apartment relative to its affine-root hyperplanes.
