statements.title: Characterization of affine root systems
statements.statement_plain: A subset Psi of A* is an affine root system exactly when its gradient Phi = nabla Psi is a finite root system, every associated affine endomorphism fixing its root hyperplane and having the corresponding gradient reflection as derivative preserves Psi, and for each gradient root a the affine roots with gradient a contain at least two elements and have no accumulation point in A*.
statements.statement_latex: For a subset \(\Psi\subset A^{*}\), \(\Psi\) is an affine root system if and only if: (1) \(\Phi=\nabla\Psi\subset V^{*}\) is a finite root system; (2) for every \(\psi\in\Psi\), the affine endomorphism \(r_{\psi}\) of \(A\) fixing \(H_{\psi}\) and having derivative \(r_{\dot\psi}\) preserves \(\Psi\); and (3) for every \(a\in\Phi\), the set \(\{\psi\in\Psi\mid\dot\psi=a\}\) contains at least two elements and has no accumulation point in \(A^{*}\).
assumptions_latex: \Psi\subset A^{*}
statements.conclusion_latex: \Psi\text{ is an affine root system}\Longleftrightarrow\left[\Phi=\nabla\Psi\subset V^{*}\text{ is a finite root system};\ \forall\psi\in\Psi,\ r_{\psi}\text{ fixes }H_{\psi}\text{, has derivative }r_{\dot\psi}\text{, and preserves }\Psi;\ \forall a\in\Phi,\ \{\psi\in\Psi\mid\dot\psi=a\}\text{ has at least two elements and no accumulation point in }A^{*}\right].
statements.scope_note: Characterizes affine root systems in an affine space by finiteness of the gradient root system, invariance under the associated affine reflections, and discrete non-singleton fibers over each gradient root.

statements.title: Local vector facets and chamber characterization
statements.statement_plain: Fix a point x in the apartment. Cones whose canonical projections lie in the same local vector facet determine the same facet filter. The inverse image of that vector facet is the largest cone of corresponding directions, and these local vector facets are in bijection with the facet filters based at x. This inverse image is the direction of the facet at x, its span dimension is the facet dimension and is independent of x, and the indicated interior convex subsets form a basis of the filter. A facet is a chamber exactly when it has full dimension.
statements.statement_latex: Fix x\in A. If the canonical projections of cones E and E' lie in the same vector facet of \Phi_x, let E''\subseteq V be the inverse image of that vector facet. Then E'' is the largest convex cone of directions corresponding to the common facet filter, and E''\mapsto F_{x,E''} is a bijection from the vector facets of \Phi_x in V onto the facets of the form F_{x,E}. The cone E'' is the direction of F_{x,E''} at x, and \dim F_{x,E''}=\dim\operatorname{span}(E''), independently of x. The convex subsets X\subseteq x+E'' belonging to F_{x,E''} and having all their points interior form a basis of that filter. A facet F is a chamber if and only if \dim F=\dim V.
assumptions_latex: x\in A.
E\text{ and }E'\text{ are cones used to define }F_{x,E}\text{ and }F_{x,E'},\text{ and their canonical projections lie in the same vector facet of }\Phi_x.
E''\subseteq V\text{ is the inverse image of that vector facet.}
statements.conclusion_latex: E''\text{ is the largest convex cone of directions corresponding to the common facet filter, and }E''\longmapsto F_{x,E''}\text{ is a bijection from the vector facets of }\Phi_x\text{ in }V\text{ onto the facets of the form }F_{x,E}.\text{ Moreover, }E''\text{ is the direction of }F_{x,E''}\text{ at }x,\quad \dim F_{x,E''}=\dim\operatorname{span}(E''),\text{ this dimension is independent of }x,\text{ and }\{X\in F_{x,E''}:X\subseteq x+E'',\ X\text{ is convex and all its points are interior}\}\text{ is a basis of }F_{x,E''}.\text{ Finally, }F\text{ is a chamber}\iff\dim F=\dim V.
statements.scope_note: Facet filters and their directions in the apartment determined by a valued root datum.

statements.title: Germ of a Filter Base and Intersection with a Subset
statements.statement_plain: For a filter base F on a set X, its germ gamma is the filter generated by F. For Y contained in X, gamma is contained in Y when some member of gamma, equivalently of F, lies inside Y. If a member of gamma is disjoint from Y, define gamma intersect Y as empty; otherwise intersect each member of gamma with Y to obtain a filter base on X, and take its generated germ, which is contained in Y.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a set and let \(\mathcal F\) be a filter base on \(X\). The germ \(\gamma\) of \(\mathcal F\) is the filter generated by \(\mathcal F\). For a subset \(Y\subseteq X\), say that \(\gamma\) is contained in \(Y\) if some member of \(\gamma\) (equivalently, some member of \(\mathcal F\)) is contained in \(Y\). If there is a member \(Z\in\gamma\) disjoint from \(Y\), set \(\gamma\cap Y=\varnothing\). Otherwise, the intersections \(Z\cap Y\) for \(Z\in\gamma\) form a filter base on \(X\); denote its generated germ by \(\gamma\cap Y\), which is contained in \(Y\).
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a set.
\(\mathcal F\) is a filter base on \(X\).
\(Y\subseteq X\).
\(\gamma\) is the germ (the filter generated) by \(\mathcal F\).
statements.conclusion_latex: The germ \(\gamma\) of \(\mathcal F\) is the filter generated by \(\mathcal F\). It is contained in \(Y\) when some \(Z\in\gamma\) (equivalently, some \(Z\in\mathcal F\)) satisfies \(Z\subseteq Y\). If some \(Z\in\gamma\) satisfies \(Z\cap Y=\varnothing\), define \(\gamma\cap Y=\varnothing\); otherwise the sets \(Z\cap Y\) for \(Z\in\gamma\) form a filter base on \(X\), whose generated germ is denoted \(\gamma\cap Y\) and is contained in \(Y\).
statements.scope_note: Definition of filter-base germs and their containment and subset-intersection operations in the canonical-apartment facet/chamber setup.

statements.title: Affine Action and Kernel of the Monomial Normalizer
statements.statement_plain: The monomial normalizer N of G has a surjective permutation map s to the symmetric group on r+1 letters. Its induced affine action v on the valuation space A, with origin at phi^omega, satisfies the stated coordinate transformation formula: for sigma=s(n), the (sigma(i),sigma(j))-coordinate at v(n) applied to x equals the (i,j)-coordinate at x plus the valuation of n_{sigma(j),j} minus that of n_{sigma(i),i}. The kernel of v is precisely the subgroup of t in T whose diagonal-entry valuations are all equal.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathrm{N}\) be the monomial subgroup of \(\mathrm{G}\) with surjective permutation map \(s:\mathrm{N}\to\mathfrak{S}_{r+1}\), acting via \(v\) on the affine valuation space \(\mathrm{A}\) identified with \(\mathrm{V}\) at origin \(\varphi^{\omega}\). Then the affine coordinates transform by \(\left(a_{\sigma(i)\sigma(j)}\right)(v(n)\cdot x)=\left(a_{ij}\right)(x)+\omega(n_{\sigma(j),j})-\omega(n_{\sigma(i),i})\), where \(\sigma=s(n)\), and \(\ker v=\{t\in\mathrm{T}:\omega(t_{ii})\text{ is independent of }i\}\).
assumptions_latex: \(\mathrm{N}\subset\mathrm{G}\) consists of elements with monomial matrix \((n_{ij})\), and there is a surjective homomorphism \(s:\mathrm{N}\twoheadrightarrow\mathfrak{S}_{r+1}\) such that the only nonzero entries of an element \(n\) are \(n_{s(n)(i),i}\).

\(\mathrm{A}\) is the affine space under the dual \(\mathrm{V}\) of \(\mathrm{V}^{*}\) of valuations equivalent to \(\varphi^{\omega}\), and \(v:\mathrm{N}\to\operatorname{Aff}(\mathrm{A})\) is the homomorphism defined in (6.2.10); identify \(\mathrm{A}\) with \(\mathrm{V}\) by taking \(\varphi^{\omega}\) as origin.
statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(n\in\mathrm{N}\), with \(\sigma=s(n)\), and every \(x\in\mathrm{A}\), \(\left(a_{\sigma(i)\sigma(j)}\right)\!\left(v(n)\!\cdot x\right)=\left(a_{ij}\right)(x)+\omega\!\left(n_{\sigma(j),j}\right)-\omega\!\left(n_{\sigma(i),i}\right)\) for \(\mathrm{I}\le i,j\le r+\mathrm{I}\); moreover \(\mathrm{H}=\ker v\) is exactly the subgroup of \(t\in\mathrm{T}\) for which \(\omega(t_{ii})\) is independent of \(i\) for \(\mathrm{I}\le i\le r+\mathrm{I}\).

statements.title: Affine Weyl group of the apartment
statements.statement_plain: The affine Weyl group is the subgroup of affine automorphisms of the apartment generated by reflections in root hyperplanes. When an affine root is represented by an element u of the corresponding root group, m(u) acts as reflection in its hyperplane, yielding an inclusion in N(k)/Z(k)_b. For a simply connected semisimple group, the inclusion is an equality.
statements.statement_latex: The affine Weyl group \(W^{\mathrm{aff}}\) is the subgroup of affine automorphisms of the apartment \(\mathcal A\) generated by reflections in the root hyperplanes. If \(\psi=\psi_a^u\) for an affine root \(\psi\) with derivative \(a\in\Phi\) and \(u\in U_a(k)^*\), then \(m(u)\) acts on \(\mathcal A\) by reflection in \(\mathcal H_\psi\), so \(W^{\mathrm{aff}}\subset N(k)/Z(k)_b\). For a simply connected semisimple group, this containment is an equality.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) is the apartment with root system \(\Phi\) underlying its affine roots.
\(\psi\) is an affine root with derivative \(a\in\Phi\), and \(u\in U_a(k)^*\) satisfies \(\psi=\psi_a^u\).
For the equality assertion, the group is simply connected and semisimple.
statements.conclusion_latex: \(W^{\mathrm{aff}}\) is the subgroup of affine automorphisms of \(\mathcal A\) generated by reflections in its root hyperplanes. For \(\psi=\psi_a^u\), the element \(m(u)\) acts on \(\mathcal A\) by reflection in \(\mathcal H_\psi\), hence \(W^{\mathrm{aff}}\subset N(k)/Z(k)_b\); for a simply connected semisimple group, this containment is an equality.

statements.title: Rank-one normalizer realization of the affine Weyl group
statements.statement_plain: For the quasi-split simple rank-one group in the source, the valuation map gives T(k) a translation action on the canonical apartment. statements.statement_plain: For each affine root alpha, every chamber across its wall and outside the corresponding half-apartment is moved by some element of U_alpha. The common fixed points of U_alpha and U_alpha-star are exactly the wall of alpha, and U_alpha together with U_beta fixes a wall and no chamber exactly when beta is the opposite root alpha-star. statements.title: Normalizer quotients and affine Weyl actions under simply connected and adjoint passage
statements.statement_plain: The normalizer quotients form a chain from the simply connected quotient through the two quotients associated with G to the adjoint quotient, and the middle map from the zero quotient to the one quotient is surjective. The adjoint quotient embeds into the extended affine Weyl group with image containing the affine Weyl group, while the action of the original normalizer factors through the one quotient. The two intermediate maps are generally not injective for the stated centralizer-preimage and quotient reasons, whereas all three maps from the simply connected quotient are injective.

statements.title: Special and Extra-Special Points in an Affine Root System
statements.statement_plain: For an affine root system Ψ with gradient root system Φ, extra-special points exist; every extra-special point is special; and every special or extra-special point is a vertex. If Φ is reduced, special and extra-special points coincide. Every chamber has an extra-special vertex. At an extra-special point x, the gradient map identifies the indivisible roots of Ψ_x with those of Φ. If Ψ is irreducible, any given basis can be enumerated as ψ_0,…,ψ_ℓ so that the gradients of ψ_1,…,ψ_ℓ form a basis of Φ.
statements.statement_latex: \text{Let }\Psi\text{ be an affine root system with }\Phi=\nabla\Psi.\ \text{Then: (1) extra special points exist; (2) every extra special point is special; (3) every special or extra special point is a vertex; (4) if }\Phi\text{ is reduced, a point is special iff it is extra special; (5) every chamber }\mathcal C\text{ has an extra special vertex; (6) for extra-special }x,\ \nabla:(\Psi_x)^{\mathrm{nd}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Phi^{\mathrm{nd}};\ \text{and (7) if }\Psi\text{ is irreducible, any given basis may be enumerated }\{\psi_0,\ldots,\psi_\ell\}\text{with }\{\dot\psi_1,\ldots,\dot\psi_\ell\}\text{a basis of }\Phi.
assumptions_latex: \Psi\text{ is an affine root system with gradient root system }\Phi=\nabla\Psi.
statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&\text{(1) Extra special points exist.}\quad \text{(2) Every extra special point is special.}\\&\text{(3) Every special or extra special point is a vertex.}\\&\text{(4) If }\Phi\text{ is reduced, a point is special if and only if it is extra special.}\\&\text{(5) Every chamber }\mathcal C\text{ has an extra special vertex.}\\&\text{(6) If }x\text{ is extra special, then }\nabla\text{ identifies }(\Psi_x)^{\mathrm{nd}}\text{ with }\Phi^{\mathrm{nd}}.\\&\text{(7) If }\Psi\text{ is irreducible, any given basis can be enumerated }\{\psi_0,\ldots,\psi_\ell\}\text{ so that }\{\dot\psi_1,\ldots,\dot\psi_\ell\}\text{ is a basis of }\Phi.\end{aligned}

statements.title: Levi apartment projection preserves special and extra-special points
statements.statement_plain: For the canonical projection from the apartment of G to that of a Levi subgroup M containing S, the affine roots and hyperplanes of M are obtained from those of G by pullback. Special and extra-special points map to points of the same type (and therefore to vertices), but an arbitrary vertex of the G-apartment need not map to a vertex in the Levi apartment.
statements.statement_latex: Let q:\mathcal A(S,G)\to\mathcal A(M,S) be the canonical projection for a Levi subgroup M containing S. Under the induced inclusion of dual spaces, \Psi(M,S)\subseteq\Psi(S,G) and \Psi'(M,S)\subseteq\Psi'(S,G). For every \alpha\in\Psi(M,S), the affine root hyperplane in \mathcal A(S,G) is the preimage under q of the corresponding hyperplane in \mathcal A(M,S). Consequently, q sends special points, and likewise extra-special points, of \mathcal A(S,G) to special, respectively extra-special, points of \mathcal A(M,S) (thus vertices); in general, the image of a vertex need not be a vertex.

statements.title: Quarter-germ invariance and metric properties of apartment retractions
statements.statement_plain: For an apartment A and a quarter C in it, the associated retraction is unchanged when C is replaced by an equipollent quarter, hence depends only on the quarter germ. It does not increase distances, and its restriction to the closure of a chamber is isometric.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be an apartment of the affine building \(\mathcal I\), let \(\mathfrak C\subset A\) be a quarter, and let \(\rho=\rho_{A;\mathfrak C}\) be the associated retraction. Replacing \(\mathfrak C\) by any equipollent quarter \(\mathfrak C'\subset A\) leaves the retraction unchanged: \(\rho_{A;\mathfrak C'}=\rho_{A;\mathfrak C}\), so it depends only on the quarter germ. The map \(\rho\) is distance non-increasing, \(d(\rho(x),\rho(y))\le d(x,y)\) for all \(x,y\in\mathcal I\), and its restriction to the closure of a chamber is isometric.

statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\mathfrak C'\subset A\) is equipollent to \(\mathfrak C\), then \(\rho_{A;\mathfrak C'}=\rho_{A;\mathfrak C}\). Moreover \(d(\rho(x),\rho(y))\le d(x,y)\) for all \(x,y\in\mathcal I\), and \(\rho\) restricts isometrically to the closure of a chamber.
statements.scope_note: Properties of the retraction \(\rho_{A;\mathfrak C}\) associated with a quarter \(\mathfrak C\) in an apartment \(A\) of the affine building.

statements.title: Normalizer and Intersection Characterization of the Canonical Apartment
statements.statement_plain: The paired root-subgroup data determines the walls, and the apartment is the convex hull of those walls. statements.conclusion_latex: For \(g\in G\), \(g\in N\) if and only if conjugation by \(g\) permutes the subgroups \(P_{\alpha}\) for \(\alpha\in\Sigma\). Moreover, \(H=\bigcap_{\alpha\in\Sigma}P_{\alpha}=\bigcap_{\alpha\in\Sigma}\operatorname{Norm}(P_{\alpha})\), and the apartment \(\mathbf A\) is the convex hull of the union of the walls \(\partial\alpha\) determined by the paired subgroups.

statements.statement_plain: In the source's rank-one quasi-split setting, if ell/k is unramified, the affine root system is {a + Z, -a + Z, 2a + Z, -2a + Z}, G_0 is isomorphic to SU_3, and the derived group of G_{1/2} is isomorphic to SL_2. If ell/k is ramified, the affine root system is {a + one-half Z, -a + one-half Z, 2a + one-half + Z, -2a + one-half + Z}, G_0 is isomorphic to PGL_2, and G_{1/4} is isomorphic to SL_2. The symbols are used as in the source's local notation.
statements.statement_latex: If \(\ell/k\) is unramified, the affine root system is \(\{a+\mathbf Z,-a+\mathbf Z,2a+\mathbf Z,-2a+\mathbf Z\}\), \(G_0\simeq\mathrm{SU}_3\), and \((G_{1/2})_{\mathrm{der}}\simeq\mathrm{SL}_2\). If \(\ell/k\) is ramified, the affine root system is \(\{a+\tfrac12\mathbf Z,-a+\tfrac12\mathbf Z,2a+\tfrac12+\mathbf Z,-2a+\tfrac12+\mathbf Z\}\), \(G_0\simeq\mathrm{PGL}_2\), and \(G_{1/4}\simeq\mathrm{SL}_2\).

statements.title: Root-wise SL2 homomorphism and Weyl representative
statements.statement_plain: In a connected semisimple simply connected split k-group, each nonzero root vector X_a determines a unique k-defined homomorphism from SL2 whose differential maps the standard Cartan and positive-root matrices to the coroot H_a and X_a. The associated Weyl representative w(X_a) is defined as the image of the matrix [[0,1],[-1,0]].
statements.statement_latex: For each a\in\Phi and nonzero X_a\in\mathfrak g_a(k), let \eta_{X_a}:{\rm SL}_2\to G be the unique k-defined homomorphism with d\eta_{X_a}(\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{bmatrix})=H_a=d a^\vee(1) and d\eta_{X_a}(\begin{bmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{bmatrix})=X_a; set w(X_a)=\eta_{X_a}(\begin{bmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{bmatrix}).
assumptions_latex: G is a connected, semisimple, simply connected split k-group with Lie algebra \mathfrak{g}.
T\subset G is a split maximal torus and \Phi=\widetilde{\Phi}=\Phi(T).
a\in\Phi and 0\ne X_a\in\mathfrak{g}_a(k).
statements.conclusion_latex: There is a unique k-defined homomorphism \eta_{X_a}:{\rm SL}_2\to G whose differential sends \begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{bmatrix} to H_a=d a^\vee(1)\in\mathfrak t(k) and \begin{bmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{bmatrix} to X_a; define w(X_a)=\eta_{X_a}\!\left(\begin{bmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{bmatrix}\right).
statements.scope_note: Canonical root-wise SL2 homomorphism and associated Weyl representative in the split case.

statements.title: Apartment axioms from an omega-compatible valuation
statements.statement_plain: If φ is an ω-compatible valuation of the root datum of (G,S) and G, its equipollence class A(S) satisfies apartment axioms A0 and A1. Transporting φ by Int(g) for each g in G(k) defines A(gSg^{-1}); this class depends only on the conjugate torus, not on the chosen g, and the resulting affine spaces satisfy A2.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varphi\) be an \(\omega\)-compatible valuation of the root datum of \((G,S)\) and \(G\). The equipollence class \(\mathcal A(S)\) of \(\varphi\) satisfies parts A0 and A1 of Axiom 4.1.4. For each \(g\in G(k)\), define \(\mathcal A(gSg^{-1})\) as the equipollence class of the valuation of the root datum of \(gSg^{-1}\) obtained by transporting \(\varphi\) via \(\operatorname{Int}(g)\). This class depends only on \(gSg^{-1}\), not on \(g\), and the resulting collection of affine spaces satisfies part A2 of Axiom 4.1.4.
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi\) is an \(\omega\)-compatible valuation of the root datum of \((G,S)\) and \(G\).
For every \(g\in G(k)\), the valuation for \(gSg^{-1}\) is obtained by transporting \(\varphi\) via \(\operatorname{Int}(g)\).

For every \(g\in G(k)\), the class \(\mathcal A(gSg^{-1})\) depends only on the torus \(gSg^{-1}\), not on the choice of \(g\), and the resulting collection of affine spaces satisfies part A2 of Axiom 4.1.4.

statements.title: BruhatTits building and its apartments
statements.statement_plain: The resulting set B is the BruhatTits building for G(k), with action g·(h,y) = (gh,y). Every point of B can be moved by an element of G(k) into the apartment A. The map x ↦ (1,x) embeds A into B, and the stabilizer of x in G(k) is P_x for every x in A. A is the standard apartment, and all apartments are of the form gA with g in G(k).

The map x\mapsto(1,x) injects \mathcal{A} into \mathcal{B}, and the stabilizer of each x\in\mathcal{A} is \mathcal{P}_x. The image \mathcal{A}\subset\mathcal{B} is the standard apartment; every apartment is g\mathcal{A} for some g\in G(k).

statements.title: Canonical and Structural Maps; Apartments and Their Subsets
statements.statement_plain: The map j from A to I determined in (2.2.1) is the canonical map. A map phi from A to I is structural if phi(x)=g times j(x) for one element g of G and every x in A. Apartments, half-apartments, quadrants, and walls of I are respectively the images under structural maps of A, an affine root, a quadrant, and a wall of A.

A map \varphi:\mathbf{A}\to\mathcal{I} is a structural map if there exists g\in\mathrm{G} such that \varphi(x)=g\,j(x) for every x\in\mathbf{A}. Apartments, half-apartments, quadrants, and walls of \mathcal{I} are respectively the images under structural maps of \mathbf{A}, an affine root, a quadrant, and a wall of \mathbf{A}.

statements.title: Apartment-gluing quotient and fiber equivalence
statements.statement_plain: For a maximal k-split torus S with normalizer N and associated affine apartment A, the action map from G(k) times A onto the building B is surjective and G(k)-equivariant. Two pairs (g,x) and (h,y) represent the same building point exactly when some n in N(k) satisfies nx=y and g^{-1}hn lies in the stabilizer G(k)_x; that stabilizer may instead be replaced by G(k)_x^natural or an intermediate subgroup.

In this equivalence relation, G(k)_x may be replaced by G(k)_x^{\natural} or any intermediate subgroup.

statements.title: Canonical Apartment and Group Action in the Quotient Building
statements.statement_plain: For the quotient building constructed from a valued root datum, the result depends only on the valuation's equipollence class. The canonical apartment embeds injectively. Left translation descends to a G-action; on the embedded apartment, N acts through its prescribed affine action v; and every point lies in a G-translate of the apartment. For a discrete valuation, the construction recovers up to isomorphism the building attached to the group's Tits system.
statements.statement_latex: Let \({}^{\varphi}\mathcal I=(G\times A)/(R)\) be the building constructed from a valuation \(\varphi\) of the root datum. Then \({}^{\varphi}\mathcal I\) depends only on the equipollence class of \(\varphi\). The canonical map \(j:A\to{}^{\varphi}\mathcal I\), \(j(x)=[(1,x)]\), is injective. Left translation on the first factor descends to a G-action on \({}^{\varphi}\mathcal I\), with \([(g,x)]=g\cdot x\) for \(g\in G, x\in A\), and the induced action of \(N\) on A is \(n\cdot x=v(n)(x)\). Moreover \({}^{\varphi}\mathcal I=G\cdot A\). If \(\varphi\) is discrete, this quotient construction recovers, up to isomorphism, the building of \(\mathbf G\) associated with its Tits system.
assumptions_latex: \varphi\text{ is a valuation of the root datum, and }{}^{\varphi}\mathcal I=(G\times A)/(R)\text{ is the preceding quotient construction}.
A\text{ is the canonical apartment; }N\text{ acts on }A\text{ through }v;\ G\text{ acts on }G\times A\text{ by left translation on the first factor}.
statements.conclusion_latex: {}^{\varphi}\mathcal I\text{ depends only on the equipollence class of }\varphi;\quad j:A\hookrightarrow\mathcal I\text{ is injective};\quad [(g,x)]=g\cdot x,\quad n\cdot x=v(n)(x),\quad \mathcal I=G\cdot A;\quad \varphi\text{ discrete}\Rightarrow {}^{\varphi}\mathcal I\cong\mathcal I_{\mathrm{Tits}}(\mathbf G).
statements.scope_note: The equality \(\mathcal I=G\cdot A\) means every point lies in a G-translate of the canonical apartment; it does not assert point-transitivity. The final isomorphism assertion is only for discrete \(\varphi\). Equipollence invariance refers to the data defining relation (R).

statements.title: Action of Affine Root Subgroups (Axiom 4.1.8)
statements.statement_plain: Let S be a maximal k-split torus of G and A its corresponding apartment in the building, with psi in the specified affine-root set. Then U_psi fixes the half-apartment where psi is nonnegative. For every subset Omega of A, G(k)^0_Omega is generated by Z(k)^0 and the affine-root subgroups U_phi for affine roots nonnegative on Omega. statements.title: Uniqueness of the Building from the Canonical Apartment
statements.statement_plain: Assuming the stated axioms for the building, a G(k)-set obtained as the union of G(k)-translates of the canonical apartment and satisfying Axiom 4.1.8(1) is uniquely G(k)-equivariantly bijective with the building by a bijection that fixes the apartment pointwise.
statements.statement_latex: Let S\subset G be a maximal k-split torus with associated canonical affine apartment \mathcal A. If a G(k)-set \mathcal B' contains \mathcal A via an N(k)-equivariant embedding, satisfies \mathcal B'=\bigcup_{g\in G(k)}g\mathcal A and Axiom 4.1.8(1), then the identity on \mathcal A extends uniquely to a G(k)-equivariant bijection \mathcal B\to\mathcal B'.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal B\text{ satisfies Axioms }4.1.1,4.1.4,4.1.9\text{, and }4.1.8(2).
S\subset G\text{ is a maximal }k\text{-split torus, }\mathcal A\text{ is its associated canonical affine apartment, and }N\text{ is the normalizer of }S.
\mathcal B'\text{ is a }G(k)\text{-set equipped with an }N(k)\text{-equivariant embedding }\mathcal A\hookrightarrow\mathcal B'.
\mathcal B'=\bigcup_{g\in G(k)}g\mathcal A.
\mathcal B'\text{ satisfies Axiom }4.1.8(1).
statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The identity on }\mathcal A\text{ extends uniquely to a }G(k)\text{-equivariant bijection }\mathcal B\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B'.
statements.scope_note: Uniqueness of the underlying G(k)-set from the canonical apartment, the apartment-covering condition, and the specified axioms.

statements.title: Automorphism-Induced Building Map
statements.statement_plain: A bornological automorphism of G preserving T and all root groups induces a unique equivariant self-map of the building I that preserves the apartment A affinely. The induced map is bijective and its distances are bounded above and below by positive constant multiples of the original distances.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\gamma:\mathrm{G}\to\mathrm{G}\) be a bornological group automorphism preserving \(\mathrm{T}\) and the set of root groups \(\{\mathrm{U}_a\}\). There exists a unique map \(\gamma_*:\mathcal{I}\to\mathcal{I}\) such that (a) \(\gamma_*(g.x)=\gamma(g).\gamma_*(x)\) for all \(g\in\mathrm{G}\), and (b) \(\gamma_*(A)=A\) with \(\gamma_*|_A\) an affinity. The map \(\gamma_*\) is bijective and there exist \(m,\mathbf{M}\in\mathbf{R}_+^*\) such that \(m d(x,y)\le d(\gamma_*(x),\gamma_*(y))\le \mathbf{M}d(x,y)\) for all \(x,y\in\mathcal{I}\).
assumptions_latex: \(\gamma:\mathrm{G}\to\mathrm{G}\) is a bornological group automorphism preserving \(\mathrm{T}\) and the set \(\{\mathrm{U}_a\}\).
statements.conclusion_latex: There exist unique maps \(\gamma_*:\mathcal{I}\to\mathcal{I}\) satisfying \(\gamma_*(g.x)=\gamma(g).\gamma_*(x)\) for all \(g\in\mathrm{G}\), with \(\gamma_*(A)=A\) and \(\gamma_*|_A\) an affinity; this map is bijective, and there exist \(m,\mathbf{M}\in\mathbf{R}_+^*\) such that \(m d(x,y)\le d(\gamma_*(x),\gamma_*(y))\le \mathbf{M}d(x,y)\) for all \(x,y\in\mathcal{I}\).
statements.scope_note: Induced action of a bornological automorphism on the building \(\mathcal{I}\) and its distinguished apartment \(A\).

statements.title: Quadrants, Germs, Chambers, and Facets of the Building
statements.statement_plain: A quadrant, germ of a quadrant, chamber, or facet of the building I is defined as the image under some element of G of the corresponding object in an apartment A. A germ of A defined by a filter base F on A is identified with the germ defined by F in I.

assumptions_latex: Let \(A\) be an apartment of the building \(\mathcal I\), with \(G\) acting on \(\mathcal I\).
statements.conclusion_latex: For \(X\) equal to a quadrant, germ of a quadrant, chamber, or facet, an \(X\) of \(\mathcal I\) is the image under some \(g\in G\) of an \(X\) of \(A\). A germ of \(A\) defined by a filter base \(\mathcal F\) on \(A\) is identified with the germ defined by \(\mathcal F\) in \(\mathcal I\).

statements.title: Building Realization by Invariant Norms
statements.statement_plain: The valuation construction is onto the G-invariant homothety classes of additive norms on X. A norm class with parameters c_i corresponds to the point represented by φ^ω+v, where a_i(v)=c_i. For locally compact K, the metric topology on the apartment agrees with the quotient topology of norms modulo homothety, even if the metrics differ. Reductive-group buildings over local fields may have an extra Euclidean factor; for GL_{r+1}, the enlarged building consists of norms themselves rather than homothety classes.
statements.statement_latex: The valuation construction associated with \(\varphi^\omega\) maps onto the set of \(\mathbf G\)-invariant homothety classes of additive norms on \(\mathbf X\). For a norm class \([\gamma]\) whose parameters are \(c_i\), the corresponding point of \(\mathcal I\) is represented by \(\varphi^\omega+v\) with \(a_i(v)=c_i\). When \(\mathrm K\) is locally compact, the topology on \(\mathcal I\) from the stated metric agrees with the quotient topology on \(\mathcal N(\mathbf X)\) modulo homothety, despite a possible difference of metrics. Over a local field, a reductive-group building may be a product with a Euclidean affine space; for \(\mathrm{GL}_{r+1}\), the modified building uses norms rather than their homothety classes.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathrm K\) is locally compact for the quotient-topology assertion.
\(\mathbf G\) is reductive over a local field for the possible Euclidean affine product factor.
statements.conclusion_latex: The valuation construction gives a surjective correspondence with the \(\mathbf G\)-invariant homothety classes of additive norms on \(\mathbf X\): a norm class \([\gamma]\) with parameters \(c_i\) is represented in \(\mathcal I\) by \(\varphi^\omega+v\), where \(a_i(v)=c_i\). If \(\mathrm K\) is locally compact, the metric topology on \(\mathcal I\) agrees with the quotient topology of \(\mathcal N(\mathbf X)\) modulo homothety, although the metrics may differ. For a reductive group over a local field, the associated building may have a Euclidean affine factor; for \(\mathrm{GL}_{r+1}\), the modified building consists of norms themselves rather than homothety classes.
statements.scope_note: Realization and topology of the building through invariant additive norms, with enlarged-building and GL_{r+1} special cases.

statements.title: Fixed-Point and Conjugacy Rigidity of P_{x,E}
statements.statement_plain: When the valuation is dense, the subgroup P_{x,E} fixes exactly x in the apartment A. If an element g of G conjugates P_{x,E} into the point stabilizer P-hat_x, then g itself belongs to P-hat_x.
statements.statement_latex: Assume the valuation \(\varphi\) is dense. Let \(x\) be a point of \(A\) and \(E\) a vectorial facet. (i) The only point of \(A\) fixed by \({\mathbf P}_{x,\mathrm E}\) is \(x\). (ii) For \(g\in\mathrm G\), if \(g{\mathbf P}_{x,\mathrm E}g^{-1}\subseteq {\widehat{\mathrm P}}_{x}\), then \(g\in {\widehat{\mathrm P}}_{x}\).
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi\) is a dense valuation.
\(x\in A\).
\(E\) is a vectorial facet.
statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Fix}_{A}({\mathbf P}_{x,\mathrm E})=\{x\}\); moreover, for every \(g\in\mathrm G\), \(g{\mathbf P}_{x,\mathrm E}g^{-1}\subseteq {\widehat{\mathrm P}}_{x}\Rightarrow g\in {\widehat{\mathrm P}}_{x}\).
statements.scope_note: Proposition for a valued root datum with dense valuation, apartment \(A\), point \(x\in A\), and vectorial facet \(E\).

statements.title: Unique G-Invariant Injection into the Norm Building
statements.statement_plain: For a class t-bar in K modulo K-sigma,epsilon, define omega(t-bar) as the supremum of omega over its representatives. There is a unique G-invariant injection from the building I of G for valuation phi^omega into the norm building J. At a point phi^omega plus v with a_i(v)=c_i, its image is the norm gamma on x equal to the sum of e_i x_i and x_0, given by the infimum of omega(x_i)-c_i for i from 1 to r and one half omega(q(x_0)).
statements.statement_latex: For \(\bar{t}\in K/K_{\sigma,\varepsilon}\), define \(\omega(\bar{t})=\sup\{\omega(t)\mid t\in\bar{t}\}\). There exists a unique \(G\)-invariant injection \(\iota:\mathcal I\hookrightarrow\mathcal J\) such that, whenever \(v\in V\) has \(a_i(v)=c_i\), the image \(\iota(\varphi^{\omega}+v)\) is the norm \(\gamma\) given by \(\gamma(\sum_{i=1}^{r}e_i x_i+x_0)=\inf\{\omega(x_i)-c_i\ (1\le i\le r),\tfrac12\omega(q(x_0))\}\).
assumptions_latex: \(\bar{t}\in K/K_{\sigma,\varepsilon}\), with \(\omega(\bar{t})=\sup\{\omega(t)\mid t\in\bar{t}\}\).
\(\mathcal I\) is the building of \(G\) for the valuation \(\varphi^{\omega}\), and \(\mathcal J\) is the stated building of norms.
\(v\in V\) satisfies \(a_i(v)=c_i\), and elements are decomposed as \(x=\sum_{i=1}^{r}e_i x_i+x_0\).
statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists!\) a \(G\)-invariant injection \(\iota:\mathcal I\hookrightarrow\mathcal J\) such that, for every \(v\in V\) with \(a_i(v)=c_i\), \(\iota(\varphi^{\omega}+v)=\gamma\), where \(\gamma(\sum_{i=1}^{r}e_i x_i+x_0)=\inf\bigl\{\omega(x_i)-c_i\ (1\le i\le r),\ \tfrac12\omega(q(x_0))\bigr\}\).
statements.scope_note: For the building \(\mathcal I\) of \(G\) associated with \(\varphi^{\omega}\), the theorem uniquely specifies a G-invariant injection into the norm building \(\mathcal J\) by its valuation-dependent norm on the displayed apartment.

statements.title: Equivariant Bounded Open Facet Subgroups in a Rank-One Apartment
statements.statement_plain: In the explicit quasi-split simple rank-one construction, the real-line apartment is a simplicial complex. Each simplex is assigned a bounded open subgroup of G(k), and the quotient normalizer acts simplicially with this assignment carried to conjugate subgroups.

statements.title: Enlarged Bruhat-Tits building
statements.statement_plain: If C is the maximal K-split torus in the center of H, the enlarged Bruhat-Tits building is V(C) times the reduced building. H(K) acts by translations on V(C), while the derived subgroup and every bounded subgroup act trivially. Apartments correspond to maximal K-split tori and are affine spaces under their cocharacter vector spaces. Enlarged facets are products V(C) times reduced facets, and boundedness means bounded projection to the reduced building.
statements.statement_latex: Let C be the maximal K-split torus contained in the center of H. The enlarged Bruhat-Tits building is \widetilde{\mathcal B}(H)=V(C)\times\mathcal B(H). The group H(K) acts on V(C) by translations, with H_{\mathrm{der}}(K) and every bounded subgroup acting trivially. Apartments of the enlarged and reduced buildings correspond bijectively to maximal K-split tori; for a maximal K-split torus T, its enlarged apartment is an affine space under V(T)=\mathbf R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}X_*(T). Facets are V(C)\times F for facets F of \mathcal B(H), and a subset of the enlarged building is called bounded when its projection to \mathcal B(H) is bounded.
assumptions_latex: C\text{ is the maximal }K\text{-split torus contained in the center of }H.
T\text{ is a maximal }K\text{-split torus of }H.
V(T)=\mathbf{R}\otimes_{\mathbf{Z}}X_*(T).
statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde{\mathcal B}(H)=V(C)\times\mathcal B(H),\quad H(K)\text{ acts on }V(C)\text{ by translations, while }H_{\mathrm{der}}(K)\text{ and every bounded subgroup act trivially. Apartments of both buildings correspond bijectively to maximal }K\text{-split tori; the apartment associated to }T\text{ is an affine space under }V(T). Facets of the enlarged building are }V(C)\times F\text{ for facets }F\subset\mathcal B(H),\text{ and boundedness is defined by bounded projection to }\mathcal B(H).

statements.title: Enlarged building and its product geometry
statements.statement_plain: Let X*_K(G) be the group of K-rational characters of G, and equip the dual V^1 of X*_K(G) tensor R with a Euclidean metric. The enlarged building is I^1 = I x V^1. An element g of G(K) sends (x,v) to (g.x, v + theta(g)), where theta(g) pairs with every K-rational character chi as minus the valuation of chi(g). Its apartments, chambers, and facets are the corresponding objects of I multiplied by V^1, and each enlarged apartment has the Euclidean product metric.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_{\mathbf K}^{*}(\mathbf G)\) be the group of \(\mathbf K\)-rational characters of \(\mathbf G\), and let \(V^{1}=\left(X_{\mathbf K}^{*}(\mathbf G)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf R\right)^{\vee}\) carry a Euclidean metric. Set \(\mathcal I^{1}=\mathcal I\times V^{1}\). For \(g\in\mathbf G(\mathbf K)\), \(x\in\mathcal I\), and \(v\in V^{1}\), define \(g\cdot(x,v)=(g\cdot x,v+\theta(g))\), where \(\theta(g)\in V^{1}\) is characterized by \(\langle\theta(g),\chi\rangle=-\omega(\chi(g))\) for every \(\chi\in X_{\mathbf K}^{*}(\mathbf G)\). Apartments, chambers, and facets of \(\mathcal I^{1}\) are the products with \(V^{1}\) of the corresponding objects in \(\mathcal I\); each apartment \(A'\times V^{1}\) has the Euclidean product (sum) metric from \(A'\) and \(V^{1}\).
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal I\) is the building of \(\mathbf G\) over \(\mathbf K\).
\(\omega\) is the valuation on \(\mathbf K\) used to evaluate \(\chi(g)\).
\(V^{1}=\left(X_{\mathbf K}^{*}(\mathbf G)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf R\right)^{\vee}\) is equipped with a Euclidean metric.
statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal I^{1}=\mathcal I\times V^{1}\), \(g\cdot(x,v)=(g\cdot x,v+\theta(g))\), \(\langle\theta(g),\chi\rangle=-\omega(\chi(g))\), with apartments, chambers, facets, and product Euclidean metrics as specified.
statements.scope_note: Defines the enlarged building, the induced group action, product apartments/chambers/facets, and the Euclidean product metric.

statements.title: Boundedness criterion for point stabilizers and motivation for the enlarged building
statements.statement_plain: For every point x in the building, the stabilizer in G(k)^1 is bounded and open. Since the action factors through the adjoint quotient, the full stabilizer G(k)_x is its corresponding preimage and contains Z_G(k). It is bounded exactly when the maximal k-split torus A_G in the center is trivial; the enlarged building is introduced to obtain bounded point stabilizers.
statements.statement_latex: \text{For every }x\in\mathcal B(G),\ G(k)^1_x\text{ is bounded and open, }G(k)_x=q^{-1}\!\left(G_{\mathrm{ad}}(k)^1_x\right)\text{ for }q:G(k)\to G_{\mathrm{ad}}(k),\text{ and }Z_G(k)\subseteq G(k)_x.\text{ Moreover, }G(k)_x\text{ is bounded if and only if the maximal }k\text{-split torus }A_G\subseteq Z_G\text{ is trivial.\text{ The enlarged building is introduced so that point stabilizers are bounded.}
assumptions_latex: x\in\mathcal B(G)
G(k)\text{ acts on }\mathcal B(G)\text{ through }q:G(k)\to G_{\mathrm{ad}}(k)
G(k)^1_x\text{ is bounded and open (Axiom 4.1.2)}
statements.conclusion_latex: G(k)_x=q^{-1}\!\left(G_{\mathrm{ad}}(k)^1_x\right),\quad Z_G(k)\subseteq G(k)_x,\quad G(k)_x\text{ is bounded}\iff A_G=1,\text{ where }A_G\text{ is the maximal }k\text{-split torus in }Z_G;\text{ the enlarged building is introduced to obtain bounded point stabilizers}.

statements.statement_plain: Every G_der(k)-equivariant isometry from the reduced building B(G) to the enlarged building is obtained by sending x to (x,v) for a fixed v in V(A_G). Consequently, the set of such isometries is canonically isomorphic to the real vector space V(A_G).

statements.statement_plain: An additive norm gamma in X is decomposable if there are a basis u_1 through u_{r+1} of X-tilde and real numbers c_i such that, for every choice of coordinates x_i in K, gamma of the sum of u_i x_i is the infimum of omega(x_i) minus c_i over the indices i.

statements.title: Compatible Systems of Euclidean Metrics
statements.statement_plain: A compatible system assigns a Euclidean metric to V(S) for every maximal k-split torus S of G so that conjugation by every element of G(k) acts isometrically between the corresponding spaces. A Weyl-group-invariant metric on one such V(S), transported to all the others, specifies the system. The system induces a metric on the enlarged building, from which it can be recovered.
statements.statement_latex: A compatible system of metrics on the spaces V(S), as S ranges over the maximal k-split tori of G, is a choice of a Euclidean metric on every V(S) such that, for all such S and every g\in G(k), the conjugation isomorphism V(S)\xrightarrow{\sim}V(gSg^{-1}) is an isometry. Such a system is specified by choosing a Weyl-group-invariant Euclidean metric on V(S) for one maximal k-split torus S and transporting it to the spaces V(S_1) for all other maximal k-split tori S_1. It induces a metric on \widetilde{\mathcal B}(G), and the compatible system can be recovered from that metric.
assumptions_latex: S\subset G\text{ ranges over the maximal }k\text{-split tori of }G.
statements.conclusion_latex: \text{A compatible system induces a metric on }\widetilde{\mathcal B}(G)\text{ and is recoverable from that metric.}
statements.scope_note: Compatible Euclidean metrics on the apartment vector spaces associated with maximal k-split tori and the resulting metric on the enlarged Bruhat-Tits building.

statements.title: Compatible Systems of Weyl-Invariant Metrics
statements.statement_plain: For a maximal k-split torus S of G, form the real cocharacter space of the maximal torus S' in the intersection of S with the derived group. A Euclidean metric invariant under the rational Weyl group transports through conjugacy to the corresponding spaces for every maximal k-split torus. This family is called a compatible system of metrics, and one is fixed for subsequent use. If G is k-simple, the choice is unique up to rescaling.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subset G\) be a maximal \(k\)-split torus, let \(S'\) be the maximal torus in \(S\cap G_{\mathrm{der}}\), and set \(V(S')=\mathbf R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}X_*(S')\). A \(W_G(S)(k)\)-invariant Euclidean metric on one such \(V(S')\) transports, via the conjugacies between maximal \(k\)-split tori, to a well-defined family of metrics on all such spaces. Such a family is called a compatible system of metrics, and one is henceforth fixed. If \(G\) is \(k\)-simple, this choice is unique up to rescaling.
assumptions_latex: S\subset G\text{ is a maximal }k\text{-split torus}
S'\text{ is the maximal torus in }S\cap G_{\mathrm{der}}
V(S')=\mathbf R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}X_*(S')
statements.conclusion_latex: \text{A }W_G(S)(k)\text{-invariant Euclidean metric on one }V(S')\text{ induces a compatible system on all such spaces; if }G\text{ is }k\text{-simple, the choice is unique up to rescaling.}

statements.title: Diameter, Curve Length, and Joining Points in a Metric Space
statements.statement_plain: In a metric space, a subset has finite diameter exactly when it is bounded. A curve is a continuous map from [0,1] to X, and its length is the supremum over all finite partitions of [0,1] of the sum of successive distances. The curve is said to join x and y when its endpoints are x and y.
statements.statement_latex: Let (X,d) be a metric space. For A\subseteq X, \operatorname{diam}(A)<\infty iff A is bounded. A curve is a continuous map c:[0,1]\to X with length \ell(c)=\sup_{0=t_0<\cdots<t_n=1}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}d(c(t_i),c(t_{i+1})), where the supremum ranges over all finite partitions of [0,1]. The curve c is said to join x,y\in X when c(0)=x and c(1)=y.
assumptions_latex: (X,d) is a metric space.
A\subseteq X.
c:[0,1]\to X is continuous.
x,y\in X.
statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{diam}(A)<\infty\Longleftrightarrow A\text{ is bounded};\quad \ell(c)=\sup_{0=t_0<\cdots<t_n=1}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}d(c(t_i),c(t_{i+1}));\quad c\text{ is said to join }x,y\text{ when }c(0)=x\text{ and }c(1)=y.
statements.scope_note: For a metric space (X,d), subset A\subseteq X, continuous curve c:[0,1]\to X, and points x,y\in X.

statements.title: Geodesic and uniquely geodesic metric spaces
statements.statement_plain: A metric space (X,d) is geodesic when every two points are joined by a geodesic. It is uniquely geodesic when each pair of points is joined by exactly one geodesic.
statements.statement_latex: A metric space \((X,d)\) is geodesic if every pair of points \(x,y\in X\) is joined by a geodesic; it is uniquely geodesic if every pair \(x,y\in X\) is joined by exactly one geodesic.
assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a metric space.
statements.conclusion_latex: \((X,d)\) is geodesic exactly when every pair of points is joined by a geodesic; it is uniquely geodesic when every pair is joined by exactly one geodesic.
statements.scope_note: For a metric space \((X,d)\), with geodesics as defined in the preceding metric-space definition.

statements.title: Invariant Metric, Retractions, Segments, and Contractibility of the Building
statements.statement_plain: The building I has a unique G-invariant metric restricting to the Euclidean metric on each apartment. Retraction onto an apartment centered at a chamber is distance nonincreasing, with equality for points in a common apartment and preservation of distances from a point in the chamber closure. Metric segments are exactly the affine segments in apartments containing their endpoints, and isometries fixing both endpoints fix the segment pointwise. The stated epsilon stability estimate holds for points on a segment. Geodesic interpolation is continuous, so the building is contractible.
statements.statement_latex: \begin{aligned}\text{(i)}\;&\text{There is a unique distance }d\text{ on }\mathcal I\text{ restricting on every apartment }\mathrm A'\text{ to its Euclidean distance, and }d\text{ is }\mathrm G\text{-invariant}.\\\text{(ii)}\;&\text{If }\mathrm C\text{ is a chamber, }x\in\overline{\mathrm C},\text{ and }\rho:\mathcal I\to\mathrm A'\text{ is the retraction centered at }\mathrm C\text{ onto an apartment containing }\mathrm C,\text{ then }d(\rho(y),\rho(z))\le d(y,z)\text{ for all }y,z\in\mathcal I;\text{ equality holds when }\mathrm C,y,z\text{ lie in one apartment, and }d(x,\rho(y))=d(x,y)\text{ for every }y.\\\text{(iii)}\;&\text{For }x,y\in\mathcal I,\ S=\{z\in\mathcal I:d(x,y)=d(x,z)+d(z,y)\}\text{ is contained in every apartment containing }x,y\text{ and equals its affine segment }[xy];\text{ every isometry fixing }x,y\text{ fixes }[xy]\text{ pointwise}.\\\text{(iv)}\;&\text{If }z\in[xy],\ \varepsilon\ge0,\ d(x,z')\le d(x,z)+\varepsilon d(x,y),\text{ and }d(y,z')\le d(y,z)+\varepsilon d(x,y),\text{ then }d(z,z')^2\le4\,d(x,z)d(y,z)\varepsilon+d(x,y)^2\varepsilon^2.\\\text{(v)}\;&\text{For }t\in[0,1],\ tx+(1-t)y\text{ is the unique }z\in[xy]\text{ with }d(y,z)=t\,d(x,y);\ (t,x,y)\mapsto tx+(1-t)y\text{ is continuous, and }\mathcal I\text{ is contractible.}\end{aligned}
assumptions_latex: \mathcal I is the Bruhat-Tits building, with each apartment \mathrm A' carrying its Euclidean distance and with a \mathrm G-action.
In (ii), \mathrm C is a chamber, x\in\overline{\mathrm C}, and \rho is the retraction onto an apartment \mathrm A' containing \mathrm C, centered at \mathrm C.
In (iv), x,y,z,z'\in\mathcal I, z\in[xy], and \varepsilon\in\mathbf R_{\ge 0}.
In (v), x,y\in\mathcal I and t\in[0,1].
statements.conclusion_latex: The assertions (i)--(v) hold; in particular, the metric is \mathrm G-invariant, chamber-centered retractions are distance nonincreasing, affine and metric segments coincide, the stated stability estimate holds, geodesic interpolation is continuous, and \mathcal I is contractible.
statements.scope_note: For the Bruhat-Tits building \mathcal I with its Euclidean apartment metrics and \mathrm G-action.

statements.title: Metric properties of reduced and enlarged Bruhat-Tits buildings
statements.statement_plain: For every maximal k-split torus S, compatible Weyl-invariant Euclidean metrics on V(S') with S'=S/A_G induce a complete, non-positively curved, uniquely geodesic metric on the Bruhat-Tits building B(G). Choosing any Euclidean metric on V(A_G) and combining it with V(S') in V(S)=V(S') direct sum V(A_G) gives an enlarged building B~(G) with the same completeness, curvature, and unique-geodesic properties.

After choosing any Euclidean metric on V(A_G) and using V(S)\simeq V(S')\oplus V(A_G), the resulting metric on the enlarged building \widetilde{\mathcal B}(G) is also complete, non-positively curved, and uniquely geodesic.

statements.title: Uniqueness of Midpoints Satisfying the Nonpositive-Curvature Inequality
statements.statement_plain: In a uniquely geodesic metric space, any two points x and y have at most one point m satisfying the midpoint inequality from Definition 1.1.8. This inequality geometrically expresses that geodesic triangles are pinched, or thinner, than their Euclidean comparison triangles.

\(x,y\in X\).

statements.title: Euclidean apartment structures and enclosure
statements.statement_plain: Each building apartment has a unique Euclidean affine structure transported equivariantly from a reference apartment, and therefore a distance. For a subset M of an apartment, transporting the reference enclosure gives a choice-independent enclosure cl(M), contained in every apartment containing M; M is closed exactly when cl(M)=M.
statements.statement_latex: For every apartment \(\mathrm A'\) of \(\mathcal I\), there is a unique Euclidean affine-space structure such that, whenever \(\mathrm A'=g\mathrm A\) for \(g\in G\), the map \(x\mapsto g.x\) is an isomorphism \(\mathrm A\to\mathrm A'\); hence \(\mathrm A'\) has a distance \(d_{\mathrm A'}\). If \(M\) is a subset of an apartment, then \(g\,\mathrm{cl}(g^{-1}M)\) is independent of the choice of \(g\in G\) with \(M\subset g\mathrm A\); this set is the enclosure \(\mathrm{cl}(M)\), it is contained in every apartment containing \(M\), and \(M\) is closed iff \(\mathrm{cl}(M)=M\).
assumptions_latex: \(\mathrm A'\) is an apartment of \(\mathcal I\).
\(\mathrm A'=g\mathrm A\) for some \(g\in G\), where \(\mathrm A\) is the reference apartment.
\(M\) is a subset of an apartment, and \(g\in G\) is chosen with \(M\subset g\mathrm A\).
statements.conclusion_latex: Every apartment \(\mathrm A'\) has a unique Euclidean affine-space structure transported from \(\mathrm A\) so that each map \(x\mapsto g.x\) with \(\mathrm A'=g\mathrm A\) is an affine isomorphism, hence an induced distance \(d_{\mathrm A'}\). For any subset \(M\) of an apartment, \(\mathrm{cl}(M):=g\,\mathrm{cl}(g^{-1}M)\) is independent of the admissible \(g\), is contained in every apartment containing \(M\), and \(M\) is closed exactly when \(\mathrm{cl}(M)=M\).
statements.scope_note: Apartments of the Bruhat-Tits building \(\mathcal I\), with the fixed reference apartment \(\mathrm A\), the \(G\)-action, and the enclosure operation defined in the cited preceding result.

statements.title: Nearest-point projection onto closed convex subsets
statements.statement_plain: In a complete nonpositively curved geodesic space, every point has a unique nearest point in a closed convex subset. The nearest-point projection is continuous and equivariant under every isometry preserving the subset.
statements.statement_latex: Let (X,d) be a complete non-positively curved geodesic space and let Y\subseteq X be closed and convex. For every x\in X there is a unique point \pi(x)\in Y with d(x,\pi(x))=\min_{y\in Y}d(x,y). The map \pi:X\to Y is continuous, and every isometry f of X preserving Y satisfies \pi(f(x))=f(\pi(x)) for all x\in X.
assumptions_latex: (X,d)\text{ is a complete non-positively curved geodesic space}
Y\subseteq X\text{ is closed and convex}
statements.conclusion_latex: \forall x\in X\ \exists!\,\pi(x)\in Y\text{ such that }d(x,\pi(x))=\min_{y\in Y}d(x,y);\quad \pi:X\to Y\text{ is continuous};\quad \forall f\in\operatorname{Isom}(X),\ f(Y)=Y\Rightarrow \pi(f(x))=f(\pi(x))\ \forall x\in X.
statements.scope_note: Nearest-point projection onto a closed convex subset of a complete non-positively curved geodesic space.

statements.title: Sequence characterization of points in the building completion
statements.statement_plain: For a unit-length vector v in a vector chamber D, every point of the completed building can be represented as the limit of u_p acting on an apartment point y, with lambda_p decreasing to zero and successive u_p controlled by U_{y+lambda_p v+D}. Conversely, these conditions ensure convergence in the completion. The limit lies in the original building exactly when all u_p belong to a single left coset u U_{y+lambda_p v+D} for some u in U_D^+, and then the limit is u.y.
statements.statement_latex: Let v\in V be a length-one element contained in a vector chamber D. For every x\in\widehat{\mathcal I}, there exist y\in A, a decreasing real sequence (\lambda_p)_{p\ge1} with \lambda_p\to0, and elements u_p\in U_D^+ such that u_{p+1}\in u_pU_{y+\lambda_p v+D} for all p\ge1 and x=\lim_{p\to\infty}u_p\cdot y. Conversely, any triplet satisfying these conditions has u_p\cdot y converging to an element x\in\widehat{\mathcal I}; the limit is in \mathcal I exactly when there is u\in U_D^+ with u_p\in uU_{y+\lambda_p v+D} for all p\ge1, in which case x=u\cdot y.
assumptions_latex: v\in V has length 1 and is contained in a vector chamber D.
x\in\widehat{\mathcal I} for the existence direction.
For the converse, y\in A, (\lambda_p)_{p\ge1} is a decreasing sequence of real numbers with \lambda_p\to0, and u_p\in U_D^+ satisfy u_{p+1}\in u_pU_{y+\lambda_p v+D} for every p\ge1.
statements.conclusion_latex: Every x\in\widehat{\mathcal I} admits such a triplet (y,(\lambda_p),(u_p)) with x=\lim_{p\to\infty}u_p\cdot y. Conversely, every triplet satisfying the stated conditions gives a sequence u_p\cdot y converging to some x\in\widehat{\mathcal I}. This limit belongs to \mathcal I if and only if there exists u\in U_D^+ such that u_p\in uU_{y+\lambda_p v+D} for every p\ge1; in that case x=u\cdot y.
statements.scope_note: Metric completion of the valued-root-datum building and the criterion for a convergent sequence to have its limit in the original building.

statements.title: Equivariant splitting of the subgroup apartment orbit
statements.statement_plain: For x_0 in A, let I'_1 be the G_1^0-orbit of x_0 plus Ker(p). Its intersection with A is exactly x_0 plus Ker(p), and the restricted projection is a G_1^0-equivariant isometry onto I_1. If j is its inverse, (y,w) maps to j(y)+w bijectively from I_1 times L_1 onto the orbit G_1·A. A homomorphism theta_1 from G_1 to L_1 gives the action in these coordinates: it vanishes on G_1^0 and equals (p composed with the source valuation map v) on T_1.
statements.statement_latex: Let x_0\in A and define \mathcal I'_1=G_1^0\cdot(x_0+\operatorname{Ker}p). Then \mathcal I'_1\cap A=x_0+\operatorname{Ker}p, and the restriction \pi'=\widetilde\pi|_{\mathcal I'_1} is a G_1^0-equivariant isometry onto \mathcal I_1. Writing j=(\pi')^{-1}, the map (y,w)\mapsto j(y)+w is a bijection \mathcal I_1\times L_1\xrightarrow{\sim}G_1\cdot A. Moreover, there is a homomorphism \theta_1:G_1\to L_1 such that for all g\in G_1, y\in\mathcal I_1, w\in L_1, g\cdot(j(y)+w)=j(g\cdot y)+w+\theta_1(g); furthermore \theta_1(g)=0 for g\in G_1^0 and \theta_1(t)=(p\circ v)(t) for t\in T_1.
assumptions_latex: x_0\in A
\mathcal I'_1=G_1^0\cdot(x_0+\operatorname{Ker}p)

statements.title: Rational Closure and Rationally Closed Subroot Systems
statements.statement_plain: For a root system R in a real vector space V and a subset S of R, the rational closure of S consists of roots that are rational linear combinations of elements of S. A subroot system R' is rationally closed when it equals its rational closure. If R'' is properly contained in R' and both are rationally closed subroot systems of R, then the rank of R'' is strictly smaller than the rank of R'.

If R^{\prime\prime}\subsetneq R^{\prime}\subset R are subroot systems and both are rationally closed in R, then \operatorname{rank}(R^{\prime\prime})<\operatorname{rank}(R^{\prime}).

statements.title: Equivalent criteria for bounded subsets and building orbits
statements.statement_plain: For a subset of G(k)^1, group-theoretic boundedness, containment in finitely many Iwahori double cosets for one and hence any apartment-chamber pair, and boundedness of every orbit in the building are equivalent.
statements.statement_latex: For a subset \(\mathcal X\subseteq G(k)^1\), the following are equivalent: (1) \(\mathcal X\) is bounded in \(G(k)\) in the stated group-theoretic sense; (2) for one, hence any, pair \((\mathcal C,\mathcal A)\), where \(\mathcal A\) is an apartment of \(\mathcal B\) and \(\mathcal C\) is a chamber of \(\mathcal A\), there is a finite subset \(\{n_1,\ldots,n_r\}\subseteq N(k)\) such that \(\mathcal X\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^r\mathcal I n_i\mathcal I\), with \(\mathcal I\) and \(\mathcal S\) the Iwahori subgroup and maximal \(k\)-split torus corresponding to \(\mathcal C\) and \(\mathcal A\); and (3) for every \(x\in\mathcal B\), the orbit \(\mathcal X\cdot x\) has bounded diameter.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal X\subseteq G(k)^1
statements.conclusion_latex: (1)\Longleftrightarrow(2)\Longleftrightarrow(3)

statements.title: Building isomorphisms induced by valued-field and group isomorphisms
statements.statement_plain: Given Henselian valued fields k1 and k2, a field isomorphism between them, and a compatible isomorphism between connected reductive groups over those fields, the pair induces an isomorphism of their Bruhat-Tits buildings. The map is equivariant with respect to the group actions: mapping g1 applied to x1 equals applying f_G(g1) after mapping x1.
statements.statement_latex: Let $k_1,k_2$ be Henselian valued fields, let $f:k_1\xrightarrow{\sim}k_2$, and let $f_G:G_1\to G_2$ be an isomorphism of connected reductive groups covering $f$. Then $(f,f_G)$ induces a building isomorphism $f_{\mathcal B}:\mathcal B(G_1,k_1)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B(G_2,k_2)$ satisfying $f_{\mathcal B}(g_1x_1)=f_G(g_1)f_{\mathcal B}(x_1)$.
assumptions_latex: $k_1$ and $k_2$ are Henselian valued fields.
$f:k_1\xrightarrow{\sim}k_2$ is a field isomorphism.
$G_i$ is a connected reductive $k_i$-group for $i=1,2$.
$f_G:G_1\to G_2$ is an isomorphism covering $f$, meaning the induced map $G_1\times_{k_1}k_2\to G_2$ is an isomorphism of $k_2$-groups.
statements.conclusion_latex: There is an isomorphism of Bruhat--Tits buildings $f_{\mathcal B}:\mathcal B(G_1,k_1)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B(G_2,k_2)$ such that $f_{\mathcal B}(g_1x_1)=f_G(g_1)f_{\mathcal B}(x_1)$ for every $g_1\in G_1(k_1)$ and $x_1\in\mathcal B(G_1,k_1)$.
statements.scope_note: Functoriality of Bruhat--Tits buildings under compatible isomorphisms of Henselian valued fields and connected reductive groups.

statements.title: Relative Root Data and Apartments under Restriction of Scalars
statements.statement_plain: Restriction of scalars carries a relative root subgroup of H over ell to the corresponding closed, connected, unipotent relative root subgroup of G over k, preserving S-normalization and the associated Lie-algebra weight space; its k-points equal the ell-points of the original subgroup. The induced root-data valuations and Chevalley valuations agree, and the associated apartments are identified as affine spaces over V(S').
statements.statement_latex: Let a\in\Phi(S,H) and let U_a^H be the corresponding relative root subgroup. It is a closed connected unipotent ell-subgroup of H, normalized by S, with Lie algebra the a-weight space in Lie(H). For G=\mathrm{R}_{\ell/k}H and U_a^G=\mathrm{R}_{\ell/k}U_a^H, the group U_a^G is a closed connected unipotent k-subgroup of G, normalized by S, with Lie algebra the a-weight space in Lie(G); hence it is the relative root subgroup of G corresponding to a, and U_a^G(k)=U_a^H(\ell). The identification of these root subgroups identifies valuations of the root data of (G,S) and (H,S); an ell-pinning of H induces a k-pinning of G with matching Chevalley valuations, and the apartments \mathcal A(S,G) and \mathcal A(S,H) are identified as affine spaces over V(S').

statements.title: Existence, apartment correspondence, and central-kernel invariance
statements.statement_plain: A building \(\mathcal B(G)\) exists with a polysimplicial action of \(G(k)\). Its apartments correspond equivariantly and bijectively to maximal split tori of \(G\); for a maximal \(k\)-split torus \(S\), the stabilizer of \(\mathcal A(S)\) is \(N_G(S)(k)\). Any surjective homomorphism with central kernel induces an equivariant isomorphism of buildings. Consequently the buildings of \(G\), its adjoint and derived groups, and its simply connected cover are canonically identified, and the action factors through \(G_{\mathrm{ad}}(k)\).
statements.statement_latex: There exists a building \(\mathcal B(G)\), in the sense of Definition 1.5.5, equipped with an action of \(G(k)\) by polysimplicial automorphisms. Its apartments are in bijective \(G(k)\)-equivariant correspondence with the maximal split tori of \(G\). If \(S\) is a maximal \(k\)-split torus, \(\mathcal A=\mathcal A(S)\) its corresponding apartment, and \(N=N_G(S)\), then \(\operatorname{Stab}_{G(k)}(\mathcal A)=N(k)\). Every surjective homomorphism \(f:G\to G'\) with central kernel induces an equivariant isomorphism \(\mathcal B(G)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B(G')\). In particular, the buildings of \(G\), \(G_{\mathrm{ad}}\), \(G_{\mathrm{der}}\), and \(G_{\mathrm{sc}}\) are canonically identified, and the action of \(G(k)\) on its building factors through \(G_{\mathrm{ad}}(k)\).
assumptions_latex: S\subset G\text{ is a maximal }k\text{-split torus and }N=N_G(S)\text{ for the apartment-stabilizer clause.}
f:G\twoheadrightarrow G'\text{ is a surjective homomorphism with central kernel for the functoriality clause.}
statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal B(G)\text{ exists with a }G(k)\text{-action by polysimplicial automorphisms; its apartments correspond bijectively and }G(k)\text{-equivariantly to maximal split tori of }G; \operatorname{Stab}_{G(k)}(\mathcal A(S))=N(k); f\text{ induces an equivariant isomorphism }\mathcal B(G)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B(G'); \mathcal B(G),\mathcal B(G_{\mathrm{ad}}),\mathcal B(G_{\mathrm{der}}),\mathcal B(G_{\mathrm{sc}})\text{ are canonically identified and the }G(k)\text{-action factors through }G_{\mathrm{ad}}(k).
statements.scope_note: Axiom as stated in Chapter 4 under its standing Bruhat-Tits setup; no enlarged-building claim is made. The maximal-split-torus and central-kernel conditions apply to their respective clauses.

statements.title: Closed facet associated with a parahoric subgroup
statements.statement_plain: For x in the fixed-point building and its associated parahoric subgroup P, define the closed facet associated with P as the intersection of the P-fixed-point set in the ambient building with the fixed-point building. This set is closed and convex, contains x, and no strictly larger parahoric fixes x. A split integral torus in the associated group scheme with maximal split generic fiber S has maximal bounded subgroup S(O) contained in P; the P-fixed-point set lies in the enlarged building of the centralizer of S, and the closed facet lies in the corresponding apartment.
statements.statement_latex: Let x\in\mathfrak B and P:=P_x be its associated parahoric subgroup, with \mathcal G_x^0(\mathcal O)=P. Define \overline{\mathcal F}_P:=\mathcal B(H)^P\cap\mathfrak B, where \mathcal B(H)^P is the set of points fixed by P (the union of facets pointwise fixed by P). Then \overline{\mathcal F}_P is the closed convex facet associated with P, contains x, and x is fixed by no parahoric subgroup properly containing P. If \mathcal G_x^0 contains a closed split \mathcal O-torus \mathcal S with maximal K-split generic fiber S, then \mathcal S(\mathcal O) is the maximal bounded subgroup of S(K) and lies in P; consequently \mathcal B(H)^P\subset\widetilde{\mathcal B}(Z_{H'}(S)) and \overline{\mathcal F}_P is contained in the apartment \mathcal A:=\widetilde{\mathcal B}(Z_{H'}(S))^\Theta=\widetilde{\mathcal B}(Z_{H'}(S))\cap\mathfrak B.

P:=P_x\subset G(K) is the parahoric subgroup associated with x
\mathcal G_x^0 is the associated \mathcal O-group scheme with \mathcal G_x^0(\mathcal O)=P
\mathcal S\subset\mathcal G_x^0 is a closed split \mathcal O-torus whose generic fiber S is a maximal K-split torus of G

statements.title: Facets of the affine Tits-system complex indexed by parahorics
statements.statement_plain: Let P range over the parahoric subgroups of G, with type tau(P) in T. The complex I consists of pairs (P,x) with x in the chamber C_tau(P). For each P, F(P) is a facet of I of type tau(P) and codimension equal to the cardinality of tau(P). If P is contained in P', then F(P') is a facet of F(P) and tau(P') contains tau(P). For every type Y containing tau(P), F(P) has exactly one facet of type Y. The notation overline F denotes the union of the facets of F.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be the set of parahoric subgroups of \(G\). For each \(\mathbf P\in\mathcal P\), let \(\tau(\mathbf P)\in\mathbf T\) be its type, and define \(\mathcal I=\{(\mathbf P,x)\mid \mathbf P\in\mathcal P,\ x\in\mathbf C_{\tau(\mathbf P)}\}\). For \(\mathbf P\in\mathcal P\), set \(\mathrm F(\mathbf P)=\{(\mathbf P,x)\mid x\in\mathbf C_{\tau(\mathbf P)}\}\). This is a facet of \(\mathcal I\) of type \(\tau(\mathrm F(\mathbf P))=\tau(\mathbf P)\) and codimension \(\operatorname{Card}\tau(\mathbf P)\). If \(\mathbf P,\mathbf P'\in\mathcal P\) with \(\mathbf P\subset\mathbf P'\), then \(\mathrm F(\mathbf P')\) is a facet of \(\mathrm F(\mathbf P)\) and \(\tau(\mathbf P')\supset\tau(\mathbf P)\). Conversely, for every type \(Y\supset\tau(\mathbf P)\), \(\mathrm F(\mathbf P)\) has exactly one facet of type \(Y\). Write \(\overline{\mathrm F}\) for the union of the facets of a given facet \(\mathrm F\).
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\) is the set of parahoric subgroups of \(G\).
For each \(\mathbf P\in\mathcal P\), its type \(\tau(\mathbf P)\in\mathbf T\) and the chamber \(\mathbf C_{\tau(\mathbf P)}\) are given.
statements.conclusion_latex: The sets \(\mathcal I=\{(\mathbf P,x)\mid \mathbf P\in\mathcal P,\,x\in\mathbf C_{\tau(\mathbf P)}\}\) and \(\mathrm F(\mathbf P)=\{(\mathbf P,x)\mid x\in\mathbf C_{\tau(\mathbf P)}\}\) define a facet structure: \(\mathrm F(\mathbf P)\) has type \(\tau(\mathbf P)\) and codimension \(\operatorname{Card}\tau(\mathbf P)\); if \(\mathbf P\subset\mathbf P'\), then \(\mathrm F(\mathbf P')\) is a facet of \(\mathrm F(\mathbf P)\) with \(\tau(\mathbf P')\supset\tau(\mathbf P)\); for every \(Y\supset\tau(\mathbf P)\), \(\mathrm F(\mathbf P)\) has exactly one facet of type \(Y\). The notation \(\overline{\mathrm F}\) denotes the union of the facets of a given facet \(\mathrm F\).

statements.title: Parahoric subgroup attached to a nonempty apartment subset
statements.statement_plain: Let Ω be a nonempty subset of the apartment. For each root a, define U_{a,Ω,0} as the intersection of U_{a,x,0} over x in Ω. Let G(k)_Ω^sharp be generated by these groups for all roots, and define N_Ω^sharp and Z_Ω^sharp by intersecting it with N(k) and Z(k), respectively. The parahoric subgroup attached to Ω is P_Ω = G(k)_Ω^0 = Z(k)^0 G(k)_Ω^sharp, and N_Ω^0 = N(k) ∩ G(k)_Ω^0 = N_Ω^sharp Z(k)^0.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varnothing\neq\Omega\subset\mathcal A\). For each \(a\in\Phi\), define \(U_{a,\Omega,0}=\bigcap_{x\in\Omega}U_{a,x,0}\). Define \(G(k)_{\Omega}^{\sharp}\) to be the subgroup of \(G(k)\) generated by the groups \(U_{a,\Omega,0}\) for all \(a\in\Phi\), and set \(N_{\Omega}^{\sharp}=N(k)\cap G(k)_{\Omega}^{\sharp}\) and \(Z_{\Omega}^{\sharp}=Z(k)\cap G(k)_{\Omega}^{\sharp}\). The parahoric subgroup attached to \(\Omega\) is \(\mathcal P_{\Omega}=G(k)_{\Omega}^{0}=Z(k)^{0}G(k)_{\Omega}^{\sharp}\), and \(N_{\Omega}^{0}=N(k)\cap G(k)_{\Omega}^{0}=N_{\Omega}^{\sharp}Z(k)^{0}\).
assumptions_latex: \varnothing\neq\Omega\subset\mathcal A
statements.conclusion_latex: U_{a,\Omega,0}=\bigcap_{x\in\Omega}U_{a,x,0},\quad G(k)_{\Omega}^{\sharp}=\langle U_{a,\Omega,0}:a\in\Phi\rangle,\quad N_{\Omega}^{\sharp}=N(k)\cap G(k)_{\Omega}^{\sharp},\quad Z_{\Omega}^{\sharp}=Z(k)\cap G(k)_{\Omega}^{\sharp},\quad \mathcal P_{\Omega}=G(k)_{\Omega}^{0}=Z(k)^{0}G(k)_{\Omega}^{\sharp},\quad N_{\Omega}^{0}=N(k)\cap G(k)_{\Omega}^{0}=N_{\Omega}^{\sharp}Z(k)^{0}

statements.statement_plain: For parahoric subgroups P and Q of G(K), the facet set F_P is convex and open dense in its closure, and its closure is the closure denoted by overline F_P. The source further states that F_P differs from this closure unless P is maximal parahoric. If F_P and F_Q intersect, then at every common point z both subgroups equal the connected stabilizer G_z^0(O); consequently each point of B(H)^Theta lies in a unique facet.

(3) If \(\mathcal F_P\cap\mathcal F_Q\neq\varnothing\), then for every z in this intersection, \(P=\mathcal G_z^0(\mathcal O)=Q\). statements.title: Facet stabilizers and transitivity in the building
statements.statement_plain: For a facet F in the building, its subgroup in G(k)^0 is both the setwise and pointwise stabilizer, fixes exactly the closure of F, and acts transitively on apartments containing F. G(k)^0 and G(k) act transitively on apartment-chamber pairs; consequently the normalizer in G(k) of a maximal k-split torus acts transitively on chambers of its apartment. Two building points lie in the same facet exactly when their G(k)^0 point stabilizers are equal.
statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal F be a facet of \mathcal B(G). Then (1) G(k)^0_{\mathcal F} is both the setwise and pointwise stabilizer of \mathcal F in G(k)^0; (2) \operatorname{Fix}_{\mathcal B(G)}(G(k)^0_{\mathcal F})=\overline{\mathcal F}; (3) G(k)^0_{\mathcal F} acts transitively on the apartments containing \mathcal F; (4) G(k)^0, and hence G(k), acts transitively on ordered pairs (\mathcal A,\mathcal C) with \mathcal C a chamber in \mathcal A. In particular, for a maximal k-split torus S\subset G with corresponding apartment \mathcal A and normalizer N(k)\subset G(k), N(k) acts transitively on the chambers of \mathcal A; (5) for x,y\in\mathcal B(G), x and y lie in the same facet if and only if G(k)^0_x=G(k)^0_y.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal F\text{ is a facet of }\mathcal B(G).
statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&G(k)^0_{\mathcal F}=\operatorname{Stab}_{G(k)^0}(\mathcal F)=\operatorname{Fix}_{G(k)^0}(\mathcal F),\\&\operatorname{Fix}_{\mathcal B(G)}\!\left(G(k)^0_{\mathcal F}\right)=\overline{\mathcal F},\\&G(k)^0_{\mathcal F}\text{ acts transitively on apartments containing }\mathcal F,\\&G(k)^0\text{ and }G(k)\text{ act transitively on ordered apartment-chamber pairs};\\&\text{if }S\subset G\text{ is maximal }k\text{-split with apartment }\mathcal A,\ N(k)\text{ acts transitively on chambers of }\mathcal A,\\&x,y\in\mathcal B(G):\ x,y\text{ lie in the same facet}\Longleftrightarrow G(k)^0_x=G(k)^0_y.
statements.scope_note: All stabilizers and pointwise stabilizers in the first, second, and fifth assertions are taken in G(k)^0; N(k) denotes the normalizer in G(k) of a maximal k-split torus S, and \mathcal A is its corresponding apartment.

statements.title: Intersection criterion for distinct maximal parahoric subgroups
statements.statement_plain: In an irreducible Tits system, for distinct maximal parahoric subgroups P and P', their intersection Q is a parahoric subgroup exactly when Q is a maximal proper subgroup of P. This equivalence is false in general for reducible Tits systems.

Set \(\mathcal Q:=\mathcal P\cap\mathcal P'\). Then \(\mathcal Q\) is a parahoric subgroup if and only if \(\mathcal Q\) is a maximal proper subgroup of \(\mathcal P\). This assertion is false without the irreducibility assumption.
assumptions_latex: The Tits system \((\mathcal G,\mathcal I,\mathcal N,R)\) is irreducible.
\(\mathcal P\neq\mathcal P'\) are maximal parahoric subgroups of \(\mathcal G\).
statements.conclusion_latex: With \(\mathcal Q:=\mathcal P\cap\mathcal P'\), \(\mathcal Q\) is parahoric if and only if it is a maximal proper subgroup of \(\mathcal P\); the assertion can fail when irreducibility is dropped.
statements.scope_note: Intersection criterion for two distinct maximal parahoric subgroups in an irreducible Tits system, including the failure boundary for reducible systems.

statements.title: Maximal Boundedness and Conjugacy of Parahoric Stabilizers
statements.statement_plain: For parahoric subgroups P and P' of G with types X and X', Stab(P) is maximal bounded exactly when X is maximal among parahoric types invariant under the stabilizer Xi_X of X in Xi. Stab(P) and Stab(P') are conjugate in G exactly when X' lies in the Xi-orbit of X.

Moreover, \(\operatorname{Stab}(P)\) and \(\operatorname{Stab}(P')\) are conjugate in \(G\) if and only if there exists \(t\in\Xi\) such that \(X'=t(X)\).

statements.title: Sharp chamber subgroup root-group factorizations
statements.statement_plain: For a chamber C in the apartment, an interior point x, and a chosen positive root system, the sharp normalizer subgroup at x equals the sharp centralizer subgroup. The sharp chamber subgroup factors, at depth 0 or 0+, as negative nondivisible root groups, the sharp centralizer, and positive nondivisible root groups. For a facet F in the closure of C with the compatible positive system determined by C, the same subgroup factors using depth 0+ on negative facet root groups and depth 0 on positive facet root groups.
statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal C\subset\mathcal A be a chamber, let x\in\mathcal C, and let \Phi^+\subset\Phi be a positive system. Then N_x^\sharp=Z_x^\sharp and, for r=0 or 0+, G(k)_{\mathcal C}^\sharp=\prod_{a\in\Phi^{-,\mathrm{nd}}}U_{a,x,r}\cdot Z_x^\sharp\cdot\prod_{a\in\Phi^{+,\mathrm{nd}}}U_{a,x,r}. If \mathcal F\subset\overline{\mathcal C} is a facet and \Phi^+ contains \Phi_{\mathcal F}(\mathcal C)^+, then G(k)_{\mathcal C}^\sharp=\prod_{a\in\Phi^{-,\mathrm{nd}}}U_{a,\mathcal F,0+}\cdot Z_x^\sharp\cdot\prod_{a\in\Phi^{+,\mathrm{nd}}}U_{a,\mathcal F,0}.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal C\subset\mathcal A\text{ is a chamber and }x\in\mathcal C.
\Phi^+\subset\Phi\text{ is a positive system of roots}.
\mathcal F\subset\overline{\mathcal C}\text{ is a facet and }\Phi^+\supset\Phi_{\mathcal F}(\mathcal C)^+\text{ for the second factorization}.
r\in\{0,0+\}\text{ for the first factorization}.
statements.conclusion_latex: N_x^\sharp=Z_x^\sharp,\qquad G(k)_{\mathcal C}^\sharp=\prod_{a\in\Phi^{-,\mathrm{nd}}}U_{a,x,r}\cdot Z_x^\sharp\cdot\prod_{a\in\Phi^{+,\mathrm{nd}}}U_{a,x,r}\quad(r\in\{0,0+\});\qquad G(k)_{\mathcal C}^\sharp=\prod_{a\in\Phi^{-,\mathrm{nd}}}U_{a,\mathcal F,0+}\cdot Z_x^\sharp\cdot\prod_{a\in\Phi^{+,\mathrm{nd}}}U_{a,\mathcal F,0}.
statements.scope_note: Factorizations of the sharp subgroup attached to a chamber, first via root groups based at an interior point and then via facet root groups for a facet in the chamber closure. Products range over positive and negative nondivisible roots.

statements.title: Maximal Pro-p Subgroups and Iwahori Radicals
statements.statement_plain: Assume k is a local field. For every point x in the building B(G), the Moy-Prasad subgroup P_{x,0+} is an open pro-p subgroup of G(k), and it is maximal exactly when x lies in a chamber, equivalently when P_{x,0} is an Iwahori subgroup. statements.statement_latex: Assume that k is a local field. For any x\in\mathcal B(G), the group \mathcal P_{x,0+} is an open pro-p subgroup of G(k). Every maximal open pro-p subgroup H of G(k)^0 equals \mathcal P_{x,0+} for an Iwahori subgroup \mathcal P_{x,0}, and \mathcal P_{x,0} is the normalizer of \mathcal P_{x,0+} in G(k)^0.

statements.title: Disconnected parahoric subgroup chains
statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty subset Omega of an apartment A in the building, Definition 7.8.1 forms the open subgroup chain G(k)^0_Omega <= G(k)^b_Omega <= G(k)^1_Omega <= G(k)^dagger_Omega <= G(k)_Omega from the chain Z(k)^0 <= Z(k)^1 <= N(k)^1_Omega <= N(k)^dagger_Omega <= N(k)_Omega in the stabilizer of Omega in N(k). The sharp subgroup is normalized by N(k)_Omega; each first-chain term is the product with the corresponding second-chain term, all inclusions except the last in each chain have finite index, and for Omega={x}, G(k)^1_x = G(k)^dagger_x.
statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty subset \(\Omega\) of an apartment \(\mathcal A\subset\mathcal B\), with \(G(k)^\sharp_\Omega\subset G(k)^0_\Omega\) as in Definition 7.4.1, define \(G(k)^0_\Omega\subset G(k)^b_\Omega\subset G(k)^1_\Omega\subset G(k)^\dagger_\Omega\subset G(k)_\Omega\) as open subgroups by multiplying \(G(k)^\sharp_\Omega\) with the corresponding terms of \(Z(k)^0\subset Z(k)^1\subset N(k)^1_\Omega\subset N(k)^\dagger_\Omega\subset N(k)_\Omega\), where \(N(k)_\Omega\) is the stabilizer of \(\Omega\) in \(N(k)\), \(N(k)^1_\Omega\) is its pointwise stabilizer in \(N(k)^1=N(k)\cap G(k)^1\), and \(N(k)^\dagger_\Omega\) its setwise stabilizer in \(N(k)^1\). assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\subset\mathcal B\) is an apartment and \(\varnothing\neq\Omega\subset\mathcal A\).
The subgroups \(G(k)^\sharp_\Omega\subset G(k)^0_\Omega\) are those of Definition 7.4.1.

It also identifies the Iwahori-Weyl group with the Iwahori double-coset space and, for any two facets in the closure of a common chamber, identifies the corresponding affine-Weyl double-coset space with the double-coset space of their connected parahoric subgroups.

\mathcal F_1,\mathcal F_2\subset\overline{\mathcal C}\text{ are facets for assertion (3).}

statements.title: Maximal parahorics and maximal bounded subgroups
statements.statement_plain: For a vertex x of the Bruhat-Tits building, the subgroup G(k)^1_x is a maximal open and bounded subgroup of G(k). Every maximal bounded subgroup of G(k) equals G(k)^1_x for some point x in the building; if G(k)^0=G(k)^1, then x is a vertex. For any subgroup K of G(k), K is maximal parahoric if and only if it is maximal bounded in G(k)^0.
statements.statement_latex: \begin{aligned}(1)&\ x\in\mathcal B(G)\text{ a vertex}\Rightarrow G(k)^1_x\text{ is maximal open and bounded in }G(k).\\(2)&\ H\le G(k)\text{ maximal bounded}\Rightarrow H=G(k)^1_x\text{ for some }x\in\mathcal B(G);\ G(k)^0=G(k)^1\Rightarrow x\text{ is a vertex}.\\(3)&\ \mathcal K\le G(k):\ \mathcal K\text{ maximal parahoric}\Longleftrightarrow\mathcal K\text{ maximal bounded in }G(k)^0.\end{aligned}

G(k)^0=G(k)^1\text{ (for the vertex conclusion in clause 2; this holds, for example, when }G\text{ is semisimple and simply connected)}
\mathcal K\le G(k)

statements.title: Standing assumptions and notation for the Iwahori-Tits system
statements.statement_plain: Assume G is semisimple and simply connected. For a chamber C in the apartment A, J = G(k)_c^0 is the corresponding Iwahori subgroup; write Gcal = G(k), Ncal = N(k), and Zcal = Z(k)^0 = Z(k)^1. Let R be the reflections in the affine Weyl group whose hyperplanes contain a codimension-one face of C. R corresponds bijectively to the walls of C, and if G is absolutely simple, to the vertices of C.

statements.title: Admissible Parabolics and Parahoric Subgroups
statements.statement_plain: In the Iwahori-Tits system of G(k), the admissible parabolic subgroups are exactly the parahoric subgroups of G(k). An admissible parabolic subgroup is standard if and only if it equals G(k)_F^0 for a facet F of the distinguished chamber C.
