statements.title: Facet Stabilizer and Iwahori-Tits Decomposition
statements.statement_plain: For a facet F in the closure of a chamber C, the affine Weyl subgroup generated by reflections in the C-simple affine roots vanishing on F is exactly the stabilizer of F, and the connected facet subgroup G(k)_F^0 decomposes as G(k)_C^0 W_F^aff G(k)_C^0.
statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal{F}\subset\mathcal{A} be a facet in the closure of a chamber \mathcal{C}\subset\mathcal{A}, and let W_{\mathcal{F}}^{\mathrm{aff}} be generated by reflections in the \mathcal{C}-simple affine roots vanishing on \mathcal{F}. Then W_{\mathcal{F}}^{\mathrm{aff}} is the stabilizer of \mathcal{F} in W^{\mathrm{aff}}, and G(k)_{\mathcal{F}}^{0}=G(k)_{\mathcal{C}}^{0}\,W_{\mathcal{F}}^{\mathrm{aff}}\,G(k)_{\mathcal{C}}^{0}.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal{F}\subset\mathcal{A} is a facet contained in the closure of a chamber \mathcal{C}\subset\mathcal{A}.
W_{\mathcal{F}}^{\mathrm{aff}}\subset W^{\mathrm{aff}} is generated by reflections along the \mathcal{C}-simple affine roots that vanish on \mathcal{F}.
statements.conclusion_latex: W_{\mathcal{F}}^{\mathrm{aff}}=\operatorname{Stab}_{W^{\mathrm{aff}}}(\mathcal{F}),\qquad G(k)_{\mathcal{F}}^{0}=G(k)_{\mathcal{C}}^{0}\,W_{\mathcal{F}}^{\mathrm{aff}}\,G(k)_{\mathcal{C}}^{0}.
statements.scope_note: Facet and chamber subgroups in the Iwahori-Tits system associated with a valued root datum.

statements.title: Saturated Tits system and parabolic-facet correspondence
statements.statement_plain: For an apartment A of B and a chamber C in A, let S be the corresponding maximal k-split torus with normalizer N, Gcal = G(k)^0, I = Gcal_C^0(o), and Ncal = N(k) intersect Gcal. Then (I,Ncal) is a saturated Tits system in Gcal and B is its restricted building. Facets F of B correspond order-reversingly to parabolic subgroups G(k)_F^0 of Gcal, and the points fixed by G(k)_F^0 are exactly the closure of F.
statements.statement_latex: Given an apartment \(\mathcal A\) and chamber \(\mathcal C\subset\mathcal A\) as above, \((\mathcal I,\mathcal N)\) is a saturated Tits system in \(\mathcal G=G(k)^0\) whose restricted building is \(\mathcal B\). The map \(\mathcal F\mapsto G(k)_{\mathcal F}^{0}\) gives an order-reversing bijection between facets of \(\mathcal B\) and parabolic subgroups of \(\mathcal G\), and the fixed-point set of each \(G(k)_{\mathcal F}^{0}\) is exactly \(\overline{\mathcal F}\).
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) is an apartment of \(\mathcal B\), and \(\mathcal C\) is a chamber contained in \(\mathcal A\).
\(S\) is the maximal \(k\)-split torus of \(G\) corresponding to \(\mathcal A\), and \(N\) is its normalizer in \(G\).
\(\mathcal G=G(k)^0\), \(\mathcal I=\mathcal G_{\mathcal C}^{0}(\mathfrak o)\), and \(\mathcal N=N(k)\cap\mathcal G\).
statements.conclusion_latex: \((\mathcal I,\mathcal N)\) is a saturated Tits system in \(\mathcal G\), and \(\mathcal B\) is the (restricted) building of this Tits system. Moreover, \(\mathcal F\mapsto G(k)_{\mathcal F}^{0}\) is an order-reversing bijection from the facets of \(\mathcal B\) to the parabolic subgroups of \(\mathcal G\), and \(\operatorname{Fix}_{\mathcal B}(G(k)_{\mathcal F}^{0})=\overline{\mathcal F}\).
statements.scope_note: Unramified-descent setting of the restricted Bruhat-Tits building and the subgroup \(G(k)^0\); notation and hypotheses are those of the source chapter.

statements.title: Six Axioms for the Double Tits-System Data
statements.statement_plain: From (5.2.1) through (5.2.27), assume that the preceding data satisfy six conditions: (A1) conjugation by each n in N sends P_alpha to the source-denoted P_{v(n),alpha}; (A2) beta containing alpha implies P_beta is contained in P_alpha, and the intersection over beta strictly containing alpha is H; (A3) for alpha and beta with intersection of nonempty interior, the specified set Omega gives a product P_alpha P_Omega that is a group; (A4) the displayed union of two double-coset-type subsets is a subgroup of G; (A5) P_{x+D} intersected with P_{x-D} is H for every x and vector chamber D; and (A6) G is generated by the subgroups P_alpha.
statements.statement_latex: \begin{aligned}(A1)&\quad \forall n\in\mathrm N\;\forall\alpha\in\Sigma,\quad n\mathrm P_\alpha n^{-1}=\mathrm P_{\mathrm v(n),\alpha}.\\(A2)&\quad \forall\alpha,\beta\in\Sigma,\quad \beta\supseteq\alpha\Rightarrow \mathrm P_\beta\subseteq\mathrm P_\alpha,\qquad \bigcap_{\substack{\beta\in\Sigma\\\beta\supset\alpha}}\mathrm P_\beta=\mathrm H.\\(A3)&\quad \alpha,\beta\in\Sigma,\ \operatorname{int}(\alpha\cap\beta)\ne\varnothing,\ \Omega=\bigcap\{\gamma:\gamma\text{ is an affine root containing }\alpha\cap\beta\text{ but not }\alpha\}\\&\qquad\Rightarrow \mathrm P_\alpha\mathrm P_\Omega\text{ is a group}.\\(A4)&\quad \forall\alpha\in\Sigma,\quad \mathrm P_\alpha\mathrm P_{(\alpha^*)_+}\cup\mathrm P_\alpha\mathrm v^{-1}(r_\alpha)\mathrm P_\alpha\text{ is a subgroup of }\mathrm G.\\(A5)&\quad \forall x\in\mathbf A\;\forall\text{ vector chambers }\mathbf D,\quad \mathbf P_{x+\mathbf D}\cap\mathbf P_{x-\mathbf D}=\mathbf H.\\(A6)&\quad \mathbf G=\left\langle\bigcup_{\alpha\in\Sigma}\mathrm P_\alpha\right\rangle.\end{aligned}
assumptions_latex: \text{The preceding data and the source-local notation are fixed.}
\text{These conditions are assumed from (5.2.1) through (5.2.27).}
statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The preceding data satisfy conditions (A1)--(A6).}

statements.title: Subgroups P_Omega and semidirect decomposition in a double Tits system
statements.statement_plain: Assuming the double Tits-system axioms (B1) and (B5), H normalizes every root group U_alpha and the subgroup U_Omega. Define U_Omega as the subgroup generated by U_alpha for roots alpha in Sigma containing Omega. Then P_Omega = H U_Omega equals the subgroup generated by H and all corresponding P_alpha. If Omega contains a quarter, P_Omega is the semidirect product H ⋉ U_Omega, so H and U_Omega intersect trivially. Under (B1), checking (B5) for one fixed vector chamber is sufficient.
statements.statement_latex: Assume (B1) and (B5). Then H normalizes each root group U_\alpha and each U_\Omega, and P_\Omega:=H\,U_\Omega is the subgroup generated by H and all P_\alpha with \alpha\in\Sigma and \alpha\supset\Omega. Whenever \Omega contains a quarter, P_\Omega is the semidirect product H\ltimes U_\Omega. Moreover, by (B1), verification of (B5) for a single fixed vector chamber suffices.
assumptions_latex: The double Tits-system axiom (B1) holds.
The double Tits-system axiom (B5) holds; under (B1), it is enough to verify (B5) for one fixed vector chamber.
\Omega contains a quarter for the semidirect-product conclusion.
statements.conclusion_latex: (B1) implies that H normalizes every root group U_\alpha and hence U_\Omega. For U_\Omega=\langle U_\alpha\mid \alpha\in\Sigma,\ \alpha\supset\Omega\rangle, define P_\Omega:=H\,U_\Omega; this is equivalently the subgroup generated by H and all P_\alpha with \alpha\in\Sigma and \alpha\supset\Omega. If \Omega contains a quarter, then P_\Omega\cong H\ltimes U_\Omega, equivalently H\cap U_\Omega=\{\mathrm I\}.
statements.scope_note: Consequence of the double Tits-system axioms for the subgroups attached to a subset \Omega of the root-space geometry.

statements.title: Fixed points and inclusion reversal for closed-subset stabilizers
statements.statement_plain: Assuming condition (ii bis), every closed subset Omega_1 of the apartment A is exactly the set of points of A fixed by all elements of its pointwise stabilizer P_{Omega_1}. For closed subsets Omega_1 and Omega_1', P_{Omega_1} is contained in P_{Omega_1'} if and only if Omega_1' is contained in Omega_1.
statements.statement_latex: Assume (ii bis). For every closed subset \(\Omega_1\subseteq\mathbf A\), the common fixed-point set in \(\mathbf A\) of its pointwise stabilizer is exactly \(\Omega_1\): \(\operatorname{Fix}_{\mathbf A}(\mathrm P_{\Omega_1})=\Omega_1\). For any two closed subsets \(\Omega_1,\Omega_1'\subseteq\mathbf A\), one has \(\mathrm P_{\Omega_1}\subseteq\mathrm P_{\Omega_1'}\) if and only if \(\Omega_1'\subseteq\Omega_1\).
assumptions_latex: (ii bis) is satisfied.
\(\Omega_1\) and \(\Omega_1'\) are closed subsets of the apartment \(\mathbf A\).
statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Fix}_{\mathbf A}(\mathrm P_{\Omega_1})=\Omega_1\), and \(\mathrm P_{\Omega_1}\subseteq\mathrm P_{\Omega_1'}\) if and only if \(\Omega_1'\subseteq\Omega_1\).
statements.scope_note: Here \(\mathrm P_{\Omega}\) is the pointwise stabilizer of \(\Omega\) in the double Tits system, and \(\operatorname{Fix}_{\mathbf A}\) denotes common fixed points within the apartment \(\mathbf A\). The source makes no corresponding claim for common fixed points in the whole building and warns that such an equality can fail (for example for an affine root or for the entire apartment).

statements.title: Propagation of double-coset membership along a chamber ray
statements.statement_plain: Let x and x' lie in the apartment A, let D and D' be vector chambers, and let L be an open half-line of V with origin o contained in D. Suppose g lies in the double coset B_(x,D) n B_(x',D') for some n in N. As the first point moves through x+L, either g remains in the same n-indexed double coset for every point, or there exist y in x+L and n' in N such that the original membership holds for every point strictly between x and y, g belongs at y to the n'-indexed double coset, and the corresponding lambda value is strictly larger. In all cases, g belongs to B_(z,D) N B_(x',D') for every z in x+L.
statements.statement_latex: \text{Let }x,x'\in\mathrm A,\ \mathrm D,\mathrm D'\text{ be vector chambers, and let }\mathrm L\subset\mathrm D\text{ be an open half-line of }\mathrm V\text{ with origin }o.\text{ If }g\in\mathbf G,\ n\in\mathrm N,\text{ and }g\in\mathbf B_{x,\mathrm D}n\mathbf B_{x',\mathrm D'},\text{ then either }g\in\mathbf B_{z,\mathrm D}n\mathbf B_{x',\mathrm D'}\text{ for all }z\in x+\mathrm L,\text{ or there are }y\in x+\mathrm L\text{ and }n'\in\mathrm N\text{ such that }g\in\mathbf B_{z,\mathrm D}n\mathbf B_{x',\mathrm D'}\text{ for all }z\in\rbrack x,y\lbrack,\ g\in\mathbf B_{y,\mathrm D}n'\mathbf B_{x',\mathrm D'},\text{ and }\lambda(y,\mathrm D;n'\!\cdot x',{}^vv(n')(\mathrm D'))>\lambda(x,\mathrm D;n\!\cdot x',{}^vv(n)(\mathrm D')).\text{ Moreover, }g\in\mathbf B_{z,\mathrm D}\mathrm N\mathbf B_{x',\mathrm D'}\text{ for every }z\in x+\mathrm L.
assumptions_latex: x,x'\in \mathrm A
\mathrm D\text{ and }\mathrm D'\text{ are vector chambers}
\mathrm L\subset \mathrm V\text{ is an open half-line with origin }o\text{ and }\mathrm L\subset \mathrm D
g\in \mathbf G,\quad n\in \mathrm N
g\in \mathbf B_{x,\mathrm D}\,n\,\mathbf B_{x',\mathrm D'}
statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{gathered}\text{Either }g\in \mathbf B_{z,\mathrm D}n\mathbf B_{x',\mathrm D'}\text{ for every }z\in x+\mathrm L,\\\text{or there exist }y\in x+\mathrm L\text{ and }n'\in \mathrm N\text{ such that }g\in \mathbf B_{z,\mathrm D}n\mathbf B_{x',\mathrm D'}\text{ for every }z\in\rbrack x,y\lbrack,\\g\in \mathbf B_{y,\mathrm D}n'\mathbf B_{x',\mathrm D'},\quad \lambda\!\left(y,\mathrm D;n'\!\cdot x',{}^vv(n')(\mathrm D')\right)>\lambda\!\left(x,\mathrm D;n\!\cdot x',{}^vv(n)(\mathrm D')\right).\\\text{Moreover, in either case }g\in \mathbf B_{z,\mathrm D}\,\mathrm N\,\mathbf B_{x',\mathrm D'}\text{ for every }z\in x+\mathrm L.\end{gathered}

statements.title: Dominance Inequality for Apartment Retractions
statements.statement_plain: For a dominant displacement x minus y in the apartment of a maximal k-split torus, the retraction centered at a chamber does not increase that displacement in the positive-root order after applying any g in G(k).
statements.statement_latex: Let S\subset G be a maximal k\text{-split torus with apartment }\mathcal A and choose \Phi^+\subset\Phi(S,G). For the retraction \rho:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A centered at a chamber of \mathcal A, every g\in G(k) and x,y\in\mathcal A with dominant x-y\in V(S) satisfy \rho(gx)-\rho(gy)\le x-y, where v'\le v means \alpha(v-v')\ge0 for all \alpha\in\Phi^+.
assumptions_latex: S\subset G is a maximal k\text{-split torus with apartment }\mathcal A.
\Phi^+\subset\Phi(S,G) is a chosen positive root system; U is the unipotent radical of the corresponding minimal parabolic.
\rho:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A is the retraction centered at a chamber of \mathcal A.
g\in G(k),\ x,y\in\mathcal A, and x-y\in V(S) is dominant.
For v,v'\in V(S), v'\le v iff every \alpha\in\Phi^+ satisfies \alpha(v-v')\ge0.
statements.conclusion_latex: \rho(gx)-\rho(gy)\le x-y.

Moreover, }\widehat{\mathrm G}=K\,\widehat{\mathbf V}_{\mathbf D}\,K\text{ and, if }\varphi:\mathrm G\to\widehat{\mathrm G}\text{ is of connected type, the canonical map }\widehat{\mathbf V}_{\mathbf D}\to K\backslash\widehat{\mathbf G}/K\text{ is bijective}.

statements.title: Superspecial, Absolutely Special, and Hyperspecial Points
statements.statement_plain: For a point x in the Bruhat-Tits building, superspecial means being special over every finite unramified extension, absolutely special means being special over every finite separable extension, and hyperspecial means being superspecial when G splits over an unramified extension. Every special point is a vertex. The parahoric subgroup \mathcal P_x is called superspecial, absolutely special, or hyperspecial according to the corresponding property of x.

k'/k\text{ ranges over finite unramified extensions}

statements.title: Characterization and existence of absolutely special points
statements.statement_plain: Assume G is quasi-split. Let T be a maximally split maximal torus, let A be its corresponding apartment, and let o be a Chevalley valuation in A. For every point x = o + v in A, the following are equivalent: x is absolutely special; a(v) belongs to v_a Z for every non-divisible relative root a in Phi; x equals t dot o for some t in T_ad(k); and x is a Chevalley valuation. In particular, absolutely special points exist.
statements.statement_latex: \text{Assume }G\text{ is quasi-split. Let }T\subset G\text{ be a maximally split maximal torus, let }\mathcal A\text{ be its apartment, and let }o\in\mathcal A\text{ be a Chevalley valuation. For each }x=o+v\in\mathcal A,\text{ the following are equivalent: }x\text{ is absolutely special; }a(v)\in v_a\mathbf Z\text{ for every non-divisible }a\in\Phi;\ x=t\cdot o\text{ for some }t\in T_{\mathrm{ad}}(k);\text{ and }x\text{ is a Chevalley valuation. In particular, absolutely special points exist.}
assumptions_latex: G\text{ is quasi-split}
T\subset G\text{ is a maximally split maximal torus}
\mathcal A\text{ is the apartment corresponding to }T
o\in\mathcal A\text{ is a Chevalley valuation}
x=o+v\in\mathcal A
statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[x\text{ is absolutely special}\bigr]\Longleftrightarrow\bigl[\forall a\in\Phi\text{ non-divisible},\ a(v)\in v_a\mathbf Z\bigr]\Longleftrightarrow\bigl[\exists t\in T_{\mathrm{ad}}(k),\ x=t\cdot o\bigr]\Longleftrightarrow\bigl[x\text{ is a Chevalley valuation}\bigr];\quad\text{in particular, absolutely special points exist.}

statements.title: Conjugacy of Hyperspecial Points and Parahoric Subgroups
statements.statement_plain: Any two hyperspecial points of the Bruhat-Tits building B(G) are conjugate under G_ad(k). Consequently, the corresponding hyperspecial parahoric subgroups of G(k) are conjugate under G_ad(k).

statements.title: Special points in a rank-one standard apartment
statements.statement_plain: In the standard apartment for the source's quasi-split simple rank-one group, a point is special when the a-root or 2a-root group filtration jumps there. Because every 2a-jump forces an a-jump, the point is special exactly when its a-coordinate lies in the jump set J_a. After identifying the apartment with the real line so that a is the identity, the special points are exactly the elements of J_a.
statements.statement_latex: For v\in\mathcal A, declare v to be special when at least one of the filtrations U_a(k)_{\langle a,v\rangle} and U_{2a}(k)_{\langle 2a,v\rangle} jumps at v, that is, when U_a(k)_{\langle a,v\rangle}\ne U_a(k)_{\langle a,v\rangle+} or U_{2a}(k)_{\langle 2a,v\rangle}\ne U_{2a}(k)_{\langle 2a,v\rangle+}. Since a 2a-jump implies an a-jump, v is special if and only if \langle a,v\rangle\in J_a. Under X_*(S)=\mathbf Z and \mathcal A=\mathbf R, with a the identity, this is equivalent to v\in J_a.
assumptions_latex: The setting is the standard apartment for the quasi-split simple rank-one group treated in the source chapter.
X_*(S)=\mathbf Z\text{ identifies }\mathcal A\text{ with }\mathbf R,\text{ and under this identification }a:\mathcal A\to\mathbf R\text{ is the identity.}

statements.title: Bruhat Double Cosets, Root-Subgroup Factorizations, and Standard Parabolics
statements.statement_plain: In the preceding root-datum setting, representatives in N and elements of the Weyl group parametrise the indicated positive-unipotent and TU+ double cosets. For each Weyl element w, the subgroup nU+n^{-1} intersected with U- equals the subgroup generated by root groups U_a for a in Phi- intersect w(Phi+), and this subgroup is independent of the chosen lift n; multiplication gives the stated U+, T, and U_w+ factorizations. An element of N carrying the positive chamber to its negative exchanges U+ and U-, giving the corresponding opposite double-coset bijections. For each subset X of simple roots, the subgroup U+ T W_X U+ is parabolic, and these subgroups are in bijection with subsets of the simple roots (equivalently, subgroups containing TU+).
statements.statement_latex: Assume the preceding root-datum setting (6.1.4), including properties (6.1.6) and (6.1.12). Then: (a) the injections of N and of the Weyl group {}^{v}W induce bijections N\xrightarrow{\sim}U^{+}\backslash G/U^{+} and {}^{v}W\xrightarrow{\sim}(TU^{+})\backslash G/(TU^{+}); (b) for w\in{}^{v}W and any lift n\in N, U_{w}^{+}:=nU^{+}n^{-1}\cap U^{-}=\langle U_{a}\mid a\in\Phi^{-}\cap w(\Phi^{+})\rangle is independent of n, and multiplication gives bijections U^{+}\times T\times U_{w}^{+}\xrightarrow{\sim}U^{+}TnU^{+} and U^{+}\times U_{w}^{+}\xrightarrow{\sim}U^{+}nU^{+}; (c) some n\in N interchanges U^{+} and U^{-} by conjugation, yielding bijections N\xrightarrow{\sim}U^{+}\backslash G/U^{-} and {}^{v}W\xrightarrow{\sim}(TU^{+})\backslash G/(TU^{-}); (d) for every X\subset\Pi, with {}^{v}W_{X}=\langle r_{a}\mid a\in X\rangle, the subgroup G_{X}=U^{+}T\,{}^{v}W_{X}U^{+} is parabolic, and X\mapsto G_{X} bijects \mathcal P(\Pi) with the subgroups of G containing TU^{+}.
assumptions_latex: Work in the preceding root-datum setting (6.1.4), with the properties (6.1.6) and (6.1.12) assumed there.
statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned} &\text{(a) The injections of }N\text{ and }{}^{v}W\text{ induce bijections }N\xrightarrow{\sim}U^{+}\backslash G/U^{+}\text{ and }{}^{v}W\xrightarrow{\sim}(TU^{+})\backslash G/(TU^{+}).\\ &\text{(b) For }w\in{}^{v}W\text{ and any }n\in N\text{ lifting }w,\ U_{w}^{+}:=nU^{+}n^{-1}\cap U^{-}=\langle U_{a}\mid a\in\Phi^{-}\cap w(\Phi^{+})\rangle\text{ is independent of the lift }n;\\ &\qquad (u,t,u')\mapsto utnu'\text{ and }(u,u')\mapsto unu'\text{ are bijections }U^{+}\times T\times U_{w}^{+}\xrightarrow{\sim}U^{+}TnU^{+},\ U^{+}\times U_{w}^{+}\xrightarrow{\sim}U^{+}nU^{+}.\\ &\text{(c) There exists }n\in N\text{ with }nU^{+}n^{-1}=U^{-}\text{ and }nU^{-}n^{-1}=U^{+};\text{ consequently }N\xrightarrow{\sim}U^{+}\backslash G/U^{-}\text{ and }{}^{v}W\xrightarrow{\sim}(TU^{+})\backslash G/(TU^{-}).\\ &\text{(d) For every }X\subset\Pi,\ {}^{v}W_{X}=\langle r_{a}\mid a\in X\rangle\text{ and }G_{X}=U^{+}T\,{}^{v}W_{X}U^{+}\text{ is parabolic; }X\mapsto G_{X}\text{ bijects }\mathcal P(\Pi)\text{ with the subgroups of }G\text{ containing }TU^{+}.\\end{aligned}

statements.title: Closed root-subset subgroup schemes and product decomposition of GL(M)
statements.statement_plain: For a closed set of positive or negative matrix-root indices, the associated product of root subgroup schemes forms a closed subgroup scheme B_Psi of GL(M). Multiplication with the diagonal subgroup gives a semidirect-product subgroup. Under the stated closure condition, adjoining one root subgroup gives a semidirect product in which B_Psi is normal. Multiplication of the individual root subgroup schemes onto B_Psi is an isomorphism for every ordering of the factors.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Psi\) be a closed subset of \(\Theta^{+}\) or \(\Theta^{-}\), and let \(\mathfrak B_{\Psi}\) be the image of \(\prod_{(i,j)\in\Psi}\mathfrak L_{ij}\) under \(x\mapsto1+x\). Then: (i) \(\mathfrak B_{\Psi}\) is a closed subgroup scheme of \(\mathfrak{GL}(M)\); (ii) multiplication identifies \(\mathfrak D\times\mathfrak B_{\Psi}\) by a closed immersion with a semidirect-product subgroup of \(\mathfrak{GL}(M)\); (iii) if \((i,j)\notin\Psi\) and \((j,k)\in\Psi\Rightarrow(i,k)\in\Psi\), then \(\Psi\cup\{(i,j)\}\) is closed and \(\mathfrak B_{\Psi\cup\{(i,j)\}}\) is the semidirect product of the root subgroup \(\mathfrak B_{ij}\) with \(\mathfrak B_{\Psi}\), with \(\mathfrak B_{\Psi}\) normal; (iv) multiplication of the individual \(\mathfrak B_{ij}\) over any ordering of \(\Psi\) is a scheme isomorphism onto \(\mathfrak B_{\Psi}\).
assumptions_latex: \(\Psi\) is a closed subset of \(\Theta^{+}\) or \(\Theta^{-}\).
For (iii), \((i,j)\in\Theta^{+}\) or \(\Theta^{-}\), \((i,j)\notin\Psi\), and whenever \((j,k)\in\Psi\) one has \((i,k)\in\Psi\).
statements.conclusion_latex: (i) The image of \(\prod_{(i,j)\in\Psi}\mathfrak L_{ij}\) under \(x\mapsto 1+x\) is a closed subgroup scheme \(\mathfrak B_{\Psi}\) of \(\mathfrak{GL}(M)\). (ii) Multiplication gives a closed immersion \(\mathfrak D\times\mathfrak B_{\Psi}\hookrightarrow\mathfrak{GL}(M)\) whose image is the corresponding semidirect-product subgroup. (iii) Under the stated condition, \(\Psi' = \Psi\cup\{(i,j)\}\) is closed and \(\mathfrak B_{\Psi'}\) is the semidirect product with factors \(\mathfrak B_{ij}\) and \(\mathfrak B_{\Psi}\) (with \(\mathfrak B_{\Psi}\) the normal factor). (iv) For every ordering of \(\Psi\), multiplication \(\prod_{(i,j)\in\Psi}\mathfrak B_{ij}\to\mathfrak B_{\Psi}\) is a scheme isomorphism.
statements.scope_note: Decompositions of the general linear group scheme associated with closed sets of positive or negative matrix-root indices.

statements.title: Nibbling orders on positively closed root subsets
statements.statement_plain: For a positively closed subset ψ of Φ, a nibbling order is a total order in which each element is extremal among the elements greater than it, meaning it is an extremal generator of the convex cone generated by those elements. Removing an extremal element leaves a positively closed subset, and every tail of a nibbling order is positively closed.
statements.statement_latex: For a positively closed subset \(\psi\) of \(\mathbf{\Phi}\), a nibbling order is a total order on \(\psi\) such that every element is extremal in the set of elements greater than it, i.e. an extremal generator of the convex cone generated by those greater elements. Removing an extremal element preserves positive closure, and every tail of a nibbling order is positively closed.
assumptions_latex: \(\psi\subseteq\mathbf{\Phi}\) is a positively closed subset.
\(\psi\) is equipped with a total order, written \((a_1,\ldots,a_r)\).
statements.conclusion_latex: A nibbling order on \(\psi\) is a total order such that each element of \(\psi\) is extremal among the elements of \(\psi\) greater than it, equivalently an extremal generator of the convex cone generated by those greater elements. If \(a\) is extremal in \(\psi\), then \(\psi\setminus\{a\}\) is positively closed. If \((a_1,\ldots,a_r)\) is a nibbling order on \(\psi\), then each tail \((a_i,\ldots,a_r)\) is positively closed.
statements.scope_note: Definition of nibbling orders and the stated positive-closure consequences for root subsets in schematic root-data constructions.

statements.title: Schematic Root Data From Root-Function Filtrations
statements.statement_plain: A function on the roots determines the schematic root-group schemes \(\mathfrak U_{f,a}\), using both f(a) and f(2a) for pluriel roots. Along with the canonical torus scheme (or its smooth locus), they form a schematic root datum. In the discrete valuation case one may normalize the function and optimize it by taking the indicated infima without changing the schemes; the corresponding products of filtered root groups stay equal. In the dense case the optimization equals the original function, while in the discrete case it may differ.
statements.statement_latex: Given the stated root-function hypotheses, define \(\mathfrak U_{f,a}\) from \(f(a)\) (and \(f(2a)\) for pluriel roots). Together with \(\mathfrak T\) (or its smooth locus), these schemes form a schematic root datum; discrete-case normalization and the optimization \(f'\) preserve the schemes and the displayed products of filtered root groups.
assumptions_latex: Let \(f:\Phi\to\mathbf R\). When \(\omega\) is dense, assume \(f(a)\in\Gamma'_a\) and \(f(2a)\le 2f(a)\) for all \(a\in\Phi\), with \(f(2a)=2f(a)\) when \(2a\notin\Phi\).
Define \(\mathfrak U_{f,a}=\mathfrak U_{a,f(a)}\) for non-pluriel \(a\), and \(\mathfrak U_{f,a}=\mathfrak U_{a,(f(a),f(2a))}\) for pluriel \(a\).
If \(\omega\) is discrete, replacing \(f\) by \(g\) with \(g(a)=f(a)\) when \(a/2\notin\Phi\), and \(g(a)=\inf\{f(a),2f(a/2)\}\) when \(a/2\in\Phi\), leaves every \(\mathfrak U_{f,a}\) unchanged.
For \(a\in\Phi\), define \(f'(a)=\inf\{k\in\Gamma'_a\mid k\ge f(a)\text{ or (if }a/2\in\Phi\text{) }k\ge 2f(a/2)\}\).
statements.conclusion_latex: The family \((\mathfrak U_{f,a})_{a\in\Phi}\), together with the canonical torus scheme \(\mathfrak T\) (or its smooth locus when it exists), forms a schematic root datum. Moreover, \(\mathfrak U_{f,a}(\mathcal O)=U_{a,f(a)}U_{2a,f(2a)}\), with \(U_{2a}=\{1\}\) for non-pluriel \(a\). The optimized function satisfies \(\mathfrak U_{f,a}=\mathfrak U_{f',a}\) and \(U_{a,f(a)}U_{2a,f(2a)}=U_{a,f'(a)}U_{2a,f'(2a)}\); if \(f\) satisfies (QC\(_0\)), then \(U_{2a,f(2a)}=U_{2a,f'(2a)}\). For dense \(\omega\), \(f'=f\); for discrete \(\omega\), \(f'\) may differ from \(f\). If \(f=f'\) (\(f\) is optimal), its values satisfy the relations cited in §4.3.5 and (QC\(_0\)).
statements.scope_note: Definition and normalization/optimization of schematic root-group schemes attached to a root-function on \(\Phi\), including their integral-point identities and dense/discrete valuation cases.

statements.title: Normalization preserving schematic root subgroup schemes
statements.statement_plain: When omega is discrete, replace f(a) by the infimum of f(a) and 2f(a/2) whenever a/2 is a root, leaving f(a) unchanged otherwise. This does not change any associated schematic root subgroup scheme. One may therefore impose condition QC_o with the quantifier stated in the source. When omega is dense, condition Sch implies QC_o.
statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\omega\) is discrete. Define \(g(a)=f(a)\) when \(a/2\notin\Phi\), and \(g(a)=\inf\{f(a),2f(a/2)\}\) when \(a,a/2\in\Phi\). Then \(\mathfrak U_{f,a}=\mathfrak U_{g,a}\) for all \(a\in\Phi\). Consequently one may reduce to functions satisfying \((QC_o)\), namely \(f(2a)\leq\inf\bigl(\Gamma_{2a}\cap[2f(a),+\infty[\bigr)\) for every \(a\in\Phi\). Moreover, when \(\omega\) is dense, \((Sch)\) implies \((QC_o)\).
assumptions_latex: For the normalization, \(\omega\) is discrete and \(f\) is defined on \(\Phi\).
Define \(g(a)=f(a)\) for \(a\in\Phi\) with \(a/2\notin\Phi\), and \(g(a)=\inf\{f(a),2f(a/2)\}\) for \(a,a/2\in\Phi\).
statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak U_{f,a}=\mathfrak U_{g,a}\) for every \(a\in\Phi\), so one may reduce to the condition \((QC_o)\): \(f(2a)\leq\inf\bigl(\Gamma_{2a}\cap[2f(a),+\infty[\bigr)\) for every \(a\in\Phi\). When \(\omega\) is dense, \((Sch)\) implies \((QC_o)\).
statements.scope_note: Normalization of a root-system function without changing its associated schematic root subgroup schemes; the discrete normalization and the dense-valuation implication are distinct clauses.

statements.title: Schematic closure in an integral model
statements.statement_plain: For a closed subscheme Y of X in an integral model Xcal over o, its schematic closure Ycal is an integral model of Y. For every flat o-algebra R, Ycal(R) equals Xcal(R) intersected with Y(R tensor_o k) inside X(R tensor_o k). Taking generic fibers bijects closed flat subschemes of Xcal with closed subschemes of X, and schematic closure is the inverse.
statements.statement_latex: Let Y\subset X be a closed subscheme and let \mathcal{X} be an integral model of X over \mathfrak{o}. If \mathcal{Y} is the schematic closure of Y in \mathcal{X}, then (1) \mathcal{Y} is an integral model of Y; (2) for every flat \mathfrak{o}-algebra R, \mathcal{Y}(R)=\mathcal{X}(R)\cap Y(R\otimes_{\mathfrak{o}}k) inside X(R\otimes_{\mathfrak{o}}k); and (3) taking generic fiber \mathcal{Y}\mapsto\mathcal{Y}_k gives a bijection between closed flat subschemes of \mathcal{X} and closed subschemes of X, inverse to schematic closure.
assumptions_latex: Y\subset X is a closed subscheme.
\mathcal{X} is an integral model of X over \mathfrak{o}.
R is a flat \mathfrak{o}-algebra (for clause (2)).
statements.conclusion_latex: (1) The schematic closure \mathcal{Y} of Y in \mathcal{X} is an integral model of Y. (2) For every flat \mathfrak{o}-algebra R, \mathcal{Y}(R)=\mathcal{X}(R)\cap Y(R\otimes_{\mathfrak{o}}k), with the intersection taken in X(R\otimes_{\mathfrak{o}}k). (3) The generic-fiber map \mathcal{Y}\mapsto\mathcal{Y}_k is a bijection from closed flat subschemes of \mathcal{X} to closed subschemes of X, with inverse given by schematic closure in \mathcal{X}.
statements.scope_note: Integral models over \mathfrak{o} and schematic closures of closed subschemes.

statements.title: Schematic closure model and bounded points of a torus
statements.statement_plain: For a torus T over the fraction field K, embed it into the Weil restriction of a split form and take the schematic closure in the canonical integral model. The closure is a flat finite-type O-group scheme with generic fiber T, and its O-valued points equal the bounded subgroup T_b(K), equivalently the intersection of T(K) with the bounded points of the induced ambient torus.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal O\) be a Prüferian domain with fraction field \(K\), and let \(T\) be a torus defined over \(K\), not necessarily induced (the source states it is split over \(K\)). Using the canonical closed immersion \(T\hookrightarrow T^{\sharp}:=\Pi_{\widetilde K/K}T_{\widetilde K}\) with \(T_{\widetilde K}\) split, let \(\mathfrak T^{\sharp}\) be the canonical finite-type \(\mathcal O\)-model of \(T^{\sharp}\), and let \(\mathfrak T^{a}\) be the schematic closure of \(T\) in \(\mathfrak T^{\sharp}\). Then \(\mathfrak T^{a}\) is a flat finite-type \(\mathcal O\)-group scheme with generic fiber \(T\), and \[\mathfrak T^{a}(\mathcal O)=\mathfrak T^{\sharp}(\mathcal O)\cap T(K)=T_b^{\sharp}(K)\cap T(K)=T_b(K).\]
assumptions_latex: \mathcal O\text{ is a Prüferian domain with fraction field }K.
T\text{ is a torus defined over }K,\text{ not necessarily induced; the source states it is split over }K.

\widetilde K/K\text{ is the extension used in }T^{\sharp}:=\Pi_{\widetilde K/K}T_{\widetilde K},\text{ with }T_{\widetilde K}\text{ split, and }T\hookrightarrow T^{\sharp}\text{ is the canonical closed immersion}.
\mathfrak T^{\sharp}\text{ is the canonical finite-type }\mathcal O\text{-model with generic fiber }T^{\sharp}.
\mathfrak T^{a}\text{ is the schematic closure of }T\text{ in }\mathfrak T^{\sharp}.
statements.conclusion_latex: \mathfrak T^{a}\text{ is a flat finite-type }\mathcal O\text{-group scheme with generic fiber }T,\qquad \mathfrak T^{a}(\mathcal O)=\mathfrak T^{\sharp}(\mathcal O)\cap T(K)=T_b^{\sharp}(K)\cap T(K)=T_b(K).
statements.scope_note: The bounded-subgroup notation \(T_b(K)\) and \(T_b^{\sharp}(K)\) is retained locally from the source; the intersection is taken inside \(T^{\sharp}(K)\).

statements.title: Naive restriction of schemes is left adjoint to base change
statements.statement_plain: For a morphism of schemes Z'→Z, composing X→Z' with Z'→Z gives a Z-scheme X|_Z, called naive restriction. This functor is left adjoint to base change along Z'→Z; for affine schemes it is the corresponding forgetful functor on algebras.
statements.statement_latex: Given a morphism of schemes \(Z'\to Z\), define \(\operatorname{Res}^{\mathrm{naive}}_{Z'/Z}:\mathrm{Sch}/Z'\to\mathrm{Sch}/Z\) by \(X\mapsto X|_Z\), where \(X|_Z\) has structure map \(X\to Z'\to Z\). Then \(\operatorname{Res}^{\mathrm{naive}}_{Z'/Z}\) is left adjoint to \((-)\times_Z Z':\mathrm{Sch}/Z\to\mathrm{Sch}/Z'\).
assumptions_latex: Z'\to Z\text{ is a morphism of schemes}
X\text{ is a }Z'\text{-scheme}
statements.conclusion_latex: The naive restriction functor \(X\mapsto X|_Z\), obtained by composing \(X\to Z'\to Z\), is left adjoint to the base-change functor \((-)\times_Z Z'\).
statements.scope_note: For a morphism of schemes Z'→Z, regards each Z'-scheme as a Z-scheme via composition. In the affine case, this is the forgetful functor that retains the ring while restricting its structure algebra.

statements.title: Weil restriction (scalar restriction) of an affine scheme
statements.statement_plain: Given a ring map A to B and an affine scheme X over B, the scalar restriction (Weil restriction) from B to A is an A-scheme X#, denoted Pi_{B/A}X, unique up to unique isomorphism. It represents the functor sending each A-algebra R to the set of X-points over B tensor_A R; equivalently, maps from any A-scheme Y to X# correspond to B-maps from its base change Y_B to X.
statements.statement_latex: For an affine B-scheme \mathfrak{X}, its scalar restriction (Weil restriction) from B to A is the A-scheme \Pi_{B/A}\mathfrak{X}=\mathfrak{X}^{\#}, unique up to unique isomorphism, characterized naturally by \mathfrak{X}^{\#}(R)\cong\mathfrak{X}(B\otimes_A R) for every A-algebra R; equivalently, \operatorname{Mor}_A(\mathfrak{Y},\mathfrak{X}^{\#})\cong\operatorname{Mor}_B(\mathfrak{Y}_B,\mathfrak{X}) for every A-scheme \mathfrak{Y}.
assumptions_latex: A\to B is a ring homomorphism, and R is an A-algebra (so B\otimes_A R is defined).
\mathfrak{X} is an affine B-scheme.
statements.conclusion_latex: There exists an A-scheme \mathfrak{X}^{\#}, unique up to unique isomorphism, representing the functor R\mapsto\mathfrak{X}(B\otimes_A R) on A-algebras; equivalently, for every A-scheme \mathfrak{Y}, \operatorname{Mor}_A(\mathfrak{Y},\mathfrak{X}^{\#})\cong\operatorname{Mor}_B(\mathfrak{Y}_B,\mathfrak{X}). It is denoted \Pi_{B/A}\mathfrak{X} (or \mathfrak{X}^{\#}).

statements.title: Base-change compatibility and injectivity for distributions
statements.statement_plain: For an A-algebra B, distributions at a section commute with base change: B tensor the distributions of X at s maps bijectively to the distributions of the base-changed scheme X' at the induced section s'. If moreover \(\mathrm{A}\subset\mathrm{B}\), then the canonical map \({}^{s}\!\operatorname{Dist}(\mathfrak X)\to{}^{s'}\!\operatorname{Dist}({\mathfrak X}')\) is injective.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathrm{B}\) is an \(\mathrm{A}\)-algebra, and \({\mathfrak X}'\) and \(s'\) are obtained from \((\mathfrak X,s)\) by base change.

statements.conclusion_latex: The canonical map \(\mathrm{B}\otimes {}^{s}\!\operatorname{Dist}(\mathfrak X)\to{}^{s'}\!\operatorname{Dist}({\mathfrak X}')\) is bijective. statements.title: Canonical integral model of an induced torus equals its flat closure
statements.statement_plain: For an induced torus over the fraction field of a discrete valuation ring, the canonical integral model agrees with the canonical flat-closure model. In the basic case \(T=\Pi_{L/K}\mathfrak{Mult}_{L}\) for a finite separable extension \(L/K\), the model \(\mathfrak T=\Pi_{\mathcal O_L/\mathcal O}\mathfrak{Mult}_{\sigma_L}\) has this equality; the general induced-torus case follows by products and analogous operations.

statements.title: Base Change of Distributions at a Section
statements.statement_plain: After base change from A to B, powers of the ideal defining a section correspond to the images of the original ideal powers, and the quotient coordinate rings identify by tensor product. Duality gives canonical base-change maps for finite-order and full distributions. For the source's specialization B = K, both natural maps are injective, and the distribution base-change map is an isomorphism when the scheme is finite type over A.
statements.statement_latex: Let B be an A-algebra and let (\mathfrak X',s') be obtained from (\mathfrak X,s) by base change A\to B. For each order m, the power I(s')^m of the section ideal is the canonical image of B\otimes_A I(s)^m in B[\mathfrak X'], and B[\mathfrak X']/I(s')^m is canonically identified with B\otimes_A(A[\mathfrak X]/I(s)^m). Duality induces canonical B-linear maps B\otimes_A{}^s\!\operatorname{Dist}_m\mathfrak X\to{}^{s'}\!\operatorname{Dist}_m\mathfrak X' and B\otimes_A{}^s\!\operatorname{Dist}\mathfrak X\to{}^{s'}\!\operatorname{Dist}\mathfrak X'. For B=K, the maps {}^s\!\operatorname{Dist}\mathfrak X\to K\otimes_A{}^s\!\operatorname{Dist}\mathfrak X and K\otimes_A{}^s\!\operatorname{Dist}\mathfrak X\to{}^{s'}\!\operatorname{Dist}\mathfrak X_K are injective; when \mathfrak X is of finite type over A, the latter map is bijective.
assumptions_latex: B\text{ is an }A\text{-algebra};\quad \mathfrak X'=\mathfrak X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}B,\text{ with }s'\text{ induced by }s.
m\text{ is the order parameter in }I(s)^m\text{ and }{}^s\!\operatorname{Dist}_m.
B=K\text{ for the stated injectivity assertions, with }K\text{ having the source's standing meaning}.
\mathfrak X\text{ is of finite type over }A\text{ for the final bijectivity assertion.}
statements.conclusion_latex: I(s')^m=\operatorname{im}\!\left(B\otimes_A I(s)^m\to B[\mathfrak X']\right),\qquad B[\mathfrak X']/I(s')^m\cong B\otimes_A\bigl(A[\mathfrak X]/I(s)^m\bigr).\ \text{These identifications induce canonical }B\text{-linear maps }B\otimes_A{}^s\!\operatorname{Dist}_m\mathfrak X\to{}^{s'}\!\operatorname{Dist}_m\mathfrak X'\text{ and }B\otimes_A{}^s\!\operatorname{Dist}\mathfrak X\to{}^{s'}\!\operatorname{Dist}\mathfrak X'.\ \text{For }B=K,\ {}^s\!\operatorname{Dist}\mathfrak X\to K\otimes_A{}^s\!\operatorname{Dist}\mathfrak X\text{ and }K\otimes_A{}^s\!\operatorname{Dist}\mathfrak X\to{}^{s'}\!\operatorname{Dist}\mathfrak X_K\text{ are injective; if }\mathfrak X\text{ is finite type, the latter is bijective.}

statements.title: Dynamic-Method Subgroup-Scheme Properties
statements.statement_plain: For a cocharacter of a group scheme, the positive-limit (parabolic) functor is represented by a closed subgroup scheme and its zero-evaluation kernel is closed normal. The fixed-point subgroup is the scheme-theoretic intersection of the positive and negative limit subgroups. These constructions commute with arbitrary base change and restrict by scheme-theoretic intersection to stable closed subgroup schemes. For quotient maps between connected finite-type group schemes over a field, the induced maps on the three subgroups are faithfully flat and surjective. When the group scheme is finite type over the base, every fiber of the unipotent subgroup scheme is unipotent.
statements.statement_latex: For a cocharacter \(\lambda:\mathbf G_m\to\mathcal G\), the dynamic-method subgroup schemes \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal G}(\lambda)\), \(\mathcal U_{\mathcal G}(\lambda)\), and \(\mathcal Z_{\mathcal G}(\lambda)\) satisfy the six representability, scheme-theoretic intersection, base-change, stable-subgroup, quotient, and unipotent-fiber assertions listed in the conclusion.
assumptions_latex: \(\lambda:\mathbf G_m\to\mathcal G\) is a cocharacter of the group scheme \(\mathcal G\) over a base ring \(A\).
For clause (4), \(\mathcal H\) is a closed subgroup scheme of \(\mathcal G\) stable under the induced \(\mathbf G_m\)-action.
For clause (5), \(A\) is a field; \(\mathcal G\) and \(\mathcal H\) are connected and of finite type; and \(\mathcal G\to\mathcal H\) is a quotient map (faithfully flat and surjective).
For clause (6), \(\mathcal G\) is of finite type over \(A\).
statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal G}(\lambda)\) is represented by a closed subgroup scheme of \(\mathcal G\), and \(\mathcal U_{\mathcal G}(\lambda)\) by a closed normal subgroup scheme of \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal G}(\lambda)\); \(\mathcal Z_{\mathcal G}(\lambda)=\mathcal P_{\mathcal G}(\lambda)\cap\mathcal P_{\mathcal G}(-\lambda)\) scheme-theoretically and is the scheme-theoretic centralizer of \(\lambda\) in \(\mathcal G\); formation of \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal G}\), \(\mathcal U_{\mathcal G}\), and \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\) commutes with arbitrary extensions of the base ring; for every \(\mathbf G_m\)-stable closed subgroup scheme \(\mathcal H\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal H}=\mathcal P_{\mathcal G}\cap\mathcal H\), \(\mathcal U_{\mathcal H}=\mathcal U_{\mathcal G}\cap\mathcal H\), and \(\mathcal Z_{\mathcal H}=\mathcal Z_{\mathcal G}\cap\mathcal H\) scheme-theoretically; under the clause (5) hypotheses, the induced maps on \(\mathcal P\), \(\mathcal U\), and \(\mathcal Z\) are faithfully flat and surjective; under the clause (6) hypothesis, every fiber of \(\mathcal U_{\mathcal G}(\lambda)\) is unipotent.
statements.scope_note: Dynamic-method subgroup schemes attached to a cocharacter, with representability, fixed-point/centralizer intersection, arbitrary base change, stable-subgroup compatibility, quotient functoriality under the stated field hypotheses, and unipotent fibers under finite-type hypotheses.

statements.title: Unique Extension Criterion for Affine Model Morphisms
statements.statement_plain: For affine models over the valuation ring o with generic fibers X and Y, a morphism theta from X to Y extends to the models exactly when its pullback maps the Y-model coordinate subalgebra into the X-model coordinate subalgebra; such an extension is unique.
statements.statement_latex: For affine \mathfrak{o}-schemes \mathcal{X},\mathcal{Y} with generic fibers X,Y and a morphism \theta:X\rightarrow Y, an extension \widetilde{\theta}:\mathcal{X}\rightarrow\mathcal{Y} exists if and only if \theta^*(\mathfrak{o}[\mathcal{Y}])\subseteq\mathfrak{o}[\mathcal{X}], and when it exists it is unique.

\theta:X\rightarrow Y is a morphism inducing \theta^*:k[Y]\rightarrow k[X].
statements.conclusion_latex: There is at most one extension \widetilde{\theta}:\mathcal{X}\rightarrow\mathcal{Y}; such an extension exists if and only if \theta^*(\mathfrak{o}[\mathcal{Y}])\subseteq\mathfrak{o}[\mathcal{X}].

statements.title: Identities for successive dilatations
statements.statement_plain: For the successive dilatations of a smooth affine group scheme at its trivial subgroup, the congruence subgroups have trivial intersection, each dilated coordinate ring is obtained by adjoining the appropriately rescaled identity ideal, its points over a flat algebra shift the congruence level by the dilatation index, and its Lie lattice is the corresponding power-of-the-maximal-ideal scaling of the original Lie lattice.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\subset\mathfrak o[\mathcal G]\) be the ideal of the trivial subgroup. For the successive dilatations \(\mathcal G_n\), one has \(\bigcap_n\mathcal G(\mathfrak m^n)=\{1\}\), \(\mathfrak o[\mathcal G_n]=\mathfrak o[\mathcal G][\pi^{-n}I]\subset k[\mathcal G]\), \(\mathcal G_n(\mathcal M_R^m)=\mathcal G(\mathcal M_R^{m+n})\subset\mathcal G(R\otimes_{\mathfrak o}k)\) for every flat \(\mathfrak o\)-algebra \(R\) with \(\mathcal M_R=\mathfrak mR\), and \(\operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal G_n)=\operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal G)\otimes_{\mathfrak o}\mathfrak m^n\subset\operatorname{Lie}(G)\).
assumptions_latex: \(\mathfrak o\) is a discretely valued ring with maximal ideal \(\mathfrak m\), uniformizer \(\pi\), and fraction field \(k\); \(\mathcal G\) is a smooth affine group scheme over \(\mathfrak o\) with generic fiber \(G\), and \(\mathcal G_n\) denotes its successive dilatations at the trivial subgroup.
For the identity involving \(R\), the \(\mathfrak o\)-algebra \(R\) is flat and \(\mathcal M_R=\mathfrak mR\).
statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigcap_n\mathcal G(\mathfrak m^n)=\{1\}\); \(\mathfrak o[\mathcal G_n]=\mathfrak o[\mathcal G][\pi^{-n}I]\) as subrings of \(k[\mathcal G]\), where \(I\subset\mathfrak o[\mathcal G]\) is the ideal of the trivial subgroup; \(\mathcal G_n(\mathcal M_R^m)=\mathcal G(\mathcal M_R^{m+n})\) inside \(\mathcal G(R\otimes_{\mathfrak o}k)\); and \(\operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal G_n)=\operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal G)\otimes_{\mathfrak o}\mathfrak m^n\) as lattices inside \(\operatorname{Lie}(G)\).
statements.scope_note: Four structural identities for the successive dilatations at the trivial subgroup of a smooth affine group scheme over a discretely valued base.

statements.title: Schematic bounded subgroups and unique Galois descent of integral models
statements.statement_plain: For a smooth affine k-group X, a bounded open subgroup U of X(K) is schematic exactly when it is the O-points of an integral model of X, which need not be smooth. If U is stable under Gal(K/k), that integral model descends uniquely to an integral model of X.
statements.statement_latex: Let X be a smooth affine k-group and let \mathcal{U}\subset X(K) be a bounded open subgroup. Then \mathcal{U} is schematic if and only if there exists an integral model \mathcal{X} of X, not necessarily smooth, with \mathcal{X}(\mathcal{O})=\mathcal{U}. If \mathcal{U} is stable under \operatorname{Gal}(K/k), then \mathcal{X} uniquely descends to an integral model of X.
assumptions_latex: X is a smooth affine k-group.
\mathcal{U}\subset X(K) is a bounded open subgroup.
\mathcal{O} denotes the valuation ring used for the integral model's points.
For the descent clause, \mathcal{U} is stable under \operatorname{Gal}(K/k).
statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal{U} is schematic if and only if there exists an integral model \mathcal{X} of X, not necessarily smooth, such that \mathcal{X}(\mathcal{O})=\mathcal{U}; if \mathcal{U} is stable under \operatorname{Gal}(K/k), then \mathcal{X} uniquely descends to an integral model of X.
statements.scope_note: Characterization of schematic bounded open subgroups of a smooth affine k-group by integral models, together with unique Galois descent under subgroup stability.

statements.title: Universal Property of Smoothening
statements.statement_plain: The natural morphism from the smoothening of X to X is universal for homomorphisms from smooth group schemes: every such homomorphism factors uniquely through the smoothening. If the original homomorphism is a closed immersion, its factor through the smoothening is also a closed immersion.
statements.statement_latex: Let i^{\infty}:\mathcal X^{\infty}\to\mathcal X be the natural morphism. For every smooth group scheme \mathcal Z and homomorphism f:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal X, there exists a unique homomorphism f^{\infty}:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal X^{\infty} such that f=i^{\infty}\circ f^{\infty}. If f is a closed immersion, then f^{\infty} is a closed immersion.
assumptions_latex: i^{\infty}:\mathcal X^{\infty}\to\mathcal X\text{ is the natural smoothening morphism}
\mathcal Z\text{ is a smooth group scheme}
f:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal X\text{ is a homomorphism}
statements.conclusion_latex: \exists!\,f^{\infty}:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal X^{\infty}\text{ with }f=i^{\infty}\circ f^{\infty};\quad f\text{ a closed immersion}\Rightarrow f^{\infty}\text{ a closed immersion}.
statements.scope_note: Universal property of the natural morphism from the smoothening \(\mathcal X^{\infty}\) to \(\mathcal X\).

statements.title: Structure and product decomposition of a connected parahoric integral model
statements.statement_plain: For the connected parahoric model attached to Omega, its torus model is maximal. For every root a, U_{a,Omega,0} is an open bounded schematic connected subgroup of U_a(K), and its smooth model is the corresponding root group of the parahoric model. Products of the nondivisible positive and negative root-group models are smooth closed subgroup schemes with unipotent fibers, independently of factor order; multiplication of the negative root groups, the torus model T^0, and the positive root groups into G_Omega^0 is an open immersion.
statements.statement_latex: For the connected parahoric integral model \(\mathcal G_{\Omega}^{0}\) attached to \(\Omega\), with maximal \(K\)-split torus \(S\) and root system \(\Phi=\Phi^{+}\sqcup\Phi^{-}\) (\(\Phi^{-}=-\Phi^{+}\)), the torus, root-group models, and their products satisfy the assertions stated below.

statements.title: Integral Model at the Unique Special Fixed Vertex
statements.statement_plain: If a reductive d-group scheme has generic fiber G, then G splits over K and G(K) has a Bruhat-Tits building. Its integral points fix exactly one point x; that point is a special vertex, and the model over O is isomorphic to the connected parahoric group scheme at x.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{G}\) be a reductive \(\mathfrak{d}\)-group scheme with generic fiber \(G\). Then \(G\) splits over \(K\), and there is a Bruhat--Tits building \(\mathcal{B}(G_K)\) for \(G(K)\). A unique point \(x\in\mathcal{B}(G_K)\) is fixed by \(\mathcal{G}(\mathcal{O})\); the identity automorphism of \(G_K\) extends to an \(\mathcal{O}\)-isomorphism \(\mathcal{G}_{\mathcal{O}}\cong\mathcal{G}_{x}^{0}\), and \(x\) is a special vertex.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal{G}\) is a reductive \(\mathfrak{d}\)-group scheme.
\(G\) is the generic fiber of \(\mathcal{G}\).
statements.conclusion_latex: \(G\) splits over \(K\), so \(G(K)\) has a Bruhat--Tits building \(\mathcal{B}(G_K)\). There is a unique point \(x\in\mathcal{B}(G_K)\) fixed by \(\mathcal{G}(\mathcal{O})\); the identity automorphism of \(G_K\) extends to an \(\mathcal{O}\)-isomorphism \(\mathcal{G}_{\mathcal{O}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal{G}_{x}^{0}\), and \(x\) is a special vertex of \(\mathcal{B}(G_K)\).
statements.scope_note: The proposition identifies the reductive integral model with the connected parahoric model attached to its unique integral-point-fixed special vertex.

statements.title: Functor-of-Points Definition by Lambda-Parameterized Limits
statements.statement_plain: For every test ring R, P_G(lambda) is the closed subgroup functor consisting of elements g in G(R) whose limit under t acting on g as t approaches 0 exists. U_G(lambda) consists of those elements for which that limit equals the identity element 1.

For each test ring \(R\), the subgroup functor \(\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{G}}(\lambda)\) (a closed subgroup) and the subgroup functor \(\mathcal{U}_{\mathcal{G}}(\lambda)\) are defined by
\[
\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{G}}(\lambda)(R)=\{g\in\mathcal{G}(R)\mid \lim_{t\to0} t\cdot g\ \text{exists}\},
\qquad
\mathcal{U}_{\mathcal{G}}(\lambda)(R)=\{g\in\mathcal{G}(R)\mid \lim_{t\to0} t\cdot g=1\}.
\]

statements.title: Integral points and normalizer subgroups attached to a quasi-concave function
statements.statement_plain: For the integral models and subgroups attached to a quasi-concave function f, each modeled root group on integral points equals its filtered root group, and the corresponding positive and negative unipotent groups agree as well. The torus subgroup at zero is H intersected with G^1. The groups P_f^0 and P_f^1 lie in the indicated integral-point groups, with P_f^1 equal to P_f intersected with G^1. Their normalizer intersections factor through H^0 and H^1 and all have the same valuation image W_f. In general, N_f^1 is not equal to N_f intersected with G^1.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be quasi-concave, with \(U_f\) generated by the \(U_{f,a}\), \(U_f^{\pm}\) generated by the \(U_{f,a}\) for \(a\in\Phi^{\pm}\), \(N_f=U_f\cap N(K)\), \(P_f=HU_f\), \(H=\ker(v:N(K)\to W)\), and \(G^1=\ker\theta\). Then \(\mathfrak U_{f,a}(\mathcal O)=U_{f,a}=U_{a,f(a)}\cdot U_{2a,f(2a)}\) for every \(a\in\Phi\), and \(\mathfrak U_f^{\pm}(\mathcal O)=U_f^{\pm}\). Moreover, \(\mathfrak T(0)=\ker v\cap\ker\theta=H\cap G^1=:H^1\). Defining \(H^0:=\mathfrak T^0(\mathcal O)\), \(P_f^0:=H^0U_f\), and \(P_f^1:=H^1U_f\), one has \(P_f^0\subseteq\mathfrak G_f^0(\mathcal O)\), \(P_f^1\subseteq\mathfrak G_f(\mathcal O)\), and \(P_f^1=P_f\cap G^1\). Finally, \(N_f^0:=P_f^0\cap N(K)=H^0N_f\), \(N_f^1:=P_f^1\cap N(K)=H^1N_f^0=H^1N_f\), and \(W_f:=v(N_f^0)=v(N_f^1)=v(N_f)\); in general, \(N_f^1\ne N_f\cap G^1\).
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is quasi-concave; }U_f\text{ and }U_f^{\pm}\text{ are generated by the root subgroups }U_{f,a}\text{ as stated.}
N_f=U_f\cap N(K),\quad P_f=HU_f,\quad H=\ker\bigl(v:N(K)\to W\bigr),\quad G^1=\ker\theta.
statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{gathered}\mathfrak U_{f,a}(\mathcal O)=U_{f,a}=U_{a,f(a)}\cdot U_{2a,f(2a)}\quad(a\in\Phi),\\ \mathfrak U_f^{\pm}(\mathcal O)=U_f^{\pm},\qquad \mathfrak T(0)=\ker v\cap\ker\theta=H\cap G^1=:H^1,\\ H^0:=\mathfrak T^0(\mathcal O),\quad P_f^0:=H^0U_f\subseteq\mathfrak G_f^0(\mathcal O),\quad P_f^1:=H^1U_f\subseteq\mathfrak G_f(\mathcal O),\quad P_f^1=P_f\cap G^1,\\ N_f^0:=P_f^0\cap N(K)=H^0N_f,\quad N_f^1:=P_f^1\cap N(K)=H^1N_f^0=H^1N_f,\\ W_f:=v(N_f^0)=v(N_f^1)=v(N_f),\qquad N_f^1\ne N_f\cap G^1\text{ in general.}\end{gathered}

statements.title: Smooth concave-function models and their open product chart
statements.statement_plain: Let f be a concave function on the extended root system with no infinite values. The associated subgroup is schematic and connected, and its corresponding smooth model has connected fibers. Every root-group morphism extends to a closed immersion of the corresponding integral root-group model. For either sign, multiplying the nondivisible-root factors in any order gives the same smooth closed subgroup scheme, whose fibers are unipotent. Multiplication from the negative-root factors, the torus model at f(0), and the positive-root factors into the model is an open immersion.

statements.title: Distribution algebra of an A-group scheme
statements.statement_plain: Let X be an A-group scheme with identity section e. The distributions on X supported at e form an associative A-algebra, which need not be commutative. Its unit is e*, its multiplication is induced by pullback along the group multiplication map, and the multiplication is compatible with the filtration by distributions on the infinitesimal neighborhoods indexed by m.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathfrak{X}\) be an \(A\)-group scheme with identity section \(e\), and set \(\operatorname{Dist}(\mathfrak{X})={}^e\!\operatorname{Dist}(\mathfrak{X})\). The multiplication morphism \(\pi:\mathfrak{X}\times\mathfrak{X}\to\mathfrak{X}\) gives \(\operatorname{Dist}(\mathfrak{X})\) the structure of an associative, not necessarily commutative, \(A\)-algebra with unit \(e^*\), compatible with its filtration by \(\operatorname{Dist}({}_m\mathfrak{X})\). For \(\delta,\delta'\in\operatorname{Dist}(\mathfrak{X})\), the product is \(\delta\delta'=(\delta\otimes\delta')\circ\pi^*\).
assumptions_latex: \(\mathfrak{X}\) is an \(A\)-group scheme.
\(e\) is the identity section of \(\mathfrak{X}\).

statements.title: Faithful representation can be normalized to dominant torus weights
statements.statement_plain: A faithful representation on a finite-type projective A-module decomposes into irreducible torus components. Over K_s, the distinct characters in each component form a single Galois orbit. Twisting by a sufficiently large power of chi and adjoining chi preserves faithfulness and makes every torus weight dominant, so the representation can be chosen with only dominant torus weights.
statements.statement_latex: Given a faithful finite-type projective A-module representation sigma, write V=K\otimes_A M_0 as a sum of irreducible Z-components. After extension to K_s, the distinct characters lambda_{j,k} in each component are transitively permuted by Gamma. For sufficiently large n making lambda_{j,k}\chi^n dominant, the replacement sigma'=((sigma\otimes\chi^n)\oplus\chi) on M'_0=((M_0\otimes(\otimes^n D))\oplus D) remains faithful, so all torus weights may be assumed dominant.
assumptions_latex: M_0 is a projective A-module of finite type, and sigma is a faithful linear representation of the represented group on M_0.
V=K\otimes_A M_0; Z is a torus, and the represented group is quasi-split over K.
K_s/K has Galois group Gamma; for each irreducible Z-component V_j, the characters lambda_{j,k} occurring after extension to K_s are pairwise distinct and transitively permuted by Gamma.
n is chosen sufficiently large so that every lambda_{j,k} chi^n is dominant.
statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing sigma by sigma'=((sigma\otimes\chi^n)\oplus\chi) on M'_0=((M_0\otimes(\otimes^n D))\oplus D) preserves faithfulness and yields a representation whose torus weights lambda_{j,k}\chi^n are all dominant; thus sigma may be assumed to have only dominant weights.
statements.scope_note: Representation-theoretic normalization used in constructing a faithful module, including complete reducibility of torus components and Galois permutation of weights.

statements.title: Intrinsic Quadratic Subextension and Norm-One Criterion for a Plural Radical Ray
statements.statement_plain: For a plural (multipliable) radical ray a, the image of L2 in End(Ua/U2a) under the pinning-defined field isomorphism is independent of the pinning; call it L2a, giving a quadratic extension La/L2a. A K-rational element of the connected normalizer of Ua in the adjoint group induces a scalar c(g) on Ua/U2a, and it acts identically on U2a exactly when c(g) has norm one from La to L2a.
statements.statement_latex: For a plural radical ray a, the image L_{2a}:=\iota_{\bar{x}_a}(L_2) in L_a=\operatorname{End}(U_a/U_{2a}) is independent of the pinning \bar{x}_a, so L_a/L_{2a} is quadratic. For every K-rational element g of the connected normalizer of U_a in the adjoint group of G, if c(g) is its induced scalar on U_a/U_{2a}, then g acts identically on U_{2a} if and only if N_{L_a/L_{2a}}(c(g))=1.

g\in N_{\operatorname{Ad}(G)}(U_a)^{\circ}(K), and c(g)\in L_a^{\times} is the scalar induced by g on U_a/U_{2a}.

statements.title: Length-m Witt vector functor
statements.statement_plain: For an F_p-algebra A and m>=1, the length-m Witt vectors W_m(A)=A^m carry addition and multiplication defined by the universal Witt polynomials S_i and P_i, with zero (0,...,0) and one (1,0,...,0); by convention W_0(A)={0}. The Teichmuller map [a]=(a,0,...,0) is multiplicative, and the sum of [a_i]p^i has coordinates (a_0,a_1^p,...,a_{m-1}^{p^{m-1}}). If A is perfect, every Witt vector has a unique such expansion and p^iW_m(A) consists exactly of vectors whose first i entries vanish (for i<=m); if A is not perfect, both assertions fail.
statements.statement_latex: \text{For an }\mathbf F_p\text{-algebra }A\text{ and }m\ge1,\ W_m(A)=A^m\text{ is endowed with Witt operations via }S_i,P_i\text{, with the stated identities and Teichmuller/ideal properties; }W_0(A)=\{0\}.
assumptions_latex: A\text{ is an }\mathbf F_p\text{-algebra and }m\ge 1\text{ for the construction }W_m(A)=A^m.
W_0(A):=\{0\}\text{ by convention}.
For the unique Teichmuller expansion and the ideal characterization, }A\text{ is perfect, i.e. }a\mapsto a^p\text{ is bijective};\text{ when }A\text{ is not perfect, both assertions fail.
statements.conclusion_latex: W_m(A)=A^m\text{ with }(a_0,\ldots,a_{m-1})+(b_0,\ldots,b_{m-1})=(S_0(a,b),\ldots,S_{m-1}(a,b))\text{ and }(a_0,\ldots,a_{m-1})(b_0,\ldots,b_{m-1})=(P_0(a,b),\ldots,P_{m-1}(a,b));\ 0=(0,\ldots,0),\ 1=(1,0,\ldots,0).\text{ With }[a]=(a,0,\ldots,0),\ a\mapsto[a]\text{ is multiplicative and }\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}[a_i]p^i=(a_0,a_1^p,a_2^{p^2},\ldots,a_{m-1}^{p^{m-1}}).\text{ If }A\text{ is perfect, every }w\in W_m(A)\text{ has a unique expansion }\sum_{0\le i<m}[a_i]p^i\text{, and }p^iW_m(A)\ (i\le m)\text{ is exactly the set of vectors whose first }i\text{ entries vanish; if }A\text{ is not perfect, both properties fail.}
statements.scope_note: Definition and stated coordinate properties of the truncated (length-m) Witt vector functor.

statements.title: Factorization of a Solvable Group by Pairwise-Disjoint Weight Semigroups
statements.statement_plain: For a smooth connected solvable k-group acted on by a split k-torus, partitioning its S-weight set into parts whose generated character semigroups are pairwise disjoint makes multiplication from the corresponding subgroups H_Ai to G an isomorphism.
statements.statement_latex: Let G be a smooth connected solvable k-group equipped with an action of a split k-torus S. Given a disjoint-union decomposition \widehat{\Phi}(S,G)=\coprod_{i=1}^{n}\Psi_i, and writing A_i\subset X^*(S) for the subsemigroup generated by \Psi_i, if the A_i are pairwise disjoint then multiplication induces an isomorphism of k-schemes H_{A_1}\times\cdots\times H_{A_n}\xrightarrow{\sim}G.
assumptions_latex: G is a smooth connected solvable k-group equipped with an action of a split k-torus S.
\widehat{\Phi}(S,G)=\coprod_{i=1}^{n}\Psi_i is a disjoint-union decomposition.
For each i, A_i\subset X^*(S) is the subsemigroup generated by \Psi_i, and the A_i are pairwise disjoint.
statements.conclusion_latex: The multiplication morphism H_{A_1}\times\cdots\times H_{A_n}\longrightarrow G of k-schemes is an isomorphism.
statements.scope_note: The subgroups H_{A_i} are the S-invariant weight-semigroup subgroups supplied by the preceding construction in the source.

statements.title: Case-(a) smooth model and closed fiber of the quadratic norm-one torus
statements.statement_plain: If the residue characteristic of overline K is not 2 or omega(alpha)=0, then the scheme T is smooth. In the extracted case (a), assume residue characteristic overline K=2, omega(alpha)>0, Car(tilde K)=2, and alpha=0 (so car K is not 2). The model T^R defined by O[U,V]/(U-U^2-beta V^2), with generic fiber T, is a smooth group scheme. Its closed fiber is Z/2Z times the additive group, hence non-connected, when tilde K/K is ramified; when unramified it is a non-split connected one-dimensional unipotent group. Under the stated ramified or unramified hypotheses, the valuation of u^2+beta v^2 equals the infimum of the two summand valuations for all u,v in a strict henselization of K. Therefore u=u^2+beta v^2 implies u and v are integral, and T^R(O^hs)=T(K^hs)=T(O^hs).
statements.statement_latex: If \(\operatorname{car}\overline{\mathrm K}\neq2\) or \(\omega(\alpha)=0\), then \(\mathfrak T\) is smooth. Otherwise, in the extracted case (a) assume \(\operatorname{car}\overline{\mathrm K}=2\), \(\omega(\alpha)>0\), \(\operatorname{Car}\widetilde K=2\), and \(\alpha=0\) (hence \(\operatorname{car}K\neq2\)). Define \(\mathfrak T^{R}\) by \(\mathcal O[\mathfrak T^{R}]=\mathcal O[U,V]/(U-U^{2}-\beta V^{2})\), with generic fiber \(T\). Then \(\mathfrak T^{R}\) is a smooth group scheme. Its closed fiber is \(\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z\times\mathfrak{Add}\) (non-connected) if \(\widetilde K/K\) is ramified, and is a non-split connected one-dimensional unipotent group if \(\widetilde K/K\) is unramified. For all \(u,v\in{}^{\mathrm{hs}}K\), under the corresponding ramified or unramified hypotheses, \(\omega(u^{2}+\beta v^{2})=\inf\{\omega(u^{2}),\omega(\beta v^{2})\}\); consequently the equation \(u=u^{2}+\beta v^{2}\) forces \(u,v\in{}^{\mathrm{hs}}\mathcal O\), and \(\mathfrak T^{R}({}^{\mathrm{hs}}\mathcal O)=T({}^{\mathrm{hs}}K)=\mathfrak T({}^{\mathrm{hs}}\mathcal O)\).
assumptions_latex: \operatorname{car}\overline{\mathrm K}=2,\ \omega(\alpha)>0,\ \operatorname{Car}\widetilde K=2,\ \alpha=0\ \text{(case (a), hence }\operatorname{car}K\neq2\text{)}
\widetilde K/K\ \text{ramified: }\omega\text{ is discrete, }\beta\text{ is a uniformizer, and }\omega(u^2),\omega(\beta v^2)\text{ have different parity}
\widetilde K/K\ \text{unramified: the residual extension }\overline{\widetilde K/K}\text{ is inseparable quadratic and }U^2+\beta V^2\text{ remains irreducible over a separable closure of }K
statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\operatorname{car}\overline{\mathrm K}\neq2\) or \(\omega(\alpha)=0\), then \(\mathfrak T\) is smooth. In the extracted case (a), \(\mathfrak T\) is otherwise non-smooth, and the model \(\mathfrak T^{R}\) defined by \(\mathcal O[\mathfrak T^{R}]=\mathcal O[U,V]/(U-U^{2}-\beta V^{2})\), with generic fiber \(T\), is a smooth group scheme. Its closed fiber is isomorphic to \(\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z\times\mathfrak{Add}\) (hence non-connected) when \(\widetilde K/K\) is ramified, and to a non-split connected one-dimensional unipotent group when \(\widetilde K/K\) is unramified. For \(u,v\in{}^{\mathrm{hs}}K\), \(\omega(u^{2}+\beta v^{2})=\inf\{\omega(u^{2}),\omega(\beta v^{2})\}\); hence \(u=u^{2}+\beta v^{2}\) implies \(u,v\in{}^{\mathrm{hs}}\mathcal O\), and \(\mathfrak T^{R}({}^{\mathrm{hs}}\mathcal O)=T({}^{\mathrm{hs}}K)=\mathfrak T({}^{\mathrm{hs}}\mathcal O)\).

statements.title: Characterization of reductive special fibers
statements.statement_plain: Assume that \overline{K} is separably closed. For a smooth \mathcal{O}-group scheme \mathfrak{H} with generic fiber G, its closed fiber is reductive if and only if it is connected reductive, if and only if G is split over K and \mathfrak{H} is the group scheme \mathfrak{G}_{x}^{0} attached to a special point x of \mathcal{I}, equivalently if and only if \mathfrak{H} is a Chevalley scheme.
statements.statement_latex: Assume \overline{K} is separably closed and let \mathfrak{H} be a smooth \mathcal{O}-group scheme with generic fiber G. Then the following conditions are equivalent: (a) \overline{\mathfrak{H}} is reductive; (b) \overline{\mathfrak{H}} is connected reductive; (c) G is split over K and there exists a special point x\in\mathcal{I} such that \mathfrak{H}\simeq\mathfrak{G}_{x}^{0}; (d) G is split over K and \mathfrak{H} is a Chevalley scheme.
assumptions_latex: \overline{K} is separably closed.
\mathfrak{H} is a smooth \mathcal{O}-group scheme with generic fiber G.
statements.conclusion_latex: The following conditions are equivalent: (a) the closed fiber \overline{\mathfrak{H}} is reductive; (b) the closed fiber \overline{\mathfrak{H}} is connected reductive; (c) G is split over K and there exists a special point x\in\mathcal{I} such that \mathfrak{H}\simeq\mathfrak{G}_{x}^{0}; (d) G is split over K and \mathfrak{H} is a Chevalley scheme.

statements.statement_plain: For subsets Ω and Ω′ of the apartment satisfying Ω ≺ Ω′, the kernel of the special-fiber morphism \(\bar\rho_{\Omega,\Omega'}\) is a smooth connected unipotent group. \[
\prod_{a\in\Phi^{\mathrm{nd}}}\ker\left(\overline{\mathcal U}_{a,\Omega',0}\to\overline{\mathcal U}_{a,\Omega,0}\right)\xrightarrow{\sim}\ker(\bar\rho_{\Omega,\Omega'}).

statements.title: Maximal torus in the special fiber under fixed-point descent
statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty bounded subset of the apartment of G attached to a maximal K-split torus S, choose a containing apartment of H for a maximal K-split torus T with the required Theta-fixed equality. If the associated smooth affine group scheme H_Omega^1 contains a split 0-torus model with generic fiber T, then the schematic closure of S in that model is fixed pointwise by Theta, lies in the connected fixed-point group scheme G_Omega^0, and its special fiber is a maximal torus of the special fiber of G_Omega^0.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A\) be the apartment of \(\mathcal B(G)\) corresponding to a maximal \(K\)-split torus \(S\subset G\), and let \(\Omega\subset\mathcal A\) be non-empty and bounded. Let \(A\) be an apartment of \(\mathcal B(H)\) corresponding to a maximal \(K\)-split torus \(T\supset S\) with \(\mathcal A=A\cap\mathfrak B=A^{\Theta}\), and suppose \(\mathcal H^{1}_{\Omega}\) contains a closed split \(0\)-torus \(\mathcal T\) with generic fiber \(T\). Then the schematic closure \(\mathcal S\) of \(S\) in \(\mathcal T\) is fixed pointwise by \(\Theta\), is contained in \(\mathcal G^{0}_{\Omega}=(\mathcal H^{1}_{\Omega})^{\Theta,0}\), and has special fiber \(\overline{\mathcal S}\) equal to a maximal torus of \(\overline{\mathcal G}^{0}_{\Omega}\).
assumptions_latex: \(\Theta\) acts on \(\mathcal H^{1}_{\Omega}\), with \(S\subset G\subset H^{\Theta}\), and \(S\) is a maximal \(K\)-split torus of \(G\).
\(\mathcal A\) is the apartment of \(\mathfrak B=\mathcal B(G)\) corresponding to \(S\), and \(\Omega\subset\mathcal A\) is non-empty and bounded.
There is an apartment \(A\) of \(\mathcal B(H)\), corresponding to a maximal \(K\)-split torus \(T\supset S\) of \(H\), such that \(\mathcal A=A\cap\mathfrak B=A^{\Theta}\).
\(\mathcal H^{1}_{\Omega}\) contains a closed split \(0\)-torus \(\mathcal T\) with generic fiber \(T\).
statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\mathcal S\) is the schematic closure of \(S\) in \(\mathcal T\), then \(\Theta\) fixes \(\mathcal S\) pointwise and \(\mathcal S\subset\mathcal G^{0}_{\Omega}=(\mathcal H^{1}_{\Omega})^{\Theta,0}\); moreover, the special fiber \(\overline{\mathcal S}\) is a maximal torus of \(\overline{\mathcal G}^{0}_{\Omega}\).

statements.title: Extension of \(\mathfrak U_{a,(k,\ell)}\) to Arbitrary Parameters
statements.statement_plain: For real k and ell, the dense-valuation case does not seek a scheme when the admissibility conditions from 4.3.5 fail. For discrete valuation, replace k by the least element k' of Gamma'_a at least k and replace ell by the least element ell' of Gamma'_{2a} at least min(2k, ell). Define the scheme at (k,ell) to be the scheme at (k',ell'). The adjusted values satisfy condition (2) of 4.3.5, and at 0 the displayed expression is U_{a,k'} U_{2a,ell'} = U_{a,k} U_{2a,ell}. The bounds are ell' <= 2k' in the unramified case and ell' <= 2k' + c in the ramified case when Gamma'_{2a}=c+2 Gamma'_a.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(k,\ell\in\mathbf R\). If \(\omega\) is dense and conditions (1) and (2) of 4.3.5 are not satisfied, no scheme \(\mathfrak U_{a,(k,\ell)}\) is sought. If \(\omega\) is discrete, set \(k'=\inf\{h\in\Gamma'_a\mid h\ge k\}\) and \(\ell'=\inf\{h\in\Gamma'_{2a}\mid h\ge\inf(2k,\ell)\}\). Then \(k'\in\Gamma'_a\), \(\ell'\in\Gamma'_{2a}\), and condition (2) of 4.3.5 holds for \((k',\ell')\); define \(\mathfrak U_{a,(k,\ell)}:=\mathfrak U_{a,(k',\ell')}\). At 0, \(\mathfrak U_{a,(k,\ell)}(0)=U_{a,k'}\,U_{2a,\ell'}=U_{a,k}\,U_{2a,\ell}\). If \(L_a\) is unramified, then \(\ell'\le 2k'\); if \(L_a\) is ramified with \(\Gamma'_{2a}=c+2\Gamma'_a\), then \(\ell'\le 2k'+c\).

statements.title: Generic-fiber Lie algebra and root-space lattices
statements.statement_plain: For a smooth affine group scheme over a valuation ring, passing to its generic fiber identifies the Lie algebra after tensoring with the fraction field. The root-space decomposition base-changes accordingly: the integral and generic root sets agree, and each integral root space is a lattice in the corresponding generic root space.
statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal{G} be a smooth affine group scheme over a valuation ring \mathfrak{o}, with fraction field k and generic fiber G, and let \mathcal{S} be a torus with generic fiber S. Then \operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal{G}) is an \mathfrak{o}-lattice in \operatorname{Lie}(G), and \operatorname{Lie}(G)=\bigoplus_a\bigl(\operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal{G})_a\otimes_{\mathfrak{o}}k\bigr). The \mathcal{S}-roots of \mathcal{G} coincide with the S-roots of G, and for each root a, \operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal{G})_a is an \mathfrak{o}-lattice in \operatorname{Lie}(G)_a.
assumptions_latex: \mathfrak{o} is a valuation ring (in the source context, a DVR) with fraction field k=\operatorname{Frac}(\mathfrak{o}).
\mathcal{G} is a smooth affine group scheme over \mathfrak{o}, with generic fiber G.
\mathcal{S} is a torus acting on \operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal{G}) by root spaces, and S is its generic fiber.
statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal{G})\text{ is an }\mathfrak{o}\text{-lattice in }\operatorname{Lie}(G),\qquad \operatorname{Lie}(G)=\bigoplus_a\left(\operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal{G})_a\otimes_{\mathfrak{o}}k\right);\quad \Phi(\mathcal{G},\mathcal{S})=\Phi(G,S),\text{ and }\operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal{G})_a\text{ is an }\mathfrak{o}\text{-lattice in }\operatorname{Lie}(G)_a\text{ for every }a.
statements.scope_note: Integral Lie-algebra and root-space lattice behavior under passage from a smooth group scheme to its generic fiber.

statements.title: Pro-unipotent preimage as the pro-p Sylow subgroup
statements.statement_plain: If the residue field is finite, the maximal reductive quotient of the identity-component special fiber is isomorphic to the indicated torus special fiber, whose residue-field points form the maximal prime-to-p quotient of T(k)^0. The elements of T(k)^0 that reduce to unipotent elements therefore form its pro-p Sylow subgroup, equal to T(k)^0 intersected with the standard 0+ subgroup.
statements.statement_latex: If \mathfrak{f} is finite, the maximal reductive quotient of \overline{\mathcal{T}}^0 is isomorphic to \overline{\mathcal{S}}, and \overline{\mathcal{S}}(\mathfrak{f}) is the maximal quotient of T(k)^0 whose order is prime to p. Consequently, the subgroup of T(k)^0 consisting of elements whose image in \overline{\mathcal{T}}^0(\mathfrak{f}) is unipotent is the pro-p Sylow subgroup of T(k)^0, and it equals T(k)^0\cap T(k)_{0+}^{\mathrm{std}}.
assumptions_latex: \mathfrak{f}\text{ is finite}
statements.conclusion_latex: \left\{t\in T(k)^0:\text{the image of }t\text{ in }\overline{\mathcal{T}}^0(\mathfrak{f})\text{ is unipotent}\right\}=\text{the pro-}p\text{-Sylow subgroup of }T(k)^0=T(k)^0\cap T(k)_{0+}^{\mathrm{std}}.

statements.title: Tits Index of the Maximal Reductive Facet Quotient
statements.statement_plain: Assume that G is residually quasi-split. For a special k-torus T, a Gamma-stable chamber C associated with T, and a Gamma-stable facet F in the closure of C, Gamma preserves the affine root system, its basis determined by C, and the subset giving the type of F. The resulting action on the facet type equips the Dynkin diagram of the maximal reductive quotient of the connected special fiber, relative to the image of the maximal torus, with the structure of a Tits index.
statements.statement_latex: Assume that $G$ is residually quasi-split. Let $T$ be a special $k$-torus of $G$, let $C$ be a $\Gamma$-stable chamber associated with $T$, and let $F$ be a $\Gamma$-stable facet contained in the closure of $C$. Let $\Psi$ be the affine root system of $G_K$ with respect to $T_K$, let $\Delta$ be the basis determined by $C$, and let $\Delta_F\subseteq\Delta$ be the type of $F$. Then $\Gamma$ preserves $\Psi$, $\Delta$, and $\Delta_F$. The induced $\Gamma$-action on $\Delta_F$ endows the Dynkin diagram of the maximal reductive quotient $\mathrm{G}_F$ of $\overline{\mathcal G}_F^{0}$, with respect to the isomorphic image $\mathrm T$ of the maximal torus $\overline{\mathcal T}$, with the structure of a Tits index.
assumptions_latex: $G$ is residually quasi-split.
$T$ is a special $k$-torus of $G$.
$C$ is a $\Gamma$-stable chamber associated with $T$.
$F$ is a $\Gamma$-stable facet contained in the closure of $C$.
$\Psi$ is the affine root system of $G_K$ with respect to $T_K$, $\Delta$ is the basis determined by $C$, and $\Delta_F\subseteq\Delta$ is the type of $F$.
statements.conclusion_latex: The $\Gamma$-action on $\Delta_F$ endows the Dynkin diagram of the maximal reductive quotient $\mathrm{G}_F$ of $\overline{\mathcal G}_F^{0}$, relative to the isomorphic image $\mathrm T$ of $\overline{\mathcal T}$, with the structure of a Tits index.

statements.title: Proper parabolics and non-central split tori in the reductive quotient
statements.statement_plain: For a perfect field F and a smooth connected affine F-group G, with bar G its quotient by the unipotent radical, G has a proper parabolic F-subgroup if and only if bar G has a non-central F-split torus.
statements.statement_latex: \text{Let }F\text{ be perfect and }G\text{ a smooth connected affine }F\text{-group, with }\bar G=G/\mathcal R_u(G).\text{ Then }\exists\text{ a proper parabolic }F\text{-subgroup of }G\iff \bar G\text{ has a non-central }F\text{-split torus}.
assumptions_latex: F is a perfect field.
G is a smooth connected affine algebraic F-group.
statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(\exists\text{ a proper parabolic }F\text{-subgroup of }G\bigr)\Longleftrightarrow\bigl(\bar G\text{ has a non-central }F\text{-split torus}\bigr).
statements.scope_note: Here \(\bar G=G/\mathcal R_u(G)\) is the connected reductive quotient by the unipotent radical, as defined in the source's reductive-quotient context.

statements.title: Reductive quotient of a Levi parahoric as a Levi factor of the ambient quotient
statements.statement_plain: For a Levi subgroup M of G and x in the Levi building B(G)_M, the map from the Levi parahoric's special fiber to the ambient reductive quotient G_x is onto the Levi subgroup centralizing the image of the special-fiber torus. Its kernel is the unipotent radical of that special fiber, so the reductive quotient M_{pi(x)}^0 is canonically isomorphic to this Levi subgroup.
statements.statement_latex: For a Levi subgroup \(M\subset G\), a point \(x\in\mathcal{B}(G)_M\), and the standard model \(\mathcal{A}\) of the maximal \(k\)-split torus in the center of \(M\), the induced map \(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{\pi(x)}^{0}\to G_x\) is surjective onto \(L=C_{G_x}(\operatorname{im}\overline{\mathcal{A}})\), has kernel \(\operatorname{R_u}(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{\pi(x)}^{0})\), and therefore yields \(M_{\pi(x)}^{0}\cong L\).
assumptions_latex: M\subset G is a Levi subgroup.
x\in\mathcal{B}(G)_M.
\mathcal{A} is the standard model of the maximal k-split torus in the center of M.
statements.conclusion_latex: The homomorphism \(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{\pi(x)}^{0}\to G_x\) induced by inclusion into \(\overline{\mathcal{G}}_{x}^{0}\) and projection to \(G_x\) is surjective onto the Levi subgroup \(L=C_{G_x}(\operatorname{im}\overline{\mathcal{A}})\). Its kernel is \(\operatorname{R_u}(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{\pi(x)}^{0})\), so it induces a canonical isomorphism \(M_{\pi(x)}^{0}=\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{\pi(x)}^{0}/\operatorname{R_u}(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{\pi(x)}^{0})\xrightarrow{\sim}L\subset G_x\).
statements.scope_note: Levi subgroup associated to a point in the Levi building; identifies the reductive quotient of the corresponding parahoric Levi special fiber with the Levi factor of the ambient reductive quotient centralizing the special-fiber central torus.
