statements.title: Root systems and Weyl group of reductive special-fiber quotients
statements.statement_plain: (i) The root system of Gbar_j^theta modulo R, relative to the maximal Kbar-split torus q(Sbar), identified with Sbar, is Phi_f, the roots a in Phi satisfying f(a)+f(-a)=0. (ii) The canonical map from Aut A to Aut V* identifies W_f with the Weyl group of Phi_f; this Weyl group acts on the span of Phi_f and trivially on its orthogonal complement. (iii) If Kbar is separably closed, and R' is the unipotent radical of Gbar_f^0, then the reductive quotient Gbar_f^0 modulo R' (defined over an algebraic closure of Kbar) has root system equal to the non-multipliable roots Phi_f^nm of Phi_f.
statements.statement_latex: (i) The root system of \(\overline{\mathfrak G}_{j}^{\theta}/\mathrm R\) relative to the maximal \(\overline{\mathrm K}\)-split torus \(q(\overline{\mathfrak S})\) (identified with \(\overline{\mathfrak S}\)) is \(\Phi_f=\{a\in\Phi\mid f(a)+f(-a)=0\}\). (ii) The canonical map from \(\operatorname{Aut}A\) into \(\operatorname{Aut}\mathbf V^*\) induces an isomorphism of \(\mathbf W_f\) onto the Weyl group of \(\Phi_f\), acting naturally on the subspace of \(\mathbf V^*\) generated by \(\Phi_f\) and trivially on its orthogonal complement. (iii) Suppose \(\overline{\mathrm K}\) is separably closed and let \(\mathrm R'\) be the unipotent radical of \(\overline{\mathfrak G}_f^0\). Then the root system of the reductive group \(\overline{\mathfrak G}_f^0/\mathrm R'\), defined over the algebraic closure of \(\overline{\mathrm K}\), is the set \(\Phi_f^{nm}\) of non-multipliable elements of \(\Phi_f\).
assumptions_latex: For part (iii), \(\overline{\mathrm K}\) is separably closed.
In part (iii), \(\mathrm R'\) is the unipotent radical of \(\overline{\mathfrak G}_f^0\).
statements.conclusion_latex: (i) The root system of \(\overline{\mathfrak G}_{j}^{\theta}/\mathrm R\) relative to the maximal \(\overline{\mathrm K}\)-split torus \(q(\overline{\mathfrak S})\), identified with \(\overline{\mathfrak S}\), is \(\Phi_f=\{a\in\Phi\mid f(a)+f(-a)=0\}\). (ii) The canonical map \(\operatorname{Aut}A\to\operatorname{Aut}\mathbf V^*\) induces an isomorphism from \(\mathbf W_f\) onto the Weyl group of \(\Phi_f\), acting on the subspace spanned by \(\Phi_f\) and trivially on its orthogonal complement. (iii) Under the separable-closedness assumption, the root system of the reductive quotient \(\overline{\mathfrak G}_f^0/\mathrm R'\) (defined over an algebraic closure of \(\overline{\mathrm K}\)) is the set \(\Phi_f^{nm}\) of non-multipliable elements of \(\Phi_f\).

statements.title: Structure of the reductive quotient attached to a concave function
statements.statement_plain: Assume f(0)=0. The maximal reductive quotient associated with the special fiber of the concave-function integral model has the torus induced by S as a maximal torus. Its relevant centralizers are T and its special fiber, its roots form the reduced system Phi_{x,f}, and its root datum is the stated character-cocharacter datum. Each root group is canonically the corresponding quotient of special-fiber root-group models.
statements.statement_latex: Assume f(0)=0 and let G_{x,f}=\overline{\mathcal G}_{x,f}/\overline{\mathcal R}_u(\overline{\mathcal G}_{x,f}) be the maximal reductive quotient. Then: (1) the closed immersion \mathcal S\hookrightarrow\mathcal G_{x,f} identifies \mathcal S with a maximal torus of \mathcal G_{x,f}, and its special fiber \overline{\mathcal S} with a maximal torus of \overline{\mathcal G}_{x,f}; (2) Z_{\mathcal G_{x,f}}(\mathcal S)=\mathcal T and Z_{\overline{\mathcal G}_{x,f}}(\overline{\mathcal S})=\overline{\mathcal T}; (3) \Phi_{x,f} is a reduced root system, and if S is the image of \overline{\mathcal S} in G_{x,f}, then the root datum of G_{x,f} with respect to S is (X^*(S),\Phi_{x,f},X_*(S),\Phi_{x,f}^{\vee}); (4) for each b\in\Phi_{x,f}, let a\in\Phi be the unique non-divisible root of which b is a positive multiple. The b-root group of G_{x,f} is canonically isomorphic to \overline{\mathcal U}_{a,x,f}/\overline{\mathcal U}_{a,x,f}^{+}.
assumptions_latex: G_{x,f}=\overline{\mathcal G}_{x,f}/\overline{\mathcal R}_u(\overline{\mathcal G}_{x,f})
statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal S\hookrightarrow\mathcal G_{x,f} identifies \mathcal S with a maximal torus of \mathcal G_{x,f}, and \overline{\mathcal S} with a maximal torus of \overline{\mathcal G}_{x,f}; Z_{\mathcal G_{x,f}}(\mathcal S)=\mathcal T and Z_{\overline{\mathcal G}_{x,f}}(\overline{\mathcal S})=\overline{\mathcal T}; \Phi_{x,f} is a reduced root system and the root datum of G_{x,f} relative to S is (X^*(S),\Phi_{x,f},X_*(S),\Phi_{x,f}^{\vee}); for every b\in\Phi_{x,f}, if a\in\Phi is the unique non-divisible root of which b is a positive multiple, then the b-root group of G_{x,f} is canonically isomorphic to \overline{\mathcal U}_{a,x,f}/\overline{\mathcal U}_{a,x,f}^{+}.

statements.title: Unipotent radicals and reductive quotients for nested subsets with equal span
statements.statement_plain: If Ω lies in the closure of Ω′ and the two subsets span the same subspace of the apartment, then the kernel of the induced map from the connected special fiber for Ω′ to the reductive quotient for Ω is exactly the unipotent radical of the former special fiber. The induced map between reductive quotients is an isomorphism, and the special-fiber morphism maps the unipotent radical for Ω′ onto the unipotent radical for Ω.

Then \(\ker(\bar\pi)=\mathcal R_u(\overline{\mathcal G}_{\Omega'}^{0})\), and \(\bar\pi\) induces an isomorphism \(\mathrm G_{\Omega'}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm G_{\Omega}\). Moreover, \(\bar\rho_{\Omega,\Omega'}(\mathcal R_u(\overline{\mathcal G}_{\Omega'}^{0}))=\mathcal R_u(\overline{\mathcal G}_{\Omega}^{0})\).

statements.title: Connected-unipotent Greenberg kernels and affine extensions
statements.statement_plain: If each smooth surjection between successive Greenberg transforms has connected unipotent kernel, then the kernel of Gr(f) is connected unipotent. Any extension of affine finite-type group schemes H by H' over the base ring f is itself affine and of finite type.

Furthermore, any exact extension \(1\to H'\to E\to H\to 1\) of affine finite-type \(\mathfrak f\)-group schemes has \(E\) affine of finite type.

statements.title: Characterization of Vector Groups
statements.statement_plain: Over an algebraically closed field R, a smooth connected affine commutative unipotent group G is a vector group, isomorphic to G_a^n, precisely when in positive characteristic every nonidentity element has order p (equivalently, the group has exponent p).
statements.statement_latex: Let R be an algebraically closed field. A smooth connected affine commutative unipotent R-group G is isomorphic to \(\mathbb G_a^n\) for some n\ge0 (a vector group) exactly when, if char(R)=p>0, every nonidentity element has order p (equivalently, [p]_G=0).
assumptions_latex: R is an algebraically closed field.
G is a smooth connected affine commutative unipotent group over R.
If char(R)=p>0, every nonidentity element of G has order p (equivalently, G has exponent p).
statements.conclusion_latex: G\cong\mathbb G_a^n\text{ for some }n\ge 0; equivalently, G\text{ is a vector group}.
statements.scope_note: Characterization over an algebraically closed field; in positive characteristic, the exponent-p condition is required.

statements.title: Centralizer model over the valuation ring

Moreover, \mathcal{Z}(\mathfrak{o})=Z(k)^{0}.

statements.title: Reductive model tori, split generic fiber, connected special fiber, and quasi-splitness
statements.statement_plain: For a smooth affine group scheme over o with connected reductive generic fiber and reductive identity component in the special fiber, maximal split and maximal tori lift between special, integral, and generic fibers. The generic torus is maximal and makes G split over K; the special fiber is connected, so the model is reductive. If the residue field has dimension at most one, G is quasi-split over k.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal G\) be a smooth affine \(\mathfrak o\)-group scheme whose generic fiber \(G\) is a connected reductive \(k\)-group and whose special-fiber identity component \(\overline{\mathcal G}^{0}\) is reductive. Then closed tori \(\mathcal S\subset\mathcal T\) exist with \(\mathcal S\) maximal \(\mathfrak o\)-split and \(\mathcal T\) a maximal closed \(\mathfrak o\)-torus splitting over \(\mathcal O\); their fibers satisfy that \(T\) splits over \(K\), \(\overline{\mathcal S}\) is maximal \(\mathfrak f\)-split, and \(\overline{\mathcal T}\) is a maximal \(\mathfrak f\)-torus of \(\overline{\mathcal G}^{0}\). Furthermore, \(T\) is maximal in \(G\), \(G_K\) is split, \(\overline{\mathcal G}\) is connected, and residue-field dimension \(\leq 1\) implies that \(G\) is quasi-split over \(k\).
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal G\) is a smooth affine \(\mathfrak o\)-group scheme.
Its generic fiber \(G\) is a connected reductive \(k\)-group.
The identity component \(\overline{\mathcal G}^{0}\) of its special fiber is reductive.
statements.conclusion_latex: There exist closed \(\mathfrak o\)-tori \(\mathcal S\subset\mathcal T\) such that \(\mathcal S\) is \(\mathfrak o\)-split and maximal among closed \(\mathfrak o\)-split tori of \(\mathcal G\), while \(\mathcal T\) is a maximal closed \(\mathfrak o\)-torus splitting over \(\mathcal O\); the generic fiber \(T\) of \(\mathcal T\) splits over \(K\), the special fiber \(\overline{\mathcal S}\) is a maximal \(\mathfrak f\)-split torus, and \(\overline{\mathcal T}\) is a maximal \(\mathfrak f\)-torus of \(\overline{\mathcal G}^{0}\). Moreover, \(T\) is a maximal torus of \(G\), \(G_K\) is split, \(\overline{\mathcal G}\) is connected (hence \(\mathcal G\) is a reductive group scheme), and if \(\mathfrak f\) has dimension \(\leq 1\), then \(G\) is quasi-split over \(k\).
statements.scope_note: Retains the source's notation and its stated residue-field condition “dimension \(\leq 1\)” verbatim; the special fiber of \(\mathcal S\) is denoted \(\overline{\mathcal S}\) to match the proof.

statements.title: Functoriality of Strong Association and Reductive Quotient Isomorphisms
statements.statement_plain: Strong association of facets is reflexive and symmetric. The canonical isomorphisms between their reductive quotient groups are inverse under swapping facets, equivariant under conjugation by G(k), and compose for a triple in one apartment when the second and third facets are strongly associated.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F_1,\mathcal F_2,\mathcal F_3\) be facets of \(\mathcal B(G)\) and let \(g\in G(k)\). Then: (1) \(\mathcal F_1\) is strongly associated to itself and \(\varphi_{\mathcal F_1,\mathcal F_1}=\operatorname{id}_{G_{\mathcal F_1}}\). If \(\mathcal F_1,\mathcal F_2\) are strongly associated, then (2) \(\mathcal F_2,\mathcal F_1\) are strongly associated and \(\varphi_{\mathcal F_1,\mathcal F_2}=\varphi_{\mathcal F_2,\mathcal F_1}^{-1}\), and (3) \(g\mathcal F_1,g\mathcal F_2\) are strongly associated with \(\varphi_{g\mathcal F_2,g\mathcal F_1}=\operatorname{Int}(g)\circ\varphi_{\mathcal F_2,\mathcal F_1}\circ\operatorname{Int}(g)^{-1}\). If moreover \(\mathcal F_2,\mathcal F_3\) are strongly associated and an apartment contains all three facets, then (4) \(\mathcal F_1,\mathcal F_3\) are strongly associated and \(\varphi_{\mathcal F_3,\mathcal F_1}=\varphi_{\mathcal F_3,\mathcal F_2}\circ\varphi_{\mathcal F_2,\mathcal F_1}\).
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F_1,\mathcal F_2,\mathcal F_3\) are facets of \(\mathcal B(G)\), and \(g\in G(k)\).
For (2) and (3), \(\mathcal F_1\) and \(\mathcal F_2\) are strongly associated.
For (4), \(\mathcal F_2\) and \(\mathcal F_3\) are strongly associated and there exists an apartment of \(\mathcal B(G)\) containing \(\mathcal F_1,\mathcal F_2,\mathcal F_3\).
statements.conclusion_latex: (1) \(\mathcal F_1\) is strongly associated to itself and \(\varphi_{\mathcal F_1,\mathcal F_1}=\operatorname{id}_{G_{\mathcal F_1}}\). If \(\mathcal F_1\) and \(\mathcal F_2\) are strongly associated, then (2) \(\mathcal F_2\) and \(\mathcal F_1\) are strongly associated and \(\varphi_{\mathcal F_1,\mathcal F_2}=\varphi_{\mathcal F_2,\mathcal F_1}^{-1}\), and (3) \(g\mathcal F_1\) and \(g\mathcal F_2\) are strongly associated with \(\varphi_{g\mathcal F_2,g\mathcal F_1}=\operatorname{Int}(g)\circ\varphi_{\mathcal F_2,\mathcal F_1}\circ\operatorname{Int}(g)^{-1}\). statements.title: Two constructions of integral models for an induced torus
statements.statement_plain: For an induced torus T over k with splitting field ell/k and Galois group Theta, one integral model is obtained from the invariant o-algebra (o_ell[X*(T)])^Theta. Alternatively, expressing T as a product of restrictions of scalars of the multiplicative group and applying the corresponding integral Weil restrictions produces a smooth model. This is the standard model and the finite-type Neron-Raynaud model.
statements.statement_latex: \text{Let }T\text{ be an induced }k\text{-torus with splitting field }\ell/k\text{ and Galois group }\Theta.\text{ Using }k[T]=\bigl(\ell[X^{*}(T)]\bigr)^{\Theta},\text{ one construction uses the }\mathfrak{o}\text{-algebra }\bigl(\mathfrak{o}_{\ell}[X^{*}(T)]\bigr)^{\Theta}.\text{ Writing }T\text{ as a product }\prod_i\operatorname{R}_{\ell_i/k}\mathbf{G}_{\mathrm m,\ell_i}\text{ gives a second construction from }\prod_i\operatorname{R}_{\mathfrak{o}_{\ell_i}/\mathfrak{o}}\bigl(\mathbf{G}_{\mathrm m,\mathfrak{o}_{\ell_i}}\bigr).\text{ This second model is smooth, standard, and finite-type Neron-Raynaud.}
assumptions_latex: T\text{ is an induced torus over }k.
\ell/k\text{ is a splitting field of }T\text{ with Galois group }\Theta.
\mathfrak{o}\text{ and }\mathfrak{o}_{\ell}\text{ are the corresponding valuation rings.}
statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The }\mathfrak{o}\text{-subalgebra }\bigl(\mathfrak{o}_{\ell}[X^{*}(T)]\bigr)^{\Theta}\text{ gives one integral-model construction. If }T\cong\prod_i\operatorname{R}_{\ell_i/k}\mathbf{G}_{\mathrm m,\ell_i},\text{ then }\prod_i\operatorname{R}_{\mathfrak{o}_{\ell_i}/\mathfrak{o}}\bigl(\mathbf{G}_{\mathrm m,\mathfrak{o}_{\ell_i}}\bigr)\text{ gives a smooth integral model, namely the standard and finite-type Neron-Raynaud model.}
statements.scope_note: Two constructions of integral models for an induced torus are described. The invariant-coordinate-ring construction is not asserted to be smooth and is noted as especially useful when the splitting extension is unramified; no unramifiedness is required for the constructions as stated.

statements.title: Definition of an o-torus
statements.statement_plain: An o-torus is an o-group scheme T that is locally for the fpqc topology isomorphic to G_m^r for some integer r at least 0. Equivalently, after base change along a finite unramified extension ell/k to o_ell, it becomes G_m^r. The torus is split when it is already isomorphic to G_m^r over o.
statements.statement_latex: An \mathfrak{o}-torus is an \mathfrak{o}-group scheme \mathcal{T} that is, locally for the fpqc topology, isomorphic to \mathbf{G}_{\mathrm m}^{r} for some r\ge 0. Equivalently, there exists a finite unramified extension \ell/k such that \mathcal{T}\times_{\mathfrak{o}}\mathfrak{o}_{\ell}\cong\mathbf{G}_{\mathrm m}^{r}. It is called split when \mathcal{T}\cong\mathbf{G}_{\mathrm m}^{r}.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal{T}\text{ is an }\mathfrak{o}\text{-group scheme}
r\in\mathbf{Z}_{\ge 0}
statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal{T}\text{ is an }\mathfrak{o}\text{-torus}\iff\mathcal{T}\text{ is fpqc-locally isomorphic to }\mathbf{G}_{\mathrm m}^{r}\text{ for some }r\ge 0\iff\exists\text{ finite unramified }\ell/k\text{ with }\mathcal{T}\times_{\mathfrak{o}}\mathfrak{o}_{\ell}\cong\mathbf{G}_{\mathrm m}^{r};\quad \mathcal{T}\text{ is split}\iff\mathcal{T}\cong\mathbf{G}_{\mathrm m}^{r}.
statements.scope_note: Integral group schemes over the base ring \mathfrak{o}; the equivalent splitting criterion uses a finite unramified extension \ell/k and its corresponding ring \mathfrak{o}_{\ell}.

statements.title: Schematic filtrations of tori
statements.statement_plain: A decreasing separated filtration of T(K)^1 is called schematic when each nonnegative-level subgroup is schematic in the previously defined sense, the indicated points of its associated smooth model lie in the next level, and its set of jumps is discrete. A level is a jump when the union of the strictly higher levels differs from the subgroup at that level.
statements.statement_latex: A decreasing separated filtration \(\left(T(K)_r^*\right)_{r\geq 0}\) of \(T(K)^1\) is called schematic if: (1) for every \(r\geq 0\), \(T(K)_r^*\) is schematic in the previously defined sense; (2) \(\mathcal T_r^*(\mathcal M)\subset T(K)_{r+1}^*\), where \(\mathcal T_r^*\) is the smooth model determined by \(\mathcal T_r^*(\mathcal O)=T(K)_r^*\); and (3) the set of jumps of the filtration is discrete. Here \(r\) is a jump if \(T(K)_{r+}^*\neq T(K)_r^*\), where \(T(K)_{r+}^*=\bigcup_{s>r}T(K)_s^*\).
assumptions_latex: \left(T(K)_r^*\right)_{r\geq 0}\text{ is a decreasing separated filtration of }T(K)^1.
statements.conclusion_latex: \left(T(K)_r^*\right)_{r\geq 0}\text{ is called schematic exactly when conditions (1)--(3) hold.}
statements.scope_note: This definition uses the prior notion of a schematic subgroup and the local notation \(\mathcal O\) and \(\mathcal M\) for the smooth-model conditions.

statements.title: Characteristic-two special fiber of the standard torus model

statements.title: Character lattices and splitness across fibers of an integral torus
statements.statement_plain: For an integral torus over a Henselian discrete valuation ring, taking the generic or special fiber preserves its character and cocharacter lattices as Galois modules. Therefore the integral torus, its generic fiber, and its special fiber are split simultaneously.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{T}\) be an \(\mathfrak{o}\)-torus over a Henselian discretely valued ring, with generic fiber \(T\) and special fiber \(\mathrm{T}\). Under the canonical identification of the unramified Galois groups, passage to either fiber induces equivariant isomorphisms on character and cocharacter groups; hence \(\mathcal{T}\) is split iff \(\mathrm{T}\) is split iff \(T\) is split.
assumptions_latex: Let \(k\) be a Henselian discretely valued field with ring of integers \(\mathfrak{o}\) and residue field \(\mathfrak{f}\).
Let \(\mathcal{T}\) be an \(\mathfrak{o}\)-torus, and let \(T\) and \(\mathrm{T}\) denote its generic and special fibers, respectively.

Let \(K/k\) be the maximal unramified extension, with ring of integers \(\mathcal{O}\) and residue field \(\overline{\mathfrak{f}}\), so that \(\operatorname{Gal}(K/k)=\operatorname{Gal}(\mathcal{O}/\mathfrak{o})=\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathfrak{f}}/\mathfrak{f})\).
statements.conclusion_latex: The fiber maps \(X^*(\mathcal{T})\to X^*(T)\), \(X_*(\mathcal{T})\to X_*(T)\), \(X^*(\mathcal{T})\to X^*(\mathrm{T})\), and \(X_*(\mathcal{T})\to X_*(\mathrm{T})\), induced by taking generic or special fibers, are isomorphisms of abelian groups equivariant for the identified Galois groups. Consequently, \(\mathcal{T}\) is split if and only if \(\mathrm{T}\) is split if and only if \(T\) is split.
statements.scope_note: For an \(\mathfrak{o}\)-torus, generic and special fiber character and cocharacter groups agree as Galois modules, yielding equivalent splitness of the integral torus and both fibers.
review_flags: Builder proposal omitted the necessary \(\mathfrak{o}\)-torus hypothesis; the assertion would be false for general integral models whose special fiber is not a torus.

statements.title: Norm surjectivity on standard filtrations of weakly induced tori
statements.statement_plain: Assume k equals K and T is weakly induced. Let L over K be a tame Galois extension over which T becomes induced, let e be its ramification index, and set R to be the restriction of scalars of T_L. statements.title: Product decomposition for standard models of induced tori
statements.statement_plain: For induced k-tori T1 and T2 with T=T1 times T2, the tensor product over the base valuation ring of their Theta-invariant character-group algebras equals the Theta-invariant algebra for T, as d-lattices inside k[T1] tensor k[T2] = k[T]. The splitting field of T is the compositum over k of the splitting fields of T1 and T2, and the assertion for T is equivalent to the separate assertions for the two factors.
statements.statement_latex: Let T_1 and T_2 be induced k-tori and let T=T_1\times T_2. Then the natural inclusion of \Theta-invariant lattices \mathfrak{o}_{\ell'}[X^*(T_1)]^{\Theta}\otimes_{\mathfrak{o}}\mathfrak{o}_{\ell'}[X^*(T_2)]^{\Theta}\subseteq\mathfrak{o}_{\ell'}[X^*(T)]^{\Theta}, identified inside k[T_1]\otimes_k k[T_2]=k[T], is an equality of \mathfrak d-lattices. Moreover, the splitting field of T is the compositum over k of the splitting fields of T_1 and T_2, so the assertion for T is equivalent to the corresponding assertions for T_1 and T_2 separately.
assumptions_latex: T_1 and T_2 are induced tori over k.
T=T_1\times T_2, hence X^*(T)=X^*(T_1)\oplus X^*(T_2), with the \Theta-action induced on these character groups.
Choose \Theta-invariant bases of X^*(T_1) and X^*(T_2), whose disjoint union is a \Theta-invariant basis of X^*(T).
statements.conclusion_latex: \mathfrak{o}_{\ell'}[X^*(T_1)]^{\Theta}\otimes_{\mathfrak{o}}\mathfrak{o}_{\ell'}[X^*(T_2)]^{\Theta}=\mathfrak{o}_{\ell'}[X^*(T)]^{\Theta}\quad\text{as }\mathfrak d\text{-lattices in }k[T_1]\otimes_k k[T_2]=k[T].\ \text{The splitting field of }T\text{ over }k\text{ is the compositum of the splitting fields of }T_1\text{ and }T_2,\text{ and the assertion for }T\text{ is equivalent to the combined assertions for the two factors.}
statements.scope_note: Standard integral-model invariant lattices for products of induced tori.

statements.title: Standard models and filtrations of weakly induced tori
statements.statement_plain: For a weakly induced torus, the standard integral model is smooth. Its standard filtration is schematic, connected, and congruent. At every positive depth, over any possibly non-algebraic unramified Henselian discretely valued extension, the integral points are exactly the torus elements whose every character value differs from 1 by valuation at least that depth, and the corresponding special fiber is a vector group.
statements.statement_latex: Let T be a weakly induced k-torus and let \omega be the normalized discrete valuation on k, extended uniquely to all algebraic extensions of k. Then \mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{std}} is smooth, and its standard filtration is schematic, connected, and congruent, with corresponding smooth models \mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{std}}_r. For every r>0 and every possibly non-algebraic unramified extension k_1/k of Henselian discretely valued fields, \mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{std}}_r(\mathfrak{o}_1)=\{t\in T(k_1)\mid\forall\chi\in X^*(T),\ \omega(\chi(t)-1)\ge r\}; for r>0, the special fiber of \mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{std}}_r is a vector group.
assumptions_latex: T is a weakly induced k-torus.
\omega is the normalized discrete valuation on k, extended uniquely to all algebraic extensions of k.
For (3), r>0 and k_1/k is a possibly non-algebraic unramified extension of Henselian discretely valued fields, with ring of integers \mathfrak{o}_1.
statements.conclusion_latex: The standard model \mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{std}} of T is smooth. Its standard filtration is schematic, connected, and congruent, with corresponding smooth models \mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{std}}_r. For every r>0 and every possibly non-algebraic unramified Henselian discretely valued extension k_1/k, \mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{std}}_r(\mathfrak{o}_1)=\{t\in T(k_1)\mid \forall\chi\in X^*(T),\ \omega(\chi(t)-1)\ge r\}. For r>0, the special fiber of \mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{std}}_r is a vector group.

statements.title: Torus models and root groups in parahoric integral models
statements.statement_plain: In the parahoric integral-model setup, the maximal split torus S associated with the apartment satisfies S(K)^1 contained in G(K)_Omega^1. Its standard model is a closed torus in G_Omega^1, with relative roots Phi(S,G) and root groups U_{a,Omega,0}. If T is the centralizer of S, then T is maximal, its connected Neron model T^0 contains S's model by a closed immersion, and T^0 embeds as the centralizer of S's model in G_Omega^0.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be the maximal \(K\)-split torus corresponding to the apartment \(\mathcal A\), let \(T=C_G(S)\), and let \(\mathcal S\) and \(\mathcal T^0\) be as above. Then \(S(K)^1\subseteq G(K)_\Omega^1\); \(\mathcal S\) is a closed subgroup of \(\mathcal G_\Omega^1\) with \(\mathcal S\)-roots \(\Phi(S,G)\) and root groups \(\mathcal U_{a,\Omega,0}\); and the extensions \(\mathcal S\hookrightarrow\mathcal T^0\hookrightarrow\mathcal G_\Omega^0\) are closed immersions, with \(\mathcal T^0\) the centralizer of \(\mathcal S\) in \(\mathcal G_\Omega^0\).
assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\) is in the parahoric integral-model setup defining \(\mathcal G_\Omega^1\) and \(\mathcal G_\Omega^0\).
\(S\) is the maximal \(K\)-split torus of \(G\) corresponding to the apartment \(\mathcal A\), and \(T=C_G(S)\).
\(\mathcal S\) is the standard integral model (equivalently here, the connected Neron model) of \(S\), and \(\mathcal T^0\) is the connected Neron model of \(T\).
statements.conclusion_latex: \(S(K)^1\subseteq G(K)_\Omega^1\). The inclusion \(S\hookrightarrow G\) extends to a closed immersion \(\mathcal S\hookrightarrow\mathcal G_\Omega^1\), whose \(\mathcal S\)-root system is \(\Phi(S,G)\) and whose root group for \(a\in\Phi(S,G)\) is \(\mathcal U_{a,\Omega,0}\). Moreover, \(T\) is a maximal torus, \(\mathcal S\hookrightarrow\mathcal T^0\hookrightarrow\mathcal G_\Omega^0\) are closed immersions extending \(S\hookrightarrow T\hookrightarrow G\), and \(\mathcal T^0=C_{\mathcal G_\Omega^0}(\mathcal S)\).

statements.title: Unramified base change of the standard torus model
statements.statement_plain: For a k-torus T and a possibly non-algebraic unramified extension k1/k of Henselian discretely valued fields, with ramification degree one and separable residue extension, the standard model of the base-changed torus T_{k1} is naturally the base change of the standard model of T from the valuation ring o to the ring of integers o1 of k1.

assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a \(k\)-torus.
\(k_1/k\) is a possibly non-algebraic extension of Henselian discretely valued fields.
The ramification degree satisfies \(e(k_1/k)=1\), and the induced possibly non-algebraic extension of residue fields is separable (the stated sense of unramified).
statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{std}}_{k_1}\cong\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{std}}\times_{\mathfrak{o}}\mathfrak{o}_1\), where \(\mathfrak{o}_1\) is the ring of integers of \(k_1\).
statements.scope_note: \(\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{std}}\) denotes the standard model of \(T\) over \(\mathfrak{o}\), and \(\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{std}}_{k_1}\) denotes the standard model of the base-changed torus \(T_{k_1}\).

statements.title: Generators and Root Groups of the Integral Model Attached to a Bounded Subset
statements.statement_plain: Let Omega be a nonempty bounded subset of the apartment of S, and let the associated smooth affine integral group scheme have generic fiber G and closed split torus with generic fiber S. Its integral-point group is generated by the connected centralizer subgroup Z(k)^0 and the affine-root filtration groups whose affine roots are nonnegative on Omega. For every root a, the integral points of the corresponding root-group model equal the product of filtration groups indexed by affine roots with derivatives a and 2a when 2a is a root, and equal the first filtration group when 2a is not a root; in the former case the product reduces to the first factor when the stated affine-root inequality holds.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varnothing\neq\Omega\subset\mathcal A(S)\) be bounded, and let \(\mathcal G^0_\Omega\) be the associated smooth affine \(\mathfrak o\)-group scheme with generic fiber \(G\). Let \(\mathcal S\) be its closed \(\mathfrak o\)-split torus with generic fiber \(S\), and for \(a\in\Phi\) let \(\mathcal U_{a,\Omega}\) be its \(a\)-root group relative to \(\mathcal S\). Then \(G(k)^0_\Omega=\mathcal G^0_\Omega(\mathfrak o)\) is generated by \(Z(k)^0\) and all \(U_\psi\) with \(\psi\in\Psi\) and \(\psi(\Omega)\subset\mathbf R_{\geq0}\). Moreover, for every \(a\in\Phi\), there is an affine root \(\psi_a^\Omega\), with derivative \(a\) and nonnegative on \(\Omega\), such that if \(2a\in\Phi\) then \(\mathcal U_{a,\Omega}(\mathfrak o)=U_{\psi_a^\Omega}U_{\psi_{2a}^\Omega}\), while if \(2a\notin\Phi\) then \(\mathcal U_{a,\Omega}(\mathfrak o)=U_{\psi_a^\Omega}\); in the former case the product equals \(U_{\psi_a^\Omega}\) when \(\psi_{2a}^\Omega\geq2\psi_a^\Omega\).
assumptions_latex: \varnothing\neq\Omega\subset\mathcal A(S)\text{ is bounded}.
\mathcal G^0_\Omega\text{ is the associated smooth affine }\mathfrak o\text{-group scheme with generic fiber }G.
\mathcal S\subset\mathcal G^0_\Omega\text{ is the closed }\mathfrak o\text{-split torus with generic fiber }S.
\mathcal U_{a,\Omega}\text{ is the }a\text{-root group of }\mathcal G^0_\Omega\text{ relative to }\mathcal S\text{ for }a\in\Phi.
statements.conclusion_latex: G(k)^0_\Omega=\mathcal G^0_\Omega(\mathfrak o)=\left\langle Z(k)^0,\ U_\psi\ \middle|\ \psi\in\Psi,\ \psi(\Omega)\subset\mathbf R_{\geq0}\right\rangle.\quad\text{For every }a\in\Phi\text{ there is an affine root }\psi_a^\Omega\text{ with derivative }a\text{ and }\psi_a^\Omega(\Omega)\subset\mathbf R_{\geq0}\text{ such that }\mathcal U_{a,\Omega}(\mathfrak o)=\begin{cases}U_{\psi_a^\Omega}U_{\psi_{2a}^\Omega},&2a\in\Phi,\\U_{\psi_a^\Omega},&2a\notin\Phi,\end{cases}\text{ and, when }2a\in\Phi\text{ and }\psi_{2a}^\Omega\geq2\psi_a^\Omega,\text{ the product equals }U_{\psi_a^\Omega}.
statements.scope_note: Describes the generators of the integral points of the smooth affine model attached to a nonempty bounded subset and identifies each integral root group through affine-root filtration subgroups.

statements.title: Integral models and congruence shifts for root filtration subgroups
statements.statement_plain: Each root filtration subgroup U_{a,x,r} is schematic and connected and has a smooth connected integral model. For a multipliable root of type R2, the subgroup involving both the root and its double has the same property. If the valuation of K has value group Z, congruence level n shifts the filtration parameter by n for nonmultipliable roots, while for multipliable roots it shifts both parameters when s is at most 2r. In the multipliable case, the one-parameter shift identity fails: the congruence model retains the second parameter 2r+n.
statements.statement_latex: The root filtration subgroup U_{a,x,r} is schematic and connected and admits a smooth connected integral model \mathcal U_{a,x,r}. If a is of type R2, then U_{a,x,r}U_{2a,x,s} is likewise schematic and connected and admits a smooth connected integral model \mathcal U_{a,x,r,s}. Assuming \omega(K^\times)=\mathbf Z, for every integer n\ge0 one has (\mathcal U_{a,x,r})_n=\mathcal U_{a,x,r+n} when a is nonmultipliable (type R1 or R3), and (\mathcal U_{a,x,r,s})_n=\mathcal U_{a,x,r+n,s+n} when a is multipliable (type R2) and s\le2r. For multipliable a, (\mathcal U_{a,x,r})_n=(\mathcal U_{a,x,r,2r})_n=\mathcal U_{a,x,r+n,2r+n}, so (\mathcal U_{a,x,r})_n=\mathcal U_{a,x,r+n} does not hold.
assumptions_latex: a\text{ is of type R2 whenever }U_{a,x,r}U_{2a,x,s}\text{ is considered}
\omega(K^\times)=\mathbf Z\text{ for the congruence identities}
n\in\mathbf Z_{\ge 0}
s\le 2r\text{ in the multipliable congruence identity}
statements.conclusion_latex: U_{a,x,r}\text{ is schematic and connected and admits a smooth connected integral model }\mathcal U_{a,x,r}.\text{ If }a\text{ is of type R2, then }U_{a,x,r}U_{2a,x,s}\text{ is likewise schematic and connected and admits a smooth connected integral model }\mathcal U_{a,x,r,s}.\text{ If }\omega(K^\times)=\mathbf Z,\text{ then for every }n\ge0,\ (\mathcal U_{a,x,r})_n=\mathcal U_{a,x,r+n}\text{ for nonmultipliable }a\text{ (types R1 or R3), while }(\mathcal U_{a,x,r,s})_n=\mathcal U_{a,x,r+n,s+n}\text{ for multipliable }a\text{ (type R2) with }s\le2r.\text{ For multipliable }a,\ (\mathcal U_{a,x,r})_n=(\mathcal U_{a,x,r,2r})_n=\mathcal U_{a,x,r+n,2r+n},\text{ so the analogous one-parameter identity }(\mathcal U_{a,x,r})_n=\mathcal U_{a,x,r+n}\text{ does not hold}.

statements.title: Lie Algebras of Unitary Root Filtration Integral Models
statements.statement_plain: The unitary root group X and its variant X^lambda have Lie algebra L direct sum L^0, and the specified isomorphism has identity differential there. After undoing the filtration shift by mu, the Lie algebra of the integral model associated to the filtered product at real levels r and s is the direct sum of the lattice M_L at exponent 2r' and the lattice lambda varpi M_L at exponent s' minus one half, with r' and s' given by the stated least admissible indices.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=U_{L/K}\) be the closed subvariety of \((\mathrm R_{L/K}\mathbf A^1)^2\) defined by \(u\bar u=v+\bar v\), and put \(L^0=\{V\in L\mid V+\bar V=0\}\). Then \(\operatorname{Lie}(X)=\operatorname{Lie}(X^\lambda)=L\oplus L^0\), and the differential at the identity of the specified isomorphism \(X\to X^\lambda\) is the identity on this space. For \(r,s\in\mathbf R\), define \(\widetilde X(K)_r=X(K)_{r-\mu/2}\), \(\widetilde Z(K)_s=Z(K)_{s-\mu}\), and let \(\widetilde{\mathcal X}_{r,s}\) be the integral model associated to \(\widetilde X(K)_r\widetilde Z(K)_s\). If \(r'=\inf\{h\in J_{a/2a}:h\ge r-\mu/2\}\) and \(s'=\inf\{h\in J_{2a}:h\ge\min(2r,s)-\mu\}\), while \(\varpi\) and \(\lambda\) are chosen with \(\lambda\varpi\in L^0\), then \[\operatorname{Lie}(\widetilde{\mathcal X}_{r,s})=\mathcal M_L^{2r'}\oplus\lambda\varpi\cdot\mathcal M_L^{s'-1/2}.\]
assumptions_latex: X=U_{L/K}=\{(u,v)\in(\mathrm R_{L/K}\mathbf A^1)^2\mid u\bar u=v+\bar v\},\qquad L^0=\{V\in L\mid V+\bar V=0\}.
r,s\in\mathbf R,\qquad \widetilde X(K)_r=X(K)_{r-\mu/2}=\{(u,v)\in U_{L/K}(K)\mid \omega(v)/2\ge r\}.
\widetilde Z(K)_s=Z(K)_{s-\mu}=\{(0,v)\in U_{L/K}^0(K)\mid \omega(v)\ge s\},\quad \widetilde{\mathcal X}_{r,s}\text{ is the integral model associated to }\widetilde X(K)_r\widetilde Z(K)_s.
r'=\inf\{h\in J_{a/2a}\mid h\ge r-\mu/2\},\qquad s'=\inf\{h\in J_{2a}\mid h\ge\min(2r,s)-\mu\}.
\varpi\text{ is a uniformizer of }L,\quad \lambda\in L^{\mathrm{tr}=1,\max},\quad \lambda\varpi\in L^0.
statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Lie}(X)=\operatorname{Lie}(X^\lambda)=L\oplus L^0,\qquad d(X\xrightarrow{\sim}X^\lambda)_{(0,0)}=\operatorname{id}_{L\oplus L^0},\qquad \operatorname{Lie}(\widetilde{\mathcal X}_{r,s})=\mathcal M_L^{2r'}\oplus\lambda\varpi\cdot\mathcal M_L^{s'-1/2}.

statements.title: Closed Root-Index Subsets and Elementary GL_n Subgroup Schemes
statements.statement_plain: For indices from 1 through n, Theta is the set of ordered pairs of distinct indices; Theta-plus and Theta-minus consist respectively of pairs with i less than j and i greater than j. A subset Psi of Theta is closed when (i,j) and (j,k) in Psi imply (i,k) in Psi. The map x to 1 plus x is an automorphism of the scheme L, and on each L_ij it is a group-scheme isomorphism onto a closed subgroup scheme B_ij of GL(M).
statements.statement_latex: \(\Theta=\{(i,j)\mid 1\le i\ne j\le n\}\), \(\Theta^{+}=\{(i,j)\in\Theta\mid i<j\}\), and \(\Theta^{-}=\{(i,j)\in\Theta\mid i>j\}\). A subset \(\Psi\subseteq\Theta\) is closed if \((i,j),(j,k)\in\Psi\) imply \((i,k)\in\Psi\). The morphism \(x\mapsto1+x\) is an automorphism of the scheme \(\mathfrak{L}\); for each \((i,j)\in\Theta\), its restriction to \(\mathfrak{L}_{ij}\) is a group-scheme isomorphism onto a closed subgroup scheme \(\mathfrak{B}_{ij}\subseteq\mathfrak{GL}(M)\).
assumptions_latex: n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1};\quad \Theta=\{(i,j)\mid 1\le i\ne j\le n\}.
\mathfrak{L} and the subschemes \mathfrak{L}_{ij} are the objects defined in the surrounding GL(M) construction.
statements.conclusion_latex: A subset \(\Psi\subseteq\Theta\) is closed if \((i,j),(j,k)\in\Psi\Rightarrow(i,k)\in\Psi\). statements.title: Extension of a Group Law from Two Product Decompositions
statements.statement_plain: Let Y be a K-group scheme with closed K-group subschemes X1 and X2. Let Y extend to a flat A-scheme and each Xi extend to a flat A-group scheme. If multiplication in both orders extends to A-scheme isomorphisms from the corresponding products of the integral models onto the model of Y, then the group law of Y extends to a group law on that model.

If the product maps in both orders extend to }A\text{-scheme isomorphisms }\alpha:\mathfrak X_1\times\mathfrak X_2\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathfrak Y\text{ and }\beta:\mathfrak X_2\times\mathfrak X_1\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathfrak Y,\text{ then the group law on }Y\text{ extends to a group law on }\mathfrak Y.

statements.title: Affine-level classification of rank-one derived subgroups
statements.statement_plain: The group G_v has residue-field rank one. The affine level determines three cases: level in (1/2)J_{2a} minus J_{a/{2a}} gives roots {2a,-2a} and derived group SL_2/f; level in J_{a/{2a}} minus (1/2)J_{2a} gives roots {a,-a} and derived group PGL_2/f; and v in J_{a/{2a}} intersect (1/2)J_{2a} gives a three-dimensional unipotent quotient, roots {a,-a,2a,-2a}, and derived group SU_3 for the quadratic extension f_l/f, with l/k necessarily unramified.
statements.statement_latex: The group \(G_v\) has \(\mathfrak f\)-rank one, with root subgroups \(U_a(k)_{\langle-a,v\rangle}/U_a(k)_{\langle-a,v\rangle+}\) and \(U_{-a}(k)_{\langle a,v\rangle}/U_{-a}(k)_{\langle a,v\rangle+}\). If \(\langle a,v\rangle\in\tfrac12J_{2a}\setminus J_{a/{2a}}\), the first quotient is a one-dimensional \(\mathfrak f\)-vector space on which \(T\) acts by \(2a\); the root system is \(\{2a,-2a\}\) and \(G_v^{\mathrm{der}}\simeq\mathrm{SL}_2/\mathfrak f\). If \(\langle a,v\rangle\in J_{a/{2a}}\setminus\tfrac12J_{2a}\), the first quotient is one-dimensional over \(\mathfrak f\), \(T\) acts by \(a\), the root system is \(\{a,-a\}\), and \(G_v^{\mathrm{der}}\simeq\mathrm{PGL}_2/\mathfrak f\). If \(v\in J_{a/{2a}}\cap\tfrac12J_{2a}\), the first quotient is a three-dimensional unipotent group over \(\mathfrak f\), the root system is \(\{a,-a,2a,-2a\}\), and \(G_v^{\mathrm{der}}\simeq\mathrm{SU}_3\) for the quadratic extension \(\mathfrak f_\ell/\mathfrak f\); in this case \(\ell/k\) is necessarily unramified.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is the quasi-split simple rank-one group in the source example, with indicated torus \(T\) and root \(a\).
\(\mathfrak f\) is the residue field and the displayed affine root-group quotients are defined at \(v\).
\(J_{2a}\), \(J_{a/{2a}}\), and the quadratic extension \(\mathfrak f_\ell/\mathfrak f\) are the source-defined data; the unramified assertion concerns the corresponding \(\ell/k\) in the third case.
statements.conclusion_latex: The three stated affine-level conditions yield the corresponding graded-root-group dimensions, relative root systems, and derived-group identifications for \(G_v\).
statements.scope_note: In the quasi-split simple rank-one setting of Proposition 3.10.4, with residue field \(\mathfrak f\), torus \(T\), root \(a\), and the source-defined index sets \(J_{2a}\) and \(J_{a/{2a}}\), the affine root-group quotients determine the relative roots and the derived subgroup of \(G_v\).

statements.title: Sufficient Conditions for Goodness of a Family at a Weight
statements.statement_plain: In the split-case construction, each of three conditions is sufficient for the family f of root-group ideals to be good for the weight omega: all g(lambda) are invertible; all f(a) are contained in A; or every weight lambda in Pi equals omega minus some root a in Phi. In the second case one may take every hat g(lambda) equal to A, and in the third use hat g(omega)=A and hat g(lambda)=f(lambda-omega) otherwise. The third condition holds for the standard representations of SL_n and Sp_2n.
statements.statement_latex: \text{Each of the following conditions is sufficient for }f\text{ to be good for }\omega:\quad (i)\ g(\lambda)\text{ is invertible for every }\lambda\in\Pi;\quad (ii)\ f(a)\subset A\text{ for every }a\in\Phi;\quad (iii)\text{ every }\lambda\in\Pi\text{ has the form }\omega-a\text{ for some }a\in\Phi.\ \text{Condition (iii) holds for the standard representations of }\mathrm{SL}_n\text{ and }\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}.
assumptions_latex: A is the coefficient ring in the split-case schematic-root-datum setup, with fraction field K.
\Phi is the root system, \Pi is the weight set, and \omega is the distinguished weight of the representation.
f=(f(a))_{a\in\Phi} is a family of invertible fractional ideals of A; g(\lambda) (\lambda\in\Pi) is the fractional ideal defined from the associated module M_f.
Goodness for \omega means existence of invertible fractional ideals \widehat g(\lambda) satisfying the required containment relations.
statements.conclusion_latex: \left(\forall\lambda\in\Pi,\ g(\lambda)\text{ is invertible}\right)\ \lor\ \left(\forall a\in\Phi,\ f(a)\subset A\right)\ \lor\ \left(\forall\lambda\in\Pi\ \exists a\in\Phi:\lambda=\omega-a\right)\ \Longrightarrow\ f\text{ is good for }\omega;\ \text{in the second case take }\widehat g(\lambda)=A,\ \text{and in the third take }\widehat g(\omega)=A,\ \widehat g(\lambda)=f(\lambda-\omega)\ (\lambda\ne\omega).\ \text{The third condition holds for the standard representations of }\mathrm{SL}_n\text{ and }\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}.
statements.scope_note: Sufficient goodness criteria in the split-case construction of a schematic root datum and its weight module.

statements.title: Minimal Congruent Filtration and Smooth Models of a Torus
statements.statement_plain: For every nonnegative depth r, the minimal congruent subgroup of T(K)^1 and its smooth model are defined piecewise. At r=0 they are T(K)^0, the Iwahori subgroup, and its model \mathcal T^0. For 0<r<1, T(K)_r^mc is generated by \mathcal T^0(\mathcal M) and the images of the standard depth-r subgroups R(K)_r^std for all induced tori R equipped with K-homomorphisms R to T; its smooth model is denoted \mathcal T_r^mc. For r at least 1, write r=r_0+n with n in N and 0<=r_0<1; then \mathcal T_r^mc is the nth congruence subgroup of \mathcal T_{r_0}^mc and T(K)_r^mc consists of its \mathcal O-points.
statements.statement_latex: For each r\geq0, define the subgroup T(K)_{r}^{\mathrm{mc}} of T(K)^1 and the smooth model \mathcal T_{r}^{\mathrm{mc}} by the three cases stated in the conclusion.
assumptions_latex: r\geq 0
statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned} &T(K)_{r}^{\mathrm{mc}}\subseteq T(K)^{1}.\\ &r=0:\quad T(K)_{0}^{\mathrm{mc}}=T(K)^{0}\text{ (the Iwahori subgroup)},\quad \mathcal T_{0}^{\mathrm{mc}}=\mathcal T^{0}.\\ &0<r<1:\quad T(K)_{r}^{\mathrm{mc}}=\left\langle \mathcal T^{0}(\mathcal M),\ f\!\left(R(K)_{r}^{\mathrm{std}}\right)\ \middle|\ f:R\to T\text{ a }K\text{-homomorphism},\ R\text{ induced}\right\rangle;\ \mathcal T_{r}^{\mathrm{mc}}\text{ is its smooth model}.\\ &r\geq1:\quad r=r_{0}+n,\ n\in\mathbf N,\ 0\leq r_{0}<1;\ \mathcal T_{r}^{\mathrm{mc}}\text{ is the }n\text{th congruence subgroup of }\mathcal T_{r_{0}}^{\mathrm{mc}},\quad T(K)_{r}^{\mathrm{mc}}=\mathcal T_{r}^{\mathrm{mc}}(\mathcal O).\end{aligned}
statements.scope_note: Defines the minimal congruent subgroup filtration of T(K)^1 and its smooth models at all nonnegative depths using the source's notation.

statements.title: Algebraic fundamental group and Kottwitz homomorphism
statements.statement_plain: For a connected reductive k-group G, the algebraic fundamental group pi_1(G) is a finitely generated abelian group with Theta-action. Kottwitz constructs a functorial homomorphism from G(k) to the inertia-coinvariant, Gamma-invariant part pi_1(G)_I^Gamma; it is continuous for the analytic topology on G(k) and the discrete topology on the target, and surjective when dim(f) is at most 1, in particular when k equals K.

statements.title: Kottwitz homomorphism for a torus
statements.statement_plain: For every K-torus T, there is a unique surjective homomorphism from T(K) to the inertia-coinvariant cocharacter group X_*(T)_I. For every finite Galois splitting field L/K, composing the norm from T(L) to T(K) with this homomorphism equals the valuation homomorphism from T(L) to X_*(T) followed by projection to X_*(T)_I, with the valuation on L normalized so that L^× maps onto Z. If T comes by base change from a k-torus, the homomorphism is Gal(K/k)-equivariant.
statements.statement_latex: For every K-torus T there exists a unique surjective homomorphism \(\kappa_T:T(K)\to X_*(T)_I\) such that, for every finite Galois extension \(L/K\) splitting T, \(\kappa_T\circ N_{L/K}=(X_*(T)\to X_*(T)_I)\circ\omega_{T,L}\), where \(\omega_{T,L}:T(L)\to X_*(T)\) is the valuation homomorphism for the valuation on L normalized so that \(L^{\times}\twoheadrightarrow\mathbf Z\). If T is obtained by base change from a k-torus, then \(\kappa_T\) is \(\operatorname{Gal}(K/k)\)-equivariant.
assumptions_latex: T is a K-torus.
L/K is a finite Galois extension splitting T, with the valuation on L normalized so that L^{\times} maps onto \mathbf{Z}.
If T is obtained by base change from a k-torus, the Gal(K/k)-equivariance assertion applies.
statements.conclusion_latex: There is a unique surjective homomorphism \(\kappa_T:T(K)\to X_*(T)_I\) such that for every finite Galois splitting extension \(L/K\), \(\kappa_T\circ N_{L/K}=(X_*(T)\to X_*(T)_I)\circ\omega_{T,L}\); when T is obtained by base change from a k-torus, \(\kappa_T\) is \(\operatorname{Gal}(K/k)\)-equivariant.
statements.scope_note: Kottwitz homomorphism for a torus over K, characterized via the valuation homomorphism on finite Galois splitting extensions and projection to inertia coinvariants.

children.role: Algebraic fundamental groups, z-extensions, and reduction to simply connected derived groups.

statements.title: Construction and closure properties of z-extensions
statements.statement_plain: For a connected reductive group G, start with the finite-kernel map from the identity component of its center times the simply connected cover of its derived group. Embed the kernel into an induced torus obtained from a free Galois-module presentation, and push out to obtain 1 -> Z -> G-tilde -> G -> 1. G-tilde is connected reductive and its derived subgroup is the embedded G_sc. Fiber products of z-extensions remain z-extensions, and the stated fiber product construction pulls z-extensions back along a homomorphism G -> H.
statements.statement_latex: For a connected reductive k-group G, push out the canonical finite-kernel extension Z(G)^{\circ}\times G_{\mathrm{sc}}\to G along an induced torus embedding \mu\hookrightarrow Z obtained from a free Galois-module presentation of X^{*}(\mu). This yields the z-extension 1\to Z\to\widetilde G\to G\to1 with \widetilde G connected reductive and (\widetilde G)_{\mathrm{der}}=G_{\mathrm{sc}}. Fiber products of z-extensions over a common quotient remain z-extensions, and pulling back along any homomorphism G\to H produces a z-extension of G with a commuting diagram.
assumptions_latex: Let G be a connected reductive k-group; let G_{\mathrm{sc}} be the simply connected cover of its derived subgroup and let Z(G)^{\circ} be the identity component of its center.
The product Z(G)^{\circ}\times G_{\mathrm{sc}}\to G is surjective with finite kernel \mu.
Choose a finite Galois extension \ell/k splitting G, and choose a free Gal(\ell/k)-module M together with a quotient M\twoheadrightarrow X^{*}(\mu).
statements.conclusion_latex: Let Z be the torus with X^{*}(Z)=M, so Z is induced and \mu\hookrightarrow Z. Pushing out 1\to\mu\to Z(G)^{\circ}\times G_{\mathrm{sc}}\to G\to1 along \mu\hookrightarrow Z gives \widetilde G=(Z\times Z(G)^{\circ}\times G_{\mathrm{sc}})/\mu and an exact sequence 1\to Z\to\widetilde G\to G\to1. The group \widetilde G is connected reductive, and the natural embedded G_{\mathrm{sc}} is normal with image (\widetilde G)_{\mathrm{der}}. The fiber product over G of two z-extensions of G is a z-extension. Given z-extensions \widetilde G\to G and \widetilde H\to H and a homomorphism G\to H, the fiber product \widetilde G_{1}=\widetilde G\times_{H}\widetilde H\to G is a z-extension and gives a commuting diagram.
statements.scope_note: Construction of a z-extension of a connected reductive group from an induced torus, together with the stated fiber-product closure and pullback property.

statements.title: Canonical maximal-torus realization of the algebraic fundamental group
statements.statement_plain: For a reductive group over k, the cocharacter lattice of the simply connected preimage of a maximal torus embeds as the coroot lattice. Its quotient in the torus cocharacter lattice is finitely generated and, for a maximal k-torus, carries a Galois action. The quotients associated with any two maximal k-tori are canonically Galois-equivariantly isomorphic, independently of the conjugating element, and the isomorphisms compose compatibly.
statements.statement_latex: Let G be a reductive group over k, and let G_{\mathrm{sc}} be the simply connected cover of G_{\mathrm{der}}. For a maximal torus T\subset G, its preimage T_{\mathrm{sc}} is a maximal torus of G_{\mathrm{sc}}, and X_*(T_{\mathrm{sc}})\to X_*(T) is injective with image the coroot lattice. If T is defined over k, then \Pi(G,T):=X_*(T)/X_*(T_{\mathrm{sc}}) is a finitely generated abelian group with an action of \operatorname{Gal}(k_s/k). For maximal k-tori T,T', any g\in G_{\mathrm{sc}}(k_s) carrying T to T' induces a Galois-equivariant isomorphism \Pi(G,T)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Pi(G,T') that is independent of g, and these canonical isomorphisms are compatible with composition.
assumptions_latex: G\text{ is a reductive group over }k.
G_{\mathrm{sc}}\to G_{\mathrm{der}}\text{ is the simply connected cover of the derived subgroup of }G.
T\subset G\text{ is maximal; for the Galois action and comparison, }T\text{ and }T'\text{ are maximal }k\text{-tori, and }k_s\text{ is a separable closure of }k.
statements.conclusion_latex: X_*(T_{\mathrm{sc}})\hookrightarrow X_*(T)\text{ has image the coroot lattice, and }\Pi(G,T):=X_*(T)/X_*(T_{\mathrm{sc}})\text{ is finitely generated. For maximal }k\text{-tori }T,T',\text{ conjugation by }g\in G_{\mathrm{sc}}(k_s)\text{ carrying }T\text{ to }T'\text{ induces a choice-independent, Galois-equivariant isomorphism }\Pi(G,T)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Pi(G,T'),\text{ compatible with composition.}
statements.scope_note: Canonical realization of the algebraic fundamental group through cocharacter quotients of maximal tori; Galois assertions apply to maximal tori defined over k.

statements.title: Component Groups of Chamber and Bounded-Subset Integral Models
statements.statement_plain: For a chamber in the building of G over K, the Kottwitz map identifies the component group of its integral model with the inertia coinvariants of the algebraic fundamental group. For a Theta-invariant chamber, this identification is Galois-equivariant. More generally, for any bounded subset of an apartment, the Kottwitz map identifies the component group of its integral model with a subgroup of those coinvariants; the identification is Theta-invariant when the subset is Theta-stable.
statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal C be a chamber in \mathcal B(G_K). The component group of \mathcal G_{\mathcal C} is identified via \kappa with \pi_1(G)_I. If \mathcal C is \Theta-invariant, this identification is \operatorname{Gal}(K/k)-equivariant. More generally, if \Omega is any bounded subset of an apartment of \mathcal B(G_K), the component group of \mathcal G_\Omega is identified via \kappa with a subgroup of \pi_1(G)_I, and this identification is \Theta-invariant provided that \Omega is \Theta-stable.

\Omega\subset \mathcal B(G_K)\text{ is a bounded subset of an apartment, for the general assertion.}

statements.title: Centralizer Enlarged Building and Bruhat-Tits Group Scheme Definitions
statements.statement_plain: For a K-split torus S in H with centralizer M, the enlarged building of M is identified with the union of ambient apartments attached to maximal K-split tori containing S. For every nonempty bounded subset Omega of an apartment of the building of H, there is a smooth affine group scheme over O with generic fiber H whose O-points are exactly the elements of H(K)^1 fixing Omega pointwise. Its relative identity component is an open affine subgroup scheme, called the Bruhat-Tits group scheme of Omega, and its special fiber is denoted Hbar_Omega^0.
statements.statement_latex: For a K-split torus S of H and M=Z_H(S), view \widetilde{\mathcal B}(M) as the union of those apartments in \widetilde{\mathcal B}(H) attached to maximal K-split tori containing S. For every non-empty bounded subset \Omega of an apartment of \mathcal B(H), let \mathcal H^1_\Omega be the smooth affine \mathcal O-group scheme with generic fiber H satisfying \mathcal H^1_\Omega(\mathcal O)=H(K)^1_\Omega, the pointwise stabilizer of \Omega. Its relative identity component \mathcal H^0_\Omega is an open affine 0-subgroup scheme of \mathcal H^1_\Omega, defined as the union of the generic fiber H and the identity component of the special fiber; it is called the Bruhat-Tits group scheme associated to \Omega, and its special fiber is written \overline{\mathcal H}^0_\Omega.
assumptions_latex: S\subset H is a K-split torus, and M=Z_H(S).
\Omega is a non-empty bounded subset of an apartment of \mathcal B(H).
statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde{\mathcal B}(M) is identified with the union of apartments of \widetilde{\mathcal B}(H) corresponding to maximal K-split tori of H containing S. There exists a smooth affine \mathcal O-group scheme \mathcal H^1_\Omega with generic fiber H and \mathcal H^1_\Omega(\mathcal O)=H(K)^1_\Omega, the subgroup of H(K)^1 fixing \Omega pointwise. Its relative identity component \mathcal H^0_\Omega is an open affine 0-subgroup scheme of \mathcal H^1_\Omega and is the Bruhat-Tits group scheme associated to \Omega; its special fiber is denoted \overline{\mathcal H}^0_\Omega.

statements.title: Bruhat-Tits Group Schemes for Bounded Subsets
statements.statement_plain: For every nonempty bounded subset of an apartment, there is a smooth affine integral group scheme with generic fiber G whose integral points are the associated full bounded-subset subgroup; its relative identity component has the corresponding connected subgroup as its integral points. These subgroups are open and bounded. Over a strictly Henselian field the integral-point condition determines the full model up to isomorphism. The connected model depends only on the containing facet when the subset lies in one, and it is unchanged upon closing the subset. A maximal split torus defining the apartment extends to a closed split torus in the connected model whose special fiber is maximal split. For semisimple simply connected G, the connected and full models coincide. The coordinate rings consist of the regular functions on G that are integral-valued on the respective integral points.
statements.statement_latex: Let \Omega be a nonempty bounded subset of an apartment \mathcal A of \mathcal B(G). There is a smooth affine \mathfrak o-group scheme \mathcal G^1_\Omega with generic fiber G and \mathcal G^1_\Omega(\mathfrak o)=G(k)^1_\Omega. Its relative identity component \mathcal G^0_\Omega satisfies \mathcal G^0_\Omega(\mathfrak o)=G(k)^0_\Omega, and both subgroups are open and bounded. If k is strictly Henselian, the stated integral-point condition determines \mathcal G^1_\Omega up to isomorphism. If \Omega\subseteq\mathcal F for a facet \mathcal F, then \mathcal G^0_\Omega=\mathcal G^0_\mathcal F, and \mathcal G^0_\Omega=\mathcal G^0_{\overline\Omega}. If \mathcal A corresponds to a maximal k-split torus S, then \mathcal G^0_\Omega contains a closed \mathfrak o-split torus \mathcal S with generic fiber S, whose special fiber \overline{\mathcal S} is maximal \mathfrak f-split in \overline{\mathcal G}^0_\Omega. If G is semisimple and simply connected, then \mathcal G^0_\Omega=\mathcal G^1_\Omega. Smoothness also gives \mathcal O[\mathcal G^i_\Omega]=\{f\in K[G]\mid f(\mathcal G^i_\Omega(\mathcal O))\subseteq\mathcal O\} for i=0,1.
assumptions_latex: \Omega\ne\varnothing\text{ is a bounded subset of an apartment }\mathcal A\subset\mathcal B(G).
statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\,\mathcal G^1_\Omega/\mathfrak o\text{ smooth affine with generic fiber }G,\quad \mathcal G^1_\Omega(\mathfrak o)=G(k)^1_\Omega,\quad \mathcal G^0_\Omega(\mathfrak o)=G(k)^0_\Omega,\text{ where }\mathcal G^0_\Omega\text{ is the relative identity component. Moreover }G(k)^0_\Omega\text{ and }G(k)^1_\Omega\text{ are open and bounded; if }k\text{ is strictly Henselian, the integral-point condition determines }\mathcal G^1_\Omega\text{ up to isomorphism; if }\Omega\subseteq\mathcal F\text{ for a facet }\mathcal F,\text{ then }\mathcal G^0_\Omega=\mathcal G^0_\mathcal F;\quad \mathcal G^0_\Omega=\mathcal G^0_{\overline\Omega};\text{ if }\mathcal A\text{ corresponds to a maximal }k\text{-split torus }S,\text{ then }\mathcal G^0_\Omega\text{ contains a closed }\mathfrak o\text{-split torus }\mathcal S\text{ with generic fiber }S\text{ and }\overline{\mathcal S}\text{ maximal }\mathfrak f\text{-split in }\overline{\mathcal G}^0_\Omega;\text{ and if }G\text{ is semisimple and simply connected, then }\mathcal G^0_\Omega=\mathcal G^1_\Omega.\text{ Finally, }\mathcal O[\mathcal G^i_\Omega]=\{f\in K[G]\mid f(\mathcal G^i_\Omega(\mathcal O))\subseteq\mathcal O\}\text{ for }i\in\{0,1\}.

statements.title: Bruhat-Tits group scheme attached to a bounded apartment subset
statements.statement_plain: For every nonempty bounded subset Omega of an apartment of the Bruhat-Tits building B(H), there is a smooth affine O-group scheme H^1_Omega with generic fiber H whose O-points are exactly the elements of H(K)^1 fixing Omega pointwise. Its relative identity component H^0_Omega is an open affine O-subgroup scheme with generic fiber H and special fiber the identity component of the special fiber of H^1_Omega. This H^0_Omega is the Bruhat-Tits group scheme attached to Omega, and its special fiber is denoted overline{H}^0_Omega.
statements.statement_latex: For every nonempty bounded subset \(\Omega\) of an apartment of \(\mathcal B(H)\), there is a smooth affine \(\mathcal O\)-group scheme \(\mathcal H^1_\Omega\) with generic fiber \(H\) such that \(\mathcal H^1_\Omega(\mathcal O)=H(K)^1_\Omega\), the subgroup of \(H(K)^1\) fixing \(\Omega\) pointwise. The relative identity component \(\mathcal H^0_\Omega\) is an open affine \(\mathcal O\)-subgroup scheme with generic fiber \(H\) and special fiber equal to the identity component of \((\mathcal H^1_\Omega)_k\); it is called the Bruhat--Tits group scheme associated to \(\Omega\), and its special fiber is denoted \(\overline{\mathcal H}^0_\Omega\).

Its relative identity component \(\mathcal H^0_\Omega\) is an open affine \(\mathcal O\)-subgroup scheme whose generic fiber is \(H\) and whose special fiber is the identity component of the special fiber of \(\mathcal H^1_\Omega\); by definition it is the Bruhat--Tits group scheme attached to \(\Omega\), and its special fiber is denoted \(\overline{\mathcal H}^0_\Omega\).

statements.title: Structure of Dynamic Subgroup Schemes Associated with a Cocharacter
statements.statement_plain: Let G be a finitely presented smooth group scheme over A with a cocharacter lambda. The associated centralizer, parabolic, and unipotent subgroup schemes are smooth, and multiplication from U_G(-lambda) times P_G(lambda) to G is an open immersion. It is an isomorphism when A is a field and G is connected and solvable. When G is reductive, P_G(lambda) is parabolic and U_G(lambda) is its unipotent radical. When A is a field, U_G(lambda) is split.
statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal G be a group scheme of finite presentation and smooth over A, and let \lambda:\mathbb G_{m,A}\to\mathcal G be a cocharacter. Then \mathcal Z_{\mathcal G}(\lambda), \mathcal P_{\mathcal G}(\lambda), and \mathcal U_{\mathcal G}(\lambda) are smooth, and multiplication \mathcal U_{\mathcal G}(-\lambda)\times\mathcal P_{\mathcal G}(\lambda)\to\mathcal G is an open immersion. If A is a field and \mathcal G is connected and solvable, this open immersion is an isomorphism. If \mathcal G is reductive, \mathcal P_{\mathcal G}(\lambda) is a parabolic subgroup scheme and \mathcal U_{\mathcal G}(\lambda) is its unipotent radical. If A is a field, \mathcal U_{\mathcal G}(\lambda) is split.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal G\text{ is a group scheme of finite presentation and smooth over }A.
\lambda:\mathbb G_{m,A}\to\mathcal G\text{ is a cocharacter.}
statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal Z_{\mathcal G}(\lambda),\ \mathcal P_{\mathcal G}(\lambda),\text{ and }\mathcal U_{\mathcal G}(\lambda)\text{ are smooth, and }\mathcal U_{\mathcal G}(-\lambda)\times\mathcal P_{\mathcal G}(\lambda)\to\mathcal G\text{ is an open immersion. If }A\text{ is a field and }\mathcal G\text{ is connected and solvable, this map is an isomorphism. If }\mathcal G\text{ is reductive, }\mathcal P_{\mathcal G}(\lambda)\text{ is parabolic and }\mathcal U_{\mathcal G}(\lambda)\text{ is its unipotent radical. If }A\text{ is a field, }\mathcal U_{\mathcal G}(\lambda)\text{ is split.}
statements.scope_note: Structural properties of the dynamic subgroup schemes associated with a cocharacter; the isomorphism, parabolicity, and splitting conclusions retain their separate additional hypotheses.

statements.title: Properties of Greenberg Functors
statements.statement_plain: For every defined level n, Gr_n(X) is smooth, locally of finite type, and separated. If X is affine, Gr_n(X) is affine. If X is a group scheme, the transition Gr_{n+1}(X) to Gr_n(X) is a smooth surjective group homomorphism with vector-group kernel, and Gr_n(X^0) equals the identity component Gr_n(X)^0.
statements.statement_latex: For each level n, the Greenberg functor satisfies: (1) \(\operatorname{Gr}_{n}(\mathcal X)\) is smooth, locally of finite type, and separated; (2) if \(\mathcal X\) is affine, then \(\operatorname{Gr}_{n}(\mathcal X)\) is affine; (3) if \(\mathcal X\) is a group scheme, then \(\operatorname{Gr}_{n+1}(\mathcal X)\to\operatorname{Gr}_{n}(\mathcal X)\) is a smooth surjective group homomorphism with vector-group kernel; and (4) if \(\mathcal X\) is a group scheme, \(\operatorname{Gr}_{n}(\mathcal X^{0})=\operatorname{Gr}_{n}(\mathcal X)^{0}\).
statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}(1)\;&\operatorname{Gr}_{n}(\mathcal X)\text{ is smooth, locally of finite type, and separated}.\\(2)\;&\mathcal X\text{ affine}\implies\operatorname{Gr}_{n}(\mathcal X)\text{ affine}.\\(3)\;&\mathcal X\text{ a group scheme}\implies\operatorname{Gr}_{n+1}(\mathcal X)\to\operatorname{Gr}_{n}(\mathcal X)\text{ is a smooth surjective group homomorphism with vector-group kernel}.\\(4)\;&\mathcal X\text{ a group scheme}\implies\operatorname{Gr}_{n}(\mathcal X^{0})=\operatorname{Gr}_{n}(\mathcal X)^{0}.\end{aligned}
statements.scope_note: For each level n for which the Greenberg functor is defined; clauses (2)-(4) have exactly the affine or group-scheme hypotheses stated.

statements.title: Image Factorization and Dimension Formula for Smooth Affine Group Schemes
statements.statement_plain: For a homomorphism from a smooth affine algebraic group scheme A to an affine algebraic group scheme B over a field k, the topological image with reduced scheme structure is a smooth closed affine subgroup. The homomorphism factors through this image as a faithfully flat map followed by a closed immersion, and the dimension of A minus the dimension of its kernel equals the dimension of the image.
statements.statement_latex: Let f:A\to B be a homomorphism of affine algebraic group schemes over a field k, with A smooth over k and K=\ker(f). Endow the topological image of A in B with its reduced scheme structure. Then \operatorname{im}(f) is a smooth closed (hence affine) subgroup of B, f factors as A\to\operatorname{im}(f)\hookrightarrow B with the first map faithfully flat and the second a closed immersion, and \dim(A)-\dim(K)=\dim\operatorname{im}(f).
assumptions_latex: A and B are affine algebraic group schemes over a field k.
A is smooth over k.
f:A\to B is a homomorphism and K=\ker(f).
statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{im}(f)\subseteq B, equipped with its reduced scheme structure, is a smooth closed (hence affine) subgroup; f factors as a faithfully flat homomorphism A\to\operatorname{im}(f) followed by a closed immersion \operatorname{im}(f)\hookrightarrow B; and \dim A-\dim K=\dim\operatorname{im}(f).

statements.statement_plain: For a nontrivial split torus S over o and a nonzero character a, the kernel C_a is the diagonalizable group scheme associated with the quotient character lattice X*(S)/Za. statements.title: Integral Models and Extensions of Affine-Variety Morphisms
statements.statement_plain: For an affine variety X over k, an integral model is an affine flat finite-type scheme over \(\mathfrak{o}\) whose base change to k is isomorphic to X. A morphism between chosen models extends a morphism theta:X to Y when its base-change diagram commutes. A morphism between two models of X extends the identity on X.
statements.statement_latex: (1) For an affine variety X over k, an integral model is an affine, flat, finite-type \(\mathfrak{o}\)-scheme \(\mathcal{X}\) with an isomorphism \(\mathcal{X}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(\mathfrak{o})}\operatorname{Spec}(k)\to X\). (2) Given an affine variety Y over k, a morphism \(\theta:X\to Y\), and integral models \(\mathcal{X}\) and \(\mathcal{Y}\), an extension of \(\theta\) is an \(\mathfrak{o}\)-scheme morphism \(\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{Y}\) making the base-change diagram commute. (3) Given integral models \(\mathcal{X}_1\) and \(\mathcal{X}_2\) of X, a morphism of integral models is an extension of the identity automorphism \(\operatorname{id}_X\).
assumptions_latex: X\text{ is an affine variety over }k.
Y\text{ is an affine variety over }k,\ \theta:X\to Y\text{ is a morphism, and }\mathcal{X},\mathcal{Y}\text{ are integral models over }\mathfrak{o}.
\mathcal{X}_1\text{ and }\mathcal{X}_2\text{ are integral models of }X.
statements.conclusion_latex: (1) An integral model of X is an affine scheme \(\mathcal{X}\) over \(\mathfrak{o}\), flat and of finite type, equipped with an isomorphism \(\mathcal{X}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(\mathfrak{o})}\operatorname{Spec}(k)\to X\). (2) An extension of \(\theta\) is a morphism of \(\mathfrak{o}\)-schemes \(\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{Y}\) making the base-change diagram commute. (3) A morphism of integral models of X is an extension of \(\operatorname{id}_X\).

statements.title: Integral model attached to a schematic normal subgroup extension
statements.statement_plain: Let H be a smooth affine K-group. Let U be a bounded open subgroup of H(K), normal in a subgroup V, and suppose U is schematic with a smooth affine integral model mathcal U. Then there is a smooth separated group scheme mathcal V, not necessarily affine, with generic fiber H and mathcal V(O)=V. The map mathcal U to mathcal V uniquely extends the inclusion U into V in H(K), is an open immersion, and induces an isomorphism of relative identity components. If the index [V:U] is finite, mathcal V is affine. For every local ring extension R of O, mathcal V(R)=mathcal U(R) times V. If H is obtained by base change from a smooth affine k-group and the constructed model mathcal V is Gamma-invariant, mathcal V descends to an o-group scheme.
statements.statement_latex: \text{Let }U\subset V\subset H(K)\text{ be subgroups with }U\trianglelefteq V\text{ and }U\text{ bounded open, and suppose }U\text{ has a smooth affine integral model }\mathcal U.\text{ Then there exists a smooth separated group scheme }\mathcal V\text{ (not necessarily affine) with generic fiber }H\text{ and }\mathcal V(\mathcal O)=V.\text{ The induced map }\mathcal U\to\mathcal V\text{ uniquely extends }U\hookrightarrow V\subset H(K),\text{ is an open immersion, and induces an isomorphism on relative identity components. If }[V:U]<\infty,\text{ then }\mathcal V\text{ is affine. For every local ring extension }R/\mathcal O,\ \mathcal V(R)=\mathcal U(R)\cdot V.\text{ If }H\text{ is obtained by base change from a smooth affine }k\text{-group and the constructed }\mathcal V\text{ is }\Gamma\text{-invariant, then }\mathcal V\text{ descends to an }\mathfrak o\text{-group scheme}.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal O\text{ is strictly Henselian}.
H\text{ is a smooth affine }K\text{-group}.
U\subset V\subset H(K),\quad U\trianglelefteq V,\quad U\text{ is bounded and open in }H(K).
U\text{ is schematic and has a smooth affine integral model }\mathcal U.
statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{gathered}\exists\text{ a smooth separated, not necessarily affine, group scheme }\mathcal V\text{ with generic fiber }H\text{ and }\mathcal V(\mathcal O)=V;\\ \text{the model map }\mathcal U\to\mathcal V\text{ uniquely extends }U\hookrightarrow V\subset H(K),\text{ is an open immersion, and induces }\mathcal U^0\simeq\mathcal V^0;\\ [V:U]<\infty\Rightarrow\mathcal V\text{ is affine};\qquad \mathcal V(R)=\mathcal U(R)\cdot V\text{ for every local ring extension }R/\mathcal O;\\ \text{if }H\text{ is the base change to }K\text{ of a smooth affine }k\text{-group and the constructed }\mathcal V\text{ is }\Gamma\text{-invariant, then }\mathcal V\text{ descends to an }\mathfrak o\text{-group scheme}.\end{gathered}
statements.scope_note: The source denotes subgroups of H(K) by U,V and their integral models by calligraphic \(\mathcal U,\mathcal V\). The identity-component assertion is for relative identity components. In the local-point formula, the right factor is the subgroup V\subset H(K), while the left side uses the constructed model \(\mathcal V\). The descent clause applies to the constructed model and retains the source's k, K, Gamma, and o notation without adding identifications.

statements.title: Open-Cell Decomposition of the Congruence Kernel and Generation of Integral Points
statements.statement_plain: Under the standing notation and hypotheses for the smooth model G and its specified open cell X, the congruence kernel G(m) = ker(pi) lies in X(o). Each factor of an element of G(m) lies in the corresponding root-group or torus congruence subgroup, giving the ordered product decomposition into negative nondivisible root groups, the torus, and positive nondivisible root groups. If the special fiber of G is connected, then G(o) is generated by Z(o) together with W_a(o) = U_a(k) intersect G(o) for every root a.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X=(\prod_{a\in\Phi^{-,\mathrm{nd}}}\mathcal U_a)\times\mathcal Z\times(\prod_{a\in\Phi^{+,\mathrm{nd}}}\mathcal U_a)\) be the specified open cell of \(\mathcal G\). Then \(\mathcal G(\mathfrak m)=\ker\pi\) is contained in \(\mathcal X(\mathfrak o)\), every component of each element of \(\mathcal G(\mathfrak m)\) in this product decomposition lies in the corresponding congruence subgroup, and \[\mathcal G(\mathfrak m)=\left(\prod_{a\in\Phi^{-,\mathrm{nd}}}\mathcal U_a(\mathfrak m)\right)\times\mathcal Z(\mathfrak m)\times\left(\prod_{a\in\Phi^{+,\mathrm{nd}}}\mathcal U_a(\mathfrak m)\right).\] If the special fiber \(\overline{\mathcal G}\) is connected, then \(\mathcal G(\mathfrak o)\) is generated by \(\mathcal Z(\mathfrak o)\) and \(\mathcal W_a(\mathfrak o)=U_a(k)\cap\mathcal G(\mathfrak o)\) for all \(a\in\Phi\).
assumptions_latex: \text{Use the standing notation and hypotheses of Theorem 8.2.5 for }\mathcal G,\mathcal Z,\mathcal U_a,\pi,\mathfrak o,\mathfrak m,\text{ and }k.
\mathcal X=\left(\prod_{a\in\Phi^{-,\mathrm{nd}}}\mathcal U_a\right)\times\mathcal Z\times\left(\prod_{a\in\Phi^{+,\mathrm{nd}}}\mathcal U_a\right)\text{ is the specified open cell of }\mathcal G.
statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal G(\mathfrak m)=\ker\pi\subseteq\mathcal X(\mathfrak o),\qquad \mathcal G(\mathfrak m)=\left(\prod_{a\in\Phi^{-,\mathrm{nd}}}\mathcal U_a(\mathfrak m)\right)\times\mathcal Z(\mathfrak m)\times\left(\prod_{a\in\Phi^{+,\mathrm{nd}}}\mathcal U_a(\mathfrak m)\right);\quad \overline{\mathcal G}\text{ connected}\Longrightarrow \mathcal G(\mathfrak o)=\left\langle\mathcal Z(\mathfrak o),\mathcal W_a(\mathfrak o):a\in\Phi\right\rangle,\ \mathcal W_a(\mathfrak o)=U_a(k)\cap\mathcal G(\mathfrak o).
statements.scope_note: Under the source's standing notation and hypotheses for the smooth model and its open cell; connectedness of the special fiber is required only for the generation assertion.

statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal{G}^{0} is the largest subgroup scheme of \mathcal{G} with connected fibers; it exists as an open subscheme of \mathcal{G}, is the union of the neutral components of the generic and special fibers, and is affine if \mathcal{G} is affine.

statements.title: Topologically Semisimple and Unipotent Elements; Topological Jordan Decomposition
statements.statement_plain: Let X be a smooth affine group scheme and x an integral point. Call x topologically semisimple, respectively topologically unipotent, when every reduction modulo m^n for n>0 is semisimple, respectively unipotent. A topological Jordan decomposition of x is a commuting product x=x_ts x_tu of a topologically semisimple and a topologically unipotent integral point.
statements.statement_latex: Assume \mathcal{X} is a smooth affine group scheme and x\in\mathcal{X}(\mathfrak{o}). The element x is called topologically semisimple, respectively topologically unipotent, if for every n>0 its image in \mathcal{X}(\mathfrak{o}/\mathfrak{m}^{n})=\operatorname{Gr}_{n}(\mathcal{X})(\mathfrak{f}) is semisimple, respectively unipotent. A topological Jordan decomposition of x is a pair of commuting elements x_{\mathrm{ts}},x_{\mathrm{tu}}\in\mathcal{X}(\mathfrak{o}) such that x_{\mathrm{ts}} is topologically semisimple, x_{\mathrm{tu}} is topologically unipotent, and x=x_{\mathrm{ts}}x_{\mathrm{tu}}.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal{X} is a smooth affine group scheme.
x\in\mathcal{X}(\mathfrak{o}).
statements.conclusion_latex: For every n>0, the image of x in \mathcal{X}(\mathfrak{o}/\mathfrak{m}^{n})=\operatorname{Gr}_{n}(\mathcal{X})(\mathfrak{f}) is semisimple (respectively, unipotent). A topological Jordan decomposition of x is a commuting pair x_{\mathrm{ts}},x_{\mathrm{tu}}\in\mathcal{X}(\mathfrak{o}) such that x_{\mathrm{ts}} is topologically semisimple, x_{\mathrm{tu}} is topologically unipotent, and x=x_{\mathrm{ts}}x_{\mathrm{tu}}.

statements.title: Direct sums and additive-group descriptions of vector groups
statements.statement_plain: For finite-rank free R-modules M1 and M2, the vector group of their direct sum is naturally the product of their vector groups. After choosing a basis of a rank-n free module M, its vector group is isomorphic to the n-fold additive group. Vector groups are therefore smooth over R and are exactly the affine R-group schemes noncanonically isomorphic to finite products of the additive group.
statements.statement_latex: Let M_1 and M_2 be finite-rank free R-modules. Then the natural dual and symmetric-algebra isomorphisms induce a natural isomorphism of affine R-group schemes G_{M_1\oplus M_2}\cong G_{M_1}\times_R G_{M_2}. If M is free of rank n and a basis (m_1,\ldots,m_n) is chosen, then G_M\cong(\mathbf G_{\mathrm a})^n. Consequently G_M is smooth over R, and vector groups are precisely the affine R-group schemes non-canonically isomorphic to finite products of copies of \mathbf G_{\mathrm a}.
assumptions_latex: M_1 and M_2 are finite-rank free R-modules.
M is a free R-module of rank n with a chosen basis (m_1,\ldots,m_n).
statements.conclusion_latex: G_{M_1\oplus M_2}\cong G_{M_1}\times_R G_{M_2},\qquad G_M\cong(\mathbf G_{\mathrm a})^n.\text{ Hence }G_M\text{ is smooth over }R,\text{ and vector groups are precisely the affine R-group schemes non-canonically isomorphic to finite products of copies of }\mathbf G_{\mathrm a}.
statements.scope_note: Here G_M denotes the vector group associated in the source to a finite free R-module M. The direct-sum isomorphism is natural; the identification with (\mathbf G_{\mathrm a})^n depends on the selected basis.

statements.title: Unramified descent for buildings, apartments, affine roots, and integral models
statements.statement_plain: For a maximal unramified extension K of k, the k-building embeds G(k)-equivariantly into the building of G_K as exactly the Gal(K/k)-fixed points. A maximal k-split torus S lies in a k-torus T that becomes maximal K-split, and its apartment is the Galois-fixed apartment of T_K. Affine roots lift from S to T_K along roots with matching derivative, and every nonconstant restriction of an affine root from T_K is an affine root of S. For any subset Omega of an apartment, the two associated integral models base-change to the models over O for the image in B(G_K), with k-point groups equal to the intersections of the corresponding K-point groups with G(k).
statements.statement_latex: Let K be a maximal unramified extension of k, so that Gal(K/k) acts on B(G_K). Then the following hold. (UR1) There is a G(k)-equivariant embedding B(G) -> B(G_K) whose image is exactly B(G_K)^{Gal(K/k)}. (UR2) For every maximal k-split torus S in G, there exists a k-torus T containing S such that T_K is maximal K-split in G_K; for every such T, A(S)=A(T_K)^{Gal(K/k)}. (UR3) If psi in Psi(S) and b in Phi(T_K,G_K) restricts on S to the derivative of psi, there exists psi_b in Psi(T_K) with derivative b and restriction psi_b|_{A(S)}=psi; conversely, any eta in Psi(T_K) whose restriction to A(S) is nonconstant restricts to an affine root in Psi(S). (UR4) For every subset Omega of an apartment of B(G), base change from the o-models G^0_Omega and G^1_Omega along o -> O yields the corresponding O-models for the image Omega_K in B(G_K); in particular, G(k)^0_Omega=G(K)^0_Omega cap G(k) and G(k)^1_Omega=G(K)^1_Omega cap G(k).
assumptions_latex: K/k\text{ is a maximal unramified extension, and }\operatorname{Gal}(K/k)\text{ acts on }\mathcal B(G_K).
S\subset G\text{ is a maximal }k\text{-split torus; }T\subset G\text{ is a }k\text{-torus containing }S\text{ with }T_K\text{ maximal }K\text{-split in }G_K.
\Omega\text{ is a subset of an apartment of }\mathcal B(G);\ \mathfrak o\to\mathcal O\text{ is the valuation-ring extension for }k\subset K.
statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{gathered}\mathcal B(G)\hookrightarrow\mathcal B(G_K)\text{ is }G(k)\text{-equivariant with image }\mathcal B(G_K)^{\operatorname{Gal}(K/k)};\\ \mathcal A(S)=\mathcal A(T_K)^{\operatorname{Gal}(K/k)};\\ \psi\in\Psi(S),\ b\in\Phi(T_K,G_K),\ b|_S=d\psi\Rightarrow\exists\psi_b\in\Psi(T_K):\ d\psi_b=b,\ \psi_b|_{\mathcal A(S)}=\psi;\\ \eta\in\Psi(T_K),\ \eta|_{\mathcal A(S)}\text{ nonconstant}\Rightarrow\eta|_{\mathcal A(S)}\in\Psi(S);\\ \mathcal G^i_\Omega\otimes_{\mathfrak o}\mathcal O\cong\mathcal G^i_{\Omega_K}\ (i=0,1),\quad G(k)^i_\Omega=G(K)^i_\Omega\cap G(k).\end{gathered}
statements.scope_note: Axiom of unramified descent for a reductive group G over k: identifies the k-building with Galois-fixed points over a maximal unramified extension, descends maximal split-torus apartments and affine roots, and base-changes the two associated integral models with the stated intersection formulas.

statements.title: Unramified Descent
statements.statement_plain: Unramified descent is the process of deriving Bruhat-Tits theory for G over k from that for G_K over K.
