statements.title: Descent assumptions and Sigma-invariance of affine roots and root groups
statements.statement_plain: Assume that the maximal K-split torus S containing S^natural is defined over K^natural, and that T, mathfrak T, and mathfrak T^0 arise by base change from O^natural-group schemes. Then A_natural = I_natural intersect A is a nonempty affine subspace of A with direction V^natural = V^Sigma. Choose the valuation phi in A_natural. The affine-root value sets are Sigma-invariant: Gamma'_{sigma(a)} = Gamma'_a, and the corresponding root groups satisfy U_{sigma(a),k} = sigma(U_{a,k}) for all a, sigma, and k in Gamma'_a. Here the source writes the affine-root condition as a(x - phi) + k >= o. In general, phi in A_natural cannot be required simultaneously with phi being a Chevalley-Steinberg valuation; A_natural may contain no special point of A.
assumptions_latex: The valuation \(\varphi\) lies in \(A_{\natural}\).
statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(a\in\Phi\), \(\sigma\in\Sigma\), and \(k\in\Gamma'_{a}\), \(\Gamma'_{\sigma(a)}=\Gamma'_{a}\) and \(\mathcal U_{\sigma(a),k}=\sigma(\mathcal U_{a,k})\). In general, requiring \(\varphi\in A_{\natural}\) is incompatible with requiring \(\varphi\) to be a Chevalley--Steinberg valuation; \(A_{\natural}\) may contain no special point of \(A\).
statements.scope_note: Descent setup in Section 5.1 under the relevant Galois group \(\Sigma\), including the resulting invariance of affine-root value sets and root groups.

statements.title: Absolute and Relative Affine Root Systems Under Galois Descent
statements.statement_plain: For a special k-torus T containing a maximal k-split torus S, the affine root system on the special apartment A is the absolute system Ψ_K, while the system on the fixed apartment 𝒜 = A^Γ is the relative system Ψ_k. The absolute system is Galois-stable and reduced, whereas the relative system may be non-reduced.
statements.statement_latex: Given a special \(k\)-torus \(T\) containing a maximal \(k\)-split torus \(S\), let \(A\) be the corresponding special \(k\)-apartment and let \(\mathcal A=A^{\Gamma}\) be the apartment of \(S\), for \(\Gamma=\operatorname{Gal}(K/k)\). Define \(\Psi_K=\Psi(T,G)\subset A^*\) as the absolute affine root system and \(\Psi_k=\Psi(S,G)\subset\mathcal A^*\) as the relative affine root system. Since \(G\) and \(T\) are defined over \(k\), \(\Psi_K\) is \(\Gamma\)-stable and it is always reduced, even if the finite absolute root system \(\Phi(T,G)\) is non-reduced; the relative affine root system \(\Psi_k\) may be non-reduced.

statements.title: Affine-root bases under unramified descent
statements.statement_plain: Assume G is residually quasi-split. For a special k-torus T with maximal k-split subtorus S, restrict the affine-root basis associated with a Gamma-invariant chamber in the apartment for T to the fixed apartment. These restrictions form the affine-root basis associated with the fixed chamber for (S,G). None is constant, and two basis elements have the same restriction exactly when they are Gamma-conjugate.
statements.statement_latex: Assume that G is residually quasi-split. Let T be a special k-torus, let S\subset T be its maximal k-split subtorus, let A be the apartment corresponding to T, and let \Psi\subset A^* be the affine root system for (T_K,G_K). Set \mathcal A=A^\Gamma, and let \Psi_k\subset\mathcal A^* be the affine root system corresponding to (S,G). If C\subset A is a \Gamma-invariant chamber and \Delta is the corresponding basis of \Psi, then \Delta_k=\{\alpha|_{\mathcal A}:\alpha\in\Delta\} is the basis of \Psi_k associated to \mathcal C=C^\Gamma. Moreover, no \alpha\in\Delta has constant restriction to \mathcal A, and two elements of \Delta have equal restrictions to \mathcal A if and only if they are \Gamma-conjugate.

T\text{ is a special }k\text{-torus, and }S\subset T\text{ is its maximal }k\text{-split subtorus.}

\mathcal A=A^\Gamma,\quad \Psi_k\subset \mathcal A^*\text{ is the affine root system corresponding to }(S,G).
C\subset A\text{ is a }\Gamma\text{-invariant chamber, and }\Delta\text{ is the corresponding basis of }\Psi.

statements.title: Canonical building embedding under a valued field inclusion
statements.statement_plain: In the stated valued-field setting, the building of G(K) has a unique G(K)-equivariant isometric map into the building of G(K') carrying the chosen apartment to its corresponding apartment. This map is independent of the auxiliary Chevalley-Steinberg system and maximal K-split torus, sends the apartment A into A', and is fixed by every K-automorphism of K' that preserves the valuation.
statements.statement_latex: For the valued field inclusion K\subset K' and the associated buildings \mathcal I of \mathbf G(K) and \mathcal I' of \mathbf G(K'), there is a unique \mathbf G(K)-equivariant isometry j: \mathcal I\to\mathcal I' mapping \varphi to \varphi'. It is independent of the auxiliary Chevalley--Steinberg system and maximal K-split torus, maps \mathrm A into \mathrm A', and satisfies u\circ j=j for every valuation-preserving K-automorphism u of K'.
assumptions_latex: K\subset K' are fields in the valuation setup of Proposition 4.1.53, with valuation \omega' on K', and \mathcal I and \mathcal I' are the buildings of \mathbf G(K) and \mathbf G(K'), respectively.

A Chevalley--Steinberg system is chosen, giving apartments \varphi\subset\mathcal I and \varphi'\subset\mathcal I'; \mathrm S is a maximal K-split torus with apartment \mathrm A, and \mathrm A' is associated with a maximal K'-split torus \mathrm S''.
statements.conclusion_latex: There exists a unique isometry j:\mathcal I\to\mathcal I' such that j(\varphi)=\varphi' and j(g.x)=g.j(x) for all x\in\mathcal I and g\in\mathbf G(K). The map j is independent of the Chevalley--Steinberg system and of \mathrm S, hence canonical; j(\mathrm A)\subseteq\mathrm A'. For every K-automorphism u of K' preserving \omega', one has u\circ j=j.
statements.scope_note: Canonical functorial embedding of the Bruhat-Tits building under the valued field inclusion K\subset K', with compatibility of apartments and invariance under valuation-preserving K-automorphisms.

statements.title: Restriction and lifting of affine roots under unramified descent
statements.statement_plain: For a special k-apartment containing the k-apartment \mathcal A, every relative affine root lifts to an absolute affine root with any chosen absolute root extending its derivative. Conversely, the restriction to \mathcal{A} of any absolute affine root that is nonconstant is a relative affine root.

statements.title: Vertices of a Gamma-fixed chamber under residually quasi-split descent
statements.statement_plain: Assume that G is residually quasi-split and C is a Gamma-chamber, with fixed chamber C^Gamma. Every Gamma-orbit of vertices of C forms the vertex set of a Gamma-vertex. Its barycenter is the unique Gamma-fixed point in that Gamma-vertex and is a vertex of C^Gamma. Sending each orbit to its barycenter gives a bijection with the vertices of C^Gamma.

The map $O\mapsto b_O$ is a bijection from the set of $\Gamma$-orbits of vertices of $C$ to the vertices of $\mathcal C$.
assumptions_latex: $G$ is residually quasi-split.

statements.title: Equivalent Criteria for Residual Splitness
statements.statement_plain: The following four conditions are equivalent: Gamma acts trivially on every special k-apartment and the maximal K-split torus in the center of G is k-split; the k-rank of G equals its K-rank; every Gamma-chamber has an f-split solvable special-fiber group overline G_C^0; and every k-facet has an f-split special-fiber group overline G_F^0.

statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}(1)\;&\Gamma\text{ acts trivially on every special }k\text{-apartment, and the maximal }K\text{-split torus in }Z(G)\text{ is }k\text{-split};\\(2)\;&\operatorname{rank}_k(G)=\operatorname{rank}_K(G);\\(3)\;&\text{for every }\Gamma\text{-chamber }C,\ \overline{\mathcal G}_C^0\text{ is an }\mathfrak f\text{-split solvable }\mathfrak f\text{-group};\\(4)\;&\text{for every }k\text{-facet }\mathcal F,\ \overline{\mathcal G}_{\mathcal F}^0\text{ is an }\mathfrak f\text{-split }\mathfrak f\text{-group.}\end{aligned}

Because P lies in the Theta-fixed integral points, this map factors through the descended model G_Omega^0=(H_Omega^Theta)^0 and is the identity on the generic fiber G.
statements.statement_latex: Assume \(P\) fixes the non-empty \(\Theta\)-stable subset \(\Omega\) pointwise. Then \(P=\mathcal{G}^{0}(\mathcal{O})\subseteq\mathcal{H}_{\Omega}^{0}(\mathcal{O})^{\Theta}\), and the induced \(\mathcal{O}\)-group-scheme homomorphism \(\mathcal{G}^{0}\to\mathcal{H}_{\Omega}^{0}\) factors as \(\mathcal{G}^{0}\to\mathcal{G}_{\Omega}^{0}=((\mathcal{H}_{\Omega}^{\Theta})^{0})\), restricting to the identity on the generic fiber \(G\).
assumptions_latex: P and the associated O-group scheme \(\mathcal{G}^{0}\) are as in the preceding paragraph.
\(\Omega\) is a non-empty \(\Theta\)-stable subset of an apartment of \(\mathcal{B}(H)\) or \(\widetilde{\mathcal{B}}(H)\).
\(P\) fixes \(\Omega\) pointwise.
statements.conclusion_latex: The inclusion \(P=\mathcal{G}^{0}(\mathcal{O})\hookrightarrow \mathcal{H}_{\Omega}^{1}(\mathcal{O})=H(K)_{\Omega}^{1}\) induces an \(\mathcal{O}\)-group-scheme homomorphism \(\mathcal{G}^{0}\to\mathcal{H}_{\Omega}^{0}\), which factors through \(\mathcal{G}_{\Omega}^{0}=((\mathcal{H}_{\Omega}^{\Theta})^{0})\) and is the identity on the generic fiber \(G\).
statements.scope_note: Tamely ramified descent setting of Chapter 12; \(P\) and \(\mathcal{G}^{0}\) come from the preceding construction, and \(\Omega\) lies in an apartment of the reduced or enlarged Bruhat-Tits building.

statements.title: Counterexample to descended parahoric conjugacy
statements.statement_plain: For the specified adjoint quasi-split unitary group, the Galois-stable parahorics attached to facet types {0,2} and {1,3} are conjugate over K but not over K-natural: one is maximal and the other is not.
statements.statement_latex: In the adjoint quasi-split unitary example above, the \Sigma-stable parahoric subgroups attached to facet types \{0,2\} and \{1,3\} of a \Sigma-invariant chamber are G(K)-conjugate but not G(K^{\natural})-conjugate, since one is maximal and the other is not.
assumptions_latex: L/K^{\natural} is a quadratic extension contained in K, with nontrivial automorphism \sigma.

G is the adjoint group of the quasi-split unitary group over K^{\natural} defined by h(x)=x_{-2}^{\sigma}x_2+x_{-1}^{\sigma}x_1+x_1^{\sigma}x_{-1}+x_2^{\sigma}x_{-2} on L^4; G is split over K and G_K\simeq\operatorname{PGL}_4.

The affine Dynkin diagram of the K-splitting has type \widetilde A_3 with vertices 0,1,2,3; the image of G(K) induces the cyclic permutation group on these vertices, while Gal(L/K^{\natural}) exchanges 1 and 3.
A chamber C of the affine building over K is invariant under the Galois group \Sigma.
statements.conclusion_latex: The \Sigma-stable parahorics P_{02} and P_{13} attached to facet types \{0,2\} and \{1,3\} in C are conjugate by an element of G(K), but one is maximal and the other is not; hence they are not conjugate by any element of G(K^{\natural}).
statements.scope_note: Failure of conjugacy for descended parahoric subgroups in the non-simply-connected case.

statements.title: Standing Setup for Unramified Descent
statements.statement_plain: Assume k has a discrete valuation with value group Z, Henselian valuation ring, and perfect residue field. In fixed separable and algebraic closures, let K be the maximal unramified extension of k; the valuation extends uniquely to the algebraic closure, K has valuation ring O, and the residue field of O is an algebraic closure of the residue field of k. The Galois groups of K over k and of the residue-field algebraic closure over the residue field, together with Aut(O/o), are identified as Gamma. For any Gamma-stable set, Y^Gamma denotes the elements fixed by Gamma.
statements.statement_latex: Let k be a field with a discrete valuation \omega normalized by \omega(k^\times)=\mathbf Z, let \mathfrak o be its Henselian valuation ring, and assume its residue field \mathfrak f is perfect. Fix a separable closure k_s inside an algebraic closure \bar k, and let K be the maximal unramified extension of k contained in k_s. Denote by \omega the unique extension of the valuation to \bar k, let \mathcal O be the valuation ring of K, and let \overline{\mathfrak f} be its residue field, an algebraic closure of \mathfrak f. Identify \operatorname{Gal}(K/k), \operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal O/\mathfrak o), and \operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathfrak f}/\mathfrak f), denoting the common group by \Gamma. For a subset Y of a \Gamma-set Z, write Y^\Gamma for the elements fixed by every element of \Gamma.
assumptions_latex: k\text{ is equipped with a discrete valuation }\omega\text{ satisfying }\omega(k^\times)=\mathbf Z
\mathfrak o\text{ is the valuation ring of }k\text{ and is Henselian}
\mathfrak f\text{ is the residue field of }k\text{ and is perfect}
k_s\subseteq\bar k\text{ are fixed with }k_s\text{ a separable closure inside the algebraic closure }\bar k
statements.conclusion_latex: K\subseteq k_s\text{ is the maximal unramified extension of }k;\ \omega\text{ denotes the unique extension of the valuation to }\bar k;\ \mathcal O\text{ is the valuation ring of }K\text{ with residue field }\overline{\mathfrak f}\text{ algebraic over and algebraically closed over }\mathfrak f;\ \operatorname{Gal}(K/k),\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal O/\mathfrak o),\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathfrak f}/\mathfrak f)\text{ are identified as }\Gamma;\ Y^\Gamma=\{y\in Y:\gamma(y)=y\ \forall\gamma\in\Gamma\}.

statements.title: Finite-group fixed-point descent for buildings and parahoric data
statements.statement_plain: Let H be a connected reductive group over K and let Theta be a finite group of K-automorphisms whose order is prime to the residue characteristic of K. Then G=(H^Theta)^0 is reductive. Its enlarged Bruhat-Tits building is G(K)-equivariantly identified with the Theta-fixed enlarged building of H, with corresponding maximal-split-torus apartments and facets. Corresponding facets have parahoric subgroups G(K)_F^0=H(K)_{F'}^0 intersected with G(K)^0, isomorphic associated parahoric group schemes via the identity on G, and special-fiber maximal reductive quotients satisfying G_F=(H_{F'}^Theta)^0.
statements.statement_latex: Let H be a connected reductive K-group and let \Theta be a finite group of K-automorphisms of H. Assume that the residue characteristic of K does not divide |\Theta|, and set G:=\left(H^{\Theta}\right)^0. Then G is a reductive K-subgroup. There is a G(K)-equivariant bijection \widetilde{\mathcal B}(G)\xrightarrow{\sim}\widetilde{\mathcal B}(H)^{\Theta} identifying, for each maximal K-split torus S of G, the apartment \widetilde{\mathcal A}(S) with \widetilde{\mathcal B}(Z_H(S))^{\Theta}; facets correspond. For corresponding facets \mathcal F and \mathcal F', G(K)_{\mathcal F}^{0}=H(K)_{\mathcal F'}^{0}\cap G(K)^0, the identity on G extends to an isomorphism of the associated parahoric group schemes, and \mathrm G_{\mathcal F}=\left(\mathrm H_{\mathcal F'}^{\Theta}\right)^0 for the maximal reductive quotients of their special fibers.
assumptions_latex: H is a connected reductive K-group.
\Theta is a finite group of K-automorphisms of H.
The residue characteristic of K does not divide |\Theta|.
statements.conclusion_latex: Set G:=\left(H^{\Theta}\right)^0. Then G is a reductive K-subgroup. There is a G(K)-equivariant bijection \widetilde{\mathcal B}(G)\xrightarrow{\sim}\widetilde{\mathcal B}(H)^{\Theta} such that, for every maximal K-split torus S of G, the apartment \widetilde{\mathcal A}(S) is identified with \widetilde{\mathcal B}(Z_H(S))^{\Theta}; facets correspond under this bijection. For corresponding facets \mathcal F and \mathcal F', one has G(K)_{\mathcal F}^{0}=H(K)_{\mathcal F'}^{0}\cap G(K)^0, the identity of G extends to an isomorphism of the associated parahoric group schemes, and the maximal reductive quotients of the special fibers satisfy \mathrm G_{\mathcal F}=\left(\mathrm H_{\mathcal F'}^{\Theta}\right)^0.

statements.title: Lifting Theta-stable tori through unipotent quotients
statements.statement_plain: Let H be a smooth connected affine algebraic F-group acted on by a finite group Theta of F-automorphisms, and let U be a Theta-stable smooth connected unipotent normal F-subgroup. If the residue characteristic p does not divide the order of Theta, then every Theta-stable F-torus in H/U lifts to a Theta-stable F-torus in H mapping isomorphically onto it. In particular, the central torus of H/U has such a lift.

If the residue characteristic \(p\) does not divide \(|\Theta|\), then every \(\Theta\)-stable \(\mathrm F\)-torus \(\overline{\mathcal S}\) of \(\overline{\mathcal H}:=\mathcal H/\mathcal U\) lifts to a \(\Theta\)-stable \(\mathrm F\)-torus \(\mathcal S\) in \(\mathcal H\) mapping isomorphically onto \(\overline{\mathcal S}\); in particular, such a lift exists for the central torus of \(\overline{\mathcal H}\).

statements.title: Parabolic subgroups and unipotent radicals of finite-group fixed points
statements.statement_plain: Let H be a smooth connected affine algebraic F-group with an action of a finite group Theta, with p not dividing the order of Theta, and let G be the identity component of the Theta-fixed subgroup. The unipotent radical of G equals both the Theta-fixed unipotent radical of H and G intersected with the unipotent radical of H; the quotient of G by this radical is isomorphic to the identity component of the Theta-fixed reductive quotient of H. Every Theta-stable parabolic F-subgroup Q of H intersects G in a connected parabolic F-subgroup P equal to the identity component of Q's fixed points. Conversely, every parabolic F-subgroup P of G with a maximal F-split torus S in P is obtained from a Theta-stable parabolic Q of H containing the centralizer of S, with the same intersection and fixed-point identities.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) be a smooth connected affine algebraic \(F\)-group with an action by a finite group \(\Theta\), assume \(p\nmid|\Theta|\), and set \(\mathcal G=(\mathcal H^{\Theta})^{0}\). Then (1) \(\mathcal R_u(\mathcal G)=\mathcal R_u(\mathcal H)^{\Theta}=\mathcal G\cap\mathcal R_u(\mathcal H)\), and the induced map \(\mathcal G/\mathcal R_u(\mathcal G)\to\bigl((\mathcal H/\mathcal R_u(\mathcal H))^{\Theta}\bigr)^{0}\) is an isomorphism. (2) For every \(\Theta\)-stable parabolic \(F\)-subgroup \(\mathcal Q\) of \(\mathcal H\), the intersection \(\mathcal P:=\mathcal G\cap\mathcal Q\) is a connected parabolic \(F\)-subgroup of \(\mathcal G\) and equals \((\mathcal Q^{\Theta})^{0}\). (3) Conversely, for every parabolic \(F\)-subgroup \(\mathcal P\) of \(\mathcal G\) and maximal \(F\)-split torus \(\mathcal S\subset\mathcal P\), there exists a \(\Theta\)-stable parabolic \(F\)-subgroup \(\mathcal Q\) of \(\mathcal H\) containing \(Z_{\mathcal H}(\mathcal S)\) such that \(\mathcal P=\mathcal G\cap\mathcal Q=(\mathcal Q^{\Theta})^{0}\).
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) is a smooth connected affine algebraic \(F\)-group with an action by a finite group \(\Theta\).
\(p\nmid |\Theta|\).
\(\mathcal G=(\mathcal H^{\Theta})^{0}\).
For (2), \(\mathcal Q\) is a \(\Theta\)-stable parabolic \(F\)-subgroup of \(\mathcal H\).
For (3), \(\mathcal P\) is a parabolic \(F\)-subgroup of \(\mathcal G\) and \(\mathcal S\subset\mathcal P\) is a maximal \(F\)-split torus.
statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R_u(\mathcal G)=\mathcal R_u(\mathcal H)^{\Theta}=\mathcal G\cap\mathcal R_u(\mathcal H)\), and \(\mathcal G/\mathcal R_u(\mathcal G)\cong\bigl((\mathcal H/\mathcal R_u(\mathcal H))^{\Theta}\bigr)^0\). If \(\mathcal Q\) is \(\Theta\)-stable parabolic, then \(\mathcal P=\mathcal G\cap\mathcal Q=(\mathcal Q^{\Theta})^0\) is a connected parabolic \(F\)-subgroup of \(\mathcal G\). Conversely, for every parabolic \(\mathcal P\subset\mathcal G\) and maximal \(F\)-split \(\mathcal S\subset\mathcal P\), there is a \(\Theta\)-stable parabolic \(\mathcal Q\subset\mathcal H\) containing \(Z_{\mathcal H}(\mathcal S)\) with \(\mathcal P=\mathcal G\cap\mathcal Q=(\mathcal Q^{\Theta})^0\).

statements.title: Gamma-chamber criterion via parabolics and reductive quotients
statements.statement_plain: In unramified descent, a Gamma-facet is a Gamma-chamber exactly when its associated parabolic subgroup in the special-fiber group is minimal. Equivalently, the corresponding reductive group has no proper parabolic subgroup over the residue field, or has a unique maximal split torus over that field; this torus is central and lies in every maximal torus.
statements.statement_latex: For \(\Gamma\)-facets F' and C in \(\mathcal B(G_K)\), maximality (chamberhood) is characterized by minimality of the associated parabolic in \(\overline{\mathcal G}_F^0\); equivalently, C is a \(\Gamma\)-chamber exactly when its reductive group \(G_C\) has no proper parabolic \(\mathfrak f\)-subgroup, or equivalently has a unique maximal \(\mathfrak f\)-split torus, central and contained in every maximal torus of \(G_C\).
assumptions_latex: F is a fixed \(\Gamma\)-facet of \(\mathcal B(G_K)\), and F' is a \(\Gamma\)-facet for which \(\mathfrak p_F(F')\) is defined.
For a \(\Gamma\)-facet C, \(G_C\) is the associated reductive \(\mathfrak f\)-group; \(G_F\) is the maximal reductive quotient of \(\overline{\mathcal G}_F^0\).
statements.conclusion_latex: F' is a maximal \(\Gamma\)-facet (a \(\Gamma\)-chamber) if and only if \(\mathfrak p_F(F')\) is a minimal parabolic \(\mathfrak f\)-subgroup of \(\overline{\mathcal G}_F^0\); moreover, a \(\Gamma\)-facet C is a \(\Gamma\)-chamber if and only if \(G_C\) has no proper parabolic \(\mathfrak f\)-subgroup, if and only if \(G_C\) contains a unique maximal \(\mathfrak f\)-split torus, which is central and contained in every maximal torus of \(G_C\).
statements.scope_note: In the unramified descent setting, the projection \(\overline{\mathcal G}_F^0\to G_F\) induces an inclusion-preserving bijection between parabolic \(\mathfrak f\)-subgroups, so minimality is equivalent on the special-fiber group and its maximal reductive quotient.

statements.title: Adapted pairs of points
statements.statement_plain: For points x in the building of G and y in the building of M, the pair is adapted when, for every maximal k-split torus S whose apartment contains x, y lies in the corresponding M-subbuilding, its quotient class is fixed by the normalizer N_G(S)(k), the map phi_{S,bar y} sends x to y, and the first congruence subgroup at x+v in G(k) is contained in that at y+v in M(k) for every v in V(S/A_G). statements.statement_plain: For two adapted pairs, the associated maps are equal exactly when, for one (equivalently any) maximal k-split torus S whose apartment contains the two source points, the target points lie in the same V(S)-orbit and have the same displacement as the source points. If \(\widetilde\varphi:\widetilde{\mathcal B}(G)\to\widetilde{\mathcal B}(H)\) is an admissible embedding, then \((\widetilde x,\widetilde\varphi(\widetilde x))\) is an adapted pair for every \(\widetilde x\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}(G)\).

statements.title: Admissible maps of enlarged and reduced buildings
statements.statement_plain: A map between enlarged buildings is f-admissible when it intertwines the G(k)-action with the H(k)-action through f and, for every maximal k-split torus of G, carries its apartment into the apartment of a maximal k-split torus of H containing its image, compatibly with the induced map of translation spaces. The same conditions without tildes define f-admissibility for maps between reduced buildings.
statements.statement_latex: A map \(\varphi:\widetilde{\mathcal B}(G)\to\widetilde{\mathcal B}(H)\) is called \(f\)-admissible if: (1) it is \(f\)-equivariant, so \(\varphi(g\cdot x)=f(g)\cdot\varphi(x)\) for every \(g\in G(k)\) and \(x\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}(G)\); and (2) for every maximal \(k\)-split torus \(S\subset G\), there exists a maximal \(k\)-split torus \(T\subset H\) such that \(f(S)\subset T\), \(\varphi(\widetilde{\mathcal A}(S,G))\subset\widetilde{\mathcal A}(T,H)\), and the restricted map \(\widetilde{\mathcal A}(S,G)\to\widetilde{\mathcal A}(T,H)\) is equivariant for the map \(V(S)\to V(T)\) induced by \(f\). A map \(\varphi:\mathcal B(G)\to\mathcal B(H)\) is \(f\)-admissible if the analogous conditions hold with the tildes removed.
assumptions_latex: f:G\to H induces the displayed maps on k-points and, whenever f(S)\subset T, the map V(S)\to V(T).
statements.conclusion_latex: The two stated conditions define f-admissibility for maps of enlarged buildings; the analogous conditions with tildes removed define f-admissibility for maps of reduced buildings.

statements.title: Admissible Building Maps Induced by Isomorphisms
statements.statement_plain: If f is an isomorphism from G to H, transport of structure induces the unique f-admissible map between the reduced buildings. Together with the induced isomorphism of the vector factors, it gives an f-admissible map between the enlarged buildings, and every other such map differs by translation by the target vector space V(A_H).
statements.statement_latex: If \(f:G\xrightarrow{\sim}H\) is an isomorphism, then there exists a unique \(f\)-admissible map \(\mathcal{B}(G)\to\mathcal{B}(H)\), namely the map induced by transport of structure. Combining it with the isomorphism \(V(A_G)\to V(A_H)\) induced by \(f\) gives an \(f\)-admissible map \(\widetilde{\mathcal{B}}(G)\to\widetilde{\mathcal{B}}(H)\), and every other such map is a translate by \(V(A_H)\).
assumptions_latex: f:G\xrightarrow{\sim}H
statements.conclusion_latex: \exists!\,\varphi:\mathcal{B}(G)\to\mathcal{B}(H)\text{ that is }f\text{-admissible, namely the map induced by transport of structure; moreover, combining }\varphi\text{ with the isomorphism }V(A_G)\to V(A_H)\text{ induced by }f\text{ gives an }f\text{-admissible map }\widetilde{\mathcal{B}}(G)\to\widetilde{\mathcal{B}}(H),\text{ and every other such map is a translate by }V(A_H).
statements.scope_note: The induced f-admissible map on reduced buildings is unique; the corresponding map on enlarged buildings is unique only up to translation by the target vector space V(A_H).

statements.title: Coordinate ring of the integral Weil restriction of the multiplicative group
statements.statement_plain: For the Weil restriction S of the multiplicative group from ell to k, the adjunction character and its inverse have coordinates t_i and u_i relative to an o-basis of o_ell. The basis also gives a k[S]-basis of ell[S], and the integral Weil-restriction model has coordinate ring equal to the o-subalgebra generated by these coordinates.
statements.statement_latex: Let R=\mathfrak{o}, R'=\mathfrak{o}_{\ell}, and S=\operatorname{R}_{\ell/k}\mathbf{G}_{m,\ell}. For the adjunction q:S\times_k\ell\to\mathbf{G}_{m,\ell}, let v\in\mathrm{X}^*(S) be the corresponding character. If e_1,\ldots,e_n is an \mathfrak{o}-basis of \mathfrak{o}_{\ell} (also a k[S]-basis of \ell[S]), write v=\sum_i e_i t_i and v^{-1}=\sum_i e_i u_i with t_i,u_i\in k[S]. Then the coordinate ring of \operatorname{R}_{\mathfrak{o}_{\ell}/\mathfrak{o}}\mathbf{G}_{m,\mathfrak{o}_{\ell}} is the \mathfrak{o}-subalgebra of k[S] generated by the t_i and u_i.
assumptions_latex: R=\mathfrak{o} and R'=\mathfrak{o}_{\ell}.
S=\operatorname{R}_{\ell/k}\mathbf{G}_{m,\ell}.
q:S\times_k\ell\to\mathbf{G}_{m,\ell} is the adjunction map, with corresponding character v\in\mathrm{X}^*(S).
e_1,\ldots,e_n is a basis of the free \mathfrak{o}-module \mathfrak{o}_{\ell}.
statements.conclusion_latex: v\in\ell[S],\quad e_1,\ldots,e_n\text{ is a }k[S]\text{-basis of }\ell[S],\quad v=\sum_i e_i t_i,\;v^{-1}=\sum_i e_i u_i,\quad \mathcal{O}(\operatorname{R}_{\mathfrak{o}_{\ell}/\mathfrak{o}}\mathbf{G}_{m,\mathfrak{o}_{\ell}})=\mathfrak{o}[t_1,\ldots,t_n,u_1,\ldots,u_n]\subset k[S].
statements.scope_note: Integral model of the Weil restriction of the multiplicative group; coordinates are taken relative to an \mathfrak{o}-basis of \mathfrak{o}_{\ell}.

statements.title: Root-group filtrations and connected parahorics under restriction of scalars
statements.statement_plain: For a restriction of scalars G = R_{ell/k}H, the canonically identified root groups have the same filtration subgroup at every common apartment point and real level. The torus Iwahori subgroup is compatible with Weil restriction, and the connected parahoric subgroups G(k)_x^0 and H(ell)_x^0 therefore coincide under G(k) = H(ell).
statements.statement_latex: Let G=\operatorname{R}_{\ell/k}H be in the restriction-of-scalars setting, with the canonical identification G(k)=H(\ell), common apartment \mathcal A(S,G)=\mathcal A(S,H), common relative roots \Phi(S,G)=\Phi(S,H), and identified root groups U_a^G(k)=U_a^H(\ell). For every x\in\mathcal A(S,G), a\in\Phi(S,G), and r\in\mathbf R, the identification carries U_{a,x,r}^G onto U_{a,x,r}^H. Moreover, formation of the torus Iwahori subgroup commutes with restriction of scalars, T(\ell)^0=(\operatorname{R}_{\ell/k}T)(k)^0; consequently, G(k)_x^0=H(\ell)_x^0.
assumptions_latex: G=\operatorname{R}_{\ell/k}H
G(k)=H(\ell)\text{ under the canonical restriction-of-scalars identification}
\mathcal A(S,G)=\mathcal A(S,H)
\Phi(S,G)=\Phi(S,H)
U_a^G(k)=U_a^H(\ell)
x\in\mathcal A(S,G),\quad a\in\Phi(S,G),\quad r\in\mathbf R
statements.conclusion_latex: U_{a,x,r}^G=U_{a,x,r}^H,\qquad T(\ell)^0=\bigl(\operatorname{R}_{\ell/k}T\bigr)(k)^0,\qquad G(k)_x^0=H(\ell)_x^0.
statements.scope_note: Restriction-of-scalars compatibility for root-group filtrations, torus Iwahori subgroups, and connected parahoric subgroups. The referenced identification (7.9.1) is not expanded because its formula is absent from the extracted item.

statements.title: Coordinate Construction of Weil Restriction for an Affine Scheme
statements.statement_plain: Choose an R-basis of R' and replace each affine coordinate of X by its expansion in that basis. Expand every defining equation of X in the same basis and impose all resulting coefficient equations over R. The resulting closed subscheme of affine dn-space represents the Weil restriction: its A-points are functorially the points of X over A tensor_R R'.
statements.statement_latex: Put \(\alpha:R'[T_1,\ldots,T_d]\to R'[T_{i,j}]\) with \(\alpha(T_i)=\sum_{j=1}^n e_jT_{i,j}\). For \(f'\in I'\), write \(\alpha(f')=\sum_{j=1}^n e_jf_j\), where \(f_j=e_j^*\alpha(f')\in R[T_{i,j}]\), and let \(I\subset R[T_{i,j}]\) be generated by all such \(f_j\). Then the closed subscheme of \(\mathbf A_R^{dn}\) defined by \(I\) represents the Weil restriction \(\operatorname{Res}_{S'/S}(\mathcal X)\): for every R-algebra \(A\), the assignment \(\sigma\mapsto(\sigma\otimes\operatorname{id}_{R'})\circ\alpha\) is a functorial bijection between maps annihilating \(I\) and R'-algebra maps from \(R'[T_1,\ldots,T_d]/I'\) to \(A\otimes_RR'\).
assumptions_latex: R'\text{ is a finite free }R\text{-module of rank }n\text{ with basis }e_1,\ldots,e_n.
\mathcal X\hookrightarrow\mathbf A_{R'}^d\text{ is an affine finite-type }R'\text{-scheme defined by }I'\subset R'[T_1,\ldots,T_d].
statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Res}_{S'/S}(\mathcal X)=\operatorname{Spec}\!\left(R[T_{i,j}]/I\right),\qquad \operatorname{Res}_{S'/S}(\mathcal X)(A)\cong\mathcal X(A\otimes_RR')\quad\text{functorially in every }R\text{-algebra }A.
statements.scope_note: Coordinate construction for an affine finite-type scheme after choosing an R-basis of R'; the construction is expressed through coefficient equations and its functor-of-points characterization.

statements.title: Coordinate Algebras of a Linear Scheme under Scalar Restriction
statements.statement_plain: For a finite-projective B-module N, the linear scheme X and its scalar restriction X-sharp have coordinate algebras given by symmetric algebras on the B-dual of N and the A-dual of N. If N=B tensor_A M for finite-projective M over A, these become the displayed base-change and dual-of-B tensor dual-of-M formulas.
statements.statement_latex: Let A\to B be as above and let \mathfrak{X}=\mathfrak{N} for a finite-projective B-module N. The coordinate algebras of \mathfrak{X} and its scalar restriction \mathfrak{X}^{\sharp} are given by the stated symmetric-algebra formulas; when N is obtained by base change from a finite-projective A-module M, they identify with the corresponding base-change and dual-module expressions.
assumptions_latex: A\to B is a ring homomorphism and B is a projective A-module of finite type.
N is a projective B-module of finite type; write {}^{t}N=\operatorname{Hom}_{A}(N,A).
In the specialization, M is a projective A-module of finite type and N=B\otimes_{A}M; write {}^{t}M=\operatorname{Hom}_{A}(M,A) and {}^{t}B=\operatorname{Hom}_{A}(B,A).
statements.conclusion_latex: For \mathfrak{X}=\mathfrak{N},\ B[\mathfrak{X}]\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{B}(\operatorname{Hom}_{B}(N,B))\quad\text{and}\quad A[\mathfrak{X}^{\sharp}]\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{A}({}^{t}N).\quad\text{If }N=B\otimes_{A}M,\text{ then }\operatorname{Hom}_{B}(N,B)\cong B\otimes_{A}{}^{t}M,\ {}^{t}N\cong{}^{t}B\otimes_{A}{}^{t}M,\text{ and hence }B[\mathfrak{X}]\cong B\otimes_{A}\operatorname{Sym}_{A}({}^{t}M),\ A[\mathfrak{X}^{\sharp}]\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{A}({}^{t}B\otimes_{A}{}^{t}M).

statements.title: Normalized Dual Basis for a Finite Projective Algebra
statements.statement_plain: Let B be an A-algebra that is finitely generated and projective as an A-module, and let B dual be Hom_A(B,A). The unit copy A times 1 is a free direct summand of B. There are elements e_i in B and dual functionals e_i* with e_1=1, e_j*(e_1)=e_1*(e_j)=0 for j>1, whose dual-basis tensor represents the identity of B. Consequently, for every A-module M and every x in B tensor_A M, x equals the sum of e_i tensor (e_i* tensor id_M)(x).
statements.statement_latex: \text{Let }B^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,A).\text{ If }B\text{ is an }A\text{-algebra, finitely generated and projective over }A,\text{ then }A\cdot1\text{ is a free direct summand of }B.\text{ One may choose }e_1,\ldots,e_d\in B\text{ and }e_1^*,\ldots,e_d^*\in B^\vee\text{ with }e_1=1,\ e_j^*(e_1)=e_1^*(e_j)=0\text{ for }j>1,\text{ and }\sum_{i=1}^d e_i\otimes e_i^*=\operatorname{id}_B.\text{ For every }A\text{-module }M\text{ and }x\in B\otimes_A M,\quad x=\sum_{i=1}^d e_i\otimes\bigl(e_i^*\otimes\operatorname{id}_M\bigr)(x).

statements.title: Galois Action, Fixed Points, and Norm on a Weil Restriction
statements.statement_plain: For a finite Galois extension l/k, with either the valuation-ring pair (o,o_l) or the field pair (k,l), the Weil restriction Y of an affine finite-type R-scheme X has the displayed functor-of-points description. Gal(l/k) acts functorially on Y through id_A tensor sigma, with the stated coordinate action, and the adjunction map identifies X with the fixed-point scheme. If X is commutative, multiplying all Galois conjugates gives a norm morphism Y to X. For the multiplicative group, the norm kernel is an anisotropic norm-one torus.
statements.statement_latex: For every R-algebra A, \(\mathcal Y(A)=\mathcal X_{R'}(A\otimes_RR')=\operatorname{Hom}_{R'}(R'[\mathcal X],A\otimes_RR')=\operatorname{Hom}_{R}(R[\mathcal X],A\otimes_RR')\). Each \(\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(\ell/k)\) acts through \(\operatorname{id}_A\otimes\sigma\), inducing a functorial action on \(\mathcal Y\); if \(\sigma(e_j)=\sum_k\lambda_{j,k}e_k\), then \(\sigma(t_{i,j})=\sum_k\lambda_{k,j}t_{i,k}\). The adjunction map identifies \(\mathcal X\) with the fixed-point scheme \(\mathcal Y^{\operatorname{Gal}(\ell/k)}\). When \(\mathcal X\) is commutative, the norm morphism \(N_{\ell/k}:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal X\) is \(N_{\ell/k}(y)=\prod_{\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(\ell/k)}\sigma(y)\); for \(\mathcal X=\mathbf G_m\), its kernel \(\ker(\mathbf R_{\ell/k}\mathbf G_m\to\mathbf G_m)\) is an anisotropic norm-one torus.
assumptions_latex: \ell/k\text{ is a finite Galois extension.}
(R,R')=(\mathfrak{o},\mathfrak{o}_{\ell})\text{ or }(k,\ell).
\mathcal X\text{ is an affine scheme of finite type over }R, and }\mathcal Y=\operatorname{R}_{S'/S}(\mathcal X\times_S S').
\mathcal X\text{ is a commutative group scheme for the norm morphism and norm-one torus assertions.
statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal Y(A)=\mathcal X_{R'}(A\otimes_RR')=\operatorname{Hom}_{R'}(R'[\mathcal X],A\otimes_RR')=\operatorname{Hom}_{R}(R[\mathcal X],A\otimes_RR')\text{ for every }R\text{-algebra }A;\ \operatorname{Gal}(\ell/k)\text{ acts functorially on }\mathcal Y,\ \mathcal X\simeq\mathcal Y^{\operatorname{Gal}(\ell/k)},\ N_{\ell/k}(y)=\prod_{\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(\ell/k)}\sigma(y),\text{ and }\ker(N_{\ell/k}:\mathbf R_{\ell/k}\mathbf G_m\to\mathbf G_m)\text{ is an anisotropic torus.}

statements.title: Tensor Decomposition for Finite Separable Restriction of Scalars
statements.statement_plain: For a finite separable extension L/K and any field extension K'/K, the tensor product K' tensor_K L is a finite product of fields representing the composite extensions of L and K'. After choosing K-embeddings of L and K' into a sufficiently large algebraically closed field Omega, the factors are indexed by the double cosets Gal(Omega/K')\Gal(Omega/K)/Gal(Omega/L), with factor K'(sigma_i(L)); the isomorphism sends x tensor y to the tuple (x sigma_i(y)) over the chosen representatives.

If \Omega is an algebraically closed extension of K with \operatorname{trdeg}_K(\Omega)>\operatorname{trdeg}_K(K') and K-embeddings of L and K' into \Omega are chosen, the factors can be indexed by the double cosets \operatorname{Gal}(\Omega/K')\backslash\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega/K)/\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega/L); choosing \sigma_i\in i gives L_i=K'(\sigma_i(L)), and j(x\otimes y)=(x\sigma_i(y))_{i\in I}.

statements.title: Unit and Counit of Weil Restriction
statements.statement_plain: Base change along S' over S is left adjoint to Weil restriction. The adjunction has a functorial counit q from the base change of a Weil restriction to the original scheme and a functorial unit j from a scheme to the Weil restriction of its base change; these satisfy both triangle identities. The counit is not the norm map. For affine finite-type schemes over S=Spec R and S'=Spec R' with a chosen R-basis and dual basis, q is given on coordinate rings by expanding each coordinate in that basis. For a scheme Y over S, after extending its defining ideal and forming the corresponding Weil-restriction ideal I, j sends each coordinate T_{i,j} to the dual-basis coefficient e_j^*(1) times T_i; this ring map is surjective, and when e_1=1 only the first coordinate remains.
statements.statement_latex:
For the adjunction \((-\times_S S')\dashv \mathrm R_{S'/S}\), there are functorial maps of schemes
\[
q_{\mathcal X}:(\mathrm R_{S'/S}\mathcal X)\times_S S'\longrightarrow\mathcal X,
\qquad
j_{\mathcal Y}:\mathcal Y\longrightarrow\mathrm R_{S'/S}(\mathcal Y\times_S S'),
\]
which satisfy
\[
q_{\mathcal Y\times_S S'}\circ(j_{\mathcal Y}\times_S S')=\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal Y\times_S S'},
\qquad
\mathrm R_{S'/S}(q_{\mathcal X})\circ j_{\mathrm R_{S'/S}\mathcal X}=\operatorname{id}_{\mathrm R_{S'/S}\mathcal X}.
\]
The map q_{\mathcal X} is not the norm map. If \(\mathcal X\) has coordinate ring \(R'[T_1,\ldots,T_d]/I'\), then q_{\mathcal X} is contravariantly induced by the \(R'\)-algebra map
\[
R'[T_1,\ldots,T_d]/I'\longrightarrow (R[T_{i,j}]/I)\otimes_R R',\qquad T_i\longmapsto\sum_jT_{i,j}\otimes e_j.
\]
For \(\mathcal Y\) with coordinate ring \(R[T_1,\ldots,T_d]/J\), let \(I'\) be the ideal generated by J in \(R'[T_1,\ldots,T_d]\) and let I be the corresponding ideal defining \(\mathrm R_{S'/S}(\mathcal Y\times_S S')\). Then j_{\mathcal Y} is contravariantly induced by
\[
R[T_{i,j}]/I\longrightarrow R[T_i]/J,\qquad T_{i,j}\longmapsto e_j^*(1)T_i,
\]
which is surjective. If \(e_1=1\), then \(e_j^*(1)=\delta_{j,1}\).
assumptions_latex: (-\times_S S')\dashv \mathrm R_{S'/S}

\text{For the affine coordinate descriptions, }S=\operatorname{Spec}R,\ S'=\operatorname{Spec}R',\text{ with }R'\text{ finite free over }R\text{ and chosen basis }e_1,\ldots,e_n\text{ and dual basis }e_1^*,\ldots,e_n^*.
\mathcal X=\operatorname{Spec}(R'[T_1,\ldots,T_d]/I')\text{ and }\mathcal Y=\operatorname{Spec}(R[T_1,\ldots,T_d]/J)\text{ are affine schemes of finite type.
statements.conclusion_latex: q_{\mathcal Y\times_S S'}\circ(j_{\mathcal Y}\times_S S')=\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal Y\times_S S'},\qquad \mathrm R_{S'/S}(q_{\mathcal X})\circ j_{\mathrm R_{S'/S}\mathcal X}=\operatorname{id}_{\mathrm R_{S'/S}\mathcal X};\quad \alpha(T_i)=\sum_jT_{i,j}\otimes e_j,\quad 1=\sum_j e_j^*(1)e_j,\quad T_{i,j}\mapsto e_j^*(1)T_i.
statements.scope_note: Defines the functorial unit and counit of the base-change/Weil-restriction adjunction, their triangle identities, and the affine coordinate-ring realizations. In the Y-case, I' is the ideal generated by J after extension to R', and I is the corresponding ideal defining the Weil restriction; the induced ring map for j is surjective. The counit q is explicitly distinguished from the norm map.

statements.title: Finite Galois descent for semilinear free modules and associated group schemes
statements.statement_plain: Let L be a finite Galois extension of K^natural inside K, with valuation ring O_L and Galois group Sigma_L, and let O^natural be the valuation ring of K^natural. For a finite free O_L-module M with semilinear Sigma_L-action, all higher cohomology H^q(Sigma_L,M), q at least 1, vanishes and H^1(Sigma_L,GL(M)) is trivial. If the canonical group scheme X attached to M carries a compatible semilinear Sigma_L-action, then the fixed module M^natural is finite free over O^natural, O_L tensor over O^natural with M^natural is canonically isomorphic to M, and X is obtained by base change from the canonical O^natural-group scheme attached to M^natural.
assumptions_latex: M is a finite free O_L-module equipped with a semilinear Sigma_L-action, so each sigma acts by a sigma-semilinear automorphism of M.

For the group-scheme assertion, X is the canonical O_L-group scheme associated with M, and the Sigma_L-action on X is by sigma-automorphisms compatible with scalar multiplication: (t\cdot x)^sigma=t^sigma\cdot x^sigma.

statements.title: Galois Fixed Points and Finite-Index Apartment Stabilizers
statements.statement_plain: Let Sigma = Gal(K/K^natural) act on the building I of G. For every apartment A', there is a finite Galois extension K1 of K^natural contained in K over which the corresponding maximal K-split torus is defined and split and G is quasi-split. The subgroup Gal(K/K1) has finite index in Sigma and fixes A' pointwise. Therefore every point has finite Sigma-orbit and the induced isometry image is bounded. Any convex Sigma-stable subset M has a Sigma-fixed point in its closure in the metric completion. If the valuation omega is discrete, I is complete, the point lies in I_k, and taking M = I gives I_natural nonempty.
assumptions_latex: \Sigma=\operatorname{Gal}(K/K^{\natural}) acts on the building \mathcal I of \mathbf G.
M\subseteq\mathcal I is a convex subset stable under \Sigma.
The valuation \omega is assumed discrete only for the final conclusion that the fixed point lies in \mathcal I.
statements.scope_note: General Galois action and descent of the Bruhat-Tits building, including finite-index pointwise apartment stabilizers and fixed points for convex invariant subsets; discreteness of the valuation ensures completeness and the final nonemptiness conclusion.

It is the smallest splitting field of G' = G base-changed to K'; the base-changed torus S' is maximal split and has the same relative root system Phi, and each displayed pinning acquires its corresponding canonical base change.

statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde{\mathrm K}'/\mathrm K'\text{ is Galois with }\operatorname{Gal}(\widetilde{\mathrm K}'/\mathrm K')\cong\operatorname{Gal}(\widetilde{\mathrm K}/\mathrm K);\ \widetilde{\mathrm K}'\text{ is the smallest splitting extension of }\mathrm G'=\mathrm G_{\mathrm K'},\ \mathrm S'=\mathrm S_{\mathrm K'}\text{ is a maximal split }\mathrm K'\text{-torus, and the root system of }\mathrm G'\text{ relative to }\mathrm S'\text{ identifies with }\Phi.\text{ Every displayed pinning }x_a\text{ base-changes canonically to the corresponding pinning over }\mathrm K'.

statements.title: Quasi-split SU(3) attached to a quadratic extension
statements.statement_plain: Let l/k be a separable quadratic extension, with its nontrivial Galois automorphism applied entrywise and denoted by a bar. For the matrix J with antidiagonal entries 1, -1, 1, the associated quasi-split group SU(3) is the outer twisted form of SL(3) defined by inverse transpose followed by conjugation by J. Its k-points are precisely the matrices g in SL(3,l) satisfying bar(g) = Ad(J)g^{-t}.
statements.statement_latex: \text{Let }\ell/k\text{ be a separable quadratic extension with nontrivial Galois automorphism }x\mapsto\bar x.\text{ For }J=\begin{bmatrix}0&0&1\\0&-1&0\\1&0&0\end{bmatrix},\text{ the associated quasi-split group }G:=\mathrm{SU}_3\text{ is the outer twisted form of }\mathrm{SL}_3\text{ defined by }g\mapsto\operatorname{Ad}(J)g^{-t}.\text{ Its }k\text{-points are }\mathrm{SU}_3(k)=\left\{g\in\mathrm{SL}_3(\ell)\mid\bar g=\operatorname{Ad}(J)g^{-t}\right\}.

\ell/k\text{ is a separable quadratic extension}
x\mapsto\bar{x}\text{ is the nontrivial Galois automorphism of }\ell/k
J=\begin{bmatrix}0&0&1\\0&-1&0\\1&0&0\end{bmatrix}

statements.title: Smooth Closed Subgroups Are Determined by Geometric Points
statements.statement_plain: For an affine algebraic group A over a field F, two smooth closed F-subgroup schemes are equal if their subgroups of points over an algebraic closure of F are equal inside the geometric points of A.

statements.title: Rank-One Moy-Prasad Filtration Subgroups
statements.statement_plain: In the quasi-split simple rank-one model, for a point x in the apartment and positive depth r, P_{x,r} is the subgroup generated by the torus filtration at ceiling depth r and the two root-group filtrations at the corresponding ceiling affine levels. P_{x,r+} is the union of P_{x,s} over s>r and has the displayed floor-plus-one generator description. Set P_{x,0}=P_x. The zero-plus subgroup depends only on the facet containing x, whereas positive-depth subgroups generally do not. For a building point represented by (g,y), define P_{x,r} by conjugation from P_{y,r}.
statements.statement_latex:
For x\in\mathcal A and r>0, define the descending filtration subgroup \(\mathcal P_{x,r}\subseteq G(k)\) by
\[
\mathcal P_{x,r}=\left\langle T(k)_{\lceil r\rceil},\ u_b\!\left(\mathfrak m^{\lceil r-\langle b,x\rangle\rceil}\right)\mid b\in\{a,-a\}\right\rangle.
\]
Set
\[
\mathcal P_{x,r+}=\bigcup_{s>r}\mathcal P_{x,s}=\left\langle T(k)_{\lfloor r\rfloor+1},\ u_b\!\left(\mathfrak m^{\lfloor r-\langle b,x\rangle\rfloor+1}\right)\mid b\in\{a,-a\}\right\rangle,
\]
and \(\mathcal P_{x,0}=\mathcal P_x\). The subgroup \(\mathcal P_{x,0+}\), like \(\mathcal P_{x,0}\), depends only on the facet containing x, but this is generally false for \(r>0\). For any \(x=(g,y)\in\mathcal B\), define \(\mathcal P_{x,r}=g\mathcal P_{y,r}g^{-1}\).
assumptions_latex: G is in the quasi-split simple rank-one setting with roots {a,-a}.
x\in\mathcal A and r>0; T(k)_{\bullet} and u_b(\mathfrak m^{\bullet}) are the torus and root-group filtration subgroups used in this model.
statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal P_{x,r}=\left\langle T(k)_{\lceil r\rceil},\ u_b\!\left(\mathfrak m^{\lceil r-\langle b,x\rangle\rceil}\right)\ (b\in\{a,-a\})\right\rangle,\qquad \mathcal P_{x,r+}=\bigcup_{s>r}\mathcal P_{x,s}=\left\langle T(k)_{\lfloor r\rfloor+1},\ u_b\!\left(\mathfrak m^{\lfloor r-\langle b,x\rangle\rfloor+1}\right)\ (b\in\{a,-a\})\right\rangle;\quad \mathcal P_{x,0}=\mathcal P_x.\quad \mathcal P_{x,0+}\text{ depends only on the facet containing }x,\text{ whereas this need not hold for general }r>0.\text{ For }x=(g,y)\in\mathcal B,\ \mathcal P_{x,r}=g\mathcal P_{y,r}g^{-1}.
statements.scope_note: Rank-one explicit Moy-Prasad filtration definition on the apartment, its r-plus and depth-zero conventions, facet-dependence boundary, and conjugation to arbitrary building points.

statements.title: Structural properties of Moy-Prasad filtration subgroups
statements.statement_plain: The Moy-Prasad filtration subgroups form a decreasing separated filtration of G(k) by bounded open subgroups, independent of the auxiliary split torus and equivariant under conjugation, hence normal in the stabilizer of x. At positive depth they have an ordered negative-root, torus, positive-root product decomposition, and commutators of depths r and s lie at depth r+s. For a parabolic P=MN with x in the corresponding M-building, positive-depth subgroups have an Iwahori decomposition relative to P, and their intersection with M(k) is the filtration subgroup for M at the image x_M.
statements.statement_latex: The family (\mathcal P_{x,r})_{r\in\widetilde{\mathbf R}_{\ge0}} is a decreasing separated filtration of G(k) by bounded open subgroups. It depends only on x and r, not on the auxiliary S, and for every g\in G(k), g\mathcal P_{x,r}g^{-1}=\mathcal P_{gx,r}; hence \mathcal P_{x,r} is normal in the stabilizer G(k)_x. For r>0, any positive-root system \Phi^+ and any fixed order of its positive and negative roots give a bijection \prod_{a\in\Phi^-}U_{a,x,r}\times Z(k)_r\times\prod_{a\in\Phi^+}U_{a,x,r}\to\mathcal P_{x,r}. For r,s\in\widetilde{\mathbf R}_{\ge0}, [\mathcal P_{x,r},\mathcal P_{x,s}]\subseteq\mathcal P_{x,r+s}. If P=MN and x\in\mathcal B(G)_M, then for r>0 the group \mathcal P_{x,r} has an Iwahori decomposition with respect to P, and for every r\in\widetilde{\mathbf R}_{\ge0}, \mathcal P_{x,r}\cap M(k)=\mathcal P^M_{x_M,r}, where x_M is the image of x in \mathcal B(M).
assumptions_latex: x\in\mathcal B(G)
r,s\in\widetilde{\mathbf R}_{\ge 0}
P=MN\text{ is a parabolic subgroup and }x\in\mathcal B(G)_M\text{, with image }x_M\in\mathcal B(M)\text{ for the parabolic assertions}
statements.conclusion_latex: (\mathcal P_{x,r})_{r\in\widetilde{\mathbf R}_{\ge0}}\text{ is a decreasing separated filtration of }G(k)\text{ by bounded open subgroups, independent of }S,\quad g\mathcal P_{x,r}g^{-1}=\mathcal P_{gx,r}\text{ for }g\in G(k),\quad [\mathcal P_{x,r},\mathcal P_{x,s}]\subseteq\mathcal P_{x,r+s};\text{ for }r>0,\ \prod_{a\in\Phi^-}U_{a,x,r}\times Z(k)_r\times\prod_{a\in\Phi^+}U_{a,x,r}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal P_{x,r}\text{ for any positive-root system and fixed factor orders, and }\mathcal P_{x,r}\text{ has an Iwahori decomposition relative to }P;\text{ moreover }\mathcal P_{x,r}\cap M(k)=\mathcal P^M_{x_M,r}\text{ for all }r\in\widetilde{\mathbf R}_{\ge0}.
statements.scope_note: Uses the source's local notation for the filtration subgroups, root-group filtrations, torus filtration, building, and the Levi-building image x_M. The product bijection is asserted for any positive-root system and any fixed ordering of the factors.

statements.title: Properties and failure boundary of the standard filtration on tori
statements.statement_plain: The standard filtration on k-tori is functorial and schematic. Restricted to the full subcategory of weakly induced k-tori, it is connected and congruent, admissible, and the unique admissible filtration. On the whole category of k-tori, it is not connected and congruent and does not satisfy the Moy-Prasad isomorphism.

statements.title: Distribution algebra and associated graded algebra of a smooth group scheme
statements.statement_plain: For a smooth group scheme X, the associated graded distribution algebra is canonically the divided-power algebra of its Lie algebra. If the Lie algebra is free with a chosen basis, the distribution algebra has a filtered basis indexed by multi-indices, with multiplication modulo lower filtration given by the multinomial coefficient. Over a Q-algebra, normalized monomials give an identification of the distribution algebra with the universal enveloping algebra of the Lie algebra.
statements.statement_latex: For a smooth group scheme \mathfrak{X} over A, the canonical algebra map \Gamma(\operatorname{Lie}\mathfrak{X})\to\operatorname{GrDist}(\mathfrak{X}) is an isomorphism. If \operatorname{Lie}\mathfrak{X} is free over A with basis (\delta_i), there is a basis (\delta_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbf N^n} of \operatorname{Dist}(\mathfrak{X}) whose elements of total degree m form a basis of \operatorname{Dist}_m\mathfrak{X}/\operatorname{Dist}_{m-1}\mathfrak{X}, and \delta_\alpha\delta_\beta\equiv\frac{(\alpha+\beta)!}{\alpha!\beta!}\delta_{\alpha+\beta}\pmod{\operatorname{Dist}_{|\alpha|+|\beta|-1}\mathfrak{X}}. If A is a \mathbf Q-algebra, one may take \delta_\alpha=(1/\alpha!)\delta_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots\delta_n^{\alpha_n}, yielding \operatorname{Dist}(\mathfrak{X})\cong U(\operatorname{Lie}\mathfrak{X}).
assumptions_latex: \mathfrak{X}\text{ is smooth over }A
\operatorname{Lie}\mathfrak{X}\text{ is a free }A\text{-module with basis }(\delta_1,\ldots,\delta_n)
A\text{ is a }\mathbf{Q}\text{-algebra for the final enveloping-algebra identification}
statements.conclusion_latex: \Gamma(\operatorname{Lie}\mathfrak{X})\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{GrDist}(\mathfrak{X});\quad (\delta_\alpha)_{|\alpha|=m}\text{ gives a basis of }\operatorname{Dist}_m\mathfrak{X}/\operatorname{Dist}_{m-1}\mathfrak{X},\quad \delta_\alpha\delta_\beta\equiv\frac{(\alpha+\beta)!}{\alpha!\,\beta!}\,\delta_{\alpha+\beta}\pmod{\operatorname{Dist}_{|\alpha|+|\beta|-1}\mathfrak{X}};\quad A\text{ a }\mathbf{Q}\text{-algebra}\Rightarrow\delta_\alpha=\frac{1}{\alpha!}\delta_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots\delta_n^{\alpha_n}\text{ and }\operatorname{Dist}(\mathfrak{X})\simeq U(\operatorname{Lie}\mathfrak{X}).

statements.title: Affine-root polyhedra and rational vertices
statements.statement_plain: Enumerate the affine roots Xi as psi_1 through psi_m and set psi_ij equal to psi_j minus psi_i. For each i, C_i is the compact polyhedron in the closed chamber where all psi_ij are nonnegative. These polyhedra cover the closed chamber, psi_i is the minimum affine-root value on C_i, and every vertex of C_i is a rational point of the apartment.

Then \(\bigcup_i C_i=\overline{\mathcal C}\), \(\psi_i(x)=\min_{j\le m}\psi_j(x)\) for \(x\in C_i\), and every vertex of each \(C_i\) is a rational point of \(\mathcal A\).

statements.title: Optimal points for affine-root subsets
statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty subset S of the affine-root system Sigma, a point x in the closure of a chamber C is optimal when it maximizes the minimum value of the roots in S over that chamber closure and has rational value for every affine root. A building point x is optimal if it is optimal in this sense for some nonempty finite affine-root subset associated with a chamber in an apartment containing x.
statements.statement_latex: Let \mathfrak S\subseteq\Sigma be nonempty. statements.title: Lie Algebra of a Torus via Cocharacters
statements.statement_plain: For a k-torus T, the Lie algebra of T after extending scalars to k_s is functorially and Galois-equivariantly identified with the cocharacter group tensored with k_s, and the Lie algebra over k is the Galois-fixed subspace. Differentiating any cocharacter gives a map from Lie(G_m over k_s) to Lie(T over k_s) that sends the canonical element partial t/t to the associated Lie-algebra element.
statements.statement_latex: For a k-torus T, there is a functorial Galois-equivariant identification \operatorname{Lie}(T_{k_s})\simeq X_*(T)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}k_s, with diagonal Galois action, and hence \operatorname{Lie}(T)\simeq (X_*(T)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}k_s)^{\Theta}. For every cocharacter \lambda\in X_*(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_{k_s}(\mathbf G_{m,k_s},T_{k_s}), its differential d\lambda: \operatorname{Lie}(\mathbf G_{m,k_s})\to\operatorname{Lie}(T_{k_s}) sends the canonical element \frac{\partial t}{t} to the corresponding Lie-algebra element.
assumptions_latex: T is a k-torus.
k_s is a separable closure of k, and \Theta=Gal(k_s/k) acts diagonally on X_*(T) \otimes_{\mathbf Z} k_s.
X_*(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_{k_s}(\mathbf G_{m,k_s},T_{k_s}).
statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Lie}(T_{k_s})\simeq X_*(T)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}k_s \quad\text{(functorially and Galois-equivariantly)},\qquad \operatorname{Lie}(T)\simeq\left(X_*(T)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}k_s\right)^{\Theta};\quad d\lambda:\operatorname{Lie}(\mathbf G_{m,k_s})\to\operatorname{Lie}(T_{k_s})\text{ sends }\frac{\partial t}{t}\text{ to the element associated with }\lambda.

statements.title: Affine-root simplicial structure and simplexwise constancy for SL2
statements.statement_plain: In the standard SL2 rank-one apartment, affine roots make the real line into a simplicial complex with half-integer vertices and intervals between consecutive vertices as edges. The subgroup P_x is constant on the relative interior of each simplex, so it is denoted P_F.
statements.statement_latex: For the standard rank-one apartment \(\mathcal A\simeq\mathbf R\) of \(\mathrm{SL}_2(k)\), the affine roots induce a simplicial structure whose vertices are exactly \(\tfrac12\mathbf Z\) and whose edges are the intervals between consecutive vertices. The subgroup \(\mathcal P_x\) is constant as \(x\) varies in the relative interior of a simplex \(\mathcal F\), so it may be written \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal F}\).
assumptions_latex: k is equipped with a surjective non-archimedean discrete valuation \(\omega:k^{\times}\to\mathbf Z\), with ring of integers \(\mathfrak{o}\), maximal ideal \(\mathfrak{m}\), and perfect residue field.

\(G(k)=\mathrm{SL}_{2}(k)\) with standard apartment \(\mathcal A=X_{*}(T)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf R\simeq\mathbf R\), affine roots \(\Psi=\{b+j\mid b\in\{a,-a\},\ j\in\mathbf Z\}\), and \(\mathcal P_x\) defined from the affine-root data.
statements.conclusion_latex: The zeros of the affine roots are exactly \(\mathcal A^{(0)}=\tfrac12\mathbf Z\subset\mathbf R\), and the one-dimensional simplices are the intervals between consecutive vertices. For every simplex \(\mathcal F\) and every \(x\) in its relative interior, \(\mathcal P_x\) depends only on \(\mathcal F\); hence it is denoted \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal F}\).

statements.title: Bruhat-Tits Building of SU3 as a Tree
statements.statement_plain: For the rank-one SU3 example, the Bruhat-Tits building is the quotient of G(k) times its standard apartment A by the relation (g,x)~(h,y) exactly when some n in N(k) satisfies y=nx and g^{-1}hn lies in P_x. The map x to (1,x) embeds A as the standard apartment, P_x is the stabilizer of x, and every apartment is gA. The building is a one-dimensional simplicial complex, hence a tree, and it is locally finite when the residue field f is finite.
statements.statement_latex: \mathcal B:=(G(k)\times\mathcal A)/\sim,\quad (g,x)\sim(h,y)\Longleftrightarrow\exists n\in N(k):\ y=nx,\ g^{-1}hn\in\mathcal P_x;\quad \mathcal A\hookrightarrow\mathcal B,\ x\mapsto(1,x),\ \operatorname{Stab}_{G(k)}(x)=\mathcal P_x,\ \operatorname{Apartments}(\mathcal B)=\{g\mathcal A:g\in G(k)\},\ \mathcal B\text{ is a tree, locally finite when }\#\mathfrak f<\infty.
assumptions_latex: G denotes the SU3 group over k in the source context, with rational points G(k), and has standard apartment \mathcal A with normalizer N(k).
For each x\in\mathcal A, \mathcal P_x\subseteq G(k) is the subgroup appearing in the equivalence relation; it is the stabilizer of x.
\mathfrak f is the residue field; local finiteness is asserted when \mathfrak f is finite.
statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal B=(G(k)\times\mathcal A)/\sim,\quad (g,x)\sim(h,y)\Longleftrightarrow\exists n\in N(k):\ y=nx\ \text{and}\ g^{-1}hn\in\mathcal P_x;\quad x\mapsto(1,x)\ \text{embeds}\mathcal A\text{ as the standard apartment},\ \operatorname{Stab}_{G(k)}(x)=\mathcal P_x,\ \operatorname{Apartments}(\mathcal B)=\{g\mathcal A:g\in G(k)\},\ \mathcal B\text{ is a one-dimensional simplicial complex (a tree), locally finite if }\mathfrak f\text{ is finite}.

statements.title: Affine roots in a rank-one standard apartment
statements.statement_plain: In the rank-one standard apartment, an affine function psi=b+r is an affine root when its derivative b is one of a, -a, 2a, or -2a and r is a jump of the appropriate filtration: that of U_b(k) for b equal to 2a or -2a, and that of U_b(k)/U_2b(k) for b equal to a or -a. For every \(v\in\mathcal A\), the root system of \(G_v\) with respect to \(T\) is the set of derivatives of the affine roots that vanish at \(v\).

statements.title: Unique Opposite Pinning and Associated Rank-One SL_2 Homomorphism
statements.statement_plain: In the split rank-one setting, every K_1-pinning of the root group U_a determines a unique associated K_1-pinning of U_{-a}. Three conditions are equivalent: the two standard products m_a and m_{-a} lie in the chosen Weyl-normalizer coset, or the two pinnings arise from a K_1-homomorphism from SL_2. That homomorphism is unique; both products equal the image of the Weyl element, whose Weyl-group image is the reflection r_a, and the association works in both directions.

statements.title: Balls of an Additive Norm and Their Lattice Properties
statements.statement_plain: For an additive norm alpha and a level r, the closed ball consists of vectors of norm at least r, while the open ball is the union of all higher-level closed balls and consists of vectors of norm greater than r. The closed ball is an o-submodule. Discreteness of the nonzero norm values makes the open ball equal to one closed ball at some level s greater than r. A lattice is a finitely generated o-submodule spanning X over k. Every closed norm ball contains a lattice, but it need not be contained in a lattice and therefore need not be finitely generated.
statements.statement_latex: \text{For a level }r,\quad L_{\alpha,r}:=\{v\in X\mid \alpha(v)\ge r\},\qquad L_{\alpha,r+}:=\bigcup_{s>r}L_{\alpha,s}=\{v\in X\mid \alpha(v)>r\}.\quad L_{\alpha,r}\text{ is an }\mathfrak{o}\text{-submodule of }X.\text{ Since }\alpha(X\setminus\{0\})\text{ is discrete, there exists }s_0>r\text{ with }L_{\alpha,r+}=L_{\alpha,s_0}.\text{ A lattice is a finitely generated }\mathfrak{o}\text{-submodule generating }X\text{ over }k.\text{ The module }L_{\alpha,r}\text{ contains a lattice, but it need not be contained in a lattice and hence need not be finitely generated.}
assumptions_latex: \alpha\text{ is an additive norm on the }k\text{-vector space }X.
\mathfrak{o}\text{ is the noetherian valuation ring used for lattices in }X.
\alpha(X\setminus\{0\})\text{ is discrete.}
statements.conclusion_latex: L_{\alpha,r}=\{v\in X\mid \alpha(v)\ge r\}\text{ is an }\mathfrak{o}\text{-submodule, and }L_{\alpha,r+}=\bigcup_{s>r}L_{\alpha,s}=\{v\in X\mid \alpha(v)>r\}=L_{\alpha,s_0}\text{ for some }s_0>r.\ A lattice is a finitely generated }\mathfrak{o}\text{-submodule generating }X\text{ over }k.\ L_{\alpha,r}\text{ contains a lattice, but need not be contained in a lattice and hence need not be finitely generated.}

statements.title: Simplicial structure and barycenters from periodic lattice chains
statements.statement_plain: In the lattice-chain model, points are declared to determine the same simplex when they correspond to the same lattice chain, and face incidence is inclusion of chains. Rank r+1 chains give r-dimensional facets; single-lattice segments give vertices, while one-dimensional residue-field successive quotients give chambers. A periodic chain has grading c(L_i)=i/(r+1), well defined up to homothety, and its associated building point is the barycenter of its facet.
statements.statement_latex: Two points of \(\mathcal B\) are declared to belong to the same simplex when they correspond to the same lattice chain. The simplex containing \(x\) is a face of the simplex containing \(y\) when the lattice chain corresponding to \(x\) is contained in that corresponding to \(y\). Facets of dimension \(r\) are given by lattice chains of rank \(r+1\); vertices are chains whose segments are single lattices, and chambers are chains whose successive quotients are one-dimensional \(\mathfrak f\)-vector spaces. For a periodic lattice chain \(\mathcal L\), choose a segment \(\mathfrak{m}{L}_{0}\subsetneq L_r\subsetneq L_{r-1}\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq L_0\) and set \(c(L_i)=i/(r+1)\). This natural grading is well defined up to homothety, and the corresponding point of \(\mathcal B\) is the barycenter of the facet determined by \(\mathcal L\).
assumptions_latex: x,y\in\mathcal B\text{ correspond to lattice chains}
\mathcal L\text{ is a periodic lattice chain with a segment }\mathfrak{m}{L}_{0}\subsetneq L_r\subsetneq L_{r-1}\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq L_0
statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Facets of dimension }r\text{ correspond to lattice chains of rank }r+1;\quad c(L_i)=\frac{i}{r+1};\quad \text{the point corresponding to }\mathcal L\text{ is the barycenter of its facet}.

statements.title: Splitting additive norms, sets, and bases
statements.statement_plain: For an additive norm alpha on X, splitting over a direct sum means the norm of a sum equals the minimum of the summand norms. A nonzero vector set is splitting when the norm of every linear combination equals the minimum of the norms of its scaled vectors. A basis is a splitting basis when it is such a set, equivalently when alpha splits over the direct sum of its spanned lines. The norm is splitting when it has a splitting basis.
statements.statement_latex: Let \alpha be an additive norm on X. (1) \alpha splits over X=X_1\oplus X_2 when \alpha(v_1+v_2)=\min\{\alpha(v_1),\alpha(v_2)\} for all v_1\in X_1 and v_2\in X_2. (2) A set v_1,\ldots,v_n of nonzero vectors in X is splitting for \alpha when, for all a_1,\ldots,a_n\in k, \alpha(\sum_i a_i v_i)=\min_i\{\alpha(a_i v_i)\}. (3) A basis v_1,\ldots,v_n is a splitting basis for \alpha when it is a splitting set, equivalently when \alpha splits over X=l_1\oplus\cdots\oplus l_n with l_i=kv_i. (4) \alpha is splitting when it admits a splitting basis.

X=X_1\oplus X_2\text{ is a direct-sum decomposition}.
v_1,\ldots,v_n\in X\setminus\{0\};\ a_1,\ldots,a_n\in k.
v_1,\ldots,v_n\text{ is a basis of }X\text{ when discussing a splitting basis}.

statements.title: Correspondence between splitting additive norms and graded periodic lattice chains
statements.statement_plain: Splitting additive norms and graded periodic lattice chains determine maps in both directions: a norm yields its periodic lattice chain and the grading given by infima on lattices, while a graded chain yields a norm by taking the supremum of the grading over lattices containing each vector. Translating the norm by r translates the grading by -r, so norm homothety classes correspond to periodic lattice chains with grading defined up to shift.
statements.statement_latex: There are maps in both directions between splitting additive norms and graded periodic lattice chains. A splitting additive norm \(\alpha\) gives the periodic lattice chain \(\mathcal L=\{L_{\alpha,r}\mid r\in\mathbf R\}\) with grading \(c(L)=\inf\{\alpha(v)\mid v\in L\}\). Conversely, a graded periodic lattice chain \((\mathcal L,c)\) gives \(\alpha(v)=\sup\{c(L)\mid L\in\mathcal L,\ v\in L\}\). If \(\alpha\) corresponds to \((\mathcal L,c)\), then \(\alpha+r\) corresponds to \((\mathcal L,c-r)\), where \((c-r)(L)=c(L)-r\). Hence the homothety class \(\alpha+\mathbf R\) corresponds to the periodic lattice chain \(\mathcal L\) with grading defined up to shift, denoted \(c+\mathbf R\).

(\mathcal L,c)\text{ is a graded periodic lattice chain}
statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha+\mathbf R\longleftrightarrow(\mathcal L,c+\mathbf R),\qquad (c-r)(L)=c(L)-r

statements.title: Affine norm apartments from line decompositions
statements.statement_plain: For each decomposition of X into n lines, the associated tilde apartment is affine under R^n, while the corresponding untilde apartment is affine under R^n modulo the diagonal R. statements.title: Lattice-chain stabilizers and reductive quotients for GL(X) and SL(X)
statements.statement_plain: For a periodic lattice chain in X, the stabilizer of its barycentric point in GL(X) is the stabilizer of the chain. The connected facet subgroup is the subgroup fixing every lattice in the chain. Reduction modulo the maximal ideal maps this subgroup to the parabolic stabilizing the induced flag in L0/mL0, whose reductive quotient is the product of the general linear groups of the successive flag quotients. The source also states that an analogous description holds for SL(X).
statements.statement_latex: Let G=\mathrm{GL}(X), and let a periodic lattice chain \mathcal L define a facet \mathcal F\subset\mathcal B(X)=\mathcal B(G), with barycenter x corresponding to the equispaced grading. Then G(k)_x is the stabilizer of \mathcal L. Moreover, G(k)^0=G(k)^1=\{g\in\mathrm{GL}(X):\det(g)\in\mathfrak o^\times\}, and G(k)_{\mathcal F}^{0}=G(k)_x^{0}=G(k)_x^{1}=G(k)_x^{\dagger} is the subgroup stabilizing every lattice in \mathcal L. For L_0\in\mathcal L, let \mathfrak mL_0\subsetneq L_r\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq L_0 induce the flag \{0\}\subsetneq V_r\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq V=V_0 in V=L_0/\mathfrak mL_0. The image of G(k)_{\mathcal F}^{0} in \mathrm{GL}(V) is the parabolic stabilizer of this flag, and its reductive quotient is \prod_{i=1}^{r}\mathrm{GL}(V_{i-1}/V_i). The analogous description holds for G=\mathrm{SL}(X).
assumptions_latex: G=\mathrm{GL}(X)
\mathcal L\text{ is a periodic lattice chain defining a facet }\mathcal F\subset\mathcal B(X)=\mathcal B(G)
x\text{ is the barycenter corresponding to the equispaced grading of }\mathcal L
L_0\in\mathcal L,\quad \mathfrak mL_0\subsetneq L_r\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq L_0
V=L_0/\mathfrak mL_0,\quad \{0\}\subsetneq V_r\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq V,\quad V_0:=V
statements.conclusion_latex: G(k)_x=\operatorname{Stab}_{G(k)}(\mathcal L),\quad G(k)^0=G(k)^1=\{g\in\mathrm{GL}(X):\det(g)\in\mathfrak o^\times\},\quad G(k)_{\mathcal F}^{0}=G(k)_x^{0}=G(k)_x^{1}=G(k)_x^{\dagger}=\{g:gL=L\text{ for every }L\in\mathcal L\},\quad \operatorname{im}\bigl(G(k)_{\mathcal F}^{0}\to\mathrm{GL}(V)\bigr)=\operatorname{Stab}_{\mathrm{GL}(V)}(\{0\}\subsetneq V_r\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq V),\quad \bigl(\operatorname{im}G(k)_{\mathcal F}^{0}\bigr)_{\mathrm{red}}\cong\prod_{i=1}^{r}\mathrm{GL}(V_{i-1}/V_i)
statements.scope_note: Explicit lattice-chain description for facet stabilizers, connected parahoric subgroups, and the reductive quotient for G=GL(X); the source additionally states that an analogous description holds for G=SL(X) without spelling out its formulas.

statements.title: Apartment of self-dual additive norms from a Witt decomposition
statements.statement_plain: For a Witt decomposition of the paired space X and a decomposition of its positive part into lines, with the dual negative decomposition, the associated apartment is the set of all self-dual additive norms on X that split over the ordered sum of the positive lines, the neutral part, and the dual negative lines.
statements.statement_latex: Given the self-dual additive-norm space \mathcal{B}(X,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle), a Witt decomposition X=X^{+}\oplus X^{0}\oplus X^{-}, and a line decomposition X^{+}=\bigoplus_{i=1}^{r}l_i^{+} with dual X^{-}=\bigoplus_{i=1}^{r}l_i^{-}, define \mathcal{A}(\bigoplus l_i,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle) as the set of self-dual additive norms that split over l_{1}^{+}\oplus\cdots\oplus l_{r}^{+}\oplus X^{0}\oplus l_{r}^{-}\oplus\cdots\oplus l_{1}^{-}.
assumptions_latex: (X,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle) admits a Witt decomposition X=X^{+}\oplus X^{0}\oplus X^{-}.
X^{+}=l_{1}^{+}\oplus\cdots\oplus l_{r}^{+} is a decomposition into lines, with dual decomposition X^{-}=l_{1}^{-}\oplus\cdots\oplus l_{r}^{-}.
\alpha is a self-dual additive norm on X.
statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal{A}\!\left(\bigoplus l_i,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle\right)=\left\{\alpha\in\mathcal{B}(X,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle):\alpha\text{ splits over }l_{1}^{+}\oplus\cdots\oplus l_{r}^{+}\oplus X^{0}\oplus l_{r}^{-}\oplus\cdots\oplus l_{1}^{-}\right\}.
statements.scope_note: Apartment associated with a Witt decomposition and a line decomposition in the self-dual additive-norm model of a classical-group building.

statements.title: Dual and self-dual splitting additive norms
statements.statement_plain: Given a splitting additive norm alpha on X, define alpha-vee by transporting alpha-star through the specified isomorphism from X-sigma to X-star. Alpha is self-dual exactly when alpha equals alpha-vee. Every self-dual norm satisfies alpha(x) + alpha(y) <= omega(<x,y>) for all x and y in X.
statements.statement_latex: For a splitting additive norm \(\alpha:X\to\mathbf{R}\cup\{\infty\}\), define \(\alpha^{\vee}\) as the splitting additive norm obtained by transporting \(\alpha^*\) under the specified isomorphism \(X^{\sigma}\xrightarrow{\sim}X^*\). The norm \(\alpha\) is self-dual if \(\alpha=\alpha^{\vee}\). In particular, every self-dual norm satisfies \(\alpha(x)+\alpha(y)\leq\omega(\langle x,y\rangle)\) for all \(x,y\in X\).
assumptions_latex: \alpha:X\to\mathbf{R}\cup\{\infty\}\text{ is a splitting additive norm}
X^{\sigma}\xrightarrow{\sim}X^*\text{ is the specified isomorphism used to transport }\alpha^*
statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha^{\vee}:=\operatorname{transport}_{X^{\sigma}\simeq X^*}(\alpha^*),\qquad \alpha\text{ is self-dual}\iff\alpha=\alpha^{\vee};\qquad \alpha=\alpha^{\vee}\implies \forall x,y\in X,\ \alpha(x)+\alpha(y)\leq\omega(\langle x,y\rangle).
statements.scope_note: Splitting additive norms on X in the ambient paired space, with the valuation \(\omega\) and pairing \(\langle\ ,\ \rangle\) appearing in the source inequality.

statements.title: Dual graded periodic lattice chain
statements.statement_plain: Let (𝓛,c) be a graded periodic lattice chain. Its dual graded periodic lattice chain is defined by taking the dual lattices, equivalently the lattices denoted by L-tilde, and assigning to L-tilde the negative of the grading at the smallest member of 𝓛 that properly contains L.
statements.statement_latex: Let (\mathcal L,c) be a graded periodic lattice chain. Its dual graded periodic lattice chain (\mathcal L^{\vee},c^{\vee}) is defined by \mathcal L^{\vee}=\{L^{\vee}\mid L\in\mathcal L\}=\{L^{\sim}\mid L\in\mathcal L\} and c^{\vee}(L^{\sim})=-c(L^{-}), where L^{-} is the smallest member of \mathcal L that properly contains L.
assumptions_latex: (\mathcal L,c)\text{ is a graded periodic lattice chain.}
statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal L^{\vee}=\{L^{\vee}\mid L\in\mathcal L\}=\{L^{\sim}\mid L\in\mathcal L\},\qquad c^{\vee}(L^{\sim})=-c(L^{-}),\text{ where }L^{-}\text{ is the smallest member of }\mathcal L\text{ that properly contains }L.

statements.title: Nondegenerate epsilon-Hermitian forms
statements.statement_plain: Assume that the characteristic of f is not 2. Given an order-one-or-two automorphism sigma of k preserving omega, epsilon equal to 1 or -1, and a finite-dimensional k-vector space X, an epsilon-Hermitian form is additive in each variable, linear in the first variable, sigma-semilinear in the second, and satisfies epsilon-sigma symmetry. It is nondegenerate when the map from the sigma-twist of X to its dual, sending w to the functional obtained by pairing with w, is an isomorphism of k-vector spaces.
statements.statement_latex: Assume \operatorname{char}(f)\neq2. Let \sigma be an automorphism of k of order 1 or 2 preserving \omega, let k_0 be its fixed field, let \varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}, and let X be a finite-dimensional k-vector space. An \varepsilon-Hermitian form \langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:X\times X\to k is additive in each variable and satisfies \langle av,w\rangle=a\langle v,w\rangle, \langle v,aw\rangle=\sigma(a)\langle v,w\rangle, and \langle v,w\rangle=\varepsilon\sigma(\langle w,v\rangle). The form is nondegenerate when the map X^\sigma\to X^*,\ w\mapsto\langle-,w\rangle, is an isomorphism of k-vector spaces.
assumptions_latex: \operatorname{char}(f)\neq 2
\sigma:k\to k\text{ is an automorphism of order }1\text{ or }2\text{ preserving }\omega,\text{ with fixed field }k_0
\varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}
X\text{ is a finite-dimensional }k\text{-vector space}
statements.conclusion_latex: \langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle\text{ is }\varepsilon\text{-Hermitian when it is additive in each variable, }\langle av,w\rangle=a\langle v,w\rangle,\ \langle v,aw\rangle=\sigma(a)\langle v,w\rangle,\text{ and }\langle v,w\rangle=\varepsilon\sigma(\langle w,v\rangle);\text{ it is nondegenerate when }X^\sigma\to X^*,\ w\mapsto\langle-,w\rangle,\text{ is an isomorphism of }k\text{-vector spaces}.
statements.scope_note: Definition and standing nondegeneracy assumption for the epsilon-Hermitian forms used in the classical-group lattice models; claims found only in the longer primary-OCR block are excluded.

statements.title: Characteristic-2 boundary for self-dual and maxi-minorant norms
statements.statement_plain: In the classical-group lattice construction, the assumption that the characteristic of \widetilde t is not 2 can be dropped in the symplectic case and in the unramified unitary case. In the other cases, self-dual norms are not sufficient; one must use norms that are maxi-minorant for the Hermitian form together with its pseudo-quadratic form. For a nondegenerate Hermitian form, maxi-minorance for the form is equivalent to self-duality, and under the separate condition that the characteristic of f is not 2 or the extension k/k0 is unramified quadratic, it is also equivalent to maxi-minorance for the pair.

eq 1 and k/k_0 is unramified). Outside these cases, self-duality must be replaced by maxi-minorance for the pair (h,q). When h is nondegenerate, maxi-minorance for h is equivalent to self-duality; and when \operatorname{char}(f)
eq 2 or k/k_0 is an unramified quadratic extension, maxi-minorance for h is equivalent to maxi-minorance for (h,q).
assumptions_latex: h(x,y)=\langle x,y\rangle is a nondegenerate \varepsilon-Hermitian form over k with involution \sigma, with associated pseudo-quadratic form q
The construction discussed in Proposition 15.2.10 assumes \operatorname{char}(\widetilde t)\neq 2
