statements.title: Choice-independent building bijection for classical groups
statements.statement_plain: In the stated quasi-split classical-group setting, the apartment isomorphism sending p to alpha is independent of the auxiliary vectors, the stabilizers of p and alpha in G(k0) are equal, and there is a unique G(k0)-equivariant bijection between the group building and the norm building restricting to that apartment isomorphism; the bijection is independent of the Witt decomposition.
statements.statement_latex: In the stated quasi-split classical-group setting, the apartment isomorphism carrying p to \alpha is independent of the auxiliary vectors, the stabilizers of p and \alpha in G(k_0) coincide, and there is a unique G(k_0)-equivariant bijection between \mathcal{B}(G) and \mathcal{B}(X,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle) restricting to that apartment isomorphism; this bijection is independent of the Witt decomposition.
assumptions_latex: In the stated setting, G is quasi-split, X=X^+\oplus X^0\oplus X^- is a Witt decomposition, X^+=l_1\oplus\cdots\oplus l_r is a decomposition into lines, T is the associated maximally split maximal torus, 0\ne v_i\in l_i, and p\in\mathcal{A}(T) and \alpha\in\mathcal{A}(\bigoplus_i l_i,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle) are the points defined from this data.
statements.conclusion_latex: The affine-space isomorphism \mathcal{A}(T)\to\mathcal{A}(\bigoplus_i l_i,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle) carrying p to \alpha is independent of the choice of (v_1,\ldots,v_r), and \operatorname{Stab}_{G(k_0)}(p)=\operatorname{Stab}_{G(k_0)}(\alpha). There is a unique G(k_0)-equivariant bijection \mathcal{B}(G)\to\mathcal{B}(X,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle) restricting to this apartment isomorphism, and it is independent of the choice of Witt decomposition.
statements.scope_note: Building and apartment correspondence for quasi-split symplectic, orthogonal, and unitary groups via norm/lattice models.

statements.title: Rank-one classical valuation: existence, uniqueness, and axioms
statements.statement_plain: For rank-one orthogonal, unitary, or symplectic data, the proposition defines K_0, K_1^*, and K_1 from q, f, and the torus. It proves K_0 is contained in K_1, gives the stated central-element or norm-element containments and the condition implying K_1=K, and shows that except for (id.,I,2) each equipollence class of root-datum valuations has a unique function omega satisfying omega(x^sigma x)=2 omega(x) whose induced valuation is special. The induced function is a root-datum valuation exactly when conditions (2)-(5) hold, in which case its restriction to K_1^* is a homomorphism; under the stated containment alternatives this homomorphism condition implies (5).
statements.statement_latex: Let r=1 and assume one of conditions (I),(2) of (10.1.3). Define K_0=\bigcup_{z\in X_0}q(z), K_1^*=c_{11}(T\cap\operatorname{Is}(f,q)), and K_1=K_1^*\cup\{o\}. Then (i) K_0\subseteq K_1; if (\sigma,\varepsilon)\ne(\mathrm{id.},I), K_1 contains the invariant elements of the center Z(K), while if (\sigma,\varepsilon)=(\mathrm{id.},I), K_1 contains elements x^\sigma x=x^2 for x\in K; and G\supset\operatorname{Is}(f,q) implies K_1=K. (ii) If (\sigma,\varepsilon,\dim X_0)\ne(\mathrm{id.},I,2), every equipollence class A of valuations of (T,(U_a)_{a\in\Phi}) has a unique \omega:K\to\mathbf{R}\cup\{\infty\} satisfying \omega(x^\sigma x)=2\omega(x) for all x\in K and such that \varphi^\omega\in A; this valuation is special. (iii) For \omega satisfying that relation, \varphi^\omega is a valuation of the root datum (T,(U_a)) iff (2) \omega^{-1}(\infty)=\{0\}, (3) \omega(k+k'+f(z,z'))\ge\inf(\omega(k),\omega(k')), (4) \omega(f(z,z')-f(z',z))\ge\omega(k)+\omega(k'), and (5) \omega(c_{-1,-1}(t)k c_{11}(t^{-1}))=\omega(k)+\omega(c_{-1,-1}(t)c_{11}(t^{-1})); under these conditions, \omega|_{K_1^*}:K_1^*\to\mathbf{R} is a homomorphism. (iv) If G\subset\operatorname{Is}(f,q) or G\supset\operatorname{Is}(f,q), (5') implies (5).
assumptions_latex: r=1 and one of conditions (I),(2) of (10.1.3) holds.
For (ii), (\sigma,\varepsilon,\dim X_0)\ne(\mathrm{id.},I,2), and A is an equipollence class of valuations of the root datum (T,(U_a)_{a\in\Phi}).
For (iii), \omega:K\to\mathbf{R}\cup\{\infty\} satisfies \omega(x^\sigma x)=2\omega(x) for all x\in K; (z,k),(z',k')\in Z and t\in T are quantified in (3)-(5).
For (iv), G\subset\operatorname{Is}(f,q) or G\supset\operatorname{Is}(f,q).
statements.conclusion_latex: K_0\subseteq K_1; if (\sigma,\varepsilon)\ne(\mathrm{id.},I), K_1 contains the invariant elements of the center Z(K), while if (\sigma,\varepsilon)=(\mathrm{id.},I), K_1 contains elements x^\sigma x=x^2 for x\in K; G\supset\operatorname{Is}(f,q) implies K_1=K. If (\sigma,\varepsilon,\dim X_0)\ne(\mathrm{id.},I,2), there is a unique \omega:K\to\mathbf{R}\cup\{\infty\} satisfying \omega(x^\sigma x)=2\omega(x) and yielding a special \varphi^\omega\in A. For such \omega, \varphi^\omega is a root-datum valuation iff conditions (2)-(5) hold; these conditions imply \omega|_{K_1^*}:K_1^*\to\mathbf{R} is a homomorphism. Under the (iv) containment alternatives, (5') implies (5).

statements.title: Functorial Definitions of SL(X), GL(X), and PGL(X)
statements.statement_plain: For an n-dimensional vector space X over k, SL(X) is the algebraic group sending each k-algebra R to SL(R tensor_k X), and GL(X) is defined analogously by GL(R tensor_k X). A basis identifies SL(X) with SL_n. The functorial determinant gives a homomorphism from GL(X) to the multiplicative group with kernel SL(X); the center of GL(X) is identified with the multiplicative group, and PGL(X) is the quotient by that center.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be an \(n\)-dimensional vector space over \(k\). Define \(\mathrm{SL}(X)\) by the functor \(R\mapsto\operatorname{SL}(R\otimes_k X)\) for every \(k\)-algebra \(R\), and define \(\mathrm{GL}(X)\) analogously by \(R\mapsto\operatorname{GL}(R\otimes_k X)\). Choosing a basis of \(X\) identifies \(\mathrm{SL}(X)\) with \(\mathrm{SL}_n\). The determinant maps \(\det_R:\mathrm{GL}(X)(R)\to R^\times\) are functorial in \(R\) and induce a homomorphism \(\det:\mathrm{GL}(X)\to\mathbf G_m\) whose kernel is \(\mathrm{SL}(X)\). The center of \(\mathrm{GL}(X)\) is identified with \(\mathbf G_m\), and \(\mathrm{PGL}(X)\) is the quotient \(\mathrm{GL}(X)/\mathbf G_m\).
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is an \(n\)-dimensional vector space over \(k\).
\(R\) ranges over all \(k\)-algebras.
statements.conclusion_latex: The functorial determinant maps define \(\det:\mathrm{GL}(X)\to\mathbf G_m\) with kernel \(\mathrm{SL}(X)\); the center of \(\mathrm{GL}(X)\) is identified with \(\mathbf G_m\), and \(\mathrm{PGL}(X)=\mathrm{GL}(X)/\mathbf G_m\).

statements.title: Affine and facet structure of the building subset associated with a maximal unramified torus
statements.statement_plain: For a maximal unramified torus T of G, with C and C' as in the source setup, the associated subset A(T) of the Bruhat-Tits building is nonempty and is a union of facets; for every x in A(T), it equals V(C')·x. It is an affine subspace with direction V(C') inside some apartment. Every apartment containing A(T) corresponds to a maximal k-split torus S containing C. If F is a facet contained in A(T) and maximal with that property, then in any apartment containing A(T), the set A(T) is the affine subspace spanned by F.
statements.statement_latex: \text{Let }T\text{ be a maximal unramified torus of }G\text{ with associated }C,C'\text{ as in the source setup. Then }\mathcal{A}(T)\subseteq\mathcal{B}(G)\text{ is nonempty and a union of facets, and for every }x\in\mathcal{A}(T),\ \mathcal{A}(T)=V(C')\cdot x.\text{ There is an apartment }\mathcal{A}\text{ containing }\mathcal{A}(T)\text{ in which it is an affine subspace with direction }V(C').\text{ Every such }\mathcal{A}\text{ corresponds to a maximal }k\text{-split torus }S\supseteq C.\text{ If a facet }\mathcal{F}\subseteq\mathcal{A}(T)\text{ is maximal with this property and }\mathcal{A}\supseteq\mathcal{A}(T),\text{ then }\mathcal{A}(T)\text{ is the affine subspace of }\mathcal{A}\text{ spanned by }\mathcal{F}.
assumptions_latex: T is a maximal unramified torus of G, with associated tori C and C' as in the source setup.
\mathcal{B}(G) is the Bruhat--Tits building over k.
statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}(1)\;&\mathcal{A}(T)\subseteq\mathcal{B}(G)\text{ is nonempty and is a union of facets; for every }x\in\mathcal{A}(T),\ \mathcal{A}(T)=V(C')\cdot x.\\(2)\;&\text{There exists an apartment }\mathcal{A}\text{ of }\mathcal{B}(G)\text{ containing }\mathcal{A}(T),\text{ in which }\mathcal{A}(T)\text{ is an affine subspace with direction }V(C').\\(3)\;&\text{For every apartment }\mathcal{A}\text{ containing }\mathcal{A}(T),\text{ the corresponding maximal }k\text{-split torus }S\text{ contains }C.\\(4)\;&\text{If }\mathcal{F}\subseteq\mathcal{A}(T)\text{ is a facet maximal with this property and }\mathcal{A}\text{ contains }\mathcal{A}(T),\text{ then }\mathcal{A}(T)\text{ is the affine subspace of }\mathcal{A}\text{ spanned by }\mathcal{F}.\end{aligned}

statements.title: Properties of the maximal-unramified-torus classification map
statements.statement_plain: For the map sending a maximal unramified k-torus T and a facet in its apartment to the associated facet and residue-field torus, the map is equivariant under every k-automorphism of G and is surjective. Each fiber is a single orbit under G(k)_{F}^{0+}. The facet is maximal among facets of the building contained in the apartment exactly when the associated residue-field torus is minisotropic. For a maximal facet, its dimension equals dim(C) minus dim(C_G), and also dim(C'), where C and C_G are maximal k-split tori in T and the center of G, respectively, and C' is a maximal k-split torus in T intersected with G_der.
statements.statement_latex: \text{Let }\Phi(T,\mathcal F)=(\mathcal F,\mathrm T)\text{ be the map constructed in Section 16.5 from pairs consisting of a maximal unramified }k\text{-torus }T\text{ and a facet }\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal A(T).\text{ Then }\Phi\text{ is equivariant under every }k\text{-automorphism of }G\text{ and surjective, and each fiber over }(\mathcal F,\mathrm T)\text{ is a single }G(k)_{\mathcal F}^{0+}\text{-orbit. For a given pair, }\mathcal F\text{ is maximal among facets of }\mathcal B(G)\text{ contained in }\mathcal A(T)\text{ if and only if the associated }\mathfrak f\text{-torus }\mathrm T\text{ of }\mathrm G_{\mathcal F}\text{ is minisotropic. If }\mathcal F\text{ is maximal, then }\dim(\mathcal F)=\dim(C)-\dim(C_G)=\dim(C'),\text{ where }C\text{ and }C_G\text{ are maximal }k\text{-split tori in }T\text{ and }Z(G),\text{ respectively, and }C'\text{ is a maximal }k\text{-split torus in }T\cap G_{\mathrm{der}}.
assumptions_latex: \Phi(T,\mathcal F)=(\mathcal F,\mathrm T)\text{ is the map constructed in Section 16.5 from a maximal unramified }k\text{-torus }T\text{ and a facet }\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal A(T)\text{ to the associated facet and }\mathfrak f\text{-torus data.}
statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&\text{(1) }\Phi\text{ is equivariant under every }k\text{-automorphism of }G;\\&\text{(2) }\Phi\text{ is surjective;}\\&\text{(3) each fiber over }(\mathcal F,\mathrm T)\text{ is a single }G(k)_{\mathcal F}^{0+}\text{-orbit;}\\&\text{(4) for }(T,\mathcal F)\mapsto(\mathcal F,\mathrm T),\ \mathcal F\text{ is maximal among facets of }\mathcal B(G)\text{ contained in }\mathcal A(T)\iff \mathrm T\text{ is minisotropic in }\mathrm G_{\mathcal F};\\&\text{(5) if }\mathcal F\text{ is maximal, }\dim(\mathcal F)=\dim(C)-\dim(C_G)=\dim(C'),\text{ where }C\text{ and }C_G\text{ are maximal }k\text{-split tori in }T\text{ and }Z(G),\text{ respectively, and }C'\text{ is a maximal }k\text{-split torus in }T\cap G_{\mathrm{der}}.\end{aligned}
statements.scope_note: Properties of the building-theoretic classification map from maximal unramified tori and facets to facet and reductive-quotient torus data.

statements.title: Definition of an I-stable maximal f-torus
statements.statement_plain: Since G_F generally has no natural f-structure, an I-stable maximal f-torus T is defined to be an I-stable maximal f'-torus fixed by the natural action of Gamma = Theta/I on the set of all such tori.

assumptions_latex: \Theta=\operatorname{Gal}(\ell/k)
I\text{ is the inertia subgroup of }\Theta
\Gamma=\Theta/I
statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{T}\text{ is an }I\text{-stable maximal }\mathfrak{f}\text{-torus of }\mathrm{G}_F\text{ if and only if it is fixed by the natural }\Gamma\text{-action on the set of }I\text{-stable maximal }\mathfrak{f}'\text{-tori of }\mathrm{G}_F.

statements.title: Fixed-point facet and vertex characterization for a minisotropic maximal torus
statements.statement_plain: Let T be a minisotropic maximal k-torus of M that splits over ell and whose apartment is the single point x. Then x is the unique Theta-fixed point of the facet of the ell-building containing x, hence the facet barycenter. If ell over k is unramified, x is a vertex of the M-building; if G is k-split, the facet is just x, so x is a vertex of the ell-building.
statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a minisotropic maximal \(k\)-torus of \(M\) that splits over \(\ell\), with \(\mathcal{A}_{M}(T)=\{x\}\). Then \(x\) is the unique \(\Theta\)-fixed point of the facet \(F\) of \(\mathcal{B}(M_{\ell})\) containing \(x\), and therefore the barycenter of \(F\). If \(\ell/k\) is unramified, \(x\) is a vertex of \(\mathcal{B}(M)\); if \(G\) is \(k\)-split, then \(F=\{x\}\) and \(x\) is a vertex of \(\mathcal{B}(M_{\ell})\).
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a minisotropic maximal \(k\)-torus of \(M\) that splits over \(\ell\).
statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is the unique \(\Theta\)-fixed point of the facet \(F\) of \(\mathcal{B}(M_{\ell})\) containing \(x\), hence the barycenter of \(F\). If \(\ell/k\) is unramified, then \(x\) is a vertex of \(\mathcal{B}(M)\). If \(G\) is \(k\)-split, then \(F=\{x\}\), so \(x\) is a vertex of \(\mathcal{B}(M_{\ell})\).
statements.scope_note: Fixed-point and vertex characterization associated with a minisotropic maximal k-torus whose apartment is a single point.

statements.title: Lattice and Matrix Realization of the Rank-One Torus
statements.statement_plain: The map from Z^2 to Z_0^3 given by (x,y) -> (x, y-x, -y) is equivariant for the stated sigma-actions, so it gives an isomorphism from the Weil restriction of the multiplicative group over ell/k to T. In the given diagonal matrix realization, T(k) consists of the displayed projective diagonal matrices parametrized by nonzero x in ell.
statements.statement_latex: The map \(\mathbf Z^2\to\mathbf Z_0^3\), \((x,y)\mapsto(x,y-x,-y)\), identifies the indicated \(\sigma\)-actions, with \(\sigma(x,y)=(y,x)\), and hence yields an isomorphism \(\operatorname{R}_{\ell/k}\mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{\sim}T\). In the stated matrix realization, \[T(k)=\left\{\left.\left[\begin{array}{lll}x&&\\&x/\bar x&\\&&\bar x^{-1}\end{array}\right]\ \right|\ x\in\ell^\times\right\}.\]
assumptions_latex: T is the torus in the indicated quasi-split rank-one model over k, with the stated sigma-actions on its cocharacter lattice and on Z^2.

statements.title: Cohomological and strict cohomological dimension
statements.statement_plain: For a finite extension E/F and i>0, each class in H^i(E/F,M) has finite order dividing [E:F], so each class in H^i(F,M) is torsion. The cohomological dimension is at most n when H^i(F,M) vanishes for all torsion Gal(F_s/F)-modules M and all i>n. Strict cohomological dimension is defined similarly using all Gal(F_s/F)-modules. They satisfy cd <= scd <= cd + 1.
statements.statement_latex: For finite E/F and i>0, every element of H^i(E/F,M) has finite order dividing [E:F], hence every element of H^i(F,M) has finite order. The condition cd(Gal(F_s/F))\le n means H^i(F,M)=0 for every torsion Gal(F_s/F)-module M and all i>n; scd(Gal(F_s/F))\le n is defined by the same condition for every Gal(F_s/F)-module M. One has cd(Gal(F_s/F))\le scd(Gal(F_s/F))\le cd(Gal(F_s/F))+1.
assumptions_latex: E/F is a finite field extension.
n is an integer.
For the definition of cd, M ranges over torsion Gal(F_s/F)-modules.
For the definition of scd, M ranges over Gal(F_s/F)-modules.
statements.conclusion_latex: Every element of H^i(E/F,M) has finite order dividing [E:F], and consequently every element of H^i(F,M) has finite order. We define cd(Gal(F_s/F))\le n by the vanishing of H^i(F,M) for every torsion Gal(F_s/F)-module M and every i>n, and define scd(Gal(F_s/F))\le n by the same vanishing for every Gal(F_s/F)-module M. Moreover, cd(Gal(F_s/F))\le scd(Gal(F_s/F))\le cd(Gal(F_s/F))+1.
statements.scope_note: Definitions of cohomological and strict cohomological dimension of the absolute Galois group, together with the finite-extension torsion property and their standard inequality.

statements.title: Characterizations of Fields of Dimension at Most One
statements.statement_plain: A field F has dimension at most one exactly when (i) its absolute Galois group has cohomological dimension at most one, with vanishing p-primary Brauer groups over all algebraic extensions in characteristic p; (ii) every algebraic extension E/F has trivial Brauer group; equivalently (iii) every finite-Galois norm map from L to E is surjective. It suffices to test the conditions on finite separable extensions E/F.
statements.statement_latex: For a field F, \dim(F)\le 1 is equivalent to each of: (1) \operatorname{cd}(\operatorname{Gal}(F_s/F))\le 1, with additionally \operatorname{Br}(E)(p)=0 for every algebraic E/F when \operatorname{char}(F)=p>0; (2) \operatorname{Br}(E)=0 for every algebraic E/F; and (3) every norm map N_{L/E}:L^{\times}\to E^{\times} for algebraic E/F and finite Galois L/E is surjective. It is enough to check these conditions for finite separable E/F.
assumptions_latex: F is a field with separable closure F_s.
For algebraic E/F and finite Galois L/E, N_{L/E}:L^{\times}\to E^{\times} denotes the norm map.
statements.conclusion_latex: \dim(F)\le 1 \Longleftrightarrow \left\{\begin{array}{l}\operatorname{cd}(\operatorname{Gal}(F_s/F))\le 1,\text{ and if }\operatorname{char}(F)=p>0,\ \operatorname{Br}(E)(p)=0\text{ for every algebraic }E/F;\\\operatorname{Br}(E)=0\text{ for every algebraic }E/F;\\N_{L/E}:L^{\times}\to E^{\times}\text{ is surjective for every algebraic }E/F\text{ and finite Galois }L/E.\end{array}\right.\ \text{It suffices to verify these conditions for finite separable }E/F.
statements.scope_note: Characterization of fields of dimension at most one via cohomological dimension, Brauer-group vanishing, and surjectivity of finite-Galois norm maps.

statements.title: Cohomological classification of lifts of affine Dynkin actions
statements.statement_plain: The k-structures on G* and G induce the same action on the ordinary Dynkin diagram, called the *-action. Their actions on the extended Dynkin diagram lift this common action. The first cohomology set H^1(Gamma, Xi) parametrizes these lifts up to Xi-conjugacy. Via H^1(Gamma, Xi) = H^1(k, G_ad*), a lift corresponds to the cohomology class classifying G relative to G*. In the cases where Xi is trivial, G equals G*.
statements.statement_latex: For the k-structures on G^* and G, the induced actions on the ordinary Dynkin diagram coincide, f_*=f, defining the *-action. Their actions on the extended Dynkin diagram restrict to this common action. The map c\mapsto c\cdot\widetilde f_* gives a one-to-one correspondence between H^1(\Gamma,\Xi) and \Xi-conjugacy classes of homomorphisms \widetilde f lifting f. Under the identification H^1(\Gamma,\Xi)=H^1(k,G_{\mathrm{ad}}^*), the corresponding class is the one classifying G relative to G^*. In the cases listed in Remark 10.6.3, \Xi=\{1\} and hence G=G^*.
assumptions_latex: Given the k-structures on G^* and G and the previously defined Γ, Ξ, 𝒟_K, and \widetilde{𝒟}_K.

The induced homomorphisms f_*, f: Γ → Aut(𝒟_K) and \widetilde f_*, \widetilde f: Γ → Aut(\widetilde{𝒟}_K) are as in the proposition, with both extended-diagram actions restricting to the same ordinary action f.
statements.conclusion_latex: f_*=f=:f;\quad c\mapsto c\cdot\widetilde f_*\text{ is a bijection from }H^1(\Gamma,\Xi)\text{ to the set of }\Xi\text{-conjugacy classes of homomorphisms }\widetilde f:\Gamma\to\operatorname{Aut}(\widetilde{\mathcal D}_K)\text{ lifting }f.\quad H^1(\Gamma,\Xi)=H^1(k,G_{\mathrm{ad}}^*)\text{ identifies the class of a lift with the classifying cohomology class of }G\text{ relative to }G^*.\quad \Xi=\{1\}\text{ in the cases listed in Remark 10.6.3, hence }G=G^*.

statements.statement_plain: In the standing Chapter 10 setting, let G be a reductive k-group, C a Gamma-stable chamber in the Bruhat-Tits building of G over K, J the associated Gamma-stable Iwahori subgroup, and N its normalizer, equivalently the stabilizer of C. statements.title: Sigma-fixed SU3 root groups and the connected unipotent model
statements.statement_plain: For the SU3 unitary model over ell/k with involution bar, the chosen Borel has the upper-unitriangular unipotent radical. The sigma-fixed positive and negative root groups are given by the displayed upper- and lower-unitriangular matrices with parameters u and v in ell satisfying v plus bar(v) equals u bar(u). Each root group is identified with the k-points of the connected unipotent algebraic group U_{ell/k}. Over a k-algebra R its points are pairs in R tensor_k ell satisfying the same relation, with product (u,v)(u',v')=(u+u',v+v'+u bar(u')) and inverse (-u,bar(v)); the group is noncommutative.
statements.statement_latex: In the SU3 unitary model over \(\ell/k\), the chosen Borel's unipotent radical is \(U_a(\ell)=\left\{\begin{bmatrix}1&u&v\\0&1&w\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}\mid u,v,w\in\ell\right\}\). The sigma-fixed positive and negative root elements are respectively \(u_a(u,v)=\begin{bmatrix}1&u&v\\0&1&\bar u\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}\) and \(u_{-a}(u,v)=\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\u&1&0\\v&\bar u&1\end{bmatrix}\), where \(u,v\in\ell\) satisfy \(v+\bar v=u\bar u\). These parametrizations identify each of \(U_a(k)\) and \(U_{-a}(k)\) with the k-points of the connected unipotent algebraic group \(U_{\ell/k}\), whose functor of points is \(U_{\ell/k}(R)=\{(u,v)\in(R\otimes_k\ell)^2\mid v+\bar v=u\bar u\}\). Its multiplication is \((u,v)(u',v')=(u+u',v+v'+u\overline{u'})\), inverse is \((-u,\bar v)\), and it is noncommutative.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell/k\) is the unitary-model field extension equipped with the involution \(x\mapsto\bar{x}\), and \(\sigma\) is the induced involution on the matrix group.
For every \(k\)-algebra \(R\), \(\bar{\phantom{x}}\) extends \(R\)-linearly to \(R\otimes_k\ell\).
statements.conclusion_latex: Each sigma-fixed root group \(U_a(k)\) and \(U_{-a}(k)\) is identified with \(U_{\ell/k}(k)\). For every \(k\)-algebra \(R\), \(U_{\ell/k}(R)=\{(u,v)\in(R\otimes_k\ell)^2\mid v+\bar v=u\bar u\}\), with \((u,v)(u',v')=(u+u',v+v'+u\overline{u'})\) and \((u,v)^{-1}=(-u,\bar v)\); the group is noncommutative.
statements.scope_note: Explicit sigma-fixed positive and negative root subgroups and their connected unipotent algebraic-group realization in the SU3 unitary model.

statements.title: Invariance of the Pinning under Changing the Normalizing Maximal Split Torus
statements.statement_plain: Any other maximal split torus normalizing U_a is conjugate to S by a K-rational element of the identity-component normalizer. That normalizer factors as T times the identity-component centralizer times U_a; the intersection with U_a is its center, K-isomorphic to the skew subspace {v in L | v + sigma(v) = 0} and having trivial Galois cohomology. Consequently the conjugating element factors into rational centralizer/torus and U_a parts, and changing the pinning is given by the K-defined inner automorphism (u,v) -> (u, v + sigma(w)u - sigma(u)w) for some w in L.
statements.statement_latex: For any maximal split torus $S'$ normalizing $U_a$, there exists $g\in(\operatorname{Norm}^{0}U_a)(K)$ such that $S'=gSg^{-1}$. Moreover, $\operatorname{Norm}^{0}U_a=T\cdot\operatorname{Cent}^{0}U_a\cdot U_a$, $(T\cdot\operatorname{Cent}^{0}U_a)\cap U_a=Z(U_a)$, and this center is K-isomorphic to $\{v\in L\mid v+v^{\sigma}=0\}$ with trivial Galois cohomology. Hence $g=g_1g_2$ with $g_1\in(T\cdot\operatorname{Cent}^{0}U_a)(K)$ and $g_2\in U_a(K)$. Replacing $S$ changes the pinning only by a K-defined rational inner automorphism of $H(L,L_2)$, which in the chosen coordinates is, for some $w\in L$, $(u,v)\mapsto\bigl(u,v+w^{\sigma}u-u^{\sigma}w\bigr)$.
assumptions_latex: $S$ and $S'$ are maximal split tori normalizing $U_a$.
The rank-one parametrization of $U_a$ by $H(L,L_2)$ and the involution $\sigma$ are as in the source setup.
statements.conclusion_latex: $S'=gSg^{-1}$ for some $g\in(\operatorname{Norm}^{0}U_a)(K)$; $g$ factors as $g=g_1g_2$ with $g_1\in(T\,\operatorname{Cent}^{0}U_a)(K)$ and $g_2\in U_a(K)$, and the induced pinning change is $(u,v)\mapsto(u,v+w^{\sigma}u-u^{\sigma}w)$ for some $w\in L$.
statements.scope_note: Rank-one setup with field K, unipotent subgroup U_a, maximal split torus S normalizing U_a, and the source parametrization of U_a by H(L,L_2).

statements.title: Standing Adelic Choice of Local Maximal Parahorics
statements.statement_plain: For every non-archimedean place v of k, fix a maximal parahoric subgroup P_v of G(k_v). Require P_v to be hyperspecial if G splits over an unramified extension of k_v. If G does not split over any unramified extension of k_v, so that its localization is residually split, and G is not of outer type A_r with even r, require P_v to be special. For an outer form of type A_r with even r, assume that the vector part of the affine simple root corresponding to the selected special parahoric is a divisible root; the maximal reductive quotient of the special fiber of its Bruhat-Tits group scheme is SO_{r+1}. Require the product of the archimedean local groups and all selected finite-place parahorics to be an open subgroup of G(A).
statements.statement_latex: \text{For every }v\in V_f\text{ fix a maximal parahoric subgroup }\mathcal P_v\subset\mathcal G(k_v)\text{ satisfying the following conditions. If }\mathcal G\text{ splits over an unramified extension of }k_v,\text{ then }\mathcal P_v\text{ is hyperspecial. If }\mathcal G\text{ does not split over any unramified extension of }k_v\text{, so that }\mathcal G_{k_v}\text{ is residually split, and }\mathcal G\text{ is not of outer type }A_r\text{ with even }r,\text{ then }\mathcal P_v\text{ is special. If }\mathcal G\text{ is an outer form of type }A_r\text{ with even }r,\text{ the vector part of the affine simple root corresponding to the selected special parahoric is assumed to be a divisible root, and the maximal reductive quotient of the special fiber of the associated Bruhat--Tits group scheme is }\mathrm{SO}_{r+1}.\text{ Finally, }\prod_{v\in V_\infty}\mathcal G(k_v)\cdot\prod_{v\in V_f}\mathcal P_v\text{ is an open subgroup of }\mathcal G(A).
assumptions_latex: V_f\text{ and }V_\infty\text{ denote the non-archimedean and archimedean places of }k,\text{ respectively}.
\text{For each }v\in V_f,\ \mathcal P_v\subset \mathcal G(k_v)\text{ is chosen to be a maximal parahoric subgroup}.
statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&\mathcal G\text{ splitting over an unramified extension of }k_v\implies \mathcal P_v\text{ is hyperspecial};\\&\mathcal G\text{ not splitting over any unramified extension of }k_v,\ \mathcal G_{k_v}\text{ residually split, and not of outer type }A_r\text{ with even }r\implies \mathcal P_v\text{ is special};\\&\text{in outer type }A_r\text{ with even }r,\text{ the vector part of the corresponding affine simple root is divisible and the maximal reductive quotient of the associated special fiber is }\mathrm{SO}_{r+1};\\&\prod_{v\in V_\infty}\mathcal G(k_v)\cdot\prod_{v\in V_f}\mathcal P_v\text{ is open in }\mathcal G(A).\end{aligned}

statements.title: Euler-Poincare measure for S-arithmetic subgroups
statements.statement_plain: Under the stated finite-index torsion-free condition on the S-arithmetic subgroups, there is a possibly zero invariant Euler-Poincare measure whose quotient volume equals the absolute Euler-Poincare characteristic. It factors up to sign into local Euler-Poincare measures. Non-archimedean factors are always nonzero; an archimedean factor is nonzero exactly when the local group has a compact Cartan subgroup. Therefore the global measure is nonzero for global function fields, and its nonvanishing over a number field implies that the field is totally real.
statements.statement_latex: Assume that the S-arithmetic subgroups under consideration have torsion-free subgroups of finite index (equivalently, k is a number field, or k is a function field with G k-anisotropic). Then there exists a possibly zero G_S-invariant Euler-Poincare measure \(\mu_S^{\mathrm{EP}}\) satisfying \(\lvert\chi(\Gamma)\rvert=\mu_S^{\mathrm{EP}}(G_S/\Gamma)\) for every S-arithmetic subgroup \(\Gamma\) of G_S. Up to sign it is the product of the local measures \(\mu_v^{\mathrm{EP}}\), with non-archimedean factors always nonzero and archimedean factors nonzero exactly when \(G(k_v)\) has a compact Cartan subgroup (equivalently, G has a \(k_v\)-anisotropic maximal torus); hence it is nonzero over global function fields, and over number fields its nonvanishing implies that k is totally real.
assumptions_latex: The field k is global, and the S-arithmetic subgroups under consideration have torsion-free subgroups of finite index; equivalently, k is a number field, or k is a function field and G is k-anisotropic.
statements.scope_note: Euler-Poincare measures and characteristics for S-arithmetic subgroups of G_S over global fields under the stated finite-index torsion-free hypothesis.

statements.title: Adelic Haar Measure and Product Restriction
statements.statement_plain: For a semisimple group over a global field, the finite-place product of the specified local subgroup volumes converges absolutely. The resulting adelic Haar measure restricts on the displayed open subgroup to the product of the corresponding local measures.
statements.statement_latex: Let k be a global field, let G be semisimple over k, and let \omega^* induce the local Haar measures \omega_v^*. For the specified subgroups P_v at finite places, the product \prod_{v\in V_f}\omega_v^*(P_v) is absolutely convergent. The datum \omega^* determines a Haar measure \omega_A^* on G(A) whose restriction to H=\left(\prod_{v\in V_\infty}G(k_v)\right)\times\left(\prod_{v\in V_f}P_v\right) is \left(\prod_{v\in V_\infty}\omega_v^*\right)\cdot\left(\prod_{v\in V_f}\left.\omega_v^*\right|_{P_v}\right).
assumptions_latex: k\text{ is a global field with archimedean and finite place sets }V_\infty\text{ and }V_f.
G\text{ is semisimple over }k.

\omega^*\text{ induces local Haar measures }\omega_v^*\text{, and }(P_v)_{v\in V_f}\text{ is the specified family for which }H=\left(\prod_{v\in V_\infty}G(k_v)\right)\times\left(\prod_{v\in V_f}P_v\right)\text{ is the displayed open subgroup of }G(A).

statements.title: Euler-Poincare Characteristic and Covolume of a Principal Arithmetic Subgroup
statements.statement_plain: For each archimedean place, the Euler-Poincare measure equals the specified Haar measure times the Euler-Poincare characteristic of the compact dual, up to sign. For the stated principal arithmetic subgroup in the product of archimedean groups, its absolute Euler-Poincare characteristic is the product of the local characteristics times the covolume.
statements.statement_latex: For every archimedean place v, the Hirzebruch proportionality principle gives, up to sign, \(\mu_v^{\mathrm{EP}}=\chi_v\mu_v\), where \(\mu_v\) is the Haar measure on \(G(k_v)\) defined in 18.5.5 and \(\chi_v\) is the Euler-Poincare characteristic of the compact dual of the associated symmetric space. If \(S\) is the set of archimedean places of k, \(G_S=\prod_{v\in S}G(k_v)\), and \(\Lambda=G(k)\cap\prod_{v\notin S}P_v\) is a principal arithmetic subgroup of \(G_S\), then \[|\chi(\Lambda)|=\left(\prod_{v\in S}\chi_v\right)\mu_S(G_S/\Lambda).\]
assumptions_latex: v\text{ is an archimedean place of }k
\mu_v\text{ is the Haar measure on }G(k_v)\text{ defined in 18.5.5}
\chi_v\text{ is the Euler-Poincare characteristic of the compact dual of the symmetric space associated with }G(k_v)
S=\{v:v\text{ is an archimedean place of }k\}
G_S=\prod_{v\in S}G(k_v)
\Lambda=G(k)\cap\prod_{v\notin S}P_v\text{ is a principal arithmetic subgroup of }G_S
statements.conclusion_latex: \mu_v^{\mathrm{EP}}=\pm\chi_v\mu_v\quad(v\in S),\qquad |\chi(\Lambda)|=\left(\prod_{v\in S}\chi_v\right)\mu_S(G_S/\Lambda).

statements.title: Finiteness of exceptional places and local hyperspecial identifications
statements.statement_plain: For the finite exceptional set consisting of S together with places where the local group is not quasi-split, does not split over an unramified extension, or the chosen parahoric is not hyperspecial, the set is finite. Outside it, the local group is quasi-split and unramified, the parahoric is hyperspecial, and it is isomorphic to the quasi-split form in a way carrying parahorics and their special fibers isomorphically.
statements.statement_latex: Let \mathfrak{S}=S\cup\{v\notin S:\ G_{k_v}\text{ is not quasi-split, or }G_{k_v}\text{ does not split over an unramified extension of }k_v,\text{ or }P_v\text{ is not hyperspecial}\}. Then \mathfrak{S} is finite. For each v\notin\mathfrak{S}, G_{k_v} is quasi-split, splits over an unramified extension of k_v, and P_v is a hyperspecial parahoric subgroup of G(k_v). Moreover, a k_v-isomorphism G_{k_v}\simeq\mathcal{G}_{k_v} carries P_v isomorphically onto \mathcal{P}_v, and the corresponding special fibers satisfy \bar{M}_v\simeq\overline{\mathcal{M}}_v.
assumptions_latex: The global data k, G, finite set S, family (P_v), quasi-split inner form \mathcal{G}, parahorics (\mathcal{P}_v), and reductive special fibers \bar{M}_v and \overline{\mathcal{M}}_v are as in the preceding theorem.

For v\notin S, the exceptional conditions are evaluated over the local field k_v: G_{k_v} may fail to be quasi-split, may fail to split over an unramified extension of k_v, or P_v may fail to be hyperspecial.
statements.conclusion_latex: \mathfrak{S}=S\cup\{v\notin S:\ G_{k_v}\text{ is not quasi-split, or }G_{k_v}\text{ does not split over an unramified extension of }k_v,\text{ or }P_v\text{ is not hyperspecial}\}\text{ is finite. For every }v\notin\mathfrak{S},\ G_{k_v}\text{ is quasi-split and splits over an unramified extension of }k_v,\ P_v\text{ is hyperspecial, and there is a }k_v\text{-isomorphism }G_{k_v}\simeq\mathcal{G}_{k_v}\text{ carrying }P_v\text{ isomorphically onto }\mathcal{P}_v;\text{ hence }\bar{M}_v\simeq\overline{\mathcal{M}}_v.

statements.title: Class number relative to a coherent parahoric collection
statements.statement_plain: For an absolutely almost simple simply connected group G over a global field k, with adele algebra A and coherent parahoric subgroups P_v at finite places, the product of G(k_v) over infinite places together with the P_v double cosets in G(A) modulo G(k) is finite under the stated number-field or anisotropic function-field hypothesis. Its cardinality is the class number of G relative to P, written c(G,P).

statements.title: S-Arithmetic Subgroups and Basic Properties
statements.statement_plain: Let K be an arbitrary compact open subgroup of G(A_S), and set Lambda = G(k) intersect K, with G(k) and Lambda embedded diagonally in G_S. A subgroup H of G_S is S-arithmetic if it is commensurable with Lambda; a subgroup H' of G'_S is S-arithmetic if it is commensurable with iota(Lambda). In the standing setup these S-arithmetic subgroups have finite covolume and, because G_S is noncompact, are infinite. Under the stated strong-approximation property, the closure of Lambda in G(A_S) is K.

In the standing setup these S-arithmetic subgroups have finite covolume and, since G_S is noncompact, are infinite. If the stated strong-approximation property holds, the closure of \Lambda in G(A_S) is \mathcal K.

statements.title: Parahoric group-scheme factorizations and reduction-map surjectivity
statements.statement_plain: (i) The integral-point groups \(\mathfrak G_f^0(\mathcal O)\) and \(\mathfrak G_f(\mathcal O)\) have the displayed factorizations through the unipotent, C, H, P, and N pieces. (ii) The barred groups over \(\overline K\) factor as \(\mathfrak G_f^0(\mathcal O)\) times the corresponding barred torus group. (iii) Surjectivity of the corresponding canonical torus map implies surjectivity of the canonical map from \(\mathfrak G_f^0(\mathcal O)\), respectively \(\mathfrak G_f(\mathcal O)\), to the barred group over \(\overline{\mathbf K}\).
statements.statement_latex: \begin{aligned}(i)\;&\mathfrak G_f^0(\mathcal O)=\mathfrak U_f^+(\mathcal O)\mathfrak C_f^0(\mathcal O)=U_f^+U_f^-U_f^+H^0=P_f^0=U_f^+U_f^-N_f^0,\\&\mathfrak G_f(\mathcal O)=\mathfrak U_f^+(\mathcal O)\mathfrak C_f(\mathcal O)=\mathfrak G_f^0(\mathcal O)H^1=P_f^1=U_f^+U_f^-N_f^1.\\(ii)\;&\overline{\mathfrak G}_f^0(\overline K)=\mathfrak G_f^0(\mathcal O)\,\overline{\mathfrak T}^{0}(\overline K),\qquad \overline{\mathfrak G}_f(\overline K)=\mathfrak G_f^0(\mathcal O)\,\overline{\mathfrak T}(\overline K).\\(iii)\;&\text{If }\mathfrak T^0(\mathcal O)\to\overline{\mathfrak T}^{0}(\overline K)\text{ (respectively }\mathfrak T(\mathcal O)\to\overline{\mathfrak T}(\overline K)\text{) is surjective, then }\\&\mathfrak G_f^0(\mathcal O)\to\overline{\mathfrak G_f^0}(\overline{\mathbf K})\text{ (respectively }\mathfrak G_f(\mathcal O)\to\overline{\mathfrak G}_f(\overline{\mathbf K})\text{) is surjective.}\end{aligned}
assumptions_latex: For (iii), assume the canonical torus map \(\mathfrak T^{0}(\mathcal O)\to\overline{\mathfrak T}^{0}(\overline K)\) (respectively \(\mathfrak T(\mathcal O)\to\overline{\mathfrak T}(\overline K)\)) is surjective.
statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}(i)\;&\mathfrak G_f^0(\mathcal O)=\mathfrak U_f^+(\mathcal O)\mathfrak C_f^0(\mathcal O)=U_f^+U_f^-U_f^+H^0=P_f^0=U_f^+U_f^-N_f^0,\\&\mathfrak G_f(\mathcal O)=\mathfrak U_f^+(\mathcal O)\mathfrak C_f(\mathcal O)=\mathfrak G_f^0(\mathcal O)H^1=P_f^1=U_f^+U_f^-N_f^1.\\(ii)\;&\overline{\mathfrak G}_f^0(\overline K)=\mathfrak G_f^0(\mathcal O)\,\overline{\mathfrak T}^{0}(\overline K),\qquad \overline{\mathfrak G}_f(\overline K)=\mathfrak G_f^0(\mathcal O)\,\overline{\mathfrak T}(\overline K).\\(iii)\;&\mathfrak G_f^0(\mathcal O)\twoheadrightarrow\overline{\mathfrak G_f^0}(\overline{\mathbf K}),\qquad \mathfrak G_f(\mathcal O)\twoheadrightarrow\overline{\mathfrak G}_f(\overline{\mathbf K}).\end{aligned}
statements.scope_note: Notation and ambient hypotheses are inherited from the preceding Bruhat-Tits setup. The witnesses additionally say the torus-map surjectivity occurs in cases (A) and (B) or when “0 is henselian”; that phrase is unresolved and is intentionally not reconstructed.

statements.title: Absolute root groups in the SU3 rank-one model
statements.statement_plain: For the SU3 rank-one model over a quadratic extension ell/k, the absolute root groups for a-tilde and a-tilde-prime exist only over ell and are additive groups in standard SL3 coordinates. The b-tilde root group descends to k, but its standard additive coordinate is not Galois-equivariant; after transporting the action it is the trace-zero kernel of the Weil restriction of the additive group, with R-points x in R tensor_k ell satisfying x plus bar(x) equals zero for every k-algebra R.
statements.statement_latex: In the stated SU3 setup for a quadratic extension \ell/k with \Gamma=\{1,\sigma\}, the absolute root groups U_{\widetilde a} and U_{\widetilde a'} are defined only over \ell (not over k) and are each isomorphic over \ell to \mathbf G_{\mathrm a}/\ell via standard \mathrm{SL}_3 coordinates. The absolute root group U_{\widetilde b} is defined over k, but its standard \mathbf G_{\mathrm a} coordinate is not \Gamma-equivariant; transporting the action identifies U_{\widetilde b} with \mathrm R^0_{\ell/k}\mathbf G_{\mathrm a}:=\ker(\operatorname{Tr}_{\ell/k}:\mathrm R_{\ell/k}\mathbf G_{\mathrm a}\to\mathbf G_{\mathrm a}), whose R-points are \{x\in R\otimes_k\ell\mid x+\bar x=0\} for every k-algebra R, with \bar x=({\operatorname{id}}_R\otimes\sigma)(x).
assumptions_latex: \ell/k\text{ is quadratic with }\Gamma=\operatorname{Gal}(\ell/k)=\{1,\sigma\}
U_{\widetilde a},U_{\widetilde a'}\text{ are the absolute root groups in the stated }\mathrm{SU}_3\text{ setup}
R\text{ is a }k\text{-algebra}
\bar{x}=({\operatorname{id}}_R\otimes\sigma)(x)\text{ for }x\in R\otimes_k\ell
statements.conclusion_latex: U_{\widetilde a}\text{ and }U_{\widetilde a'}\text{ are defined over }\ell\text{ but not }k\text{ and each }\simeq\mathbf G_{\mathrm a}/\ell;\quad U_{\widetilde b}\text{ is defined over }k\text{ and }U_{\widetilde b}\simeq\mathrm R^0_{\ell/k}\mathbf G_{\mathrm a}:=\ker\!\left(\operatorname{Tr}_{\ell/k}:\mathrm R_{\ell/k}\mathbf G_{\mathrm a}\to\mathbf G_{\mathrm a}\right),\quad \mathrm R^0_{\ell/k}\mathbf G_{\mathrm a}(R)=\{x\in R\otimes_k\ell\mid x+\bar x=0\}
statements.scope_note: Explicit absolute-root-group calculation for the SU3 rank-one model over a quadratic extension ell/k; the standard SL3 coordinate on U_{b-tilde} is not Gamma-equivariant and transports the action to the trace-zero Weil restriction.

deferred.title: Universal Property of the Symmetric Algebra
deferred.statement_plain: The symmetric algebra Sym(M) is universal for R-linear maps from M into an R-algebra whose images commute: such a map extends uniquely to an R-algebra homomorphism from Sym(M). If the target is graded and M maps to degree one, the extension is graded; therefore module maps between finite-rank free modules induce graded maps between their symmetric algebras.

If A is graded and f(M)\subseteq A_1, then \operatorname{Sym}(f) is graded. Consequently, an R-linear map f:M\to N between free finite-rank R-modules induces a unique graded R-algebra map \operatorname{Sym}(M)\to\operatorname{Sym}(N).
